text: Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sarah. She loved to skip. She skipped everywhere - inside her house, outside her house, around the block and even in the rain! Today, Sarah wanted to skip in the kitchen. She skipped around the table and hopped over to the faucet. It was bright purple and made Sarah so happy. She felt silly, so she talked to the faucet. "Hi, Faucet," she said. "You're so purple! I love skipping around you." The faucet wasn't very loud, but it answered in a small voice. "Thank you, Sarah," it said. "I like it when you skip. Please keep skipping around me." So Sarah kept skipping around the faucet. Faster and faster she skipped until the faucet was a blur of purple spinning around her. She giggled and skipped and twirled until she was too tired to keep going. "That was so much fun," Sarah said and gave the faucet a big smile. "Let's skip again soon!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Josh. He had very beautiful eyes and a lovable smile. One day, Josh was walking in a maze and it was very cold. He started to shiver and he felt scared. Suddenly, Josh met an old man who was sitting in the corner. He had a very kind and thoughtful face. The old man asked to Josh: "Why are you shivering little boy?". Josh replied: "I'm scared, I don't know where I'm going". The old man told him: "Life has a lot of turns and surprises for everyone, so don't be scared and trust your heart". Then the old man gave Josh a hug and Josh smiled. The old man's advice helped Josh to understand life and he was no longer scared of the maze. In the end, Josh could get out of the maze and he learned that it is important to be thoughtful and trust your heart.

Ernie was playing in his room when he heard a terrible noise coming from outside. He stepped outside to investigate and he saw that his dad was out in the garden involved in a big project. Ernie was very curious, so he asked his dad what he was doing. His dad said he was making something with a hammer. Ernie was so excited and asked if he could help. His dad let him try hammering for a few minutes, but it was too difficult for him. After a few attempts Ernie dropped the hammer and it made a terrible noise. His dad was mad because the hammer was broken. He said Ernie was too young to help and sent him back inside. Ernie was sad and confused. He had been so careful, why was his dad so mad? Suddenly Ernie realized what had happened; he had made a terrible mess! Ernie was embarrassed and he knew he had to fix it, but he didn't know how. He was really scared and he began to cry. Ernie's dad quickly came to his side and hugged him tight. He said that it was okay and he understood why the hammer broke. He said a real hammer was much too heavy for Ernie. Then his dad went back outside and got a special toy hammer for Ernie. They spent the rest of the afternoon making things together, and it was a lot of fun.

Once there was a little girl named Amy. She was very proud, because today was the day she was going to stretch her penny. She couldn't wait! Amy carefully held the penny in her hand and stretched it out. She felt so proud as she saw it get longer and longer. Soon the penny was twice its original size! Amy smiled and showed her mom the penny. Her mom was also proud to see her daughter stretching her penny. Amy took the penny and wrapped it around her arm. She was so excited to show all of her friends her penny. Amy was so proud of what she had accomplished. She held her stretched penny high for everyone to see and was filled with joy.

Little Pete and Mommy were out for a walk in the park and as they wandered, something special caught their eye. It was a huge and shiny prize, standing all by itself in the center of the path. Pete was so excited about the prize that he asked Mommy if he could have it. She told him that he could, but only if he was really dependable. Pete didn't quite know what dependable meant but he was determined to do whatever it took to get that sparkly prize. So, over the coming week, Pete worked extra hard to be dependable. He helped Mommy unload the groceries, feed the dog, and take out the trash. Finally, the day came that Mommy decided Pete had earned his prize. She smiled and said, "I'm so proud of you! Now, here's the prize, but you must promise to always keep it safe." Pete happily agreed and smiled as he clutched the prize tight in his hands. He was so proud of himself and said, "Thank you, Mommy, for this amazing prize!" Mommy laughed and said, "You're very welcome, Pete. Now please remember, to keep something special like a prize, you must be dependable!" And from that moment on, Pete was sure to always be dependable and take extra special care of his prize.

Jimmy and Lily were best friends. They did everything together. One day, they decided to go for a walk in the park. When they arrived, they met a beautiful butterfly. Jimmy and Lily were so excited that they wanted to show their friends. They asked the butterfly to follow them and the butterfly said yes. The result of their visit was even better than expected. Everybody in the park was amazed to see the butterfly, and everyone wanted to take pictures. Jimmy and Lily were so proud and grateful for the chance to meet such a beautiful creature. They thanked the butterfly for its time and sent it on its way. Jimmy and Lily said goodbye and waved as the butterfly flew away. They were so happy to have this wonderful experience. And they would never forget the amazing result of their meeting.

Once upon a time, there was a blue bell. Every day, the bell would ring and make everyone happy. One day, the bell broke. Everyone was sad. The people decided they needed to replace the bell. They looked everywhere but couldn't find one. Then, they had a wonderful idea. They found some blue paper and a pair of scissors. They made their own bell out of the paper! The new bell wasn't as nice as the old one, but it still worked. Everyone was so happy that they could hear the bell again. Now, the blue bell rings everyday to make the people happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved listening to the radio. One day, Lily's mom came into her room and said, "Lily, can you please clean up your toys?" Lily replied, "Sure, Mommy. But can I listen to the radio while I clean?" Mommy thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, but just keep it at a low volume." Lily happily cleaned up her toys while listening to the radio. Suddenly, a silly song came on and Lily started dancing around the room. Mommy peeked in and asked, "What are you doing, Lily?" Lily giggled and said, "I'm dancing to this silly song on the radio!" Mommy smiled and said, "Okay, but don't forget to finish cleaning up." Lily nodded and continued to clean while listening to the radio. She felt happy and content knowing that she could listen to her favorite music while doing her chores.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Dave. He was three years old and very wise. One day, he decided to take a bath. So, he reached for the shampoo and heard a loud noise. Dave was scared. He looked around to see where the noise came from. Suddenly, he saw a mouse. The mouse was standing on the shampoo bottle, eating his bubble bath. Dave couldn't believe it! He felt very guilty. He knew he should not have left the shampoo bottle open. Dave said to the mouse,"What are you doing? You can't eat that." The mouse replied,"I'm sorry. I just really like bubble bath. I guess I'm a bit hungry." Dave smiled and said,"That's okay. I promise to keep shampoo bottles closed so you don't get hurt." The mouse thanked him and went on his way. Dave took a nice long bath and felt much better. From that day on, he remembered to close his shampoo bottles so he could keep his animal friends safe.

Once upon a time, there was a green bird named Bobo. He lived near a rail. One day, he saw a big cat walking near the rail. Bobo began to worry. Bobo went to his friend, Toto the dog. "Toto, help! There is a big cat near the rail. I am worried," said Bobo. Toto wanted to help his friend. Toto barked at the big cat. The big cat got scared and ran away. Bobo was happy and said, "Thank you, Toto! You saved me from the big cat. I am not worried anymore." From that day on, Bobo and Toto played near the rail and had lots of fun. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a package. It was all shiny and red, and it glowed in the dark. It was filled with exciting surprises, and Mommy said it was for a special treat. The little girl was so excited to see the package! She ran over to it and held it in her little hands. She could feel how soft it was and the wonderful way it glowed. And then she opened it. Inside, there were all sorts of funny toys. Some of them moved around and some of them sang. The little girl was so happy! She played with the funny toys all day. And every time she held them under the light, they would shine and glow. It was so much fun! The little girl was so happy she had her special package. She played with it until the bedtime. And even when the lights went out, the package kept its wonderful glow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big water bottle that she loved to carry with her everywhere. One day, she noticed that her water bottle was very heavy and she couldn't carry it anymore. Lily went to her mom and said, "Mommy, my water bottle is too heavy. Can you help me carry it?" Her mom replied, "Lily, you don't need to carry such a heavy water bottle. You can drink from a smaller one that is easier for you to carry." Lily understood what her mom said and went to get a smaller water bottle. As she was pouring water into the new bottle, she noticed that her old water bottle had a leak. She told her mom about it and her mom said, "Lily, it's important to take care of our things. We need to fix the leak so we don't waste water." Lily learned that it's important to take care of her things and to only carry what she needs.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She loved to drink her milk. One night, she wanted to do something special so Jane decided to go outside and see a firework. When she arrived outside, she saw a broken firework on the ground. She picked up the broken firework and decided to drink her milk by the firework. Jane loved drinking her milk by the broken firework. Soon, the sky lit up with bright colors. The firework sparkled and shone. Jane was so happy to see the amazing firework. She drank the last of her milk and smiled. The firework soon ended and all of the colors faded away. Jane put the broken firework in her pocket and ran back inside. Jane had a wonderful time drinking her milk and watching the firework.

John and Tara were playing in the park. John looked towards the horizon and saw an ancient house in the distance. He said to Tara, "Let's go explore the old house!" Tara agreed, so they ventured off to the house. When they got there, John saw a desk in the corner. He said, "Let's search inside the desk!" They opened it up and found the most amazing things. There were shiny coins, old jewelry, and ancient books. John wanted to keep all the treasure, but Tara said, "We have to surrender it. We can't keep these things." John was sad but he knew Tara was right. They returned the treasure to the desk and quietly left the old house. Even though they couldn't keep the treasure, they had an amazing adventure that they would never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a dancer named Sandy. She was a beautiful dancer and she loved to perform for her family and friends. One day, Sandy got hurt and she was very upset. She had hurt her ankle and was worried she would never dance again. Sandy's mother saw how distressed she was, so she decided to help. She put a bandage on Sandy's ankle and sang her a special healing song. She said, "Everyone gets hurt sometimes, but that doesn't mean you can't still dance. With a little time and patience, you will heal and be dancing again!" And that's exactly what happened. Sandy's ankle healed and she could dance again. She remembered the lesson her mom had taught her; that sometimes when life is tough, the best thing to do is to be patient and give it time. Eventually, you will heal and be better than before!

One day, a prince was playing in the garden with his ball. He saw a big bird in the sky. The bird was hungry and wanted to eat the ball. The prince was scared and ran to his mother. "Mommy, mommy, help me! The bird wants to take my ball!" he cried. His mother hugged him and said, "Don't worry, my dear. I will protect you and your ball. The bird can't hurt you." She took a stick and waved it at the bird. The bird was afraid and flew away. The prince was happy and thanked his mother. "Thank you, mommy. You are brave and kind. I love you," he said. His mother smiled and said, "I love you too, my prince. You are my precious son. Now, let's go inside and have some cookies." They went inside and ate some cookies. The prince shared his cookies with his mother. He was sorry for the bird. He hoped the bird would find some food somewhere else. He wished the bird would be his friend. He said a little prayer for the bird. He was a good prince.

Ben and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. They had a big jar to keep their finds. Ben saw a shiny thing under a leaf. He picked it up and put it in the jar. "What is that?" Mia asked. "I don't know. Let's examine it," Ben said. They took the jar inside and put it on the table. They looked at the shiny thing. It was round and had a hole in the middle. It had some letters on it. "It looks like a ring," Mia said. "Maybe it is a magic ring," Ben said. They tried to read the letters, but they were too hard. They asked their mom for help. Mom looked at the ring and smiled. She took it out of the jar and put it on her finger. "Where did you find this?" she asked. "In the garden, under a leaf," Ben said. Mom hugged them and said, "This is a very special ring. It was your grandma's ring. She gave it to me when I married your dad. I lost it a long time ago. I thought I would never see it again. You found my True ring!" Ben and Mia were happy. They had given mom a warm gift. They felt warm too. They had found a magic ring. A ring of love.

Once upon a time, there was a huge elephant. He loved to march around the jungle. One day, he saw a sink in the river. The sink was very small and the elephant was very big. He tried to drink from the sink, but his trunk was too big. So, he decided to march to another spot in the river where he could drink. The end.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit and a mouse who were good friends. The rabbit was always very careful and thought before she moved. The mouse, who was very foolish, was always in a hurry and didn't think before he moved. One day, the rabbit and mouse were walking along and saw a cactus. The mouse saw the cactus and was very excited. He quickly moved and touched it. But, to his surprise, he felt a sharp prick! He screamed in pain. The rabbit quickly ran to the mouse. The rabbit said, "You're so foolish! Why did you move so fast? You should have thought before you moved. Always use caution when touching something you're not familiar with." The mouse learned his lesson and was more careful after that. He thought before he moved and never made the same mistake again. Since then, the mouse and the rabbit had a great time exploring their new world. They never forgot the moral of their story: it is important to think before you move.

Once upon a time there was a young girl who lived in a small house. One day she decided to go for a walk in the woods near her house. While she was walking, she saw a small door in the ground. She used all her strength to push it open and saw some stairs that led up to an attic. She went up the stairs and when she entered the attic, she saw someone. He was dressed in all black and he looked like he was in a hurry. He spoke to the young girl, "You should not be here. Hurry, go back the way you came". The young girl was scared and she quickly ran back the way she had come. But before she could get very far away, the man chasing her appeared. He was coming closer and closer. The young girl started to cry and she ran faster, but she couldn't outrun the man. He quickly caught up to her and grabbed her. The young girl was never seen again.

Anna and Ben like to play sport. They have a ball and a net. They throw the ball to each other and try to catch it. Sometimes they miss and the ball falls on the grass. One day, they play sport in the park. They have fun and laugh. But then a big cloud comes. It is dark and cold. Anna and Ben hear a loud noise. It is thunder. They see a flash. It is lightning. They are scared. "Let's go home!" Anna says. "It will rain soon!" But Ben is stubborn. He likes to play sport. He does not want to stop. "No!" Ben says. "I want to play more!" He throws the ball to Anna. But Anna does not catch it. She runs to the bench. She sees a blanket. She covers herself with the blanket. She feels warm and safe. "Ben, come here!" Anna says. "It is not good to play in the storm!" But Ben does not listen. He runs after the ball. He does not see the rain. He does not feel the wind. He is wet and cold. "Ben, please!" Anna says. "You will get sick!" But Ben is still stubborn. He throws the ball to the net. He misses. The ball rolls away. He chases the ball. He does not hear Anna. He does not see the car. He is in danger. "Ben, watch out!" Anna screams. The car stops. The driver gets out. He is angry. He yells at Ben. He takes the ball. He drives away. Ben is sad. He lost his ball. He lost his sport. He runs to the bench. He sees Anna. She is still covered with the blanket. She is still warm and safe. "Anna, I'm sorry!" Ben says. "You were right. I was wrong. I was stubborn." Anna hugs Ben. She shares the blanket. She forgives Ben. "It's okay, Ben." Anna says. "We can play sport another day. But now we have to go home. Mom and Dad will be worried." They hold hands. They walk home. They are friends. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. He was enormous! One day, he went for a walk in the jungle. He met a little mouse who was lost. The elephant helped the mouse find his way home. But then, the elephant got lost too! He wandered into a place called jail. The jail was not a nice place to be. The elephant felt sad and scared. He wanted to leave and go back to the jungle. Luckily, the mouse remembered the way and came to help the elephant. Together, they found the way out of the jail and back to the jungle. From then on, the elephant and the mouse were good friends and went on many adventures together.

Once there was a girl who dreamed of becoming a princess. She was very impatient and wished she could go to the palace right away. One day, her parents told her that she could become a princess if she ate the entire bowl of rice. She was so excited and quickly started eating the bowl of rice. She ate and ate and ate until the bowl was empty. By the time she finished, she was turning into a beautiful princess! Her parents were so proud of her. She became a princess with a beautiful dress, a crown and a magical wand. She was so happy and excited to finally become a princess. Now she can enjoy living in the palace and play with her royal friends every day. Her dreams of becoming a princess had finally come true!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy model car. He played with it every day and took it with him wherever he went. Tim's model car was very special to him. One day, Tim's model car stopped working. It was dead. Tim was very sad and started to complain to his mom. "Mom, my car is dead! It won't go anymore!" he said with tears in his eyes. His mom hugged him and promised to help him fix the car. Together, they opened the car and found that the battery was dead. They replaced the battery, and the model car started working again. Tim was so happy that he stopped complaining. He thanked his mom and played with his car all day long. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a van that wanted to go on an adventure. It wanted to explore the world and have some fun. So one day, the van hung itself off the edge of a cliff. The van was too careless, and it was struggling to hang on. It shook and wobbled, and started to slip. Suddenly, a friendly bird flew by and saw the van hanging off the cliff. Quickly, the bird darted to the top of the cliff and helped the van get back on solid ground. The van thanked the bird, and they hugged goodbye. After that, the van was extra careful so it would never fall off again. The van never forgot the friendly bird, and they remained good friends.

Once, there was a little girl named Karen. She was only three years old, and she liked to go on lots of adventures. One day, she wanted to explore the garden. But when she tried to go outside, her mum wouldn't permit it. She said the garden was too dangerous for her. Karen was very sad, but then she decided to explore the house. In the living room, she spied a plastic box, cleverly hidden under a cushion. She looked inside and found lots of wondrous treasures - like beading, funny-looking rocks, and tiny plastic animals. She was very excited! Karen had fun playing with the plastic box. But then, when she wanted to get something else out of the box, it was gone! It had been taken away! Karen was very upset, and she wanted to find the hidden plastic box. Her mum finally relented and let her look outside in the garden. After a while, Karen found the plastic box, very carefully hidden behind the bushes. She was very happy - her adventures had a happy ending!

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They saw some flowers that were not open yet. Lily said, "I wonder when they will bloom. They are so pretty." Max said, "Maybe they need some water. Let's get the hose and spray them." He ran to the shed and got the hose. He turned on the tap and water came out. Lily said, "Be careful, Max. Don't spray too hard. You might hurt the flowers." She followed him to the flower bed. Max said, "OK, Lily. I will be gentle." He sprayed the water on the flowers. Some of the flowers opened and showed their colors. Lily and Max clapped and cheered. They heard their mom calling them from the kitchen. She said, "Lily and Max, it's time for lunch. I made spaghetti for you. Come and wash your hands." Lily and Max dropped the hose and ran to the house. They loved spaghetti. They washed their hands and sat at the table. Their mom served them plates of spaghetti with sauce and cheese. She said, "How was your playtime in the garden? Did you see anything interesting?" Lily and Max said, "Yes, mom. We saw some flowers bloom. They were so pretty. We gave them some water." Their mom said, "That's very nice of you. You are good helpers. Flowers need water to grow and bloom. But you know what else they need?" Lily and Max said, "What, mom?" Their mom said, "They need sunshine and love. Just like you. You are my sunshine and I love you very much." Lily and Max said, "We love you too, mom. You are the best." They hugged their mom and ate their spaghetti. They were happy and full. They thanked their mom for the lunch and asked if they could go back to the garden. Their mom said, "Yes, you can. But be careful and don't get dirty. And don't forget to be serious. Flowers are serious things." Lily and Max laughed and said, "OK, mom. We will be serious. But flowers are also fun and beautiful." They ran back to the garden and played with the flowers. They were serious and fun and beautiful. Just like the flowers.

Bob and his family were getting ready to celebrate. The sun was hot and the sky was bright. They stepped outside of their house. Bob's mom shouted, "Time to go!" Everyone jumped into the cart. Bob was the first one inside. Bob's dad pulled the cart. He asked, "Where should we celebrate?" Bob shouted, "The park!" His brother agreed. The family went to the park. Bob jumped out of the cart and ran to the playground. He saw a slide, swing and swing. He shouted, "Yay!" The family ran and played in the park until the sun set. Then they returned home. Bob's mom said, "That was a great day. Let's celebrate again soon!" Everyone agreed and returned inside the house. Bob was happy and excited. He had celebrated a lot that day!

Once, there was a little girl called Emily. She was three years old. Every night, Emily's mum would close her door and say good night. Emily didn't like it. Every time, she wanted mum to stay in her room with her. One night, Emily cried until her mum promised to stay with her. So, mum closed the bedroom door and sat on her bed. They both looked out of the window at the night sky. Suddenly, the darkness was filled with a deep, sad silence. Emily was confused and a bit scared. She asked her mum, "What's wrong? Why is silences so sad?" Mum explained that sometimes, even adults need a bit of a hug when it's quiet. Mum hugged Emily and spoke softly, "The silence will pass soon, and there will be happy noises again. It's OK." Emily felt better and smiled. She closed her eyes and soon fell asleep in her mum's warm arms.

Once there was a black cat named Start. Start was very happy and loved to run, play and rub against her favorite toy mouse. One day, Start found a big basket in the garden. She rubbed and rubbed the basket until it opened up to reveal a sparkly, red ball. Start's eyes lit up with excitement. She quickly rolled the ball around the garden, stopping occasionally to rub against a flower. Suddenly, Start spotted a small hole in the ground and decided to explore. With one final rub against the grass, Start disappeared into the darkness and has not been seen since. Hope she finds her way home soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a worry. She wanted a good night's sleep, but it was hard for her to sleep at night. Every night, she would worry and worry, until she just couldn't worry any more. But then, something funny happened. A nosy little bird came by her window one night. He looked in the window and saw the little girl. He saw how worried she was. He said, "Little girl, why don't you come outside and play with me? We can play until you feel sleepy." The little girl smiled and went outside. She played with the nosy little bird until she was too tired to keep playing. Then she said goodnight to the nosy little bird and hopped back into bed. When she woke up the next morning, she felt very relaxed and happy. She no longer had to worry about not being able to fall asleep. She had found her own special way to sleep. The End.

One day, there was an old man. He lived in the east, far away from the city. Whenever the sun went down, he liked to stand outside and look up at the stars. One night, the old man looked up and saw something very special. The moon was so big and so bright, it looked like it was touching the top of the sky. The old man was so excited, he wanted to show everyone how beautiful the moon was. So the old man closed his eyes and began to pray. He prayed loud and clear, and his voice echoed over the trees. He prayed and prayed and then, suddenly, the moon began to shine brighter than ever before. The old man smiled, knowing his prayers had been answered. And from then on, every night the old man would go out, look up at the moon, and pray.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toy jeep. He would drive it around the house and make vroom vroom sounds. One day, Timmy's sister came into the room and asked, "Can I play with your jeep, Timmy?" Timmy replied, "Sure, but be careful not to throw it too hard." His sister played with the jeep for a little while, but then she accidentally threw it too hard and it hit the wall. Timmy got upset and said, "You broke my jeep!" His sister felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Timmy. Let's try to fix it together." They worked together to fix the jeep, and when they were done, Timmy said, "It's all better now. Let's play together and have a peaceful time." They played with the jeep together, and Timmy's sister made sure not to throw it too hard again. They had a lot of fun and felt happy. The end.

Lily loved her bunny, Fluffy. Fluffy was white and soft and had long ears. Fluffy liked to bounce around the garden and eat carrots. Lily liked to hug Fluffy and play with him. One day, Fluffy got sick. He did not bounce or eat. He lay in his cage and made sad noises. Lily was very worried. She told her mom, "Mom, Fluffy is sick. He needs help." Mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will take Fluffy to the veterinarian. The veterinarian is a doctor for animals. He will make Fluffy better." Lily and Mom put Fluffy in a basket and drove to the veterinarian. The veterinarian was a nice man with a white coat and a stethoscope. He looked at Fluffy and said, "Hello, Fluffy. You are an adorable bunny. What is wrong with you?" He checked Fluffy's ears, eyes, nose, and teeth. He gave Fluffy some medicine and a bandage. He said, "Fluffy has a cold and a sore paw. He will be fine in a few days. Just keep him warm and give him lots of water and carrots." Lily was very happy. She thanked the veterinarian and hugged Fluffy. She said, "Fluffy, I love you. You are my best friend. I'm glad you are better." Fluffy snuggled with Lily and made happy noises. He felt better already. He was ready to bounce again.

Once upon a time, there was a chamber. It was a colorful place and there was fun to be had. Two friends, Charlie and Anne, were playing in the chamber. Charlie wanted to play one game, and Anne wanted to play another. Charlie tried to persuade Anne to play his game. "Please, Anne, let's play my game," said Charlie. "No way!", said Anne. "I want to play my game now." But Charlie was insistent. He wanted to win and was not ready to give in. Anne, however, was not willing to change her mind. "Okay," said Charlie. "Let's try to reverse the rules. We'll both play my game the first time, and when we're done, we'll play your game." Anne thought about it and agreed. They played Charlie's game and when it was finished, they played Anne's game. They had a lot of fun and it was a colorful time.

Once there was a girl named Rebekah who was very eager to play. One day she found a coin in the grass while she was playing tag. She decided to keep it in case she needed it one day. But, Rebekah soon started to suffer. She wasn't allowed to buy anything with the coin, and she was sad that no one wanted it. She was even more determined to find a way to use it. Rebekah asked all her friends and family but none of them knew what she could do with the coin. She thought and thought, but ended up feeling frustrated and alone. Finally, she decided to go to a local store. She asked the storekeeper if she could exchange the coin for something else. He said yes, and gave her a toy! Rebekah was so excited. Her eagerness was immediately rewarded and she had a toy to play with. She was very grateful and she promised to never forget her coin.

Once upon a time, there was a big foot. It belonged to a giant who lived in a nearby castle. He rarely ever stepped outside of his fortress. One day, the giant decided to take a walk in the forest. He was so big and his foot was so big that it left a giant footprint wherever he went. A small girl was playing in the forest when she saw a big footprint. She was very curious and followed the giant footprint until she arrived at the giant's castle. The girl was very scared. She was about to turn around and run away when suddenly the door opened. The giant smiled at her and said, "Come in and see the surprise I have waiting for you!" The girl was still scared, but the giant was so kind and friendly. She decided to take a chance and go inside. When she entered, she found the biggest surprise of all. The giant had filled the entire castle with colorful toys and sweets. The girl was so excited that she couldn't believe her eyes. The girl and the giant played together all day, and she was never scared of him again. They stayed friends long after, and the girl remembered that surprise forever.

Once upon a time, there was an eraser that wanted to bake something delicious. It asked all of its friends if they wanted to help make something. Everyone said yes and they all hopped in a big oven. The eraser put everything in the oven and started to bake. After a while, the oven was hot and smelt so yummy. Everyone was so excited. Then the oven door opened and out jumped the eraser, but it was all black and dead. All of the eraser's friends were sad, but then one of the friends had an idea. The friend took a big drink of water and splashed it on the eraser. The eraser started to come back to life and everyone laughed and cheered. The eraser was saved and everyone enjoyed their delicious treats!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a closet in her room where she kept her toys and clothes. One day, Lily could not find her favorite doll. She looked everywhere, but she could not find it. She felt sad and frustrated. Lily's mom saw her daughter's face and knew something was wrong. She asked Lily what happened, and Lily told her about the missing doll. Her mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I am sure your doll is just hiding somewhere. Let's be patient and keep looking." Lily and her mom searched the closet, under the bed, and in every corner of the room. Suddenly, Lily's mom found the doll behind a pile of clothes. Lily was so happy and relieved that she gave her mom a big hug and said, "Thank you, Mommy, for helping me find my doll." From that day on, Lily learned to be patient and to always thank her mom for her help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Kate. She had curly blonde hair and big blue eyes. She loved to dream about what she would do when she was high. One day, she was playin in the garden when she looked up in the sky. She saw a eagle flying so high, she even got surprised. Kate decided to climb a tree and try to fly like a bird. She climbed up really high and started dreaming. She closed her eyes and imagined herself soaring among the clouds. Suddenly, Kate heard a voice in the tree. It was a voice of a little bird. "Hello! What are you doing up there?" said the bird. Kate was so surprised. She quickly opened her eyes and replied "Hi! I'm dreaming of flying like you!" The bird smiled and said "Well, what are you waiting for? Let's do it together!" Kate couldn't believe it. She spread her arms, lifted her head and started to fly. She felt so happy and she could feel the wind caressing her hair. She was high up in the sky and for a moment, she thought she could touch the clouds.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved playing in the snow. One day, she looked outside and saw that it was snowing! She put on her coat, hat, and gloves, and ran outside to play. Lily built a snowman and had so much fun throwing snowballs. But then she realized that she couldn't find her scarf. She looked and looked, but it was nowhere to be found. Her mom came outside and asked what was wrong. Lily said, "I lost my scarf. I hope I can find it." Her mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, we will look for it together. But first, let's go inside and warm up with some hot cocoa." After they drank their hot cocoa, they went back outside to look for the scarf. It was very stubborn and didn't want to be found. But finally, Lily saw a little bit of red peeking out from under the snow. She dug and dug until she found her scarf. She was so happy and said, "Yay! I found it! Thank you, Mom."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved the color pink and always wore a light pink dress. One day, she went to the park to play with her friend Timmy. While they were playing, they saw a bird flying in the sky. Lily wanted to catch the bird, so she threw a rock at it. Timmy saw what she did and said, "Lily, that's not nice! You shouldn't hurt animals." Lily felt bad and knew she did something wrong. She said, "I'm sorry, Timmy. I won't do it again." Timmy forgave her, but also said, "If you hurt animals again, your mommy will punish you." Lily learned her lesson and promised to never hurt animals again. From that day on, she always played nicely and enjoyed the pink flowers and light breeze in the park with her friend Timmy.

Tom and Lily were playing a game with cards. Each card had a picture of an animal on it. They had to take turns to flip a card and say the name of the animal. If they said it right, they could keep the card. If they said it wrong, they had to give the card to the other player. The one who had the most cards at the end would win. Tom flipped a card and saw a big, green frog. He smiled and said, "Frog!" He put the card in his pile. Lily flipped a card and saw a small, brown mouse. She frowned and said, "Mouse!" She put the card in her pile. Tom flipped another card and saw a yellow and black striped bee. He said, "Bee!" He put the card in his pile. Lily flipped another card and saw a pink and slimy worm. She said, "Eww, disgusting!" She threw the card away. Tom laughed and said, "That's not how you play. You have to say the name of the animal. That's a worm." Lily said, "I don't care. I don't like worms. They are disgusting. You can have it." Tom said, "OK, thank you. That means I have more cards than you. I win!" Lily said, "No fair. You got all the nice animals. I got all the disgusting ones." Tom said, "That's just luck. Maybe next time you will get the nice ones. Do you want to play again?" Lily said, "Yes, but only if we shuffle the cards first. And no more worms!"

Once upon a time there was a family who lived in a little house. Inside the house was a door. Every day the dad would lock the door before he left to go to work. One day the dad forgot to lock the door before he left. So when the family returned, they found a sign on the door. It said, "A friendly helper locked the door for you." The family was surprised and happy to see the sign. They wondered who the helpful helper was. Was it a neighbour? Was it a friend? They looked around and only saw their cat. The dad smiled and said, "It must have been our cat!" He thanked the cat for being so helpful, and then locked the door to make sure it was safe. The end.

Jimmy loved to explore the desert near his house. One day, he took his mom's recorder and went off to find some new and exciting things! He was so excited to find a huge cactus with bright pink flowers! But Jimmy didn't know that the cactus was quite prickly and miserable. He wanted to record the cactus for his mom, but when he touched it he found out how miserable it was. He quickly put the recorder away and backed away from the cactus. He spent the rest of the day looking at beautiful rocks and plants until it was time to go home. He never forgot the miserable cactus!

Once there was a large dog. He had a collar around his neck which had a tag with his name on it. One day, the dog had a problem. His collar was too tight. He tried to stretch it but it wouldn't get any bigger. He wanted to be able to take it off. He tried everything but he couldn't solve the problem. Then one day he went to the park and saw a rabbit. The rabbit said he knew how to solve the problem. He told the dog to go to the lake and swim around for an hour. After that the collar should feel loose. The dog followed the rabbit's instructions and swam. When he came out he looked down at the collar and it was loose! He was so happy he barked with joy! Now he can take his collar off whenever he wanted. It was a great feeling! He thanked the rabbit and went back home feeling relieved.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey named Max. Max loved to eat bananas, but one day he couldn't find any. He asked his friend, a bird named Bella, if she had seen any bananas. Bella said, "I saw some bananas in the jungle, but there is a scary lion there." Max was scared, but he really wanted a banana. He decided to be brave and go to the jungle. When he got there, he saw the lion hiding behind a tree. Max quickly hid behind a bush. The lion saw Max and said, "What are you doing here?" Max said, "I'm looking for bananas. Do you know where they are?" The lion said, "Yes, but you have to be brave to get them." Max took a deep breath and said, "I can be brave!" The lion showed Max where the bananas were and Max grabbed one. He was so happy and proud of himself for being brave. From that day on, Max knew he could be brave and face his fears.

Once, there was a girl called Daisy. She was three years old and was always very hungry. One day, she went to the park with her mum. There, she saw a pond with the prettiest daisies she had ever seen. She was so amazed that she forgot to mind her mum's instructions. Daisy ran over to the pond, but it was very deep so she was scared. She called for help, but nobody was around. Just then, she saw a little fish swimming in the pond. She bravely decided to talk to it. The fish asked her if she was hungry. Daisy nodded and, without saying a word, the fish swam away. Soon, it came back with a handful of daisies which Daisy happily ate. She thanked the fish, hugged it and ran back to find her mum. From that day on, Daisy followed all of her mummy's instructions and made sure to stay close by. She also remembered what the fish said and never let her hunger get the better of her.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play in the park near their home. One day, they see a big black car in the park. It is not moving. It is not like the other cars in the traffic. The other cars are loud and fast. The black car is quiet and still. "Who is in the black car?" Tom asks Mia. "I don't know. Maybe it is a secret car. Maybe it has a spy in it," Mia says. They walk closer to the black car. They want to see inside. They are curious. They are not scared. They reach the black car. They peek through the window. They see a man in the driver's seat. He is wearing a black hat and a black coat. He is holding a black phone. He is talking to someone. He is whispering. "Hello, boss. I am in the park. I have the package. No one saw me. I will wait for your signal. Over," the man whispers. Tom and Mia gasp. They think the man is a spy. They think he has a secret package. They think he is doing something bad. They run away from the black car. They run back to their home. They tell their mom what they saw. "Mom, mom, we saw a spy in the park. He had a black car and a black phone and a black package. He was whispering to his boss. He was doing something bad," Tom and Mia say. Their mom smiles. She hugs them. She does not believe them. She thinks they have a big imagination. She thinks they made up the story. "Tom and Mia, you are very creative. You have a lot of fun playing in the park. But there are no spies in the park. There are no secret cars or packages. The man you saw was not a spy. He was a taxi driver. He was waiting for a customer. He was whispering because he did not want to disturb the birds. He was doing his job," their mom says. Tom and Mia look at each other. They are not sure. They still think the man was a spy. They still think he had a secret package. They still think he was doing something bad. They whisper to each other. "Maybe mom is wrong. Maybe the man is a spy. Maybe he is hiding something. Maybe we should go back to the park and find out," they whisper.

In the sunny meadow, there was a baby lamb. Its soft, fluffy wool was a snug texture - just perfect for snuggling. The baby lamb was very alert, because it could hear its mother's voice calling out. The lamb responded with a gentle 'baaaa'. Its mother said 'come here!' The lamb happily obeyed and ran quickly over to her. The mother said 'Hello, little one. I need you to be very alert. Be careful where you go and don't get into any trouble.' The baby lamb nodded and spoke 'Yes, Mother'. The mother then said 'Now, remember to stay alert and always listen to my voice when I call for you'. The baby lamb nodded again and said 'I will Mother.' The mother smiled and gave the baby lamb a loving pat. 'Good lamb. Always listen and stay alert!', she said. The baby lamb softly replied 'Yes, Mother.'

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there were two dogs named Bob and Tim. They loved to play with their toys. One sunny day, Bob had a big, tasty bone. Tim saw the bone and wanted to play with it too. Tim asked, "Bob, can you lend me your bone, please?" Bob said, "No, it's mine!" This made Tim sad and they started to fight over the bone. Just then, a big green bird came down from the sky. The bird took the bone away from them. Bob and Tim stopped fighting and looked up at the bird. They knew they needed to work together to get the bone back. "Let's be friends and get the bone back from the bird," said Tim. Bob agreed and they both chased the bird. They jumped high and caught the bone together. From that day on, Bob and Tim learned to share and became the best of friends.

Lily and Ben love to go to the park with their dad. They like to play on the swings, slide down the slide, and run on the grass. Sometimes they see horses in the park. The horses are big and brown and have long hair. They live in a stable near the park. One day, Lily and Ben asked their dad if they could go and see the horses. Their dad said yes, but they had to be careful and quiet. They walked to the stable and saw a man who took care of the horses. He was nice and let them pet the horses gently. "Hello, kids. Do you like horses?" he asked. "Yes, we do. They are so pretty and soft," Lily said. "What are their names?" Ben asked. "Well, this one is Daisy, and this one is Max. They are very friendly and smart," the man said. "Can we ride them?" Lily asked. "Maybe another day, when you are older and bigger. Riding horses is fun, but you need to learn how to do it safely. For now, you can just say hello and give them a carrot," the man said. He gave Lily and Ben a carrot each and showed them how to hold it in their hand. The horses came closer and nibbled the carrots gently. Lily and Ben giggled and smiled. They thanked the man and said goodbye to the horses. They went back to their dad, who was waiting for them on a bench. They told him all about the horses and how nice they were. Their dad was happy to see them so excited. "Did you have fun at the stable?" he asked. "Yes, we did. We love the park and the horses," Lily and Ben said.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his tools, especially his hammer and screwdriver. He would spend hours building things with them. One day, Timmy's friend Johnny came over to play. Johnny wanted to use Timmy's hammer, but Timmy didn't want to share. Johnny was sad and went home. Later, Timmy's mom asked him why Johnny went home early. Timmy felt bad and realized he should have shared his tools. He decided to go to Johnny's house and supply him with his tools to play with. When Timmy arrived at Johnny's house, Johnny was so happy. They spent the whole day building things together. Timmy learned that sharing is important and it made him feel good to make his friend happy. And even though Johnny's feet were smelly, they still had a great time together.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was playing in the garden. Suddenly, she saw a dove. It was flying high up in the sky. She watched it for a long time. The dove flew down closer to the girl. She was scared at first. But then she saw how beautiful the dove was. She kept watching it as it flew around her. The girl wanted to act like the dove. So, she put her arms out and started to flap them. She moved them real fast, like the wings of the dove. She felt like she was flying in the sky. Then the dove did something scary. It flew away very quickly. The girl was sad. But then she saw the dove had left her a present. It was a small white feather. The girl smiled and hugged the feather. She knew the dove would always be with her.

Once upon a time, there was a little raven. He was very spoiled. He always wanted to have whatever he desired. One day, he decided to start an adventure. He flew far away, searching for something to do. He went to the beach, then the forest. Everywhere he went, he saw something fun to do. Finally, he discovered a big mountain. He started to climb the mountain. He climbed higher and higher until he finally reached the peak. He looked around and saw the most beautiful view he had ever seen. He could see for miles and miles. Suddenly, the raven heard a sound. He turned and saw a small child at the peak of the mountain. The child had a big smile on his face. The raven was filled with joy and flew down to meet the child. They played together all day, until the sun went down and the sky started to get dark. The raven and the child said goodbye and the raven started his journey home. He flew through the night sky, feeling content and happy. His adventure had been a great one and he couldn't wait to tell his friends about it.

Once upon a time, there were two bears, Bob and Jenny. Bob was a young bear, and Jenny was an old bear. They were discussing the summer day. "The sun is shining brightly and it's making the blossoms in the trees sparkle," said Jenny. Bob looked at the ground and noticed the dust near his paws. "What's this dust?" he asked Jenny, pointing towards the dirt. Jenny smiled. "That dust is from the old path," she said. "It's been here for many, many years." Bob smiled back. He thought about the years that had gone by and how young he still was. "Let's go find some new adventures!" he said with excitement. And so they did. They explored the woods and enjoyed their summer day together.

Once there was a girl named Maya. She was three years old. One day, Maya and her mom went to a store. Maya saw a pretty cup. It was bright blue with stars all around. She felt so excited. She asked her mom to buy it for her. Mom smiled and said, "Sure, this cup looks great. Let's get it for you." Maya was so happy she could hardly contain herself. She grabbed the cup and hugged it tight. Then she said thank you to her Mom. On the way home, Maya held the cup tightly in her hands. She felt so happy and excited, like she was the luckiest girl in the world. When she reached home, she put the cup on her shelf and smiled. It made her feel great.

Lily had a bad fall from her bike. She hurt her arm and cried a lot. Mom took her to the doctor. The doctor was nice and gave her a sticker. He said he needed to take a picture of her arm with a special machine. He called it an x-ray. Lily was scared of the machine. It looked big and loud. She did not want to leave Mom. Mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will be right here with you. The x-ray will not hurt. It will help the doctor see if your arm is broken or not. It will be very quick. Can you be brave for me?" Lily nodded and held Mom's hand. The doctor put her arm on a table and covered it with a cloth. He said, "Now, Lily, I need you to stay very still and not move your arm. I will go behind that window and press a button. You will hear a beep and see a flash. That's the x-ray. It will be over in a second. Are you ready?" Lily said, "Yes, I'm ready." She closed her eyes and squeezed Mom's hand. She heard the beep and saw the flash. She did not feel anything. The doctor came back and said, "Good job, Lily! You did great. Let me see your x-ray." He showed her a picture of her arm with white lines and shapes. He said, "Look, Lily, this is your arm. See, it is not broken. It is just bruised. You will be fine. You just need some ice and a bandage." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, doctor. I'm glad my arm is not broken." Mom hugged her and said, "I'm so proud of you, Lily. You were very brave. Let's go home and have some ice cream." Lily said, "Yes, let's go home. I love you, Mom." They left the doctor's office and went to the car. Lily felt peaceful and happy. She had a good day after all.

Once there was a rabbit who lived in a big farm. Yesterday, the rabbit felt hot and dry, so it went for a walk to the meadow to find some cool, fresh grass. When the rabbit arrived the meadow, it looked around and thought, "It looks different than usual. But why?". Suddenly, the rabbit noticed that the meadow was very dry. There wasn't any fresh grass in sight. The rabbit sighed sadly and said, "Oh no! What can I do?". Then, it had an idea! The rabbit hopped all the way back to the farm and asked the farmer if he could help. The rabbit said, "Yesterday, the meadow was dry. Can you give me some fresh grass?". The farmer smiled and said, "Of course I can! Here you go!", and he gave the rabbit a big bag of fresh grass. The rabbit was so happy! It thanked the farmer and hopped back to the meadow with the bag of fresh grass. When the rabbit arrived at the meadow, it spread the grass everywhere. Soon, the meadow was full of fresh, green grass! The rabbit said, "This looks better than yesterday!".

One day, Bobby was playing in his room when his mama called him. She was standing in the living room, holding his new bright red shirt. She said, "Bobby, it's time to dress up." But Bobby didn't want to put on his shirt. He wanted to play some more. He shouted, "No! I don't want to dress!" Mama frowned. She said, "You must dress. Mama's very enthusiastic about this outfit." Bobby was still mad. He didn't want to dress. He said, "No! I want to play more!" Just then, his papa came out of the kitchen, carrying a big cake from the refrigerator. His papa said, "Come on, Bobby. Don't make mama angry. Put your shirt on and mama will give you a slice of cake." Bobby smiled. He quickly said, "Okay, papa!" He took the shirt and dressed himself quickly. He was happy to be wearing his new shirt and he was even more excited about the yummy cake.

One day, a cool cat named Tom went for a walk. He saw a big green thing with spikes. It was a cactus! Tom thought it was very cool. He wanted to play with it, but he did not want to get hurt by the spikes. So, he thought of a plan. Tom found a long stick. He thought he could use the stick to play with the cactus. But then, he saw his friend, the dog named Max. Max wanted to play with Tom. Tom wanted to play with Max too, but he wanted to play with the cactus first. So, Tom told Max to wait. He said, "Max, I have to delay our play." Tom used the stick to touch the cactus. It was fun! He did not get hurt. Then, he heard Max bark. Max was sad because he was waiting for a long time. Tom knew it was time to play with Max. He left the cactus and went to play with Max. They had a lot of fun together. Tom was happy he could play with the cactus and Max too.

Mama was in the kitchen getting dinner ready. Baby wanted to help, but Mama said no. "Mama, can I do something?" asked Baby. "No, Baby. You need to stay out," Mama said. Baby saw a big black box sitting in the corner. It had a fierce look. "Mama, what's in the box?" Baby asked. Mama sighed. "It's just some old things, Baby. You can't touch it," she said. But Baby was curious. He wanted to see what was inside. He moved closer. "No, Baby!" Mama said. "You mustn't remove things from the box!" Baby stepped back. He didn't want to make Mama mad. Mama smiled at him. "Now stay out of trouble, okay?" Baby nodded. He stayed far away from the black box.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Jean. She was three years old. One day while she was playing in the garden Jean found a basket. It was filled with special things - one of them was a special toy. Jean was so happy! But Jean's brother was very jealous. He wanted Jean's toy all for himself. So his took the toy and ran away! Jean was so sad. She wanted her toy back, but she didn't know where her brother had gone. Suddenly she had an idea. She decided to bury the basket near the tree in the garden and hope that her brother would find it. Jean dug a deep, deep hole and put the basket in it. Then she covered it up with lots and lots of dirt and stones. Then she went inside to wait. But Jean's brother was very, very stupid! He never even looked for the basket. So Jean's special toy stayed buried forever!

Lila liked to play soccer with her friends. She was very good at kicking the ball and making goals. She was independent and did not need help from anyone. She always wanted to win and have the highest score. One day, she was playing soccer with Ben and Sam. They were on the same team and they were winning. Lila scored three goals and was very happy. But then, she saw that her ball had a hole in it. It was losing air and becoming flat. She was very sad and angry. "Who did this to my ball?" she asked. "It was my favorite ball!" Ben and Sam looked at the ball and felt sorry for Lila. They did not know who made the hole, but they wanted to help. "Maybe we can repair it," Ben said. "We can use some tape and glue and make it round again." "Or maybe we can share our ball with you," Sam said. "We have another ball that is good and bouncy. You can use it and we can still play together." Lila thought about what Ben and Sam said. She liked their ideas, but she also liked her own ball. She did not want to give it up or use another one. She wanted to fix it and keep playing with it. "Thank you, but no thank you," she said. "I can repair my ball by myself. I don't need your help or your ball. I am independent and I can do it alone." She took her ball and walked away. She found some tape and glue and tried to repair the hole. But it was not easy. The tape did not stick and the glue did not dry. The ball was still flat and useless. She looked at Ben and Sam. They were playing with their ball and having fun. They were still winning and scoring goals. They smiled and waved at her. They invited her to join them. Lila felt lonely and silly. She realized that she was not independent. She needed her friends and their ball. She wanted to play and have fun with them. She wanted to share and be nice. She picked up her ball and walked back to them. She apologized and asked if she could play with them. "Of course you can," Ben and Sam said. "We are happy to share our ball with you. We are your friends and we want to play with you." They gave her a hug and handed her the ball. Lila smiled and thanked them. She kicked the ball and scored a goal. They cheered and clapped for her. They played together and had a great time. Lila learned that being independent is good, but being friendly is better.

Once upon a time, a chubby cat named Max had a job to deliver mail. Max was a very good cat. He had long hair that was soft and nice to touch. One day, Max had a letter to deliver to a little girl named Lily. Lily lived in a small house with her mom and dad. Max walked and walked until he got to Lily's house. Max gave the letter to Lily. She was very happy to get it. Lily said, "Thank you, Max!" Max was happy too. He liked to help people. Max went back to his house and took a long nap.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom gave her a big bag of candy. Lily was very happy and started eating the candy right away. While Lily was eating her candy, her friend Timmy came over to play. Timmy asked if he could have some candy too. Lily said yes, and she poured some candy into Timmy's hand. But the candy was very old and disgusting. Timmy didn't like it and he started to feel sick. He said to Lily, "This candy is yucky, I don't want to eat it anymore." Lily felt bad and said sorry to Timmy. But it was too late. Timmy got very sick and had to go to the hospital. From then on, Lily always checked the candy before she shared it with her friends. The end.

Once there was a girl who was very organized. She kept everything in its place and tried her best to stay tidy. One day, she was getting ready for a big day, and was almost finished when she realized one of her toes was out of place. She didn't know what to do! She looked around, and suddenly, an ideas come to her. She looked in her drawer and found some colorful shoe laces, they were just what she needed! She carefully weaved them around her toe and soon it was nice and organized. What a relief! She was happy to have her toe all neat and tidy again. She was ready to start her big day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a troubled little girl named Lily. She was always sad because she lost her favorite toy, a triangle. She looked everywhere in her house but could not find it. One sunny day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a big puddle of water and thought her triangle might be there. She put her hand in the water to soak it and looked for her toy. She felt something at the bottom of the puddle. Lily pulled it out and saw that it was her triangle! She was so happy that she found it. From that day on, Lily was never troubled again. She played with her triangle every day and always kept it close to her. And when she saw puddles, she would smile and remember how she found her toy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their old hats. They liked to pretend they were pirates and explorers. They found a big tree with a hole in it and decided to look inside. "Maybe there is treasure in there," Lily said. "Or a monster," Ben said. They took off their hats and put them on the ground. Then they crawled into the hole. It was dark and dusty. They saw some shiny things and some scary things. "Look, a necklace!" Lily said. "Look, a spider!" Ben said. They heard a noise outside. They peeked out of the hole and saw a dog. The dog was sniffing their hats. It picked up Lily's hat with its mouth and ran away. "Hey, that's my hat!" Lily shouted. She and Ben ran after the dog. They chased it across the park, but it was too fast. The dog disappeared behind a fence. "Oh no, my hat is gone!" Lily cried. "I'm sorry, Lily," Ben said. He gave her his hat. "You can have mine. It's old, but it's still good." Lily smiled and hugged him. "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend." They went back to the tree and played some more. They forgot about the dog and the hat. They had fun with their old hat.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the bushes. He would run and jump and laugh with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to come inside and help her serve dinner. "I don't want to come inside, Mommy. I want to play in the bushes," Timmy said. "Please come inside and help me serve dinner. It's almost ready," his mom replied. Timmy sighed and reluctantly went inside to help his mom. They had a modern kitchen with shiny appliances and a big table to eat on. They sat down to eat dinner together. But as they were eating, Timmy started to feel sick. He had eaten something that didn't agree with him. He got sicker and sicker until he had to go to the hospital. The doctors tried to help him, but it was too late. Timmy had eaten a poisonous berry from the bush outside and he didn't even know it. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, generous dog named Chewy. Chewy loved to chew on his toys all day. One day, he saw a little bird who was sad. The little bird said, "I lost my home! It's an emergency!" Chewy wanted to help, so he thought of a plan. He knew his toys could make the bird happy. Chewy gave the bird one of his toys to make a new home. The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you, Chewy!" They became best friends. The moral of the story is that sharing can help others in need and make new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pastel crayons. One day, she wanted to draw a picture of her family. Lily asked her mom, "Can I use your pastel crayons to draw a picture of us?" "Of course, Lily. You can use them," her mom said. Lily started drawing and was very successful. She drew her mom, dad, and little brother. When she was finished, she showed her mom the picture. "Wow, Lily! This is amazing! You are so talented," her mom said. Lily was very happy and proud of her successful drawing. From that day on, she loved using pastel crayons to create beautiful pictures.

Lily and Tom were very happy. They were going on a tour with their mom and dad. They wanted to see many animals at the zoo. They got in the car and drove to the zoo. When they got there, they saw a big sign. It said: "Zoo closed today. Sorry for the trouble." Lily and Tom were very sad. They wanted to see the lions and the monkeys and the penguins. They asked their mom and dad why the zoo was closed. Mom and dad said: "We don't know, sweeties. Maybe the animals are sick or the zoo needs to fix something. We are sorry, too. We know you were looking forward to the tour." Lily and Tom started to cry. They felt like their day was ruined. Mom and dad tried to cheer them up. They said: "How about we play a game? We can guess what the animals are doing inside the zoo. Maybe they are having a party or a nap or a race. What do you think?" Lily and Tom wiped their tears and thought for a moment. They liked to play games. They said: "OK, let's play. I guess the lions are roaring and playing tag. I guess the monkeys are swinging and eating bananas. I guess the penguins are sliding and splashing." Mom and dad smiled and nodded. They said: "Those are good guesses. Maybe you are right. Maybe the animals are having fun, too. Maybe we can come back another day and see them. Would you like that?" Lily and Tom nodded, too. They said: "Yes, we would like that. Thank you, mom and dad. You are the best. We love you." Mom and dad hugged them and said: "We love you, too. You are the best. Come on, let's go home and have some ice cream. How does that sound?" Lily and Tom smiled and said: "That sounds great. We like ice cream. Can we have chocolate?" Mom and dad said: "Sure, you can have chocolate. Anything you want. You are our brave and smart kids. We are proud of you." Lily and Tom felt better. They got in the car and drove home. They still wanted to see the animals, but they knew they could wait. They had a good day after all. They had a good family. They had a good game. They had a good ice cream. They were happy.

Lily loved to read books. She had many books in her room. She read them every day. She read them before bed. She read them when she was bored. She read them when she was happy. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She brought her favorite book with her. It was a book about a princess and a dragon. She put the book in her jacket pocket. She wanted to read it on the bench. But when she got to the park, she saw a boy. He was playing with a ball. He looked fun. Lily wanted to play with him. She ran to him and said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Can I play with you?" The boy looked at her and said, "No, you can't. This is my ball. Go away." Lily felt sad. She said, "But I want to be your friend. Can we share the ball?" The boy said, "No, you can't. This is my park. Go away." Lily felt angry. She said, "You are mean. You are spoiled. You don't share. You don't have any friends." The boy said, "I don't care. I have everything I want. You have nothing. Go away." Lily felt hurt. She turned around and ran back to her mom. She took out her book from her jacket pocket. She said, "Mom, I don't want to play with that boy. He is mean. He is spoiled. He doesn't share. He doesn't have any friends. I have my book. My book is better. My book is my friend." Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Some people are mean. Some people are spoiled. They don't know how to be nice. They don't know how to be happy. You are smart. You are kind. You know how to read. You know how to be happy. I'm proud of you, Lily. I love you, Lily." Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, Mom. Can we read my book together?" Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. Let's read your book together."

Once there was a little human called Kate. She wanted to win something amazing. Every day she practised hard. One day, Kate felt ready. She put on her special outfit and took a deep breath. She was ready to win something amazing! Kate went to the big room where the competition was taking place. She was the only human. Everyone cheered for her. Kate put in lots of effort and ran as fast as she could. In the end, she won! Everyone was so happy for her. She had won something amazing! Kate was so excited. She went home and celebrated with her family. It was a magical day!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. He was very ignorant and didn't know much about the world. One day, he went to play with his friend Johnny. "Hey Johnny, do you want to play catch?" asked Timmy. "Sure, but let's be careful not to split the ball," replied Johnny. Timmy didn't know what "split" meant, so he asked Johnny. Johnny explained that it meant to break something into two pieces. "Oh, I understand now," said Timmy. They played catch for a while, but then Timmy accidentally threw the ball too hard and it split into two pieces. "Oh no, I'm sorry Johnny. I didn't mean to split the ball," said Timmy. "That's okay, Timmy. We can still play with the pieces," replied Johnny with a smile. And so, they continued to play with the broken ball, and Timmy learned a new word that day.

Max and his family had come to the park to celebrate. Max was three years old. When they arrived, Max's dad opened up a special menu. On it were all sorts of tasty treats. "Yummy!" said Max, his mouth watering. "Be polite, Max" said his dad. Max nodded and said with a smile "Thank you!" "You're very welcome," replied his dad, ruffling Max's hair. Max's family enjoyed the menus treats until there was nothing left. "That was delicious," said Max, giving his dad a big hug. Max's dad smiled and said "It was certainly a delightful way to celebrate, wasn't it?" Max nodded in agreement and said, "Yes, Dad. Can we come back here to celebrate again?" His dad smiled and said, "Of course."

One day, a little girl named Mia went to a new food place with her mom. Mia was very excited to try new food. They sat down at a table and the nice lady gave them a menu to look at. Mia and her mom studied the menu. There were many yummy things to eat. Mia saw pizza, and her mom saw a big salad. "What do you want to eat, Mia?" her mom asked. "I want pizza, please," said Mia. When the food came, Mia and her mom were very happy. They ate and talked about their day. Mia liked the new food place and wanted to come back again.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and has a long tail. The dog is friendly. He wags his tail and licks their faces. "Hello, doggy!" Lily says. "What is your name?" The dog barks. He does not have a name. He is lost. He is hungry and cold. "Can we help you, doggy?" Max asks. "Do you want to come with us?" The dog nods. He follows Lily and Max to their home. They give him some water and some food. They share their meal with him. The dog is happy. He eats and drinks. He feels warm and full. "Thank you, Lily and Max," the dog says. "You are very kind. Can I stay with you?" Lily and Max look at each other. They smile. They like the dog. They want to keep him. "Of course, you can stay with us," Lily says. "We will be your family. We will give you a name. How about Spot?" The dog barks. He likes his name. He likes his new family. He gives Lily and Max a big kiss. They hug him and kiss him back. They are all happy. They are all friends. They are all warm.

Once upon a time there was a hunter who was looking for something to hunt. Everywhere that the hunter looked, he could not find any prey. But then suddenly he saw a lively fox jumping around in a meadow. The hunter was eager to catch the fox, but the fox was even more eager to escape. The hunter yelled, "Hey fox, stop running around and be my prey!" But the fox didn't listen and kept running. He shouted louder and louder, but the fox kept on. The fox exclaimed, "No way! I will resist you and keep running!" With that, the fox hopped and skipped around the meadow, dodging the hunter as best as he could. The hunter was frustrated and angry. He tried to come up with different plans to catch the fox, but nothing worked. The fox was too lively! So the hunter gave up and went home without any prey that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very hungry and she wanted something to eat. She came to her mother and said, "Mommy, I'm so hungry!" Her mother smiled and said, "Oh, Lucy! Let's go to the kitchen and get something to eat." So they went to the kitchen together. In the kitchen, Lucy saw some celery. She asked her mother, "Can I have the celery, please?" Her mother smiled and said, "Yes, you may have the celery. Now sit down and let's eat." So Lucy and her mother each had some celery. When they were finished, Lucy's mother said, "What do you want to do now?" Lucy said, "Let's dance!" So they both got up and started dancing around the kitchen. They danced and laughed until Lucy was too tired to dance anymore. When it was time for Lucy to go to bed, she was still feeling happy. She gave her mother a big hug and said, "Thank you for the yummy celery and for teaching me how to dance!" Her mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lucy. I'm glad you had a great time!" And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was excited to go on a journey with his mom and dad. They were going to the park to play and have fun. On their journey, Tim saw a small bird. The bird could talk! The bird said, "Hi, Tim! Let's be friends!" Tim was happy to have a new friend. They played together and had a lot of fun. At the end of the day, it was time for Tim and his family to go home. Tim said goodbye to his talking bird friend. He learned that being kind and making friends was important. Tim couldn't wait to go on another journey and make even more friends.

Once there was a large kitchen. Everything in the kitchen was big. The cabinets were big, the oven was big, and the fridge was also big. One day, a little boy wanted to help in the kitchen. He wanted to be just like his dad and help prepare dinner. So his mom gave him a big spoon and told him to stir the soup. The little boy was so happy! He was supporting the family by helping in the kitchen. Soon, the little boy was helping to cook dinner every day. He was becoming an expert in the kitchen. His mom was so proud of him. He was a big helper in the kitchen and the family was thankful for his support. From then on, the big kitchen was always filled with laughter. The little boy was a big part of that!

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She had a cup that was blue. Every morning she would get out of bed and drink from the cup. This made her very happy. One day, Jane asked her parents for something special. They told her that if she waited until bedtime, something good would happen. Jane was happy and couldn't wait. When bedtime came, Jane was so excited. But something seemed strange. Her parents had a surprise for her, but it didn't look like anything she had expected. Her parents offered her a new cup - one that was even bluer than her old cup. She was so excited. The cup seemed magical, and it sparkled in the light. Jane knew that this cup was special and it would make her happy.

Once upon a time, there was a mysterious human named Tom. Tom lived in a small house. He liked to clean his house every day. One sunny day, Tom met a new friend named Lucy. Lucy was a little girl who lived next door. Tom asked her, "Do you like to clean, too?" Lucy smiled and said, "Yes, I do! Can I help you clean your house?" Tom was very happy. They both went to his house and started to clean. They cleaned the floor, the windows, and the walls. When they were done, the house looked very nice. Tom and Lucy became good friends. They played and cleaned together every day. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sue. She was 3 years old, and she was very curious. She had a lovely chest full of toys and games. One day, Sue opened the chest and looked inside. She saw all the wonderful things that were waiting for her to play with. Sue said, "I want to fill my chest with even more lovely things!" Just then, her mum appeared and said, "Let me help you, Sue. We can go to the shop and fill your chest with lovely new things." So Sue and her mum went to the shop and bought lots of lovely things - dolls, balls, cars and books. Sue filled her chest and felt so happy! The chest was now full of wonderful toys, just for Sue. She hugged her mum, and said, "Thank you! I love my lovely chest!"

Sara liked to pick daisies in the park. She liked their white and yellow colors and their soft petals. She made a chain of daisies and put it on her head. She felt happy and pretty. But then she saw a big bee on a daisy. She wanted to touch it, because it looked fuzzy and cute. She reached out her hand and tried to pet the bee. But the bee did not like that. It was scared and angry. It had a sharp sting on its back. It used its sting to hurt Sara's finger. Sara felt a big pain in her finger. She cried out loud and dropped the daisy chain. She ran to her mom, who was sitting on a bench. She showed her mom her finger, which was red and swollen. Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, honey. The bee stung you. It was not nice. But it will get better soon. Let me put some ice on it." Sara felt upset and sad. She did not like the bee or the sting. She did not want to pick daisies anymore. She wanted to go home and play with her toys. Her mom said, "It's okay, Sara. You can still like daisies. They are beautiful and friendly. The bee was just scared and tried to protect itself. It did not mean to hurt you. Maybe next time, you can look at the bee from far away, and not touch it. Then it will not sting you." Sara nodded and wiped her tears. She felt a little better. She said, "Okay, mom. I will be careful next time. Can we go home now?" Her mom said, "Yes, we can. But first, let me give you a kiss and a band-aid for your finger. And you can keep your daisy chain. It still looks lovely on you." Sara smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you." Her mom said, "I love you too, Sara." They held hands and walked to the car. Sara still liked daisies, but she did not like bees. She learned a new word: sharp.

Mummy was packing her bag. She put lots of things in like socks and treats. She was packing a phone too. It was a useful phone as it could do lots of things. Mummy told her little girl to come and help with the packing. She gave her daughter the phone to put in the bag. The little girl was so happy to help. But then, suddenly, something bad happened. As the little girl was putting the phone in the bag, it fell out of her hands and broke on the floor. Both Mummy and the little girl were so sad. Mummy said, "Oh no! Now we don't have a phone for our holiday. We won't be able to take any photos!" And the little girl started to cry.

One day, a little girl named Mia was playing in her room. It was very quiet. She had many toys, but her favorite was a doll named Lucy. Mia and Lucy were best friends. They played together all the time. Mia noticed that Lucy was sad. "What's wrong, Lucy?" Mia asked. Lucy said, "I feel lonely. I want more friends to play with." Mia thought for a moment and then smiled. "I have an idea!" she said. Mia took Lucy to the park. There, they met other kids with dolls. They all played together and had a great time. Lucy was happy again. Mia and Lucy made many new friends that day, and they all played together every day after that.
