"That is a cauliflower, Lily. It is a vegetable that grows in the ground. We can eat it later, if you want." Mom said. Lily was curious. She wanted to see the cauliflower up close. She walked to the garden bed and bent down. She touched the cauliflower gently. It felt soft and bumpy. "Hello, cauliflower. I am Lily. Nice to meet you." She said. The cauliflower did not say anything. It just stayed still. But Lily felt happy. She had made a new friend in the garden. She ran back to her mom and hugged her. "Thank you, mom, for the cauliflower. I am grateful. Can we eat it for dinner?" She asked. Mom smiled and kissed her. "Of course, Lily. We can eat it for dinner. I am grateful for you, too. You are my sweet girl." She said. They went inside the house, holding hands. Lily looked forward to dinner. She wanted to share the cauliflower with her mom and dad. She thought it would be yummy. She was glad she had met the cauliflower.

Once upon a time, there was a sad rat named Remy. Remy lived in a small hole in a big house. He was sad because he had no friends to play with. One sunny day, Remy heard a little girl named Lily talking to her mom. Lily said, "Mom, I heard a mention of a rat in our house. Can I be friends with the rat?" Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful." Remy was very happy to hear this. He came out of his hole and met Lily. They played together all day and became good friends. From that day on, Remy was not a sad rat anymore.

Once there was a boy called Tom. Tom was three years old. Tom was playing outside and he noticed a tank. Tom thought the tank was good. So Tom decided to get closer and have a better look. He went up to the tank and he touched it. The tank felt cold and it was very big. Tom started to feel scared, so he decided to run away. Just then, he noticed something very special about the tank. It was full of fish! Tom was so excited and he couldn't believe it. He started to run around and tell everyone. Everyone agreed that the tank was very good. Tom was very happy. He loved looking at the fish in the tank. He kept going back to look at the tank every day. He even asked his parents if he could get his own tank. They said yes, and now Tom has a tank of his own and can look at the fish whenever he wants.

Once upon a time there was a big package that wanted to travel. So the package started to move very slow. It was such a slow pace that it took a long time for the package to get anywhere. But the package didn't give up, it kept on travelling, taking one step at a time. Finally after a long journey, the package arrived at its destination. Everyone was so excited that the package had arrived. They opened it up to find lots of toys, candy and books! Everyone was so happy with the package and everyone thanked the package for taking such a slow journey to get there. The End.

One day, Jane was walking through the woods searching for a place to take a nap. She had been walking for hours and was feeling very tired. All of a sudden, she spotted a tunnel. She thought it was the perfect place to take a nap and cautiously stepped inside. As soon as she sat down she felt a sense of calm and closed her eyes. Everything was peaceful until she heard a loud voice. "You can't take a nap here!", yelled a voice. Jane opened her eyes and saw a squirrel standing in front of her. He continued speaking, "This tunnel is my home. You have to leave or else you will be stuck here forever." Jane was feeling frustrated but knew that the squirrel was right. She slowly began to stand up and as she stepped out of the tunnel, she thanked him for reminding her that she needed to find a better place to take her nap. The next day, Jane returned to the woods feeling determined to find the perfect place to take a nap. After a while, she noticed a small clearing in a nearby park. She happily ran over to the clearing and laid down in the soft grass. She quickly drifted off to sleep and felt content to have finally taken her nap in a nice and safe place.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and listen to music. Her favorite kind of music was jazz. She would dance around her room every day to the jazz music. One day, Lily's little brother came into her room and started to bother her. He was being very naughty and wouldn't stop. Lily got very angry and slapped him on the arm. She felt guilty right away and apologized to her brother. After they made up, Lily put on some jazz music and they both danced together. They had so much fun and forgot all about their fight. From then on, Lily promised to never slap her brother again and they danced to jazz music together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Joe. Joe lived in a small house with his Mama. He had a favorite pot that he liked to play with. One day, Joe was feeling sad about something. Mama saw that Joe was sad and gave him a hug. She asked Joe what was wrong. He said that he wanted to raise the pot up high. Mama smiled and told Joe she would help him. Mama took Joe to the garden. They found a tall ladder and a strong rope. Mama helped Joe to tie the rope to the pot. Joe held the rope tight. Mama took the ladder and slowly raised it up. Joe looked up and waved as the pot went higher and higher. Mama and Joe both laughed as they watched the pot in the sky. Joe was so happy that he ran around and around. Even though Joe was still a bit sad, he felt much better. Mama was happy too, because she knew that Joe was feeling better.

Once upon a time, there was a red fish named Fin. Fin loved to swim in the big blue sea. One day, while swimming, Fin found a journal. The journal had many pictures and words. Fin wanted to show it to his best friend, Bubbles. Fin swam fast to find Bubbles. When he found her, he said, "Bubbles, look at this journal I found!" Bubbles looked at the journal and smiled. She said, "Wow, Fin! That's a pretty journal. Let's look at it together." Fin and Bubbles swam to a quiet spot and looked at the journal. They saw pictures of other fish and animals. They laughed and talked about the pictures. They had a fun time with the journal. After that, they swam back home, happy to have found a new treasure.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max liked to bring the newspaper to his owner every day. One day, Max saw a big, terrible cat in the yard. The cat wanted the newspaper too. Max knew he had to be brave and get the newspaper first. He thought of a plan. He found a ball and decided to use it to trick the cat. Max threw the ball far away. The cat ran after the ball, thinking it was the newspaper. While the cat was gone, Max quickly grabbed the newspaper and brought it to his owner. The owner was very happy with Max. The terrible cat was sad, but it learned not to mess with Max and his newspaper again. And Max and his owner lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very stubborn. She always wanted to do what she wanted to do and nothing else. One day, the little girl decided that she wanted to mail the sunrise. She got an envelope, put the sunrise inside, and then wrote a note on the envelope. She stuck a stamp on the envelope and gave it to the mailman. He was very surprised, but he mailed it anyway! The next morning, when the sun rose in the sky, it was the same sunrise that the little girl had mailed the day before! Everyone was amazed and they all cheered. The stubborn little girl had done the impossible - she had mailed the sunrise!

Once upon a time there was a poor mouse who was very unhappy. He had suffered from the rudeness of some other animals. He felt sad and alone. One day the mouse was walking around a garden, trying to find something nice to eat. Suddenly he spied two big cats playing in the sun. The mouse was scared, but stood very still, hoping that the cats wouldn't notice him. Unfortunately, the cats noticed the mouse and began to chase him. The mouse ran and ran, but the cats were just too fast. Eventually, he found a small hole in the ground and managed to squeeze through. He was very relieved, but sadly he was still stuck in the hole. The cats were still determined to get the mouse. They continued to paw at the hole and scream rude words. But then a kind rabbit came by and heard the poor mouse's cries. The rabbit quickly ran to the farmers house. The farmer was not happy with the cats' behaviour and shooed them away. The mouse was very thankful to the rabbit, and they both danced in the garden together. From then on, the mouse never suffered from the rudeness of other animals again.

John went to the market one day with his mom. He saw a beautiful blue kite that he really wanted. His mom told him he couldn't have it, but he wouldn't listen. He was too excited and ran to the kite to grab it. Suddenly, a tough foot stepped on the kite. John was scared and turned around. There was a big man with a mean look on his face. "Mommy," John said, scared. The man said, "I run the market and I won't provide for any children running around and taking things that don't belong to them." John was still scared and backed away slowly. His mom told the man she was sorry and would pay for the kite. But the man said it was too late and he wanted John to learn a lesson. He told John to never take things that don't belong to him again, and he made John leave the market. John and his mom had a bad ending that day. He never got the kite and he was reminded to never take things that weren't his.

Once upon a time, there was a small mouse named Sam. He had a deep nose and he liked to explore. One day, Sam decided to explore the nearby forest. He was so excited, but he was also a bit scared. So, Sam slowly walked forward, trembling with fear. As he walked further into the forest, he heard a loud noise. He then saw a big, deep-voiced bear! Sam was so scared he nearly passed out. The bear said, "What are you doing here?" Sam shivered and said, "I-I was just exploring." The bear smiled and said, "Well then, why don't we explore together?" Sam bravely nodded his head and followed the bear deeper into the forest. Sam learned about the trees and animals and smiled the entire time! He was no longer trembling with fear. When it was time to go home, Sam waved goodbye to his new bear friend and ran back to his home. He took a deep breath and remembered the fun day he just had.

Ben and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with their toys. One day, they saw a man with a big truck. The man had many toys in his truck. He said he would sell them for cheap. Ben and Sam ran to the man. They wanted to buy some toys. They had some money from their piggy bank. They looked at the toys. They saw cars, dolls, balls, and puzzles. They also saw a green box. The box was dull and had no picture on it. "What is in the green box?" Ben asked the man. "It is a surprise toy. It is very fun and special. You can have it for only one dollar," the man said. Ben and Sam were curious. They wanted to see the surprise toy. They gave the man one dollar and took the green box. They ran back to their house. They opened the box. But there was no toy in the box. There was only a rock. A dull, gray rock. Ben and Sam were sad and angry. They had wasted their money. They had no new toy. They had been tricked by the man. They tried to find the man and his truck. But he was gone. He had driven away with his toys and their money. Ben and Sam cried. They wished they had not bought the green box. They wished they had bought a car or a doll or a ball or a puzzle instead. They learned a hard lesson. They learned to be careful and not trust strangers. They learned to not judge a book by its cover. Or a box by its color.

Bob was walking down the street when he saw a peach tree ahead of him. Amazed by the beauty of the tree, he decided to take a closer look. He stepped up to it and started to reach for a peach when he noticed something strange. "Run!" warned a voice from the tree. "Ah!" shouted Bob, jumping back in fear. He looked up to the tree branches and noticed a small, green dragon. "Please don't be scared," the dragon said. "I will not hurt you. I only want one peach." Bob was still fearful but was also curious. "Why do you want a peach?" he asked. The dragon smiled. "The peach will help me yield my magical powers. Then I will be able to fly away and be free." When Bob heard the dragon's story, he felt his fear melting away. He reached up and carefully offered a peach to the dragon. "Thank you," said the dragon gratefully. He ate the peach, then flew away with a smile. Bob watched and whispered farewell as the dragon vanished into the air.

John was playing hockey in the park. He was whacking the puck around and having a lot of fun. But then he noticed it was getting gloomy outside, and he got a bit sad. He sighed and put away his hockey stick and skates, and went home. On the way home John saw some kids playing a game of tag. He wanted to play too, but he didn't feel like it. He continued home, sighing. When he got home, his mom asked him why he was so sad. John didn't know how to explain, so he said he was just tired. His mom hugged him and said that would be alright. He smiled and kept on walking. John eventually forgot his sadness and he remembered the fun he had playing hockey. He smiled as he remembered what happened in the park and he was glad he was home.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys, books and games, but their favorite thing was the lamp. The lamp was old and had a colorful shade with animals on it. The lamp made their room bright and cozy. One day, their mom said they had to share the lamp with their cousin Lily, who was coming to visit. Lily did not have a lamp in her room and was afraid of the dark. Anna and Ben did not want to share the lamp. They liked it too much and thought Lily would break it or lose it. When Lily arrived, she saw the lamp and smiled. She asked Anna and Ben if she could use it at night. Anna and Ben said no. They said the lamp was theirs and they needed it. Lily felt sad and troubled. She did not understand why they were so mean. That night, Anna and Ben turned on the lamp and got ready for bed. They heard Lily crying in the guest room. They felt a little sorry for her, but they still did not want to share the lamp. They closed their eyes and tried to sleep. But they could not sleep. They felt something was wrong. They looked at the lamp and realized it was not making them happy. It was making them selfish and unkind. They remembered how their mom always taught them to value other people more than things. They decided to change their minds. They got up and took the lamp to Lily's room. They knocked on the door and said they were sorry. They said they wanted to share the lamp with her and make her feel welcome. Lily was surprised and happy. She thanked them and hugged them. She said they were very nice and generous. They plugged in the lamp and turned it on. The lamp made Lily's room bright and cozy. They all smiled and felt warm in their hearts. They learned that sharing is caring and that valuing others is more important than valuing things. They became good friends and had a good night's sleep.

A little girl named Mary was playing outside on a Tuesday. Her parents had warned her not to play with fire, but Mary was feeling brave and wanted to prove that she could be responsible. Mary found a yellow stick and dragged it over to her campfire. She touched the stick to the fire and it began to burn. Mary was so excited she clapped her hands. But then Mary's parents arrived. Mary felt ashamed and scared. She knew she had made a mistake. Mary's father said, "Mary, fire can be very dangerous. We told you to be careful." He hugged her and said, "We love you, and we want you to stay safe. Remember, it's always good to be careful with fire." Mary was very sorry and promised never to play with fire again. She learned that it's important to always listen to her parents and stay safe.

Lila and Ben are playing in the farm. They see a big gray bull in the field. The bull has horns and a ring in his nose. He looks angry. "Let's go closer and say hello to the bull," Ben says. He likes animals. "No, Ben, that's not a good idea. The bull might hurt us. He is not friendly like the cows," Lila says. She is scared of the bull. But Ben does not listen to Lila. He runs to the fence and climbs over it. He walks towards the bull. He wants to touch him. "Ben, come back! You are in danger!" Lila shouts. She follows him and tries to pull him away. The bull sees Ben and Lila. He snorts and lowers his head. He charges at them. He is very fast. Lila and Ben are very afraid. They run back to the fence. But the bull is faster. He is almost on them. Lila remembers what her dad told her. If a bull chases you, you have to kneel down and stay still. Maybe he will think you are a rock and leave you alone. Lila kneels down and covers her head with her arms. She hopes the bull will not see her. Ben sees Lila kneel down. He does not understand why she does that. He thinks she is giving up. He keeps running to the fence. He thinks he can make it. But he is wrong. The bull catches up with him. He hits him with his horns. He tosses him in the air. He makes him fly. Ben screams. He is hurt. He falls to the ground. He does not move. Lila sees what happens to Ben. She cries. She is very sad. She wishes she could help him. The bull sees Lila. He does not care about her. He thinks she is a rock. He walks away. He goes back to his grass. Lila gets up. She runs to Ben. She hugs him. She calls for help. Dad hears Lila's cries. He comes to the field. He sees Ben and Lila. He sees the bull. He understands what happened. He is very angry at the bull. He is very worried about Ben. He is very proud of Lila. He picks up Ben and carries him to the car. He takes him to the doctor. He hopes he will be okay. He tells Lila she is very brave. She did the right thing. She saved her life. He tells her he loves her. He hugs her. He takes her home. He tells her they will never go near the bull again. He tells her the bull is very bad. He tells her he will find a new home for him. Lila nods. She agrees. She does not like the bull. She likes Ben. She hopes he will get better soon. She wants to play with him again. She loves him.

Once there was a little boy who was three years old. He liked to explore his house. One day, he heard something scary in his bedroom. He thought it must be a ghost! He did not want to see the ghost, so he slowly opened the door. When he looked into the room, he saw the ghost. It was floating around and it looked very scary. The little boy was afraid and he started to cry. He wanted to leave the room, but he was too scared to move. Then the ghost started to talk to him. It said "Don't be afraid, I just want to be your friend!" The little boy stopped crying, and he moved closer to the ghost. They talked and played together, and the little boy quickly forgot how scary the ghost had looked. From then on, the little boy and the ghost were best friends. They did lots of fun things together and the little boy was never scared of the ghost again.

One day, a little red car named Tommy was feeling restless. He wanted to go on a big drive. He asked his friend, a small green car named Sally, "Do you want to go on a drive with me?" Sally said, "Yes! Let's go!" They drove together, laughing and having fun. But then, they saw a big pepper blocking the road. They could not go past it. Tommy said, "We must move the pepper!" They tried to push it, but it was too big. They felt sad and did not know what to do. Then, a big blue truck named Max came. Max saw the little cars and the big pepper. He said, "I can help!" Max used his strong wheels to push the pepper away. Tommy and Sally were so happy. They thanked Max and continued their drive. They had a great day and lots of fun.

Once upon a time, a boy was walking in the forest. He saw a snake that was very long and scary. The boy was afraid of the snake but he knew he had to be brave. He took a stick and tried to cut the snake. But the snake was too quick and slithered away. The boy continued to walk and saw an ancient tree. It was very big and had many leaves. The boy felt happy and continued his journey.

Tim and Mia like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is the big box of colorful prints. The prints are pictures of animals, cars, flowers and more. They can stick the prints on the wall, on the floor, on the table or on themselves. One day, Tim and Mia are playing with the prints in their room. They make a big castle with the prints on the floor. They pretend to be a king and a queen. They have fun with their castle. But then, their baby brother Tom comes in. Tom is very curious. He sees the prints and wants to touch them. He crawls to the castle and grabs some prints. He tears them and throws them. He makes a loud noise. He destroys the castle. Tim and Mia are very sad and angry. They shout at Tom. They tell him to go away. They try to fix their castle, but it is too late. The prints are broken and messy. They cry and hug each other. Mom hears the noise and comes in. She sees the mess and the tears. She feels sorry for Tim and Mia. She also feels sorry for Tom. He does not know what he did. He is too small. She picks up Tom and cuddles him. She tells Tim and Mia that she is sorry. She helps them clean up the prints. She tells them that they can make a new castle later. She tells them that they are good children. She tells them that she loves them. She gives them a kiss and a hug. They feel better. They smile and say thank you. They love Mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to visit her grandma. Her grandma had a big pot on the stove and was stirring it with a spoon. Lily asked her grandma what she was making. Her grandma said she was making soup with crystals in it. Lily didn't know what crystals were, so her grandma showed her some shiny rocks that looked like diamonds. Lily thought they were pretty. After a while, Lily's grandma started to feel tired. She asked Lily to stay alert and keep stirring the soup. Lily was happy to help her grandma. She stirred the soup carefully, making sure it didn't spill. She looked at the crystals in the soup and thought they looked like stars. She was proud of herself for being a good helper. Finally, the soup was ready. Lily's grandma said it was the best soup she ever tasted. She gave Lily a big hug and thanked her for being such a good helper. Lily felt happy and proud. She knew that stirring the soup and being alert was important. From that day on, she loved to help her grandma in the kitchen.

Once upon a time there was an orange leak. The leak was always getting bigger and bigger. Until one day it split. The orange leak split into two. Each part of the orange leak was still leaking and getting bigger. Soon the two orange leaks had spread across the floor. But then something surprising happened. A big sunny ray of light came down from the sky and filled the two orange leaks with sunshine. The orange leaks smiled and started to jump and dance in the sunshine. From that day on, the orange leaks never split again and always stayed together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She always wanted to win but was never a winner. Every day she tried her best, but still never won. One day she found a vest. It was a blue vest with colorful flowers all over it. She was so excited that she wore it everywhere she went. The girl tried one more time, and this time she WON! The people around her cheered and clapped. She was so happy, she ran around and around with her new vest on. She was having so much fun that she got careless and stumbled. Her vest got caught on a fence. She was about to cry, but then something amazing happened. A special fairy came with a pair of scissors and cut the vest off. She was so relieved, and from then on always tried to be careful, just in case she ever WON anything like that again!

Once upon a time, there was a tiny boy. He was very tidy and he had a special cup for his milk. Every day the boy would drink his milk and he was always so happy. But one day, something different happened. The boy went to his cup, but it was empty. He said to himself, "Where is my milk?" He searched all around the house, but he couldn't find it. Then he asked his mum, "Where is my milk?" His mum replied, "The cat has gained it." The boy was so upset. He had no milk and he was very sad. The boy never saw his milk again, and he never felt so unhappy. No more milk for him again.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. The bear liked to go to the shop to buy honey. But one day, the shop was closed. The bear didn't like that. He got mad and started to fight with the door. The door didn't move, but the bear kept trying. After a while, the bear got tired and went back to his cave. But on the way, he smelled something smelly. It was a skunk! The bear didn't like the smell, so he ran away as fast as he could. From that day on, the bear made sure to check if the shop was open before going there.

Lily was sick. She had a bad cough and a sore throat. She did not want to play or eat. She only wanted to sleep. Her mom was worried. She gave Lily a pill to make her feel better. But Lily did not like the pill. It was big and bitter. She spit it out. "Please, Lily, you have to take the pill," her mom said. "It will help you get well soon." "No, no, no!" Lily cried. "I don't want the pill. It's yucky!" Her mom tried to be patient. She hugged Lily and said, "I know, sweetie, but it's good for you. How about this? If you take the pill, I will let you watch your favorite show. The one with the lovely princess and the funny dragon. You love that show, don't you?" Lily thought for a moment. She did love that show. It always made her laugh and smile. She wanted to see the princess and the dragon. Maybe the pill was not so bad after all. She nodded and said, "Okay, mom, I will take the pill. But only if you let me watch the show." Her mom smiled and said, "Deal." She gave Lily a glass of water and the pill. Lily swallowed the pill quickly and made a face. Then she ran to the couch and turned on the TV. Her mom joined her and cuddled with her. They watched the show together and laughed and smiled. Lily felt a little better. She was glad she took the pill. And she was glad her mom let her watch the show. She loved her mom very much.

Once upon a time there was a beautiful flower called Blossom. Blossom liked playing with her friends and family. Every day she would look up at the sky and dream about what could be. One day Blossom was out in the sun, and she watched as an arrow flew by her. She was so amazed by the arrow that she wanted to follow it. So she followed it around until she saw a big tree. Blossom tried to climb up the tree, but she couldn't because it was too tall. She felt helpless, like she could not do anything. That's when she noticed some petals on the tree. Blossom touched the petals, and they started to bloom. She felt so happy that she began to dance all around the tree. She had never seen a tree bloom like this before and she was so excited. Then, suddenly, a voice came out of the tree. "Thank you Blossom," it said. "Because of you my petals can now bloom." Blossom was both surprised and happy, and she smiled. "You're welcome," she said to the tree. The two of them were happy ever after, and Blossom knew that no matter how helpless she felt, she could always bloom.

Once there was a clever truck. It always wanted to help. One day it needed to do something special. So it decided to load some grass. It made sure it was very careful and intelligent when it was loading the grass. It worked very hard to make sure the grass was safely loaded. When the grass was loaded, the clever truck was very proud of itself. It had done a great job! The truck drove away, taking the grass with it. It felt so happy to have been able to help.

This morning, Mommy, Daddy and a 3 year old child were walking to church. The little child's eyes were wide with amazement at the adorable sight of the church. Everywhere the child looked there were pretty flowers and windows that seemed to go very high up into the sky. The child jumped up and down with excitement as Mommy and Daddy smiled happily. It seemed like it was going to be a great day for the family. Mommy and Daddy were so proud of their little one as they walked down the aisle of the church. The child was so adorable in their new dress. Everyone was looking and smiling at the special family. At the end of the service, Mommy and Daddy waved goodbye to their friends as they walked out of the church. The family was still beaming with joy as they set out for home. They all held hands and smiled, what had seemed like a magical morning!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Grace. Grace was always so spoiled. One day, Grace's mother wanted to show her something special. She held up a big, round cookie. Grace's face lit up with joy and she said "Cookie!" Her mother smiled and handed the cookie to Grace. Grace couldn't believe it! She knew it was for her, she was so excited! Grace then showed her cookie to her father. He smiled too and said "Yum, that looks delicious!" Grace smiled back at him and bit into her cookie. She chewed happily, savoring every bite. Grace ate the whole cookie. She then looked up at her mother with a satisfied smile. "That was yummy!" she said. Her mother smiled and hugged her, happy to see her so happy. Grace then hugged her father and said "Thank you so much for the cookie!" They both laughed and hugged her back. Grace was so spoiled, but in the end everyone was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside and picking flowers. One day, Lily went outside to play and saw that the sky was getting dark. She heard a loud noise and saw a big storm coming. Lily's mom called her to come inside, but Lily didn't want to leave her flowers. Suddenly, the wind started to blow and the rain started to pour. Lily got scared and started to scream. Her mom came to get her and they went inside. Lily was still scared and her face was pale. She asked her mom if the storm would hurt her flowers. Her mom said no, but Lily was still sad. The next day, Lily went outside and saw that her flowers were gone. The storm had blown them all away. Lily was very sad and cried.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside on the side of her house. One day, it started to rain and Lily was sad because she couldn't play outside anymore. She watched the raindrops fall and thought they were very pretty. After a while, the rain stopped and Lily went outside to play. She saw a busy ant crawling on the ground and decided to follow it. The ant led her to a big tree where there were lots of other ants working hard. Lily was amazed at how busy they were. She stayed and watched the ants for a while before going back inside. Even though it had rained, Lily still had a fun day and learned something new about the busy ants.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play by the river. One day, they saw a big raft made of wood and rope. They wanted to ride on it and have fun. "Let's go on the raft, Sam!" Tom said. "It looks like a boat!" "OK, Tom, but be careful. The water is fast and deep," Sam said. He was older and wise. They climbed on the raft and pushed it into the water. The raft moved with the current and they laughed and waved. They felt like pirates. But soon, the raft went too far and they could not see the shore. They tried to paddle with their hands, but it was hard. The water was cold and strong. "Help! Help!" Tom and Sam shouted. "We want to go back!" But no one heard them. The raft gained speed and went towards a big rock. It hit the rock and broke into pieces. Tom and Sam fell into the water and sank. They did not know how to swim. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a bag. She was excited and wanted to finish her adventure with the bag. The little girl decided to take the bag and go for a walk. She walked very slow, taking in all the sights and sounds. Suddenly she stopped. She heard someone call her name. She looked and saw her mommy. The mommy said, "What do you have in the bag?" The little girl smiled. "I'm almost finished. I'm going to explore the world." Her mommy smiled too. "Well that sounds fun. Then when you finish, you can come back home and rest." The little girl nodded and continued her journey. She was excited and happy to finish her adventure with the bag.

Joey was a very careless little boy, always running around and playing. One day, he came across a print shop. He was fascinated by all the different prints and decided he wanted one for himself. He stepped inside, but the shopkeeper resisted him. "You have to wait outside. I don't want any trouble." Joey, who was used to getting what he wanted, was very angry. He didn't understand why he couldn't have the print he wanted. Not caring about the shopkeeper, he decided to try and take it anyway. He reached for the print, but the shopkeeper grabbed him. "You have to learn to respect people and be more careful!" Joey was scared and ran away. But he never learned his lesson. The shopkeeper shook his head and thought to himself, "Why can't some people be more careful?" The moral of the story is to be careful and remember to respect and listen to others, even if we don't want to. Ignoring other people's wishes can lead to bad outcomes and nobody wants that!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play in the rain. Her mom gave her a big, red umbrella to keep her dry. But Lily didn't want to stay under the umbrella. She wanted to feel the wet raindrops on her face. Suddenly, Lily heard a loud noise. It was her friend, Timmy, playing his trumpet. He was hurrying to show her a new song he learned. Lily was so excited to hear the music that she ran to him, forgetting about the rain. As they danced and sang in the rain, Lily's clothes got very wet. But she didn't mind. She was having too much fun. When the rain stopped, they said goodbye and went back home. Lily's mom gave her a warm bath and she fell asleep with a big smile on her face, dreaming of the fun she had with her friend Timmy and his trumpet.

Tim was walking along a path through the woods. All around him the trees were tall and strong, their trunks made from lumber. Suddenly, he heard a sound coming from the distance. It was getting louder and louder! 'What is that noise?' Tim thought to himself. He looked around and soon he saw something whizzing through the trees. It was a red car, moving at incredible speed. Tim watched as it weaved between the trees, faster and faster. Suddenly, it stopped in front of Tim. The driver rolled down his window and asked him a question. 'Do you know where the sour apples are?' the driver said with a grin. Tim nodded and pointed down the path. 'If you follow this path, you'll find a big tree with sour apples,' Tim said. The driver smiled. 'Thanks! Now I can pick some apples for my grandmother,' he said before he drove away at lightning speed. Tim watched as the car disappeared into the distance. 'My, that was a fast car!' he thought.

Lily and Ben were twins who loved to play games. One day, they went to a big park with their mom and dad. There they saw a brilliant maze made of tall green plants. Lily and Ben wanted to go inside and find the way out. "Can we go, mom? Can we go, dad?" they asked. "Sure, but stay together and be careful," mom and dad said. "We will wait for you at the exit." Lily and Ben ran into the maze, holding hands. They turned left and right, following the paths. They saw flowers and birds and bugs. They had fun. But then, they heard a loud roar. It sounded like a big, scary animal. Lily and Ben stopped and looked around. They saw nothing. "What was that?" Lily whispered. "I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it's a lion or a bear." They felt scared. They wanted to go back to mom and dad. But they did not know which way to go. They were lost. They heard the roar again. It was closer. Lily and Ben started to cry. "Help! Help!" they shouted. Suddenly, they saw a man in a funny costume. He had a furry head and a long tail. He was the one who made the roar. He was not a real animal. He was a person who worked at the park. He was trying to scare the people who came to the maze. "Boo!" he said, jumping out of the plants. Lily and Ben screamed. They were very scared. They did not like the man. "Hey, don't cry, kids," the man said. "It's just a joke. I'm sorry. I didn't mean to scare you. I'm here to help you. Follow me. I'll show you the way out." The man took Lily and Ben by the hand and led them to the exit. There they saw mom and dad, who were worried. "Lily! Ben! Are you okay?" mom and dad said, hugging them. "We're okay, mom. We're okay, dad," Lily and Ben said. "But we don't like the maze. There was a man who scared us. He was not nice." Mom and dad looked at the man. They saw his costume. They understood. "Oh, he was just playing a game," mom said. "He didn't know you were so young. He thought you would laugh." "Well, we didn't laugh," Ben said. "We were scared." "I'm sorry, kids," the man said. "I won't scare you again. Here, have a candy. And a sticker. And a balloon. Do you forgive me?" Lily and Ben looked at the candy, the sticker, and the balloon. They liked them. They smiled. "Okay, we forgive you," Lily said. "But don't scare us again," Ben said. "I won't, I promise," the man said. Lily and Ben took the candy, the sticker, and the balloon. They thanked the man. They went with mom and dad to another part of the park. They found a slide and a swing and a sandbox. They played there. They had fun. They forgot about the maze and the man. They were happy.

Lily and Tom were playing with blocks. They liked to make towers and houses with the blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. Some were round, some were square, some were long and some were short. "Look, I made a big house with square blocks!" Lily said. She was proud of her house. It had a door, a window and a roof. "That's nice, Lily. But I made a castle with round blocks!" Tom said. He was proud of his castle. It had a wall, a gate and a tower. They showed each other their blocks and smiled. They were happy to play together. But then they heard a loud noise. It was a scary noise. It sounded like a roar. They looked around and saw a big dog. The dog was angry. It barked and ran towards them. "Help! Help!" Lily and Tom cried. They were afraid of the dog. They did not want the dog to bite them or knock down their blocks. They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. They hugged her and told her about the dog. "Don't worry, my loves. I'm here. You are safe." Mom said. She was calm and kind. She stroked their hair and kissed their cheeks. "Can we stay with you, mom?" Lily and Tom asked. They did not want to play with blocks anymore. They wanted to stay with mom. "Of course, you can stay with me. You can play with something else. How about a book or a puzzle?" Mom said. She took out a book and a puzzle from her bag. They had pictures and words that Lily and Tom liked. "Thank you, mom. You are the best." Lily and Tom said. They smiled and took the book and the puzzle. They sat on the bench with mom and forgot about the dog. They were happy to stay with mom.

Mia likes to sing. She sings when she wakes up, when she eats, when she plays and when she goes to bed. She sings loud and happy songs that make her feel good. But her brother Leo does not like to sing. He is grumpy and quiet. He likes to read and draw and play with his cars. He does not like loud noises that hurt his ears. One day, Mia and Leo are in the car with their mom. Mia is singing a song about a rainbow and a unicorn. Leo is reading a book about a dinosaur and a volcano. He does not want to hear Mia's song. He says, "Mia, stop singing! You are too loud and silly. You make my ears ache." Mia feels sad and stops singing. She says, "But I like to sing. Singing makes me happy. Why are you so grumpy, Leo?" Leo says, "Because I like to read. Reading makes me smart. Singing is for babies. You are a baby, Mia." Mia says, "No, I am not a baby. I am three years old. You are mean, Leo." Mom hears them and says, "Mia and Leo, please stop fighting. You are both good and special. You can like different things and still be nice to each other. Mia, you can sing, but not too loud. Leo, you can read, but not too rude. Can you do that?" Mia and Leo nod and say, "Yes, mom." Mom says, "Good. Now, how about we all sing a song together? A song that we all know and like. Do you know the song about the wheels on the bus?" Mia and Leo say, "Yes, mom." Mom says, "OK, then. Let's sing it. The wheels on the bus go round and round, round and round, round and round..." Mia and Leo join mom and sing the song. Mia sings happy and Leo sings quiet. They both smile and have fun. They are not grumpy anymore. They are friends.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play with blocks. They build a big tower with red and blue and yellow blocks. They are very proud of their tower. "Look, our tower is so high!" Ben says. "Yes, it is. We are good builders!" Mia says. They want to show their tower to their mom and dad. But they have to be quiet. Mom and dad are working in the other room. They do not like noise. "Let's make a promise," Ben says. "We will not knock down our tower. We will not shout or run. We will be quiet until mom and dad finish working." "OK, I promise," Mia says. "We will be quiet and careful." They hold hands and nod. They are good friends. They keep their promise. They wait for mom and dad to come and see their tower. They smile and whisper. They are happy.

Sara and Ben were playing outside with their kites. They liked to see how high they could make them fly in the sky. The wind was strong and helped their kites soar. But the wind was also sharp and cold. It made their noses red and their ears hurt. "Ben, I'm cold. Can we go inside?" Sara asked. "Not yet. I want to fly my kite more. It's fun!" Ben said. "But it's difficult to hold the string. It hurts my hands. And the wind is sharp. It cuts my face." Sara said. Ben looked at Sara and saw that she was shivering. He felt sorry for her. He knew she was his sister and he loved her. "Okay, Sara. We can go inside. But first, let's bring our kites down. We don't want to lose them." Ben said. They pulled their strings and made their kites come closer. They caught them and folded them. They ran to their house and opened the door. Their mom was waiting for them with hot chocolate and cookies. "Welcome back, my little ones. You look very cold. Come and warm up." Mom said. She hugged them and gave them their treats. They smiled and thanked her. They felt happy and cozy. They liked to play outside, but they also liked to be inside with their mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the deep blue sea with his friends. One day, Nemo and his friends were playing a game of tag when suddenly, Nemo saw a shiny pearl at the bottom of the sea. Excitedly, Nemo swam down to get the pearl, but as he got deeper and deeper, the silence around him grew stronger. Suddenly, Nemo heard a big voice say, "Who goes there?" It was a big, scary octopus! Nemo was scared, but he knew he had to be brave. He said, "It's just me, Nemo. I saw a pearl and wanted to dive down to get it." The octopus laughed and said, "Well, you're a brave little fish. Take the pearl and go play with your friends." Nemo quickly grabbed the pearl and swam away as fast as he could. He was happy to be back with his friends and told them all about his adventure.

One day, a big red truck was driving down the road. The truck was very angry because it had a big job to do. It needed to attach a small car to it and take it away. The truck driver saw the small car and stopped. He said, "I need to attach you to my truck and take you away." The small car was scared and did not want to go. But the angry truck did not care. The truck attached the small car and drove away. The small car was very sad and cried. The truck did not care and kept driving. In the end, the small car was taken far away and never saw its friends again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a dog named Max who she loved very much. One day, Lily's friend came over with her new puppy. Lily became envious of her friend's puppy and wished she had a puppy too. Lily's mom noticed how she was feeling and sat down to talk with her. "Lily, it's okay to want things, but it's not okay to be envious of others. You have Max, who is a wonderful dog and your best friend. You can't add another dog to your family just because your friend has one." Lily understood what her mom was saying and hugged Max tightly. She realized that she was lucky to have such a great dog and didn't need anything else to be happy. From that day on, Lily stopped feeling envious and appreciated everything she had.

Once upon a time there was a dragon. His name was Bob. He was big, and very intelligent. Bob was alone in the forest when he met another dragon. Her name was Lisa. They were both surprised to see another dragon in the forest. Bob smiled and said, "Hello Lisa. Do you want to part?" Lisa was excited and said, "Yes! Let's part!" So they flew together through the sky. High above the trees, they found a beautiful lake. They played in the lake, splashing each other with their tails. At the end of the day, Bob and Lisa said goodbye. They part again, but neither of them forgot their time together. The intelligent dragons will always remember their friendship!

Once there was a deaf boy named Bob. Bob loved to play all day, but he couldn't find anyone to join him in his fun. He looked around and all he saw was a lonely pear tree. So Bob decided to join the pear tree. He carefully climbed up the tree, being careful not to fall. He moved from branch to branch until he got to the top. From the top of the tree, Bob could see for miles. He was amazed. He had never seen such beautiful things before. He wanted to stay in the tree forever. But then he heard some noise from far away, so Bob decided to join the noise. He climbed down the tree, and went to investigate. Bob followed the noise and it led him to a group of children playing. He watched them having fun and he wanted to join them too. He had so much fun playing with them, and he never wanted to leave. From then on, Bob always joined the children in their games. He loved it so much that he forgot all about his deafness and the lonely pear tree. He felt like he belonged.

Once upon a time, there was a gray flower in a meadow. One day the flower said that the meadow was very wonderful. But the cloud in the sky disagreed. The cloud said the meadow was too green and not enough blue. The flower and the cloud did not agree. The wind came and said to the flower and the cloud, "Let's try something else." The wind blew high and strong, and made the cloud turn into lots of raindrops. The raindrops made the meadow turn from green to blue. The flower and the cloud looked around and smiled. They both agreed that the meadow was now very wonderful. The flower smiled and said, "I'm so happy we could disagree."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, while she was playing, she slipped and fell. She hurt her eye and it started to water. Her mom saw her crying and asked, "What happened, Lily?" Lily said, "I fell and my eye hurts." Her mom hugged her and said, "Let me take a look." She saw that Lily's eye was red and a little bit icy. Her mom said, "Don't worry, sweetie. I will pull you back up and we can go inside and get you some warm cocoa." Lily smiled and her mom helped her up. They went inside and enjoyed some yummy cocoa together.

Lily and Ben liked to pretend they were explorers. They had a big cardboard box that they turned into a tunnel. They crawled inside and used a flashlight to see. "Look, there's a treasure!" Lily said, pointing to a shiny necklace she had hidden in the corner. "Wow, let me see!" Ben said, reaching for it. But Lily pulled it away. "No, it's mine! I found it first!" Ben was angry. He wanted the treasure too. He tried to grab it from Lily, but she held on tight. "Stop it, Ben! You're hurting me!" Lily cried. "Give it to me, Lily! It's not fair!" Ben shouted. They both pulled and tugged, but neither would let go. The necklace broke and the beads flew everywhere. They both gasped. They looked at the broken necklace and then at each other. They felt sad and sorry. "I'm sorry, Lily. I shouldn't have been mean to you," Ben said. "I'm sorry, Ben. I shouldn't have been greedy," Lily said. They hugged and said they were still friends. They decided to share the beads and make new necklaces. They smiled and crawled out of the tunnel. They saw their mom waiting for them with a bright smile. "Did you have fun, explorers?" she asked. "Yes, mom. We had an adventure and we learned to share," they said. They showed her their new necklaces and she hugged them. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Mickey. Mickey loved to climb. He climbed trees, rocks, and even walls. One day, Mickey saw a big piece of cheese on a table. He wanted to climb up to the table and eat the cheese. But it was too high for him to climb. Mickey felt sad and hungry. He saw a fridge nearby and thought maybe he could find some cheese inside. He climbed up the fridge and opened the door. Inside, he found a big block of cold cheese. He was so happy and started eating it. But as he ate, he started to feel sick. The cheese was too cold and made him feel bad. Mickey tried to climb down from the fridge, but he was too dizzy. He fell down and hurt himself badly. From that day on, Mickey learned to be careful when climbing and eating cheese.

Once upon a time, there was a little white bunny. The bunny liked to joke and play with his friends. They lived in a big green field with lots of flowers. One sunny day, the bunny and his friends found a triangle. The triangle was shiny and pretty. They decided to play a game with the triangle. They took turns throwing the triangle and running to catch it. As they played, they laughed and joked with each other. They had so much fun with the triangle. At the end of the day, they were all tired but happy. The little white bunny and his friends went home, excited to play with the triangle again the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom. It was a beautiful day, and the sun was shining bright. But Lily was not happy. She complained to her mom that she was bored and wanted to go home. Her mom told her to be patient and enjoy the day. They sat on a bench, and Lily noticed that there was an unusual silence in the park. She asked her mom why it was so quiet, and her mom explained that sometimes it's nice to just listen to the sounds of nature. Suddenly, Lily saw a bird flying in the sky, and she pointed it out to her mom. They watched the bird fly for a while, and it made them both happy. Lily realized that sometimes it's good to be patient and enjoy the little things in life. From that day on, she never complained about being bored again. The moral of the story is to be patient and appreciate the beauty of nature.

Once upon a time there was a family who enjoyed having dinner together. Every night, the parents, Sam and Susan, and their three-year-old daughter, Liza, all sat down together to share a meal. Liza loved her parents, and she was always excited for dinner. One evening, Liza was extra excited. "What are we having for dinner tonight?" she asked, hopping up and down in her chair. Sam and Susan shared a surprised look. "It's a surprise!" they answered. Liza sat quietly for a moment and then let out a rude yell. "I want to know!" she shouted. The parents laughed. "Liza," said Sam patiently. "It's just one surprise. You don't need to be so rude." Hearing this, Liza tried to calm herself down and behave better. She crossed her arms and quietly said, "Okay. I'm sorry." After a few more minutes of anticipation, dinner was served and Liza was once again excited.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Timmy and he was 3 years old. He had a great big smile on his face. He was very enthusiastic about life. One day Timmy was in his house when he heard a sound from outside. He ran to the window to take a look. He saw a big yellow vehicle pulling up. Timmy asked his mom what it was. She replied, "It's the ice cream truck. It serves ice cream to everyone." Timmy was so excited he couldn't wait to get outside. He ran out the door and to the ice cream truck. When he got there he saw that the truck was full of different kinds of ice creams. Timmy picked one and asked the driver for it. The driver said, "Sure, that one is for you. Enjoy!" Timmy was very happy. He ran back to his house with his ice cream to show his mom. From then on, every time the ice cream truck arrived to his town, Timmy was always the first one to get some.

Once upon a time there was a mom and a child who liked to go for walks together. One day, when they stepped outside, the mom pointed to the sky and said to the child, "Look, can you see the sun up there? It looks so good and warm." The child was amazed and asked, "What is it for?" The mom said, "It is very valuable! It gives us light and warms us. We have to take care of it." The child was very intrigued and asked again, "What should we do to take care of it?" The mom thought for a moment and said, "We can go outside and play in the sun, it will make us feel good. And we can also cut back on things that harm the environment, so the sun will last forever." The child smiled and said, "I love the sun!" The mom smiled too and said, "Me too, sweetheart. We must remember to value the sun always."

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to a place with her mom. The place had many old things to look at. Lucy liked to look at old things. She saw a big, old skeleton. The skeleton was famous because it was very old and from a big animal. Lucy looked at the skeleton very closely. She wanted to see every part of it. She looked at the head, the back, and the legs. She was examining the skeleton. Her mom said, "Good job, Lucy! You are looking at it very well." After looking at the skeleton, Lucy and her mom went home. Lucy told her dad about the big, old skeleton. Her dad was happy that she had fun. Lucy said she wants to see more old things. She wants to be like the people who find old things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk outside and feel the ground beneath her feet. One day, she saw a big hill that was very high. She wanted to climb it and see what was at the top. Lily started to walk up the hill, but it was very steep. She had to be careful not to fall down. As she got higher and higher, she could see more and more of the world around her. The trees looked very small and the houses looked like tiny toys. Finally, Lily reached the top of the hill. She was so happy! She could see everything from up there. She felt like she was on top of the world. After a while, she started to walk back down the hill. She was tired but very proud of herself for climbing so high.

John had his own paint. He was very excited and happy to show it to his mom. He said, "Mommy, I own paint!" His mom replied, "That's great John, let's paint together!" So, they opened the paint and John started to draw with it. After a while, John finished his masterpiece and it looked so beautiful to him. He said to his mom, "Look mommy, I own tight paint!" His mom was surprised and said, "Wow John, that's very impressive. Let's hang it up!" But, before they could hang the painting, John had an accident and the paint got smeared all over the place. His mom tried to console him but John was devastated and sad. The bad ending had been foreshadowed ever since John opened his paint; his mom had warned him several times to be careful and not play around with the paint too much. But, inevitably, he went against his mother's advice and it cost him dearly in the end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, John and Bob. John was sad because he had no one to play with. Suddenly, he heard a sound from the sky above. It was a dove! The dove looked at John and came closer. John was so happy that the dove had come to play. John and Bob started playing together. They had so much fun! But then, John began to worry. How could he keep the dove from flying away and take it home with him? He tried so hard to think of a way, but nothing worked. Just then, the dove came close and said something magical. "My friend, if you give me something special, I can stay and unite with you forever." John and Bob worked together to find something special. They ran around and looked hard until they found a bright blue feather. The dove was so happy! When the feather was placed around her neck, the dove and John were united as one. Together they flew home happy ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a young octopus. He lived in the deep blue sea. He had many friends. They liked to play together. One day, the young octopus went to play with his friends. They played hide and seek. The young octopus was very good at hiding. He seemed to be the best hider of all his friends. The young octopus loved his life in the sea. He was always happy. He and his friends played all day long. And when the sun went down, they all went home to rest. The young octopus was always excited for the next day to come.

Once upon a time there was a grandmother who lived in a small house. Grandmother was very graceful. Every morning, Grandmother would give her granddaughter a file. The file contained pictures of all the most beautiful places in the world. Granddaughter was very excited every time she received the file from Grandmother. One day she asked, "Grandmother, why do you always give me the file?" Grandmother smiled and said, "My dear, I give you the file because I want you to be as graceful as I am. I want you to be able to appreciate all the beautiful places in the world." Granddaughter was so happy to hear this from her beloved grandmother. She ran to her grandmother and hugged her tight. Grandaughter thanked her grandmother for her loving gift. From then on, she always kept the file close to her, so that she could look at it whenever she wanted to.

Once there was a little girl who loved to dress up. She had a box full of colorful and sparkly clothes and every morning she'd get dressed up in them and go out to explore. One day she decided to go to the sea and take a look. Just as she arrived, however, she noticed all the people there were not wearing colorful clothes like she was and they were all looking a bit sad. The little girl turned to her mom and asked, "Why isn't everyone dressing up like me? Is something wrong?" Her mother smiled and said, "No, nothing's wrong. People just don't have as much colorful clothing to wear today, because the sea has been very unkind to them. It hasn't been available to them as much as it usually is, and so they don't have as many clothes available." The little girl then thought about this for a moment, before saying "But that doesn't mean they can't still be happy and dress up in whatever clothes they can find! Everyone should always be allowed to dress up and be happy!" And with that, the little girl ran off to play, wearing all her sparkly clothes and feeling the joy of the sea all around her.

Once upon a time there was an old man who had a funny haircut. He had grey hair that stuck out in all directions and an old straw hat on top. One day, he was walking down the street when he felt something poke his back. He turned around and saw a small boy with a mischievous twinkle in his eye. The old man smiled at the boy and said, "What are you doing, young man? Are you trying to give me a haircut?" The boy giggled and dashed away without saying a word. The old man shook his head and kept walking. He wanted to laugh, but he knew the boy was just having fun.

Tim and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big circle on the grass. It is made of stones. "Let's run around the circle!" Tim says. "OK!" Lily says. They hold hands and run. They run fast and slow. They run inside and outside the circle. They laugh and have fun. They see a dog. The dog is brown and furry. The dog runs to them. He wants to play too. "Hello, dog!" Tim says. He pets the dog. The dog licks his face. "Can we keep him?" Lily asks. "I don't know," Tim says. "Maybe we can ask his owner." They look around. They see a man. The man is holding a leash. The leash is for the dog. "Is this your dog?" Tim asks the man. "Yes, he is. His name is Spot. He likes to run and play," the man says. "He is a nice dog. We like him," Lily says. "I'm glad you do. He likes you too. Do you want to play with him for a while?" the man asks. "Yes, please!" Tim and Lily say. They play with Spot and the man. They run and throw a ball. They make a new friend. They are very glad.

One day, a boy named Tim found an unusual tray. It had many colors and shapes on it. He showed it to his mom. "Look, mom! I found a tray!" he said. His mom looked at the tray and said, "That is an unusual tray, Tim. Be careful with it." Tim took the tray to his room and played with it. He put his toys on the tray and carried them around. Tim's friend, Sam, came over to play. Sam saw the tray and wanted to play with it too. But Tim did not want to share. "No, Sam! This is my tray!" he said. Sam got sad and quit playing with Tim. Because Tim did not share the unusual tray, Sam went home. Tim's mom was not happy with him. She took the tray away and told Tim, "You must learn to share." Tim was sad and alone, wishing he had shared the unusual tray with Sam.

Once upon a time there was a young boy called Jack. He lived in a small village and loved to play all day. One day he found a magical sword in the woods. He had heard stories about magical swords and was very excited. He wanted to find out what the sword could do. Jack took the sword home and was about to use it, when a fairy appeared and spoke to him. She said, "Young Jack, this sword is special. It has magical powers and can be used to settle any disagreement." Jack was excited and said, "I will use it for good!" The fairy smiled and said, "Excellent. I will give you a task. Use the sword to settle any disagreements and show people the path of kindness and understanding." Jack said, "I promise!" The fairy was pleased and waved her wand. The sword glowed brightly and the fairy disappeared. From that day forward, Jack used the magical sword to help settle disagreements and spread kindness through the village.

Mommy and Jimmy were walking down a path one night. It was dark, and their shadows were long. Jimmy said, "Mommy, look at my shadow. I want to let it run faster than any other shadow". "Oh no, Jimmy," Mommy said, "It's too dark outside. Let's just take a look at the shadows for now". Jimmy said, "Okay, Mommy. Let's see how our shadows look like." Mommy and Jimmy watched their shadows stretch across the path. They were long and thin like two dark lines in the night. Jimmy said, "Mommy, look, I can make my shadow go on a walk. It's so fun!" Mommy smiled at Jimmy and said, "Let your shadow go on a walk. I'm sure it will have so much fun!" Jimmy smiled and with a little skip and a jump, his shadow went on its way. What fun they had that night!

Once upon a time there was an old lady who lived in a big, white house. She had a big garden with lots of tasty, ripe fruit. One day a small, furry creature came to her door. The old lady said hello and the creature said it was very hungry. The old lady smiled and said, "My name is Grandma, what is yours?" The small creature said, "My name is Toto. Can you please provide me some food?" Grandma said, "Of course I can! Let's pick some of my white pear and fresh apples to share." And so Toto and Grandma enjoyed a feast of white pears and red apples. They had so much fun sharing stories and eating together. Grandma said, "You are always welcome here Toto!" Toto thanked Grandma and promised to come back soon.

One day, two friends were playing together. They were so happy and excited! Then, one of the friends had an idea. She said, "Let's make a song!" The other friend thought it was a great idea. They worked together to make the song. First, they made up some words. Then, they put the words together to make a song. Next, they added some sounds to it. Finally, they practiced it over and over to improve it. When they were finished, they sang the song together. They were so happy with their song! They clapped and cheered when they finished singing. From then on, they sang their song all the time. Every time they sang it, they made it better and better. They always felt so happy when they sang their song. The friends even learned some new words to add to the song. The song was getting better and better every day!

Once upon a time, there was a brown jet. The brown jet could fly very high in the sky. It loved to fly fast and make big loops. One day, the brown jet was flying very fast. It wanted to see how fast it could go. But then, it hit a big cloud. The brown jet started to break. The brown jet was sad. It could not fly anymore. It needed help to fix the break. A kind bird saw the brown jet and wanted to help. The bird found some friends to help fix the brown jet. They all worked together to make the jet better. Soon, the brown jet could fly again. It was so happy and thanked the bird and its friends. From that day on, the brown jet flew with care and always had friends in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was ready to go to the park with his mom. He put on his jacket and shoes, and they walked to the park together. At the park, Tim saw a big tree. He wanted to climb it. But a girl named Sally was there too. She said, "I want to climb the tree first!" Tim and Sally both wanted to climb the tree at the same time. They did not know what to do. Tim's mom had an idea. She said, "I have two tickets for the ice cream truck. Whoever climbs the tree first gets a ticket!" Tim and Sally raced to the top of the tree. It was very cold up there, and they started to shiver. But they both wanted the ticket, so they kept going. In the end, Tim and Sally both reached the top at the same time. They were both so cold from shivering that they decided to share the tickets. They climbed down the tree and got their ice cream. They ate their ice cream together and became friends. From that day on, they always played together at the park.

Jane was so excited. She was getting a new sheet of paper! She had asked her mom for it earlier and was so happy when she got it! Jane held the paper in her hand and couldn't believe how smooth the paper felt. She wondered what she should do with it. Jane asked her mom if she could draw on the paper. Her mom said yes and Jane smiled. She couldn't wait to get started. She quickly grabbed a red crayon and started to draw. Jane was so excited about the paper and was learning how to draw more and more each day. At the end of the day, Jane asked her dad to help her hang up her picture. Her dad said yes and was very proud of the picture Jane had drawn. Jane was delighted. She had created something special with her new paper and was thrilled to show it off. Jane loved her new paper and was happy to have it. She couldn't wait to use it again and show it off to her family. She was so excited!

Molly was a little girl. She was three years old. She was so excited because she was going to drive for the first time. Molly's daddy took her to the park. She got in the car and sat in the driver's seat. Her daddy showed her what buttons to push and how to hold the wheel. Finally, it was time to drive. Molly's daddy let go of the wheel and stood back. Molly drove carefully around the park. She was proud of herself and careful with the car. When she had finished driving, Molly and her daddy went to the baseball field. They had so much fun pitching and catching. Molly's daddy said she was a fair pitcher. She showed that she was a good driver too. Molly had a great day. She was so happy. She drove and pitched, and she did it all very fair.

John and his mom were getting ready for bed. It was a quiet night and everything in the room felt peaceful and calm. John's mom said, "It's time for you to take a bath, John." John had other ideas. He said, "I don't want to bathe. I want to play with my pen". John's mom said, "No, you need to take a bath. It will be fun and then you can play with your pen afterward." John thought about it. He didn't want to take the bath, but he wanted to play with his pen. John and his mom argued back and forth until John's mom finally had an idea. She said, "I have something special to make the bath fun. I'll get it and you can play with it in the tub." John thought about this for a moment. He was curious about what his mother had for him, so he decided to take the bath. John's mom fetched a special toy from the kitchen. She brought it to the bathroom and when John saw it, he was so excited. John and his mom had a great time while they bathed. John played with his special toy and enjoyed the warm, quiet bath. Afterward, John was so happy he didn't even mind playing with his pen.

Once upon a time, there was a mummy and a daddy. They had a little boy called Jack. Every day, mummy and daddy would prepare Jack's breakfast. Today was special. He was getting ready to go to the park. Daddy said to Jack, "Let's go get ready for the park! What do you want to bring?" Jack said he wanted to bring his toy. He had a very special toy - a blue car. Daddy said, "Let's go." Jack, Mummy, and Daddy got ready and went to the park. Jack ran around and explored. He saw a lot of colourful flowers, so he picked some for Mummy. Mummy thanked him with a big hug. Jack and his family spent a peaceful afternoon in the park. Jack played with his toy and ran around and laughed. He felt very happy! When the sun started to set, they prepared to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the sea with his fish friends. One day, they decided to have a race to see who was the fastest. Nemo was very competitive and wanted to win the race. During the race, Nemo had to balance himself so he wouldn't swim too fast or too slow. He wanted to keep up with his friends but not get tired too quickly. As they swam, Nemo saw a big wave coming towards them. He had to quickly balance himself to avoid getting swept away by the wave. In the end, Nemo didn't win the race but he was happy because he had fun swimming with his friends in the sea. He learned that it's not always about winning, but enjoying the journey. Nemo went home that day feeling proud of himself for balancing and swimming in the sea with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a zoo that had been broken. Animals were unhappy and sad. The zookeeper was very ashamed. One day, a big bird flew over the zoo and said, "I can repair this zoo!" Everyone was excited and happy. The zookeeper said, "Please can you help us?". The bird said, "Yes, I can repair your zoo. But you must help me too." The zookeeper asked the bird, "What can I do to help you?". The bird said, "You will see". The zookeeper got some friends to help, and they all worked together to repair the zoo. After some hard work, the zoo was fixed. The bird said, "Thank you for helping me. I was so ashamed - I did not have enough feathers to fly away." Everyone was happy and cheered for the big bird. From that day on, the zoo was always in good shape. Everyone was happy and the animals were safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a smart little girl called Lucy. She loved to explore her garden and she often found special things. Today she found something even more special - a sparkling object. When she picked it up, she went to tell her mom. "Mom, look what I found in the garden," Lucy said, excitedly holding up the shiny thing in her hand. "Oh, that's mine," said her mom. "It's a special necklace. I must have dropped it when I was gardening earlier." Lucy beamed. She was so happy to have found it for her mom. "Thank you for finding this for me," said Mom. "You're so smart and I'm so proud of you." Lucy smiled and gave her Mom a big hug. She would never forget this special moment and the mine she had found in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat butter on her toast every morning. One day, she saw her little brother Max taking the butter from the fridge. Lily felt angry and sad because Max didn't ask for it. She wanted to take it back, but Max was too fast. Later that day, Lily saw Max leaning on her favorite toy. She felt even more angry and sad. She thought Max was guilty of breaking her toy. She wanted to yell at him, but she didn't know how to express her feelings. At dinner time, Lily's mom noticed that something was wrong. Lily told her mom what happened with Max. Her mom listened carefully and told Lily that it's okay to feel angry sometimes, but it's important to talk about our feelings and find a solution together. Lily felt better and decided to forgive Max. They hugged and played together again.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They liked to swing, slide and run. They also liked to talk to the birds and the squirrels. One day, they saw a big, black dog in the park. The dog looked playful. He wagged his tail and ran towards them. Lily and Ben were not afraid. They liked dogs. "Hello, doggy!" Lily said. "What is your name?" The dog did not reply. He jumped on Lily and licked her face. Lily giggled. "Stop, doggy!" Ben said. "You are too rough!" The dog did not reply. He jumped on Ben and licked his face. Ben laughed. "Let's play, doggy!" Lily said. "You can be our friend!" The dog did not reply. He ran away with Lily's shoe in his mouth. Lily and Ben chased him. "Come back, doggy!" Ben said. "That is Lily's shoe!" The dog did not reply. He dropped the shoe and ran to a man. The man was the dog's owner. He was looking for him. "Sorry, kids!" the man said. "This is Rex. He is very playful, but he does not listen well. He likes to take things that are not his." Lily and Ben got the shoe back. They were not angry. They liked Rex. "It's okay, mister!" Lily said. "Rex is fun. Can we play with him again?" The man smiled. He replied, "Sure, kids. You can play with Rex anytime. He likes you too." Lily and Ben were happy. They had a new friend. They played with Rex until it was time to go home. They waved goodbye to Rex and the man. They hoped to see them again.

Alice and her mommy were walking in the park. Alice was so excited to wear her new boots. She had shiny blue laces and were so comfy. As they walked, Alice was getting more and more nervous. When they stopped to look at the ducks, Alice started to shake her boot. Her mommy asked her why she was shaking her boot. Alice shrugged her shoulders. Mommy shook her head and smiled. Alice thought for a moment before replying. She said in a shy voice, "I'm just so excited to wear them and I just want to shake them!" Mommy laughed and said, "It's okay, sweetheart! You can shake your boots if it makes you happy." Alice smiled and hugged her mommy as she started shaking her new boots. She couldn't help but feel happy and adventurous in her new boots.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She was three years old and liked to explore. One day, she was walking around her garden when she noticed a rat scurrying across the grass. She stopped and watched. "Mommy," said Sarah. "Look at the rat!" Mommy looked up. "Yes, I see it!" Sarah and her Mommy followed the rat. It took them to an empty shed in the corner of the garden. The door was open and the rat went inside. Sarah looked at Mommy. "What is the rat doing?" she asked. Mommy smiled. "I think it's looking for a home," she said. Sarah and Mommy watched the rat for a few more moments. Together, they decided to leave the rat alone and go back to the house. Sarah was happy. "We can come back and check to see if the rat is still here," she suggested. Mommy agreed. "Yes, we can keep an eye on it." And so the little girl and her Mommy kept checking the shed until one day, it was gone. The little rat had found a new home!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures. One day, Lily was playing with her toy boat in the bathtub when she saw her dad on the phone. "Dad, what are you doing?" asked Lily. "I'm talking to Uncle Tom. He's coming to visit us tomorrow and we need to pick him up at the port," replied her dad. "What's a port?" asked Lily. "A port is a place where big boats come to load and unload things," explained her dad. The next day, Lily and her dad went to the port to pick up Uncle Tom. As they were waiting, Lily saw a big ship with a deep hull. She wondered what it was carrying. "Look, Dad! That ship is so big and deep. What do you think it's carrying?" asked Lily. "I don't know, Lily. Maybe it's carrying toys like yours," replied her dad. Later that day, when they were playing with Lily's toys, Uncle Tom gave her a surprise. He had brought her a big box of toys from the ship he had just unloaded at the port. Lily was so happy and grateful. She knew that the big ship with the deep hull had brought her new toys to play with.

Mia and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big peanut on the ground. It is brown and shiny. "Look, a peanut!" Mia says. "Can we eat it?" "I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe it is not good. Maybe it is old." They look at the peanut. It is attractive. They want to try it. "Let's spin it," Mia says. "If it lands on the pointy side, we can eat it. If it lands on the round side, we can't." "OK," Ben says. "You spin it first." Mia spins the peanut with her finger. It goes round and round. Mia and Ben watch it. They hope it lands on the pointy side. The peanut stops spinning. It lands on the round side. "Oh, no!" Mia says. "We can't eat it." "That's OK," Ben says. "Maybe we can find something else. Maybe we can find a cookie or a candy." They leave the peanut on the ground. They go to look for something else. They are still friends. They are still hungry.

Once upon a time, there was an alligator who lived in a swamp. The alligator was so bored. He had nothing to do that was fun. One day, the alligator had an idea. He thought he should gather some of his friends from the swamp and have a party. The alligator then found a frog, a turtle, and a crocodile. Together, they started to gather things for their party. They found some fruit and some leaves. All four of them had a great time. They laughed and jumped in the water. Finally, the sun began to set. The alligator thanked his friends for coming and they all said goodbye. Everyone was so happy they had gathered together and had so much fun.

Once upon a time, in a sunny park, there was a little dog named Buddy. Buddy had a big, happy face and a dry, waggy tail. He loved to play and run all day long.
