They see some flowers, some bugs and some birds on the way. They are having fun and feeling brave. But when they reach the top of the hill, they see something that makes them stop. It is a big, scary dog. It has black fur, sharp teeth and loud bark. It looks angry and hungry. It sees Anna and Ben and starts to run towards them. "Anna, Ben, stop! There is a big, scary dog!" Ben shouts. "Ben, Anna, run! We have to go back!" Anna shouts. They turn around and run down the hill as fast as they can. The dog chases them, but they are faster and smarter. They reach their house and slam the door behind them. They are safe and sound. "Anna, Ben, what happened? Why are you so scared?" their mom asks. "Mom, there was a big, scary dog on the hill. It wanted to eat us!" Anna says. "Mom, it was so big and loud. It had black fur and sharp teeth!" Ben says. "Oh, my, that sounds terrifying. I'm glad you are OK. What is the name of the dog?" their mom asks. "We don't know, mom. We didn't stay to ask. We just ran away!" Anna and Ben say. "Well, maybe you should avoid that hill from now on. There are other places to play and explore. You are very adventurous, but you also have to be careful," their mom says. "OK, mom. We will. We love you," Anna and Ben say. They hug their mom and feel better. They are still adventurous, but they also learned a lesson. Sometimes, it is good to stop and think before you do something. And sometimes, it is good to run away from danger.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl named Anna. She was just three years old and loved animals. One day Anna told her mom, "Mama, I want to mail a letter!" But Mama said, "Not now, Anna. Maybe later." So Anna decided to go to the hospital to mail the letter. On the way, she saw many animals, like birds and frogs. Finally, she arrived at the hospital. Anna went to the mailbox in front of the hospital and put her letter inside. She smiled and said, "My letter is mailed!" When Anna came back home, Mama asked, "Did you mail your letter, Anna?" Anna said, "Yes, Mama. I mailed it just fine!" Mama said, "That's great, sweetie! Now let's go and have some ice cream." Anna was so happy. She had mailed her letter and now there was ice cream in store for her!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she decided to create a special dessert for her mom. She picked some cherries from the tree and mixed them with sugar and milk. Her mom was happy and said, "This is delicious, Lily! You are a great chef!" But then, something serious happened. Lily's little brother, Jack, came running into the kitchen and accidentally knocked over the dessert. Lily was very upset and cried, "Oh no! My dessert is ruined!" Her mom tried to comfort her and said, "It's okay, Lily. We can clean it up and make another one tomorrow." But Lily was still sad and didn't want to make another dessert. She went to bed feeling very disappointed that her hard work had been destroyed.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big slide. Lily wants to go first. She runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder. Ben follows her. "Wait for me, Lily!" Ben says. Lily does not wait. She sits on the slide and pushes herself down. She goes very fast. She feels the wind in her hair. She laughs. Ben is sad. He wanted to slide with Lily. He reaches the top of the ladder. He sees Lily's zipper on her jacket. He has an idea. He pokes the zipper with his finger. It makes a noise. "Zzzzzz!" Ben says. Lily hears the noise. She looks up. She sees Ben poking her zipper. She is angry. "Stop it, Ben!" Lily says. "That is my zipper. You are not nice." Ben does not stop. He pokes the zipper again. He thinks it is funny. "Zzzzzz!" Ben says. Lily is very angry. She stands up. She tries to push Ben away. But her jacket is tight. She cannot move her arms. She is stuck. "Help, help!" Lily says. "My jacket is too tight. I cannot move." Ben sees Lily's face. She is scared. He is not funny anymore. He is sorry. "I am sorry, Lily," Ben says. "I will help you." Ben stops poking the zipper. He pulls the zipper down. Lily's jacket is loose. She can move her arms. She is free. "Thank you, Ben," Lily says. "But do not poke my zipper again. It is not nice." "I will not, Lily," Ben says. "I am sorry. Can we be friends?" Lily smiles. She nods. She hugs Ben. "Yes, we can be friends," Lily says. "But you have to wait for me on the slide. Then we can slide together." "Okay, Lily," Ben says. "I will wait for you. Let's go slide together." Lily and Ben hold hands. They walk to the slide. They sit on the slide. They push themselves down. They go very fast. They feel the wind in their hair. They laugh. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a happy girl named Molly. Every Wednesday, Molly went on an adventure with her family. They went to a nearby park, and everyone hopped on their bicycles. Molly was so excited because she loved to ride her bike. Molly and her family rode around the park for what felt like forever. They stopped in big open spaces to have picnics and once, a duck even came to join them! Molly's family laughed and smiled and enjoyed each other's company on the bicycle ride around the park. Finally, when the sun started to set, Molly and her family got back on their bikes and rode back home. Molly and her family were always happy after their Wednesday rides. Molly's family looked forward to their weekly Wednesday adventures, and Molly was always excited when she heard them mention the word 'ride'. They all loved spending time together outside and making happy memories.

Once there was a boy and he was very, very angry. He did not like lunch. He hated it. He scrunched his face up as he looked at the lunch his mom had made for him. He said he didn't want it and he pushed it away. His mom asked why he wouldn't eat it, but he wouldn't answer. He just said he hated it. Then his mom showed him the food she had bought for him at the store. He saw it and smiled. He liked the look of it. His mom put it on the plate and gave it to him. The boy ate his lunch with a big smile on his face. He laughed and said that he loved it now. His mom smiled too, it was a happy moment. The boy was happy to have a lunch he liked. He never said he hated lunch after that.

Lily and Ben were playing with paper and scissors. They wanted to make a big picture of a house with windows and a door. They cut out shapes and colors from the paper. They had a lot of fun. But they needed glue to attach the pieces together. They looked around the room, but they could not find any glue. They asked their mom, but she said she had no glue. They asked their dad, but he said he had no glue. They were sad. Then they saw a bottle on the shelf. It looked like glue. It had a white cap and a red label. They could not read the label, but they thought it was glue. They took the bottle and opened the cap. They squeezed the bottle and a sticky liquid came out. They were happy. They started to attach the paper pieces with the liquid. They made the walls, the roof, the windows and the door. They were proud of their picture. They wanted to show it to their mom and dad. But then they noticed something was wrong. The liquid was not glue. It was honey. It was sweet and sticky and messy. It dripped from the paper and the scissors and their hands. It made everything sticky. They were fearful. They heard their mom and dad coming. They did not want to get in trouble. They tried to hide the picture and the bottle and the scissors. But it was too late. Their mom and dad saw the mess. They were angry. "What did you do?" their mom asked. "We wanted to make a picture of a house. We needed glue. We found this bottle. We thought it was glue. But it was honey. We are sorry." Lily and Ben said. Their mom and dad sighed. They were not happy, but they were not mad. They knew Lily and Ben did not mean to make a mess. They helped them clean up. They explained that honey was not glue. They told them to always ask before using something they did not know. They hugged them and said they loved them. They looked at the picture of the house. It was not perfect, but it was creative. They smiled. They said it was a good try. They hung it on the fridge. Lily and Ben were happy. They learned a lesson. They said they would be more careful next time. They said they loved their mom and dad. They went to play with something else.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty monkey who lived on a small island. Every day, the naughty monkey liked to move around the island. He liked to swing from the trees and splash in the water. He hopped from tree to tree and chased butterflies. One day, he decided to go further away from the island. He moved and moved until he reached a big mountain. He climbed the mountain and as he reached the top, he saw a whole new island. It was big and beautiful and full of new things to explore. Naughty monkey couldn't resist. He moved and jumped until he reached the new island. He was so excited to explore. He explored the new trees and the new water. He had so much fun! The naughty monkey was so happy that he had moved to this new island. He was still naughty, but he was exploring and having so much fun!

A little girl named Jen needed an egg. She was very stubborn and went to the market to get the egg. There were lots of eggs in the market and she tried to pick one. But she couldn't pick one because all of them were too big. She saw an old man and asked him for help. The old man gave her a small egg and said it was just the right size. Happy, Jen thanked the old man and took the egg. She went back home with the egg. When she arrived home she wanted to cook it. But it was too hard and she needed help. She asked her mom for help and her mom said she would help. Her mom took the egg, cracked it open and made some delicious scrambled eggs! Jen was very happy and ate the scrambled eggs with a smile. She thanked her mom again and hugged her. She learned that she just needed to ask for help when she was stuck and not be too stubborn.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who enjoyed creating things. One day, the little girl saw a file on the floor. She was curious and wanted to explore it. She picked up the file and opened it. Inside, she found a blank piece of paper. The little girl got excited and decided to get creative. She grabbed some crayons and set to work. She drew a picture of a big sun, a beautiful tree and some friendly animals. Eventually, she created a magical scene. The little girl felt very calm. She knew that she had made something special. She put the crayons back and took the file with her. The little girl admired her creation and smiled. From that day on, every time she looked at her file, she felt calm. The little girl had created a magical masterpiece!

Jimmy was a young boy. He was only three years old. Every day he would look out of his window at the sea. The sea was always moving and seemed to have a life of its own. He would watch the waves move gently in and out from his window. One day, Jimmy decided to go outside and feel the sea. He walked up to the edge of the shoreline and just stood there. He closed his eyes and held out his hands. He felt the cool sea water rub against his palms. Jimmy opened his eyes again and couldn't believe what he saw. There were lots of small fishes swimming around his hands! He smiled and started to rub them with his fingers. The fishes seemed to love it and kept swimming back towards him. Jimmy was so happy he started to giggle and splash his feet around. He watched the little fishes dart in between his toes and laughed. He could see the smile on their faces and the joy that the sea brought to him. Jimmy stayed in the shallow water for hours and when the sun started to set, he stood up and waved goodbye to his little fish friends. He knew he would be back to play again soon and so he skipped off home.

Mia was grumpy. She did not want to go to class. She wanted to stay at home and play with her toys. She pouted and crossed her arms. "Mia, it's time to go to class. You will learn new things and have fun with your friends," her mom said. "No, no, no! I don't want to go! I want to play!" Mia shouted. Her mom sighed. She knew Mia liked class, but sometimes she was stubborn. She tried to make her smile. "Look, Mia, I have a surprise for you. It's in your backpack. Do you want to see it?" her mom asked. Mia was curious. She loved surprises. She opened her backpack and saw a shiny sticker book. It had stickers of animals, flowers, stars, and hearts. She gasped. "Wow! It's so pretty! Thank you, mom!" Mia said. Her mom smiled. She was glad Mia liked the gift. "You're welcome, sweetie. This is for you to accept your class. You can use the stickers to decorate your notebook, your pencil case, or your drawings. But you have to go to class first, okay?" her mom said. Mia nodded. She felt less grumpy. She wanted to use her stickers. She hugged her mom and said sorry. "I'm sorry, mom. I was grumpy. I will go to class now. I love you," Mia said. "I love you too, Mia. Have a good day at class. I'm proud of you," her mom said. They walked to the car and drove to class. Mia was happy. She couldn't wait to show her stickers to her teacher and her friends. She accepted her class and learned new things and had fun.

Once there was a little girl named Tess. Tess was three years old and loved playing with her friends. One day they decided to play hockey outside. Tess was excited to play and grabbed her stick. As they started playing, Tess noticed that her friends were ignoring her. She didn't understand why and felt very sad. She tried to talk to them, but they just continued to ignore her. Tess felt a bit teary. Fortunately, Tess's mum saw what was happening. She came out of the house, gave Tess a big hug and said, "Don't worry Tess, let's play a mild game of hockey together". Tess smiled, and felt better. She and her mum played together in the mild sunshine and soon Tess's friends were playing with them too. Tess had a wonderful time, and from then on her friends were much nicer.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Sam. One day Sam was very hungry, but all the food was gone. Sam was so sad and started to cry. Then Sam heard a noise outside. It was coming from the trees! He ran outside to have a look and he saw lots of fruit growing all around. The fruit was very yummy, so Sam started to rush around, eating it as fast as he could. Soon Sam found some jars of jam under the trees. He was so happy! He opened a jar and tasted it. It was bitter but he liked it. He kept rushing around and eating the jam until it was all gone. At the end of the day, Sam was very full and a little tired. But he was extremely happy that he had found such yummy jam!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a favorite toy truck that he loved to play with every day. One day, Timmy's truck got stuck in a tree and he couldn't get it down. He tried and tried, but it was too high up. Timmy's friend, Sally, saw him struggling and asked him what was wrong. Timmy explained the situation and Sally had an idea. She said, "I have a ladder at my house. Let's go get it and save your truck!" So, they went to Sally's house and got the ladder. Sally held the ladder while Timmy climbed up and got his truck down. Timmy was so happy and grateful to Sally for helping him save his truck. As a way to say thank you, Timmy offered to trade his dull pencil for Sally's colorful one. Sally agreed and they both went home happy. Timmy learned that it's always good to have friends who can help you when you need it.

Once upon a time there was a powerful knob. He loved to laugh and people would gather around to hear him. Everyone was happy when the powerful knob laughed. One day, the powerful knob's laughing got louder and louder and his laughter echoed across the land. Everyone was worried and the powerful knob just kept on laughing. Suddenly, the powerful knob's laughing was so loud that it shook the ground. Everyone panicked and started running away. But it was too late! The powerful knob's laughter was so powerful that it caused an earthquake. Everything was destroyed and the powerful knob was never heard from again.

Once upon a time there was a fly. She was small and quiet and wanted to explore the world. One day, she had an idea and wanted to share it with everyone. She flew off to the very distant tree to tell everyone her big idea. When she arrived, she saw all the animals gathered around the tree, listening to a big bird. They were all excited about the bird's idea. The fly couldn't believe it and was so angry. She spoke out, "No, my idea is much better!" The animals laughed at her. They all thought her idea was silly and they didn't believe she had anything important to say. The fly was so upset. She became very angry and decided to prove them all wrong by releasing her idea into the air. But her idea was never heard. As soon as it was released, a strong wind blew it away and it was never seen again. The animals all laughed and were happy to have the big bird's idea back in the centre of attention. The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and not put others down. Everyone has the right to express their ideas, even if they don't seem important to others. Showing respect, even if other's ideas seem silly or distant, can result in a much better outcome.

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. Sam has many cars and trucks. He is rich. Ben has only one car. He is not rich. One day, Sam and Ben go to the park. They see a big hill. Sam says, "Let's play on the hill. We can race our cars and trucks down the hill. I will win because I have more cars and trucks than you." Ben says, "OK, let's play. But I can win too. My car is fast and strong. It has a name. Its name is Red." Sam says, "A name? That is silly. Cars and trucks don't have names. They are just toys. I have many toys. I don't need to name them." They go to the top of the hill. They put their cars and trucks on the ground. They say, "Ready, set, go!" They push their cars and trucks down the hill. Sam's cars and trucks go fast. But they also go wild. They bump into each other. They crash and break. They stop before the end of the hill. Ben's car goes fast too. But it also goes straight. It does not bump or crash. It reaches the end of the hill. It is the winner. Ben is happy. He says, "See? Red is the best car. It has a name. It has a friend. It has me." Sam is sad. He says, "Oh no. My cars and trucks are broken. They are not fun anymore. They are just trash." Ben says, "Don't be sad, Sam. You can play with Red. Red can share. Red can be your friend too." Sam says, "Thank you, Ben. Thank you, Red. You are both nice. Can I name one of your trucks?" Ben says, "Sure, Sam. You can name one of my trucks. What do you want to name it?" Sam thinks for a moment. He says, "I want to name it Blue. Blue is a good name. Blue is a good color. Blue is a good friend."

Once upon a time, there was a graceful girl who loved to take showers. Every morning, she would take a shower to prevent being dirty. One day, a funny thing happened when the girl was in the shower. Suddenly, the water stopped flowing! She hurriedly stepped out of the shower, feeling a little bit sad. The girl went outside and saw her neighbour fixing the water pipes. He had prevented the girl from taking a shower! The girl was very kind, so she didn't get angry. Instead, she thanked the neighbour for fixing the water pipes. He was so happy that the girl was so graceful about it. With the water fixed, the girl was able to take her shower again. From that day on, she was always thankful for the water and was always kind to everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to play with his toy cars. He had a red car, a blue car, and a green car. One day, he decided to attach a motor to his red car so it could move by itself. The little boy was very excited to see his red car move all by itself. But he was also very careless and didn't attach the motor properly. Later that day, the little boy was playing with his other cars when he heard a loud noise. He turned around and saw his red car spinning out of control with smoke coming out of it. The motor had come loose and was now broken. The little boy learned that it's important to be careful when attaching things, especially motors. From that day on, he made sure to always double-check his work before playing with his toys.

Once upon a time, there was an old lady. She was very old, like grandma. Everyone called her "elderly". She lived in a small house with a big garden. One day, she went to the market to buy some apples. She asked the seller, "What is the price of these apples?" The seller smiled and said, "They are very cheap, only one dollar." The old lady was happy to hear that and bought some apples. She smiled too and said, "Thank you very much."

Once upon a time, there was a proud river. Every day, it would run and yield lots of water. It was happy with its lot and was grateful for its life. One day, it spotted a brave fish. The river was so impressed that it wanted to help the fish. It quickly made a current so the fish could swim downstream and get to where it wanted to go. The fish was delighted with the river's offer and used the current to move around. Soon it was able to reach its destination. The river was so proud to have helped the fish. From that day onward, it was filled with joy and satisfaction. The end.

One day, mama and her little boy, Jack, were in the kitchen. Mama had her measuring cup in her hand. "Let's measure how much water is in the drain," said Mama. Jack nodded his head. He liked to help Mama. Mama looked around the sink. "We need to use a pot," she said. So Jack went over to the cupboard. He took out a pot and held it up for Mama. Mama smiled. "That's perfect, Jack," she said. Mama poured water into the pot and then used the measuring cup to measure it. Jack watched as she counted the cups. When they were finished, Mama beamed. "Now we're ready," she said. Jack and Mama took the pot of water and carefully poured it into the drain. Jack watched as it disappeared. Mama said, "See Jack, we did it! We measured the water in the drain!"

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Bill and Ben. Bill had a great idea. He wanted to bring something special to show his best friend. He decided to bring a microphone. When Bill and Ben met, Bill showed his friend the microphone and they both smiled. Ben couldn't believe something so special had been brought for him. The boys decided to play a game with the microphone. Ben spoke into the microphone and Bill heard it from far away. They laughed and had so much fun. When it was time for Ben to leave, Bill had one last surprise for him. He brought a delicious treat for his friend. It was a chocolate ice cream cone! Ben was so happy and smiled big. The two boys hugged goodbye and Ben thanked Bill for bringing such fun things for him. They promised to meet again soon.

Molly was walking down the lane when she spotted an old mule. Molly was very curious and walked up to the mule to get closer. "Hi, mule!" She said. The mule blinked but didn't answer. Molly patted the mule and kept talking. "Do you want to come with me? I promise I will take good care of you." The mule still wasn't answering but Molly decided to take the mule home with her. She made sure to keep the mule tidy and clean, and she fed it good food. Every day, Molly would come out and play with the mule. She would brush it, give it treats and talk to it. She loved taking care of the mule and was very proud of it. After a while, Molly's mom noticed how happy Molly was with the mule and told her, "It looks like you have done a really good job taking care of the mule. You have been very tidy and responsible!" Molly beamed with pride and hugged the mule. From that day onwards, Molly and her mule were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there lived a kind-hearted little girl named Abigail. Abigail was thoughtful and kind to everyone she met. One day, Abigail saw a thief trying to steal a money box. Abigail quickly thought of a kind way to stop the thief. She stepped in front of the thief and said, "I can show you a way to get money without stealing!" The thief was suspicious, but he was curious too. Abigail offered to teach him some useful skills so he could earn money honestly. The thief decided to take Abigail's offer, and the two of them spent many hours together. At the end of the week, the thief had learned enough skills to work and make money. The thief thanked Abigail for her kindness and for helping him to succeed. Abigail smiled, proud of what she had done. From then on, Abigail was always there to help anyone in need. Her thoughtfulness always helped others succeed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to climb mountains with her parents. One day, they found a very ugly mountain. It was covered in brown rocks and had no trees or flowers. Lily's parents wanted to climb it, but Lily refused. She said it was too ugly and scary. Her parents tried to convince her, but she wouldn't budge. So they left her with a babysitter and went to climb the mountain without her. Unfortunately, they got lost and never came back. Lily was very sad and missed them a lot. She wished she had gone with them, even if the mountain was ugly. From that day on, Lily never refused to do something her parents wanted to do. She learned that spending time with them was more important than how things looked. She still loved climbing mountains, but she never forgot the lesson she learned from the ugly mountain.

Once upon a time, there was a frightened leopard. He was always afraid of things in the jungle. One day, he decided to pay a visit to his friend, the elephant. As he was walking, he heard a loud noise. He got so scared that he ran away as fast as he could. When he reached the elephant's house, he was relieved. He told the elephant about the noise and the elephant said that he was not in danger. The elephant suggested that they pay a visit to the lion, the king of the jungle. The leopard was very nervous about meeting the lion, but the elephant said that it would be okay. So, the leopard and the elephant went to meet the lion. When they arrived, the lion welcomed them warmly. He said that he appreciated the leopard coming to meet him and gave him a big hug. The leopard was no longer frightened. He had made a new friend and learned that paying a visit to those you are afraid of can be a good thing.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only three years old, but she was very smart. One day, she and her parents went out for a walk in the woods. Once they were in the deep woods they saw a clearing. Lucy imagined it was full of magical herbs that sparkled in the sun. She looked around, and there they were, in all their beauty. Lucy ran to them and asked her parents: "What are these?" Her father smiled and said: "These are magical herbs." He pointed at one of them and said, "This one is called a 'gentle herb'. It has a special power." Lucy was fascinated and she softly touched the gentle herb. She started dreaming about all the magical things the herb could do. Suddenly, she heard her father telling her to come back. They had to go home, but she couldn't forget the gentle herb. She was determined to come back another day.

One day, a young girl named Betty wanted to go explore outside. She put on her shoes, grabbed her favorite teddy bear, and set off to find something exciting. Betty walked and walked until she stumbled upon an unusual stone. It was big, round, and sparkly. She had never seen a stone like this before! She decided to stay with the stone and see what it did. Betty spent the whole day playing with the stone. She threw it in the air, put it in her pocket, and even gave it a hug. Then the sun began to go down and it was time to go home. Betty said goodbye to the stone and ran to her house. From that day on, she always stayed near the unusual stone whenever she went exploring - because it was her special friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her pink belt every day. One day, Lily's mom noticed that the belt was dirty. "Lily, your belt is dirty. Let's rub it clean," said her mom. Lily replied, "But mommy, the dirt is too distant. How will we clean it?" "Don't worry, we can use soap and water," said her mom. Lily and her mom went to the bathroom and rubbed the belt with soap and water. Soon, the belt was clean and shiny again. "Wow, mommy, it looks so pretty now!" exclaimed Lily. From that day on, Lily made sure to take good care of her belt and always kept it clean.

Once there was a helpful monkey who loved to climb trees. Everyday she would reach to the highest branches and grab the juiciest fruit. One day she decided to reach even higher and tried to grab a piece of fruit from the tallest tree. But as she reached, the branch broke and the monkey fell. She was so scared and yelled for help. Then, a little boy walked by and saw the monkey in trouble. The boy was really helpful and said, "Don't worry monkey, I will help you!" He smiled and walked closer to help her. But when the monkey saw him, she started to climb up the tree again. She was scared and didn't want the little boy to help her. The boy stood there looking sad. He wasn't able to help the monkey, which made him really sad. So he just walked away and the monkey stayed in the tree without help.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who liked to play together. Brick was three-years-old and loved to act and dance. One day he came up with a new game. He said to his friend, "Let's jump on the screen and act like superheroes!" His friend was excited and joined in. They jumped around on the screen and laughed. However, when Brick's friend jumped too high, he stepped on the screen and ripped it. The friends stopped playing instantly and knew they had done wrong. Brick thought for a moment and then said to his friend, "Let's be careful. We should be careful when we play so we don't break anything." The two friends learned a valuable lesson that day. They knew to be careful and not get too excited when they play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. They would run and jump and laugh all day long. One day, Lily's friend Sarah was being bossy and telling everyone what to do. Lily didn't like it when Sarah was bossy. Suddenly, Sarah fell down and hurt her shoulder. Lily knew she should stop playing and help her friend. She ran over to Sarah and asked if she was okay. Sarah said her shoulder hurt a lot. Lily knew what to do. She stopped playing and helped Sarah up. She walked her to her mom's house and told her what happened. Sarah's mom took her to the doctor and she got better soon. Lily felt happy that she could help her friend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was so happy and loved to play outside. One day she was out in her garden playing with her toy when she noticed something strange. She saw a little bubble floating in the air. She was curious and decided to pause and take a closer look. The bubble was so beautiful, so she blew on it and made it bigger. Then suddenly the bubble burst and out came a very bitter smell. It made the girl so angry that she started to shout. But then she heard a voice. It said "Don't be angry! Look at the bright side - now you have a chance to make some new bubbles!". The girl stopped and thought about it. She smiled and realised that the voice was right. She started to make more bubbles and soon she was having so much fun that she forgot about the bitter smell.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat in the harbor. The boat was so big that it could carry many things. One day, the boat sailed away from the harbor. It went far and wide on the big blue sea. The sky was dark and the waves were big. Suddenly, a lightning strike hit the boat! The boat shook and the people on it were scared. But the boat did not sink. It kept sailing until it reached a beautiful island. Everyone was happy and they explored the island. They found many treasures and had a great adventure. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a horse named Brownie. Brownie lived in a big house called a stable. The stable was very cozy and warm, and Brownie loved it there. One day, Brownie saw a bird flying in the sky. The bird was very unique because it had bright blue feathers. Brownie had never seen a bird like that before. Suddenly, a big storm came and lightning struck a tree near the stable. Brownie got scared, but he knew he was safe inside. He felt happy to be in his cozy stable, even during a storm.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a loyal dog named Max. One day, Lily was drinking water from a glass when she accidentally knocked it over. Max saw what happened and leaned over to lick up the water before it spilled everywhere. "Thank you, Max!" Lily said happily. Max barked and wagged his tail, happy to help his best friend. From that day on, Lily always made sure to keep her glass on a stable surface so Max wouldn't have to lean over to save the day again.

One day, a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue went to play in the park. They liked to run and laugh. They were very happy. Tim liked to tell jokes to make Sue laugh. But there was a big boy in the park too. His name was Max. Max was ignorant and did not like jokes. He saw Tim and Sue running and laughing. Max did not like that. He wanted them to stop. So Max went to Tim and Sue and told them to stop laughing and running. Tim and Sue did not want to stop. They just wanted to have fun. So Tim told Max a joke to make him laugh. Max did not laugh at first, but then he started to smile. Max learned to like jokes and running too. Now, Tim, Sue, and Max all played together in the park, running and laughing. They were all happy friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a special thing she loved very much. It was a small, dependable toy frog. She took it with her everywhere she went. The frog was green and soft. Sue liked to hug and kiss the frog. One day, Sue and her frog went to the park. They played on the swings and the slide. Sue put her frog down for a moment to play in the sand. But when she looked back, the frog was gone! Sue started to cry. A nice boy named Sam saw her and asked, "Why are you sad?" Sue said, "I lost my frog. It is my favorite thing." Sam said, "Don't worry, I will help you find it." They looked everywhere in the park. At last, they found the frog under a tree. Sue was very happy. She hugged and kissed her frog again. She said to Sam, "Thank you for helping me find my frog." Sam smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you have your frog back." From that day on, Sue and Sam became good friends. And Sue never let her dependable frog out of her sight again.

Sara and Tom were very happy. They were going on vacation with Mom and Dad. They packed their bags and toys. They put on their hats and sunglasses. They got in the car and drove to the airport. "Are we there yet?" Sara asked. "Soon, sweetie," Mom said. "We have to hurry. Our plane leaves in one hour." They parked the car and took their bags. They walked to the big building. There were many people and noises. Sara and Tom held Mom and Dad's hands. They looked for their gate. "Look, there it is!" Dad said. "Gate 12. Come on, let's go." They ran to the gate. They showed their tickets and passports. They got on the plane. They found their seats. They buckled their belts. "Are you excited?" Mom asked. "Yes!" Sara and Tom said. They looked out the window. They saw the sky and the clouds. They smiled. The plane took off. It went higher and higher. Sara and Tom felt funny in their ears. They yawned. They closed their eyes. They fell asleep. They woke up when the plane landed. They got off the plane. They felt the sun and the breeze. They smelled the flowers and the sea. "Wow, it's so beautiful!" Sara said. "It's our vacation!" Tom said. They followed Mom and Dad to the bus. They got on the bus. They drove to the hotel. They checked in. They went to their room. They put their bags and toys. They changed their clothes. They put on their swimsuits and sunscreen. "Let's go to the beach!" Mom said. "Yay!" Sara and Tom said. They ran to the beach. They saw the sand and the water. They saw the waves and the shells. They saw the birds and the boats. They laughed and played. They built a sandcastle. They splashed in the water. They collected some shells. They had fun. They did not see the sign. The sign said "Danger. Jellyfish. Do not swim." They did not see the jellyfish. The jellyfish were pale and soft. They looked like balloons. They floated in the water. They had long tentacles. They stung. Sara and Tom felt a sharp pain. They screamed. They ran to the shore. They had red marks on their legs and arms. They cried. Mom and Dad heard them. They ran to them. They saw the jellyfish. They saw the sign. They were scared and angry. "Oh no, oh no, oh no!" Mom said. "What have you done?" Dad said. They picked up Sara and Tom. They wrapped them in towels. They ran to the hotel. They called a doctor. They waited. The doctor came. He looked at Sara and Tom. He gave them some medicine. He bandaged their wounds. He said they would be okay. He said they had to stay in the room. He said they could not go to the beach. He said they had to go home soon. Sara and Tom felt sad and sorry. They missed the beach. They missed the fun. They had a bad vacation. They learned a lesson. They wished they had seen the sign. They wished they had not seen the jellyfish.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She was 3 years old. One day, Anna came to an old fireplace. She was very excited and said: "I'm ready to snap!" She got on her tippy toes and stretched out her hands. Snap! Anna clapped her hands together and little sparks started to fly out of the fireplace. She laughed as she watched the tiny glimmering lights flutter in the air. Anna felt happy, so she kept clapping her hands. Snap! Another burst of sparks flew from the fireplace. Now many of them were dancing around the room. Anna kept clapping and the room became brighter and brighter with each snap she made. Anna was having so much fun that she didn't want to stop. But soon, she got tired and had to rest. She looked back and smiled. Fireplace was beautiful. Anna had made it all with her little snaps. She was proud and ready for more adventures.

One day there was a jet flying in the sky. It was an unknown vehicle that no one had seen before. Rachel saw the jet and wondered what it was. She asked her Mom, "What is that?" Her Mom said, "It's a jet. It goes very high and fast." Rachel was excited to hear the explanation. Rachel asked another question, "Can I ride in a jet?" Her Mom said, "No, not right now. That is something for when you get a little older." Rachel wanted to ride in the jet, but she knew she had to wait. The jet kept flying in the sky. Rachel watched it until it went so far she could no longer see it. The unknown jet was gone and Rachel sat wondering where it had gone.

George was very excited. Today was his birthday and he knew he was going to receive a present. His mom took him to his room and opened the wide cabinet. Inside, George saw the biggest truck he had ever seen. It was blue with red wheels and it even had buttons to make noises. He was so excited he couldn't believe it. He took the present and went outside to show his friends. They all cheered when they saw it and asked if they could have a turn and play with it. George said they could and they had so much fun playing with the truck. Back inside, George said a big thank you to his mom and gave her a hug. She smiled and said it was all his gift. George was so happy that he received such a special present on his birthday.

Once upon a time there was a small girl who loved to play in the garden. She had a special spade that she liked to use so she could dig in the dirt. One day she decided to use her spade to make a hole. She worked hard until she had a nice clean hole. Suddenly she heard a voice speaking from inside the hole! She was very surprised and asked, "Who is there?" A friendly voice spoke back, "I'm a little boy. Can you help me get out of here?" The girl was so excited. She put down her spade, reached in and pulled the little boy out. He was so happy to be out of the hole. He thanked the girl for helping him. The girl gave the little boy a big hug and asked him, "What was your name?" He smiled and said, "My name is Tom." The girl was so happy that Tom was free and she was sure they would be friends forever. They giggled and ran around the garden together, making memories that they would never forget.

Once upon a time there was a mall. It was a very successful mall, people from all around visited it everyday. One morning, the mall closed its doors to everyone. Everyone was worried about what had happened. The mall owner came forward and said, "I will explain why I closed the mall. We need to fix the roof so that it doesn't leak anymore. That's why I decided to close it." Everyone was so relieved. The owner asked the people to come back in a few days when the renovations were done. Everyone could not wait to get back to shopping in the mall. The owner worked very hard and soon the mall was ready to open again. Everyone was so happy when they saw that the mall was successful again. Everyone kept shopping and having fun everyday. The mall owner was very proud of his work, and he was glad that he had made the mall successful once again.

Little Jamie was playing in the park with his best friend. They were having a great time. Suddenly, their best toy, a swirly toy car, fell out of Jamie's hands and got lost under the playground. His friend didn't think it was fair, and he started to disagree. "It's not fair! You have lots of other toys and I don't have any," he said sadly. Jamie felt guilty for dropping it. He told his friend that he was sorry and offered to buy him a new toy. His friend didn't want all of Jamie's things, so Jamie tried to think of a new solution. He held out his hand to his friend, and said, "Let's go to the shop together and buy a new toy! That way, it will be fair." His friend smiled, and they both agreed. Jamie held his hand and they went to the shop together.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little dog. She had a package filled with special treats. She wanted to open it, but it was too hard. One day, she got so curious she started chewing the package. After some hard work, the package came open. She was so excited to see what was inside. She could smell something delicious! She started to chew on the treats and she loved them. She was so happy she was able to open the package and chew on the goodies inside. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play by the stream. She would skip rocks and chase butterflies all day long. One day, as she was playing, she saw a shiny key on the ground. Excitedly, she picked up the key and went to her mommy. "Mommy, can we find the lock that this key goes to?" she asked. Her mommy smiled and said, "Sure, let's go on an adventure!" They walked along the stream, looking for a lock. Suddenly, they saw a high fence with a locked gate. The key fit perfectly and they were able to unlock the gate. Lily was so happy that they found the lock and she got to use the key. She hugged her mommy and said, "I love going on adventures with you!"

Once upon a time there lived a little pig in a big house. He had a chimney that always made him happy. He would look up at it and sometimes even talk to it. One day, the little pig noticed that the chimney was getting bigger. He watched as it grew and grew until it was tall enough to go all the way up to the sky. The little pig was very excited and started dancing around. Unfortunately, not everyone was happy about the chimney. The farmer who lived in the neighbouring house was getting very angry. He shouted out of his window and complained about how it blocked the sun from entering his house. The little pig was scared by the farmer's anger. He tried to talk to him but the farmer didn't want to listen. So the little pig had to keep living with the chimney, even though it made the farmer so angry.

Once upon a time there was a little girl and her name was Jana. She was three years old, and she lived with her mom and dad. One day Jana wanted to watch her favourite show on the TV. She asked her mom if she could watch it, but her mom told her she had to wait. Jana was patient for a while, but she really wanted to watch her show. She started to get restless and kept asking her mom every few minutes. Finally, her mom said, "OK, you can watch your show, but only for a short while." Jana was delighted and went to the TV. She was so happy that she started to dance around in front of it. She loved her show and it made her laugh, and sometimes it made her mouth water because the food looked so spicy. Meanwhile, Jana's dad was in the kitchen and he heard Jana laugh and dance. He still heard the laughter, but it was getting louder and louder. He said to her mom, "I think Jana is watching too much TV, can you go and urge her to do something else instead." So Jana's mom went to Jana, gave her a hug and urged her to find something else to do. Jana said to her mom, "OK, I'll do something else, but can I still watch my show after?" Her mom replied, "Yes, you can watch it a

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily woke up and was very excited because it was her birthday. She ran to her mom and said, "Today is my day! Can we have cake and balloons?" Her mom said, "Yes, we can have cake and balloons. But first, let's fix your hair." Lily's mom fixed her hair and they went to the store to buy cake and balloons. While they were there, Lily saw her friend Tommy. Tommy said, "Happy birthday, Lily! Are you excited?" Lily said, "Yes, I am very excited. We are going to have cake and balloons!" After they got the cake and balloons, they went back home. Lily's mom fixed the balloons and they sang "Happy Birthday" while Lily blew out the candles. Lily had a great day and was very happy. She said, "Thank you, Mom. Today was the best day ever!"

There was a girl called Beth. She was a pupil in school. She was always very tidy and she often helped tidy her classroom. One day, Beth's teacher was looking for something to praise the class for. Then, the teacher noticed the tidy classroom and said to the pupils, "That's very tidy! Beth, what's your name?" Beth replied with a big smile on her face, "My name is Beth." The teacher said, "Well, Beth. You have done a very good job keeping your classroom tidy. So, I'm giving you a reward. I'm going to give you a puppy!" All of Beth's classmates were so excited to see the puppy that the teacher brought in and Beth was so excited that she hugged the puppy tightly. She named the puppy Tidy, after her efforts to keep her classroom clean. From then on, Beth and Tidy were inseperable. They would play together everyday after school and Beth would be the one to put away all of Tidy's toys, making sure that the room was tidy!

Once upon a time there was a young boy. His name was John and he loved to play. One day, he was playing in his backyard when he bumped his knee. It really hurt! John started to cry and his mum came to help him. She was very kind, and gave John a big hug. That made John feel better, because hugs can heal a broken heart. The next day, John went to the park with his mum. As they walked, they saw a wall that was very high. John was so excited that he wanted to jump and touch it. His mum said, "you can try, but if you hurt yourself again I will have to give you another hug!" John bravely jumped until he could touch the wall. He did it! His mum gave him a tasty treat to celebrate his success. John's knee soon healed, but he will never forget the day he jumped to touch the wall.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny baby who went on a big adventure. He wanted to go on a journey to explore the world and discover something new. The baby brought with him a few of his toys and headed out. Along the way, he saw an ancient garden. He couldn't believe his eyes! He went into the garden and started to gather the things he found there. "These are so exciting!" the baby squeaked. Suddenly, he heard a voice coming from behind him. It was an old, wise owl. "What are you collecting, little one?" the owl asked. The baby was so surprised that he dropped his toys. "I am gathering rocks and sticks," he said, feeling proud. The wise owl smiled. "That is a very special thing you are doing. You will have lots of fun with those things". The baby was so happy and thanked the wise owl before packing his treasures and continuing his journey. As he went along, the baby realised he had learnt something amazing. He had learnt that even the simplest things can be special and ancient!

The little girl was walking around the garden with her big brother. She saw a big brown apple on a tree. She reached up as high as she could to get it but it was too high for her. She asked her brother to get it for her. He smiled and said, "Sure, let's give it a try". He stretched up his arms and picked the apple from the tree. He showed it to the girl and she beamed with joy. The girl said, "Thank you, Big Brother. Now I'm going to call it my special apple". She hugged the apple tightly as she walked back home with her brother. Back home, the girl asked her mum if she could take a bite. Her mum smiled and said, "Yes, of course, sweetheart". The little girl took a juicy, crunchy bite and it tasted delicious. She grinned and said, "Mum, this brown apple is the most yummiest one I've ever tasted!"

The boy was very glad. He was going for a walk by the creek. He had his recorder with him. He was so excited! He stopped in one spot and looked around. He heard the birds chirping in the trees and the water lapping against the creek's banks. He listened to the sounds and then started to record them. He played back the recording to see how it sounded. He couldn't believe how it sounded; it was like he was really there! He recorded some more sounds, and then he decided to walk a little further. He was very glad. As he walked, he recorded the sounds of the creek, the bird's chirps and the rustling of the leaves in the wind. He was so happy, he kept on recording until his recorder ran out of batteries. But even after his recorder ran out of power, he still remembered the wonderful sounds of nature. He was so glad that he got to record it all.

Once upon a time there was a wet tomato. It was red and juicy and looked so lovely in the sun. One day, a bunny came hopping along. She saw the wet tomato and thought, "that looks yummy!" The bunny set down in front of the tomato and started to eat it. Soon, the bunny's tummy was full and happy. She thanked the tomato for the delicious snack and hopped away, her cheeks bright with joy. The tomato was so happy to be eaten! Even if it was wet, it made someone happy. As the sun began setting, the tomato looked up to the sky with a grateful smile.

Adam was excited. His dad had designed a special rocket for him. It was big and colourful and even had flashing lights. He was so excited, he wanted to test it out. "Dad, let me try the rocket!" Adam pleaded. His dad smiled. "Ok, Adam, but be careful. Don't be scared, and come back soon," his dad said. Adam hopped into the rocket and began his journey into the sky. The rocket zoomed higher and higher. But soon Adam started to get scared. He felt so small and the big sky seemed so big! "Dad, I'm scared! Come and get me," he shouted. His dad heard him and rushed to the rocket. He wrapped Adam in a big hug and carried him home. Adam was so relieved to be home, safe in his dad's arms. He hugged his dad tightly and thanked him for designing the rocket. "Thank you, Dad! We can do it again," said Adam. His dad smiled back.

Once upon a time, there was a purple hedge. It was a big hedge that lived in a garden. One night, the moon came out and the hedge started to glow. It looked very pretty! The hedge was happy because it had never glowed before. The little animals in the garden saw the glowing hedge and they were amazed. They all gathered around the hedge and danced. The hedge felt loved and happy. From that day on, the hedge would glow every night and the animals would come and dance with it. The end.

Once upon a time there was a mom and a dad. They had a little boy. Whenever he wanted something he would order it. One day, they wanted to get the little boy an alarm. He was very excited to get the alarm. The alarm was loud, so when it rang it made a noise. The little boy was a bit scared of the sound, but he still liked it. The little boy learned how to use the alarm and he would set it every night before he went to bed. Every morning, when the alarm rang, he would wake up full of excitement. Sometimes, when the alarm was too loud, the little boy would get a bit fearful. But the noise was only for a short time and he wasn't afraid of it for long. The little boy was very happy with his new alarm and he enjoyed using it every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Penny. Penny was very troubled. Everywhere she went she looked sad. One day, Penny went for a walk in the woods. As she walked, she noticed something small and shiny on the ground. It was a penny! She was so excited, she bent down to pick it up. Penny kept walking and found a little bird. The bird had no feathers and it was hungry. The little girl felt so sorry for the bird and so she decided to feed it. She used her penny to buy some special birdseed to feed it. Penny fed the bird until it had eaten all the birdseed. After it had eaten, the bird hopped away and flew into the sky. Penny was so happy that the bird had now flown away to find a new home. She then put the penny in her pocket and started walking back home, feeling much less troubled.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, she found a big sheet in her house. It was clear and shiny. Lily decided to use the sheet to play hide and seek with her friends. She hid under the sheet and waited for her friends to find her. They looked everywhere but they couldn't find her. Lily giggled as she heard her friends calling her name. She was happy that the clear sheet helped her hide so well. Finally, Lily's friends found her under the sheet. They all laughed and played together. Lily was happy that she found the sheet and had so much fun playing with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a bright, happy girl named Kate. She loved to play outside and spin around in circles. Her Mom and Dad said she was very good at it too! Every day, Kate spun in the backyard and tried to go faster and faster. One day, her Mom said it was time for a special test. It was a spinning test! She had to spin until she was clean. Kate was so excited and spun her very best. When she was done, she was all clean. Her Mom was very proud. She said Kate passed the spinning test! Everyone had a big smile, and Kate got a big hug for passing the test. Kate was so happy and spun around the room to celebrate. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her cat, Mittens. One day, Lily got a letter from her grandma. She was so happy and ran to show her mom. "Mommy, look! I got a letter from Grandma!" Lily exclaimed. "That's great, sweetie. Let's read it together," her mom said. But when they opened the envelope, the letter was gone! It had vanished into thin air. "Oh no! What happened to the letter?" Lily asked, feeling hurt. "I don't know, but we can call Grandma and ask her to send another one," her mom suggested. Lily felt much better knowing that she would get another letter from her grandma soon. She hugged her mom and Mittens, happy to have such a loving family.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the morning when the mist was still around. She would run around and laugh, but one day she fell and hurt her knee. It was uncomfortable and she started to cry. Her mom came outside and saw her crying. "What happened, Lily?" she asked. "I fell and my knee hurts," Lily said. Her mom kneeled down and looked at her knee. "It's just a little scrape. Let's clean it up and put a bandage on it," she said. Lily felt better after her mom helped her. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for making me feel better." They continued to play outside in the mist and had a fun day together.

Once upon a time there was a bear, who loved to hug everyone he met. One day when he was out walking in the forest, he saw an amazing view from a tall hill. He went up to see it better and when he got to the top he saw a thin tree. The bear was suddenly filled with a lot of love and with no one to hug, he hugged the tree. As he hugged the tree, he heard a voice. "Why, thank you for the hug. I haven't been hugged in years!" said the tree. The bear was surprised and asked the tree why he hadn't been hugged in such a long time. The tree replied: "When I was small and thin, no one wanted to hug me, they all thought I was too weak. But now that I am strong, here you are hugging me." The bear smiled and hugged the tree even tighter. He thanked the tree for teaching him a moral lesson that day; it doesn't matter how small and thin something is, it can still be loved and hugged.

John was a strong man. He was always loading heavy things up onto his truck. One day, his truck was very full, so full it was difficult to drive. John was determined to get his load to the other side of town. He drove slowly and carefully over the bumpy roads. John had faced many challenges in his life, but the roads were especially harsh. John got to the other side of town safely and unloaded the truck. He had done it! He was proud of his success even though the roads had been so difficult. John said to himself, "I'm going to write this down in my history book. I want everyone to know I was able to get through these harsh roads." John faithfully stuck to his plan and wrote down his success in his history book. He remembered to be proud of himself and his accomplishments.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little monkey who lived in the jungle. He liked to play pranks on the other animals. One day, the naughty little monkey had an idea. He picked up a big stone and threw it over the cliff! He watched with glee as the stone flew through the air and landed far in the distance with a thud. But then, the monkey heard a voice. "Why did you throw that stone?", the voice said. It was the lion. He was angry with the little monkey. "That was naughty!" barked the lion. The naughty little monkey felt scared. He quickly apologised to the lion and promised he would never be naughty again. The lion smiled and said, "Good. Now go play with the other animals and have fun!" And so, the naughty little monkey learned his lesson and happily ran off to play with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside in the park. One day, Spot saw a big bone on the ground. Spot was so happy and ran to get the bone. But when Spot got close to the bone, the ground started to tremble. Spot was scared and ran away. Spot saw his friend, a little bird named Tweety, and told her what happened. Tweety said, "Maybe the ground trembled because there is a big, harsh monster under the ground." Spot was even more scared now. But then, Spot thought about the bone again. He really wanted it. So, he went back to the bone, even though he was trembling with fear. When he got there, he saw that the ground was only shaking because there was a big truck driving by. Spot was relieved and happy to finally have his bone.

Timmy was always so excited for naptime. He ran quickly to his bedroom and began to sort through his stuffed animals. One was a big and fluffy teddy bear and the other was a small and soft puppy. He couldn't decide which one he wanted to cuddle, so he asked his mom. "Mom, which should I pick?" She smiled and said, "That's for you to decide." Timmy looked at both of them and knew the one he wanted. "I'll take the teddy bear!" His mom said, "That's a great choice, honey." After choosing his favorite toy, he noticed something strange. As he held the teddy bear, a small tire rolled out of its tummy. "Mom, what's this?" "That's a surprise," she said. Timmy was so excited to figure out the surprise. He looked at the tire and saw that it fit perfectly onto the teddy bear's foot. "Mom, it fits!" he said. His mom smiled and said, "Yes, it does. Now you can have your own little car." Timmy just stared in amazement at the teddy bear with

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with toy guns. They have two toy guns: one is red and one is blue. They take turns to shoot each other with the toy guns. One day, they go to the park to play. They see a big tree with many birds. They want to shoot the birds with their toy guns. They run to the tree and point their toy guns at the birds. "Bang! Bang!" Tom says, shooting his red toy gun. "I got one!" "Bang! Bang!" Sam says, shooting his blue toy gun. "I got two!" The birds are scared. They fly away from the tree. They make loud noises. Tom and Sam laugh. They think they are very good at shooting. But then, they hear a voice. It is a man. He is angry. He is the owner of the birds. He keeps the birds in a cage near the tree. He lets them out sometimes to fly. "Hey, you two! Stop shooting my birds!" the man says. "They are not toys! They are alive! They are my pets!" Tom and Sam are surprised. They did not know the birds belong to the man. They did not know the birds are alive. They thought they are just fun to shoot. They feel bad. They drop their toy guns. They say sorry to the man. "We are sorry, mister," Tom says. "We did not know. We just wanted to play." "We are sorry, mister," Sam says. "We did not mean to hurt your birds." The man is still angry. But he sees that Tom and Sam are sorry. He sees that they are just kids. He decides to forgive them. "OK, OK," the man says. "But don't do it again. And don't play with toy guns. They are dangerous. They can hurt people and animals. Play with something else. Play with a ball or a kite or a book." Tom and Sam nod. They thank the man. They pick up their toy guns. They decide to give them away. They do not want to play with toy guns anymore. They want to play with something else. Something that does not hurt anyone. Something that is fun and safe.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in the morning. But today, they have to hurry. Mama says they have to go to the park soon. Sara and Ben put their toys in a big box. They run to the kitchen. Mama has a bowl of cereal for them. Sara and Ben like cereal. They sit on the chairs and eat with their spoons. But Sara and Ben are not careful. They spill some cereal on the table and on the floor. Mama is not happy. She says they have to clean up the mess. Sara and Ben say sorry. They get a cloth and wipe the table and the floor. Mama smiles and says they are good twins. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She says they can go to the park now. Sara and Ben are happy. They put on their coats and shoes. They hold Mama's hands and walk to the door. But Sara and Ben see something outside. It is a long, yellow bus. It has many windows and seats. It makes a loud noise. Sara and Ben are curious. They want to see the bus. They let go of Mama's hands and run to the bus. Mama calls them to come back. She says they have to be careful. The bus is not for them. The bus is for big kids who go to school. Sara and Ben stop and look at the bus. They see the big kids get on the bus. They wave to them. The big kids wave back. The bus drives away. Sara and Ben run back to Mama. They say they want to go to school too. They want to ride the bus. Mama laughs and says they are too little. They have to wait until they are bigger. She says they can go to the park now. Sara and Ben nod and smile. They like the park. They hope they will see the bus again. They hold Mama's hands and walk to the park.

Sara was a dancer who loved to shine. She wore a pink dress and pink shoes and danced with joy. She liked to show off her moves and make everyone look at her. One day, she went to a big dance show with other dancers. She wanted to be the best and the brightest. She did not care about the other dancers. She pushed and bumped them to get to the front. She did not say sorry or smile. The other dancers were sad and angry. They did not want to dance with Sara. They moved away from her and left her alone. Sara felt lonely and confused. She did not understand why they did not like her. Then, she saw a little girl in the audience. The girl was wearing a pink dress and pink shoes, just like Sara. But the girl was not happy. She was crying. Sara asked her why she was crying. The girl said that she wanted to be a dancer, but she had hurt her leg and could not dance. She said that she loved to watch the other dancers, but Sara had blocked her view and made them unhappy. Sara felt sorry for the girl. She realized that she had been selfish and rude. She wanted to make the girl happy. She gave her a hug and a smile. She asked the other dancers to join her. She said that she was sorry and that she wanted to share the dance with them. The other dancers forgave her and welcomed her. They danced together in a circle, with Sara and the girl in the middle. They all shone with joy and friendship. The moral of the story is that being a good dancer is not only about being bright and beautiful, but also about being kind and respectful. Sharing and caring make everyone happy.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy went for a walk in the park. She saw a bike with a red pedal. She wanted to try it, so she put her small foot on the pedal and started to ride. The path was rough, but Lucy was brave and kept going. As she rode her bike, she met a boy named Tim. Tim said, "Hi, I like your bike! Can I try it?" Lucy said, "Yes, but be careful. The path is rough." Tim got on the bike and started to ride. He felt the rough path but kept going, just like Lucy. Together, Lucy and Tim rode their bike on the rough path. They went fast and slow, up and down. Then, they discovered a beautiful flower garden. They stopped and looked at the pretty flowers. They smiled and said, "We found a nice place!" They played in the garden and had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a woman named Jane. Jane had a cat named Fluffy. One day, Jane was nervous because Fluffy was missing. She looked everywhere for him. Jane saw a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had Fluffy. Jane was upset that Timmy took Fluffy. Timmy said he was sorry. He did not know that Fluffy was Jane's cat. Jane was nice and decided to forgive Timmy. She knew Timmy did not mean to take Fluffy away. Jane and Timmy became friends. They played with Fluffy together. They all lived happily ever after.

Tom is a fat sheep who lives on a farm. He likes to eat grass and play with his friends. He has a lot of wool on his body, which keeps him warm and soft. One day, a man comes to the farm with a big machine. He wants to cut the wool from the sheep and take it away. Tom is scared of the machine. He does not want to lose his wool. He runs away from the man and hides behind a tree. He sees his friend Lily, a small sheep, who is also hiding. They talk to each other. "Tom, what are we going to do?" Lily asks. "The man will find us and cut our wool." "I don't know, Lily. I wish we could save our wool. It is ours, not his." Tom says. "Maybe we can trick him. Maybe we can make him think we are not sheep." Lily says. "How can we do that?" Tom asks. Lily looks around and sees a pile of hay. She has an idea. "Come on, Tom. Follow me." She says. She leads Tom to the hay and tells him to roll in it. They cover themselves with hay and look like big balls. They stay very still and quiet. The man comes to the tree and looks for the sheep. He does not see them. He only sees the hay. He thinks they ran away. He shrugs and leaves with his machine. Tom and Lily peek out from the hay and smile. They saved their wool. They are happy. They shake off the hay and run back to their friends. They tell them their story and they all laugh. They are proud of Tom and Lily. They are brave sheep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her dolls. One day, Lily's mom told her that they were going to visit her grandma. Lily was so excited because she loved her grandma very much. When they got to her grandma's house, Lily saw a beautiful vase on the table. Her mom told her that it was very fragile and she should be careful around it. Lily promised to be careful and not touch it. Later that day, Lily's grandma recommended that they all go for a walk in the park. Lily loved going for walks so she turned to her mom and asked if they could go. Her mom agreed and they all went for a lovely walk in the park. When they got back to her grandma's house, Lily was very tired and went straight to bed. She dreamed of all the fun she had that day and couldn't wait to visit her grandma again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and go on adventures. One day, Timmy's dad brought home a toy gun for him to play with. Timmy was very excited to play with it. "Can I test it out?" Timmy asked his dad. "Sure, but be careful," his dad replied. Timmy aimed the gun at a target and pulled the trigger. It was harder than he thought it would be to shoot the gun. He tried again and again until he finally hit the target. "I did it!" Timmy exclaimed. "That was a hard shot," his dad said, proud of his son. From that day on, Timmy practiced shooting his toy gun every day until he became a great shot. He even started to pretend he was a cowboy in the Wild West, shooting at bad guys and saving the day. Timmy knew that with practice, he could do anything he set his mind to.

Once upon a time there was an old tree. She was tall and strong, with many branches and leaves. She had been growing in the same place for as long as anyone could remember, and everyone thought she made the world look nicer. One day, a man came by with a saw. He wanted to cut down the old tree, and make some furniture with it. The tree was very scared! "Please don't cut me down" pleaded the tree, "I won't be able to stand up again". The man thought about it, then said "I can't do that - I'll have to use screws to put you back together". The tree felt relieved, and thanked the man. The man worked hard. He cut the tree into small pieces, then put it back together using screws. Even though the tree had a lot of bumps and scrapes from the saw, she was proud to stand up straight again. As the man worked, a lazy bird watched from a nearby branch. The bird asked why the man was taking so long. The man replied: "I'm making sure everything is secure. That tree has been standing for a very long time, and I want to make sure she stands for many years to come." The tree felt proud, and the bird flew away. From that day onwards, the tree stood tall, proud and strong.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. She loved to play in her hut. Every day, Emma would wake up, excited to explore her hut. She would clap her hands together with joy and laughter when she noticed how tidy it was. One day, Emma had made a big mess. She hadn't been careful and her hut was untidy. She started to feel sad and wanted to make it clean again. However, cleaning was difficult for her. Fortunately, Emma was clever. She thought of a way to clean her hut! She remembered that her mommy had taught her how to wipe. So, Emma grabbed a cloth and did just that. She wiped and wiped until finally her hut was clean and tidy again. Emma was so proud of her work. She smiled and danced, loving how neat and tidy her hut was. From that day on, she would always cleanup with a little wiping every day. The End.

Once upon a time there was a very shy girl. She always wanted to show her friends something, but was too shy to do it. Then one day, a very nice lady came to visit and she brought a big piece of paper. The girl was so excited that she almost forgot to be shy! The nice lady showed them how to make all sorts of things from the paper. She made a butterfly, a flower, and even a crown. Everyone loved it! The girl was so happy, she wanted to show everyone what she could make. She took the paper and carefully made her own butterfly. Everyone was so impressed and cheered her on. From that day forward, the girl was no longer shy. She loved to show her friends everything she could make with paper!

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy bunny with one ear. She loved her bunny very much. Every day, Lily played with her bunny. She took it with her everywhere. One day, Lily and her bunny went to the park. They played all day. They played in the sand and on the swings. The sun was going down and it was time to go home. But when Lily looked for her bunny, it was not there. She had lost her bunny. Lily was very sad. She looked everywhere for her bunny. She found a dead bug, but she did not find her bunny. Lily's mom saw her looking sad and asked what was wrong. Lily told her mom that she lost her bunny. Her mom hugged her and said they would find it. They went back to the park and found the bunny under a tree. Lily was so happy to have her bunny back. She promised to never lose her bunny with one ear again.

Once upon a time there was a boat. It was a beautiful boat and it was ready to sail! The boat had bright blue and yellow sails. The boat was full of people. One of them was a woman with a big smile. She said to her friends, "Let's go! We are going to make a big loop!" They all cheered with excitement. They started to sail the boat over the blue sea. The wind blew and the boat sped up. Suddenly, something strange happened. One of the passengers got deaf. Everybody was scared. But the woman on the boat said, "Don't worry. I will make a special loop that will make him better!" And so, she sailed the boat around and around in a huge loop. After a few minutes, the man was better and could hear again. They continued their journey and sailed off into the sunset.

Tim and Lily were playing in the yard. They liked to run and jump and chase each other. They saw a big garage near the house. They wondered what was inside. "Let's go see!" Tim said. He ran to the garage door and pulled it open. Lily followed him. Inside the garage, they saw many things. They saw a car, a bike, a ball, a rake, and a box. They wanted to touch everything. "Look, a ball!" Lily said. She picked up the ball and threw it to Tim. Tim caught it and threw it back. "Look, a bike!" Tim said. He got on the bike and tried to pedal. The bike was too big for him and he fell down. Lily laughed. "Look, a box!" Lily said. She opened the box and peeked inside. She saw something furry and brown. She reached out to touch it. Suddenly, the furry thing moved. It made a loud noise. It sprang out of the box and ran to the door. It was a raccoon! Tim and Lily were scared. They screamed and ran after the raccoon. They wanted to get out of the garage. "Help, help!" they shouted. "There is a raccoon in the garage!" Their mom heard them and came to the garage. She saw the raccoon and shooed it away. She hugged Tim and Lily and calmed them down. "It's okay, it's okay," she said. "The raccoon was just looking for food. He won't hurt you. But you shouldn't go into the garage without me. There might be other things that are dangerous or dirty. Do you understand?" Tim and Lily nodded. They said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They decided to play in the yard again. They did not want to see the raccoon again.

Sandra was playing in her garden when she noticed her mom walking down the path. She was feeling anxious as she hadn't done what her mom asked her to do. She was supposed to clean up the toys in the garden. Sandra's mom smiled and said, "What have you been doing here, Sandra?" Sandra felt embarrassed. She didn't want to get in trouble. She looked down and said, "Sorry, Mom. I forgot to clean up my toys." Her mom was understanding and said, "That's okay. Let's go and clean them up together. Come on." Sandra was relieved. She smiled and said, "Yes, Mom!" They went to the garden and started picking up the toys. Sandra was happy and excited to have her mom help her, and soon the garden was neat and tidy. She was no longer anxious!

Anna and Ben were going to the zoo with their mom. They were very happy and excited. They wanted to see the lions, the monkeys, and the penguins. Mom gave them each a ticket and said, "You can choose one animal to feed. Which one do you want?" Anna thought for a moment and said, "I want to feed the penguins. They are so cute and funny. They slide on the ice and swim in the water." Ben said, "I want to feed the monkeys. They are so smart and playful. They swing on the vines and make funny noises." Mom said, "OK, let's go then. But first, we have to wait in line. There are many people who want to go to the zoo today." Anna and Ben were restless. They did not like to wait. They looked around and saw many things. They saw a big sign with the zoo map. They saw a man selling balloons and popcorn. They saw a girl with a face painting of a tiger. They saw a boy with a hat that looked like a zebra. They said to mom, "Mom, can we have a balloon? Can we have popcorn? Can we have a face painting? Can we have a hat?" Mom said, "No, not now. We have to save our money for the animal food. And we have to stay in line. It's almost our turn. Be patient, please." Anna and Ben sighed. They wanted to have fun. They wanted to feed the animals. They hoped the line would move faster. They held their tickets tightly and waited.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and her toys. One day, her mommy asked her to help move some furniture around in the living room. Lily was happy to help and started to push the sofa. As she was pushing, her mommy said, "Lily, can you jog over to the other side and push from there?" Lily nodded and jogged over to the other side of the sofa. She pushed and pushed until the sofa was in the right spot. After they finished moving the furniture, Lily's mommy went to the kitchen to make some tea. While she was gone, Lily climbed up on the sofa to play with her dolls. Suddenly, the sofa tipped over and fell on top of Lily. She was hurt very badly and had to go to the hospital. Lily's mommy was very sad and wished she had been there to stop the accident. From that day on, she promised to always watch over Lily and keep her safe.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big yellow ball in the park. It was shiny and bouncy and fun. They took turns throwing and catching it. "Let's play catch with the ball!" Tom said. "OK, but be careful. Don't throw it too hard or too far," Lily said. Tom nodded and threw the ball to Lily. She caught it with both hands and smiled.
