Next time, let me help you with the avocado, okay?" mom says. "Okay, mom. Can I still eat it?" Sara says. "Of course, you can. Let's go home and make some guacamole. Do you know what that is?" mom says. "No, what is it?" Sara says. "It's a yummy dip made with avocados, tomatoes, onions and lime. You can eat it with chips or bread. Do you want to try it?" mom says. "Yes, I do. That sounds good. Let's go home, mom," Sara says. They pack their things and leave the park. Sara holds mom's hand. She still has the avocado in her sack. She is excited to try the guacamole. She thinks avocados are hard but tasty. She likes them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and sing songs. One day, she found a trumpet in her toy box. She picked it up and blew into it, making a loud sound. Suddenly, her cat jumped up and ran away. Lily felt a little fearful because she didn't want to scare her cat. She put the trumpet down and went to find her cat. When she found her cat, she said, "Don't be afraid, kitty. I won't play the trumpet anymore if it scares you." Her cat meowed and rubbed against her leg. Lily felt happy that her cat was okay. From that day on, Lily would sometimes pick up the trumpet and stand in front of the mirror, pretending to play it. But she always made sure her cat was in another room so she wouldn't scare her again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She had the most reliable toy car in the world. One day, she decided to take it for a drive. She drove and drove until she saw a big blueberry bush. She knew she wanted to eat the blueberries, so she parked her car and went closer to have a look. Suddenly, something amazing happened. Hundreds of little blueberries were ripe, just waiting to be picked. She was so excited that she filled her pockets with the blueberries before getting back in her car and driving away. The girl was so happy with her reliable toy car for taking her to the special blueberry bush!

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was very restless. She wanted to do something fun! One day she thought of a game. She stood up and twisted her body and arms around. She smiled as she spun round and round. She decided to twist even faster and went faster and faster, twirling around like a spinning top. Then, in a big twist, she fell to the floor. She giggled and then got back up onto her feet. Once again she twisted her body around and around, laughing and playing in a spinning, twirling game. She loved playing and twisting that way, so much that even when it was time to go to bed, she wanted to go on playing her twisting game. So her mom and dad agreed that before bed she could do one last big twist. Then she finally was ready to go to bed, still with a big smile on her face from all her spinning and twirling.

Lily and Ben went on a safari with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, zebras, and giraffes. Lily liked the giraffes best. They had long necks and spots. Ben liked the lions best. They had big teeth and roars. One day, they saw a huge elephant. It had a long nose and big ears. Lily and Ben wanted to touch it. Mom and Dad said no. They said the elephant was wild and could hurt them. But Lily and Ben did not listen. They sneaked out of the car and ran to the elephant. The elephant saw them and was angry. It swung its long nose and hit the car. Mom and Dad were scared. They shouted at Lily and Ben to come back. Lily and Ben were scared too. They ran back to the car. But the elephant was faster. It reached out its long nose and pinched Ben's leg. Ben cried out. It hurt a lot. Mom and Dad hugged Lily and Ben and said sorry. They said they should have listened to them. They said the elephant was not a toy. They said they loved them and wanted them to be safe. Lily and Ben said sorry too. They said they were sorry for not listening. They said they loved them and wanted to see more animals. Mom and Dad smiled and said okay. They said they would see more animals, but from a safe distance. They said they would never forget the huge elephant that pinched Ben's leg.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to do something. She wanted to do a task. So, she asked her mom if she could do it. Her mom said "Yes, you can do the task". The little girl was so excited. She put on her shoes and got ready. She was ready to do the task. First, she had to find some old clothes and put them in a bag. She searched the room and found some old clothes. She put them in the bag and then she was ready to go. Next, she went to the park. She found a big box and put all the old clothes inside. Then, she was done and the task was complete. She smiled, so happy that she did the task. The little girl was very proud of herself. She had done a big task and was ready for the next one.

Once upon a time, two friends, Tony and Lucy, were walking in a dark forest. Tony was scared. He held tight to Lucy's hand. Suddenly, a ghost appeared! He had a light in his hand. Tony was scared! He screamed and hid behind Lucy, shaking. Lucy was brave. She stepped forward and offered the ghost a smile. The ghost smiled back. He offered them a light to see the way home. Tony and Lucy thanked him, gratefully. They took the light and followed it out of the dark forest. They both felt happy and safe, knowing that the ghost had helped them find their way home. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Jack. Jack had a big lawn in front of his house. He loved to play with his dog on the lawn. One day, Jack saw that his dog's toy was broken. He needed a new one to play with. Jack went to the store to buy a new toy for his dog. The store had a lot of toys, but Jack wanted one that was flexible. He found a toy that could bend and twist, just like his dog loved. Jack bought the toy and went back home to supply his dog with a new toy. When Jack got home, his dog was very happy to see the new toy. The dog played with it on the lawn and Jack was happy to see his dog having fun. From that day on, Jack made sure to always supply his dog with new toys to play with on the lawn.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Lisa, and she loved to explore. One day, Lisa was walking around in a beautiful garden. She saw flowers, birds, and bugs crawling around. Suddenly, she saw an ugly bug on a palm tree. Lisa wanted to explore the bug, so she went closer. The bug was so small that Lisa had to lift her head to see it. "Hi there, little bug!" she said. But the bug didn't answer. Lisa decided to use her finger to lift the bug off the palm tree. She was so curious to explore him. She wanted to find out what the ugly bug was up to. Suddenly, the bug spoke. "Hello there! What are you doing?" He asked Lisa in an excited voice. Lisa smiled and said, "I'm exploring! What are you doing?" The bug replied, "I'm just flying around and looking for food!" Lisa was so happy that she could talk to the bug. She said her goodbye and watched as he flew away. She learned that even ugly bugs can be interesting. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a small, persistent ant. The ant wanted to own a big mountain. The ant knew it was a big job, but he was not scared. He was ready to work hard. Every day, the ant would climb up the mountain. He would take little rocks and dirt with him. He was very slow, but he did not give up. He kept going up and down, up and down, every day. After many days, the ant had moved a lot of rocks and dirt. The other bugs saw how hard he worked. They started to help the ant. Together, they moved more and more rocks and dirt. Finally, the ant owned the mountain. He was very happy and proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside. One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. At the park, he saw a big pile of sand. Tim was very happy and wanted to play with the sand. Tim started to build a big sand castle. He used his hands and a small shovel. As he was playing, Tim felt something different. The sand was icy and cold. Tim was surprised because it was a sunny day. Tim called his mom to show her the icy sand. His mom realized that there was ice under the sand. She told Tim that it was ice from the cold night before. Tim thought it was funny to find icy sand at the park. He laughed and continued to play, making a big icy sand castle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sophie. Sophie liked to run. Every day she would go for a big run in her village. One day, she went for a run and came upon a big building. It was a library. Sophie had never seen a library before and she was so glad. She ran right in. Inside the library, Sophie found lots of interesting things. She found books and games and puzzles. She was so happy! "Oh!" Sophie said. "What a fun place!" Suddenly, an old man in the library smiled at her and said "Would you like to borrow some books today, Sophie?" Sophie was so grateful. She took three books home. She was so happy and couldn't wait to read them. The next day she went for a run, but this time, instead of going to the library, she went to the park and played with her friends. She was so glad she had found the library and was grateful she had something new to do.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play and read books. One day, they go to the library with their mom. The library has many books and toys. Lily and Ben are happy. They see a big book with pictures of animals. They want to read it. But the book is too high for them. They try to reach it, but they cannot. They ask their mom for help, but she is busy talking to the librarian. "Who can help us?" Lily asks. "Maybe we can ask someone else," Ben says. They look around and see a girl with glasses and a ponytail. She is reading a book on a chair. She looks kind and smart. "Excuse me, can you help us?" Lily says. The girl looks at them and smiles. She puts down her book and walks to them. "Sure, what do you need?" she says. "We want to read that book, but it is too high for us. Can you get it for us, please?" Ben says. The girl nods and reaches for the book. She takes it down and gives it to Lily and Ben. "Here you go. This is a nice book. I like animals, too. What are your names?" she says. "I'm Lily and this is Ben. Thank you for helping us. You are very kind. What is your name?" Lily says. "I'm Mia. You're welcome. Do you want to read the book with me? We can share it," Mia says. Lily and Ben nod. They follow Mia to her chair. They sit together and open the book. They see many pictures of animals and learn their names and sounds. They have fun and make a new friend. They are happy.

Once upon a time, a little girl had a big dream. She wanted to be strong and tough like her big brother. But it was always so hard to be like him! One day, she got an idea. She would eat broccoli! She knew that broccoli would make her tough like her big brother. Every day, she ate broccoli. At first, it tasted yucky, but the more she ate, the better she felt. She even started to like it! Her dream was coming true. With every bite of broccoli, she got a little bit tougher and stronger. Soon, she felt like she could do anything, just like her big brother. The little girl was so happy to have reached her dream. And she kept eating broccoli every day!

Once upon a time, there was a rich man named Tom. Tom had a big house and many toys. One day, Tom saw a little bird in a small jail. The bird was sad and wanted to fly. Tom said, "Little bird, I will help you." Tom went to the jail and used his hands to lift the door. The bird was free and happy. The bird said, "Thank you, Tom!" From that day, Tom and the little bird were best friends. They played together every day. Tom learned that helping others made him happier than his big house and many toys.

Tommy loved his bicycle. It was red and shiny and had a bell. He liked to ride it around the park with his friends. One day, he saw a new bicycle in the park. It was enormous. It had big wheels and a basket and a horn. Tommy wanted to try it. He went to the boy who owned the bicycle. "Can I ride your bicycle?" he asked. The boy shook his head. "No, this is my bicycle. Go away." Tommy felt sad and angry. He wanted to ride the enormous bicycle. He thought of a plan. He waited until the boy was not looking. Then he ran to the bicycle and jumped on it. He pushed the horn and it made a loud noise. "Hey, that's my bicycle!" the boy shouted. He ran after Tommy. Tommy pedaled fast. He felt happy and excited. He rode the bicycle around the park. He did not see the hole in the ground. He hit the hole and fell off the bicycle. He scraped his knee and his elbow. He cried. The boy caught up with him. He took his bicycle back. He looked at Tommy. He saw his tears and his scrapes. He felt sorry for him. "Are you okay?" he asked. Tommy nodded. He felt sorry too. He had been mean and selfish. He had taken the boy's bicycle without asking. "I'm sorry," he said. "I should not have taken your bicycle. It was wrong." The boy smiled. He had an idea. He held out his hand. "It's okay," he said. "Do you want to be friends?" Tommy smiled too. He took his hand. "Yes, please," he said. The boy helped Tommy up. He gave him a band-aid for his knee and his elbow. He let him ride his bicycle for a little while. They shared the horn and the basket. They had fun. Tommy learned a lesson. He learned to ask before he took something. He learned to be kind and share. He learned to make a new friend. He was happy.

Jim was a 3 year old boy. He liked to count numbers and take his time. Every day Jim went to the park with his fan. He liked the fan for it kept him cool in the warm sun. One day, Jim went to the park and decided to count slowly to 10. He slowly counted and when he reached 10, he was very proud. He waved his fan and looked around the park. He saw birds flying slowly from tree to tree. He watched as the leaves fell from the trees slowly. Jim was happy as he slowed counted from 10 to 15 and waved his fan. He looked at the clouds slowly moving in the sky. Then he counted to 20 and began to laugh. He laughed and waved his fan until it was time to go home. Jim smiled. He had a good day and had enjoyed counting those slow numbers.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Millie. Millie loved playing outside in the sun, and she often went to the beach to explore the shore. Today, Millie went to the beach to look around. She was so excited that she wanted to take a big dive into the ocean. But when she looked down into the water, it looked so quiet. Millie was scared of the deep water, so she held her hands tight and couldn't move. Suddenly, she saw her mom coming. "Why don't you go for a dive?" her mom said. Millie shook her head, scared of what might happen. "Come on sweetheart," her mom said. "It's ok to be scared, but you can try it. I'll be watching you." Millie thought about it and slowly stepped into the water. She felt the warm water on her feet, but she was still frightened. She took a deep breath, then shouted, "I'm going for a dive!" She gathered all her courage and jumped into the deep water. She felt scared at first, but soon the fear was replaced by a feeling of joy. Millie was so happy that she had been brave enough to go for a dive. She floated in the water and waved her hands in the air. The sun was setting and the beach had become quiet. Millie knew that it was time to go home, but she was

Once upon a time there was a little boy who loved to play. Every day he wanted to have fun. One day, he was enjoying some delicious ice cream when he realized he didn't have much time left to play. He quickly said goodbye to his friends and ran home. When he reached his house, he was surprised to find his mother waiting for him. "Where have you been?" She asked. The little boy explained that he was having fun with his friends. His mother smiled and told him to enjoy his playtime but also remember to come home when the sun went down. The little boy agreed and promised to be on time. As he left the house, he realized how important time was and how quickly it flew by. Even though he was sad to leave his friends, he was happy he could spend time with them. From that day on, he always kept track of the time and made sure to obey his mom. He also remembered to enjoy his playtime and all the delicious treats it brought.

Lily and Ben were playing hide and seek in the park. Lily was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then looked for Ben. She saw a big tree with a hole in it. She thought Ben might be hiding there. She ran to the tree and peeked inside the hole. It was very dark and she could not see anything. She heard a small voice say, "Boo!" Lily jumped back and screamed. She saw Ben come out of the hole, laughing. He had a flashlight in his hand. "Ben, you scared me!" Lily said. "Why did you hide in the dark hole?" Ben smiled and said, "I wanted to find a good hiding spot. The dark hole was perfect. No one can see me there." Lily frowned and said, "But it is not fun to hide in the dark. It is scary and cold. And you can't see anything." Ben shrugged and said, "I don't mind the dark. I have my flashlight. And I can see you when you come close." Lily shook her head and said, "I don't like the dark. It makes me feel alone and sad. And I can't see your face." Ben looked at Lily and saw that she was upset. He felt sorry for scaring her. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to make you feel bad. Do you want me to explain why I like the dark?" Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. Explain to me why you like the dark." Ben took Lily's hand and said, "Come, I'll show you." He led her to the hole and turned on his flashlight. He said, "Look, the dark is not so bad. It is like a secret place where you can imagine anything. You can pretend you are in a cave, or a spaceship, or a castle. You can make up stories and have fun." Lily looked at the hole and saw that it was not so scary with the flashlight. She saw some rocks, some leaves, and some bugs. She said, "I see. The dark is like a game. You can use your flashlight to make shapes and shadows." Ben nodded and said, "Yes, exactly. The dark is like a game. And you can play with me. We can be friends in the dark." Lily smiled and said, "OK, Ben. I'll try to play with you in the dark. But can we also play in the light sometimes?" Ben smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. We can play in the light too. We can play hide and seek anywhere. As long as we are together." Lily hugged Ben and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. You explained to me why you like the dark. And you made me feel better." Ben hugged Lily and said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are a good friend too. You listened to me and you gave me a chance. And you made me happy." They both laughed and said, "Let's play again!" They ran out of the hole and looked for a new hiding spot. They played until it was time to go home. They had fun in the dark and in the light. They were happy.

There was once a girl who had a special memory. She loved it dearly, but one day she had to sell it. At first she was sad, but she knew it was the right thing to do. She asked for a good price and the buyer agreed. The buyer was happy and gave the girl a lot of money. But the girl felt a bitter feeling inside her. She had made the right decision, but now her special memory was gone forever. The girl learned that sometimes even when we make the right decision, it can still feel a bit sad.

Once upon a time, there was a wise cat named Tom. Tom loved to play with his toy laser. Every day, he would wait for his owner to play with him. One day, Tom saw the red laser on the wall. He jumped and tried to catch it. He ran around the room, trying to catch the red dot. Tom was having so much fun. In the end, Tom was tired from playing. He curled up on his bed and went to sleep. He dreamed of playing with his laser again. And Tom and his owner lived happily ever after.

Sara liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She liked to stir the pot, pour the milk, and taste the food. But she did not like to share her tools with her little brother, Ben. Ben was too small and too messy. He always wanted to do what Sara did, but he did not know how. One day, mom was making a cake for dad's birthday. She asked Sara and Ben to help her. Sara was happy, but Ben was happier. He wanted to crack the eggs, sift the flour, and measure the sugar. Sara did not want him to touch anything. She was bossy and said, "No, Ben, you can't do that. You will drop everything and make a mess. Go away and play with your toys." Ben was sad and angry. He did not want to play with his toys. He wanted to help mom and Sara. He waited until Sara was not looking, and then he grabbed the big jar of sugar from the counter. He tried to lift it, but it was too heavy for him. He lost his balance and dropped the jar on the floor. The jar broke and the sugar spilled everywhere. Ben started to cry. Mom and Sara heard the noise and ran to see what happened. They saw Ben sitting on the floor, surrounded by sugar and glass. Mom was worried and said, "Oh, Ben, are you okay? Did you hurt yourself?" She picked him up and checked him for cuts. Sara was angry and said, "Look what you did, Ben! You ruined the cake and the kitchen! You are so bad and stupid!" Mom scolded Sara and said, "Sara, that's not nice. Ben is your brother and he wanted to help. He made a mistake, but he did not mean to. You should not be so bossy and mean to him. You should share and be kind. How would you feel if he said those things to you?" Sara felt ashamed and sorry. She realized that she was wrong and that she hurt Ben's feelings. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was mean to you. I didn't mean to. I love you and I want to help you. Can you forgive me?" She hugged him and gave him a kiss. Ben smiled and said, "I forgive you, Sara. I love you too. I'm sorry I dropped the sugar. I wanted to help you. Can we still make the cake?" Mom smiled and said, "Of course we can, sweeties. We can clean up the mess and start over. We have more sugar and more eggs. We can work together and make a beautiful cake for dad. He will be so happy and proud of you." Sara and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We can do it. We are a team." They helped mom clean up the sugar and the glass. Then they helped her make the cake. They had fun and learned a lot. They were not bossy or messy anymore. They were happy and helpful. They made a delicious cake for dad. Dad was happy and proud of them. He hugged them and thanked them. He said, "You are the best kids in the world. I love you so much." They said, "We love you too, dad. Happy birthday." They ate the cake and celebrated. They were a happy family.

A little girl was walking through the park, when she saw an egg on the ground. She wanted to pick it up. Suddenly, she heard a voice. "Hey! Don't break it!" said a friendly voice. The little girl looked up, and saw an old man. He was smiling at her. "What will happen if I break it?" the little girl asked. "It won't be normal anymore," the old man said. "It will never start again. It's best to keep things normal." The little girl thought about what the old man said, and decided to leave the egg alone. She was happy, because she knew that she had done the right thing. The moral of this story is that it's important to keep things normal. Sometimes, when things look broken, it's best just to leave them be.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who loved to hop and play. One day, he saw a pretty flower and he wanted to draw it. He ran to get his ink and paper but he was too impatient to wait for the ink to dry. He accidentally smudged the ink and got sad. But then, he saw a butterfly spring from flower to flower. The bunny got excited and started to hop after the butterfly. He forgot about the ink and started to have fun. When he got back to his drawing, he realized that the smudge actually made the flower look even prettier. The bunny was happy and proud of his drawing. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go to the zoo and see all the animals. One day, she went to the zoo with her mom and dad. At the zoo, Lily saw a bossy monkey who was trying to take all the bananas for himself. Lily didn't like the way the monkey was acting, so she told her mom and dad. They explained to her that it's not nice to be bossy and that everyone should share. Later, Lily saw a sign that said "Please value the animals and their habitats." She asked her mom what it meant and her mom explained that it's important to take care of the animals and their homes. As they were leaving the zoo, Lily said goodbye to all the animals and promised to always value and take care of them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the sun. One day, Lily saw a lizard on the ground. The lizard was green and had a long tail. Lily wanted to say hello to the lizard, but she was scared it might hurt her. Lily went to get a cup of water to drink. She was thirsty because playing outside made her hot. When she came back to the lizard, she saw that it was still there. Lily poured some water on the ground next to the lizard. The lizard drank the water and looked happy. Lily realized that the lizard was not going to hurt her. She got closer and said hello. The lizard looked at her with its big eyes and then ran away. Lily felt happy that she made a new friend.

One day, a cat named Tom saw a big mouse. The mouse had a big piece of cheese. Tom wanted to be friends with the mouse. He said, "Hi, I am Tom. Can I have some cheese too?" The mouse looked at Tom and smiled. The mouse said, "Hi Tom, I am Jerry. Yes, you can have some cheese. But first, let me introduce you to my other friends." Jerry took Tom to meet his friends. There were many animals. There was a dog, a bird, and a rabbit. They all had cheese too. Tom was very happy. Tom and Jerry played with their friends. They all shared the cheese. They ran and jumped. They were all fit and strong. They had a great day together. And that is how Tom and Jerry became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom had a dog named Spot. They loved to play together in the park. One day, while they were playing, Tom saw some waste on the ground. He knew it was important to keep the park clean. Tom said to Spot, "We need to pick up this waste, it's important for the park." Spot barked and wagged his tail. He wanted to help Tom. So, Tom picked up the waste and put it in a bag. Tom decided to lead Spot around the park to find more waste. They found some more and picked it up. After they were done, the park was clean and beautiful. Tom and Spot felt happy and proud. They knew that keeping the park clean was important for everyone.

Once upon a time there was a man who lived in a big city. Every day he would go for walks in the big park near his house. One day he saw something unusual. It was a big box! The man was curious, so he tried to open it. But the box was locked. He looked closer and saw there was a key hole. He smiled. He had a key that he always carried with him. He used his key to unlock the box. When he opened the box, he found a lot of water inside. He had never seen so much water! The man decided to take some of the water home. He filled a bucket and put it in his backpack. The man was very proud. He had unlocked something unusual and now he had some water to drink. He was happy and went home to show his family the special water.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was feeling uncomfortable. She decided to put some perfume on. She sprayed it carefully onto her neck. Soon the room was filled with a lovely smell. She smiled, it made her feel much better. The girl did not know it, but her brother had snuck into the room. He liked the smell of the perfume and wanted some too. He went and found some of his own. He put it on his neck, it smelt strong and he felt uncomfortable. But he liked how the perfume made him smell. He decided to keep wearing it. The girl and her brother were both very happy with their new fragrances. They enjoyed being able to smell nice and smiled, feeling much better than before.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely guard. His job was to add things. He would add lots of different things together, like special stones and coins. One day the guard was feeling lonely. He was tired of always adding things and wanted a friend. So he went walking around, looking for a new friend. He walked for a long time until he came to a big hill. He started to go up the hill and slowly he saw a person walking down. He waved to the person and they waved back. It was a nice surprise! The guard smiled and he went down the hill with his new friend. The guard was happy to have a new friend so he added his new friend to his list of best friends. Now he was even happier because he didn't have to feel so lonely anymore. The guard and his new friend had lots of fun together! They added rocks and sticks on the hill to make a special game. They would add up the numbers on their fingers and try to guess the answers. It was so much fun! The guard and his new friend spent many days together, adding rocks and coins, and playing lots of games. From that day on, the guard was not so lonely anymore. He had a friend he could add things with and he was happy.

One day, Timmy saw a pink door. He wanted to open it, so he ran to the door. But it was closed tight. He was disappointed. So he looked around for something he could use to open it. Timmy found a big rock and picked it up. He was so excited! He went back to the pink door and threw the rock at it. The rock hit the door with a loud bang. Then the door opened! Timmy was very happy. He peered inside the room. Everything was pink. He ran inside the room, and started looking around. He saw a big pink bed, a pink shelf and even a pink chair! Timmy stayed in the pink room for a while. When he was ready to leave, he closed the door and went back home. He was so glad he found the pink door!

Once upon a time, there was a human called Mama. Mama was a lovely human and she would always drink from a special cup. One day, Mama wanted to share her lovely cup with everyone. She gave everyone a cup, so that everyone could enjoy a drink. Everyone was very happy and had a lovely time drinking together. Mama said that when we share a drink, it makes people feel good and happy. She explained that drinking together was a sign of love and friendship. Everyone smiled and felt so pleased that they had taken part in this delightful occasion. Mama's wonderful message was that if people share and help each other, everyone can be happier. That's why it's lovely to share a drink with people you love - because it's a way of saying that they're special and you care.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play with kites. They had many kites of different colors and shapes. One day, they saw a fancy kite in the store. It was big and shiny and had a long tail. They wanted to buy it, but it was too expensive. They asked their mom and dad to buy them the fancy kite, but they said no. They said they already had enough kites and they should be happy with what they had. Tim and Kim were sad and angry. They thought their mom and dad were mean and unfair. The next day, they decided to sneak out of their room and go to the store. They took some money from their piggy bank and ran to the store. They bought the fancy kite and hid it in their backpack. They were very happy and excited. They wanted to fly the fancy kite in the park. But when they got to the park, they saw a big problem. The wind was too strong and the fancy kite was too heavy. They tried to fly the fancy kite, but it kept falling and crashing. They tried to fix it, but it was too hard. They started to cry and regret. Then they saw their mom and dad coming. They had followed them to the park. They were very worried and angry. They scolded Tim and Kim for being dishonest and disobedient. They took the fancy kite and the money and said they would return them to the store. They said they were very disappointed and sad. Tim and Kim felt very sorry and ashamed. They realized they had made a big mistake. They hugged their mom and dad and said they were sorry. They said they learned their lesson. They said they didn't need the fancy kite. They said they loved their mom and dad and their other kites. Their mom and dad forgave them and hugged them back. They said they loved them too and they were proud of them for being sorry. They said they could still play with their other kites, but they had to be careful and respectful. They said they hoped they would be more grateful and happy with what they had. The moral of the story is: Be honest and obedient, and be happy with what you have.

One day, a ball went for a roll in the park. The ball was red and liked to roll very fast. The ball rolled down a big hill and bumped into a poor cat. The cat was sad because it hurt. "Ouch!" said the cat, "Why did you roll into me?" The ball felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, cat. I did not see you. Can I help you feel better?" The cat nodded and they went to find a nurse. They found a nurse near a big tree. The nurse was kind and helped the poor cat. She put a band on the cat's leg. The cat felt better and thanked the nurse. The ball and the cat became friends and played together in the park.

Once there was a young boy named Paul. He always liked to explore his backyard. One day, he saw a package in the corner. It was dry and shiny, so he knew he had to open it. Paul started to blink, he was so excited. He opened the package and found a treasure inside. It was a tiny yellow toy car. Paul was so happy that he started to dance around the garden. He was having so much fun that he kept blinking and twirling around. Finally, he decided to take his car for a spin. He pushed it around the garden until it was time to go inside. Paul was so happy to have the toy car that he kept blinking the rest of the day.

Mum and Dad took Anna to the park. It was a sunny day and there were lots of birds singing. Anna loved it here, and she smiled as she saw her favourite flowers. Suddenly, she spotted a small yellow bird in the tree. It was eating a snack. She wanted one too! Mum reminded Anna that snacks were for when she got home. But Anna didn't like this. She started to feel disappointed. Dad tried to cheer her up. He said he would help her make a snack when they got home. When they got home, Dad found some ingredients in the cupboard. He made a snack of bread and butter. But it tasted bitter. Dad tried again, this time with jam. That was much sweeter and Anna was very happy. Mum smiled and said that the next time they went to the park, she'd remember to take some snacks for Anna!

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. They enjoyed the sun, the grass and the flowers. They also liked to listen to the birds. The birds sang in their ears. It was peaceful. One day, a big dog came to the park. The dog was not nice. It barked and ran after Lily and Ben. Lily and Ben were scared. They tried to run away, but the dog was faster. The dog caught Ben and bit his ear. Ben cried and bled. Lily screamed and ran to help him. A man saw what happened. He ran to the dog and kicked it. The dog let go of Ben and ran away. The man called for help. He took Ben and Lily to the hospital. Ben had to get stitches in his ear. Lily had to get a hug. They were both very sad. They did not enjoy the park anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely bear called Tabby. Tabby had no friends and felt very sad. Every day, Tabby looked out of her chamber wishing she could find some friends to play with. One day, as Tabby was looking out at the forest, she spotted a rabbit. Tabby was so excited and quickly hopped out of her chamber. She raced up to the rabbit and asked if they could be friends. The rabbit didn't like Tabby, so they started to tease her. Tabby felt embarrassed and ran away. She ran through the forest until she couldn't run any further. Tabby hid in a cave and stayed there for a long time. She was so lonely. Tabby missed her chamber and wanted to go home, but she was too scared of seeing the rabbit again. Eventually, Tabby knew she had to face the rabbit. So she bravely returned to her chamber. But the rabbit was still there. Tabby was very scared and the rabbit kept on teasing her. Tabby was so sad and lonely, she never went back out of her chamber again.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Benny. Benny was very humble and always shared his carrots with his friends. One day, Benny met a hedgehog named Spike. Spike was lost and didn't know how to get back home. Benny asked Spike to tell him where he lived, but Spike didn't know. Benny then had an idea and asked Spike to climb on his back so he could show him around. As they walked, Benny asked other animals if they knew where Spike lived. Finally, a wise old owl told them where Spike's home was. Benny was happy he could help his new friend Spike.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they saw a big building with lots of windows. Lily said, "Wow, that building is perfect! I wish we could play in there." Her friend, Johnny, said, "No, we can't go in there. It's not safe. It might burn down." Lily got scared and said, "Oh no! We don't want the building to burn. Let's stay far away." They decided to play in the park instead and had lots of fun on the swings and slides. They were happy they didn't go near the building that could burn.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little town, there lived a kind witch. She had a big hat and a long dress. The witch loved to help people, but some kids were scared of her. They thought she was mean because she looked different. One day, a small girl named Lily lost her toy in a tall tree. She was very sad and cried. The kind witch saw Lily and wanted to help. The witch used her magic to get the toy back. Lily was happy and said thank you to the witch. Lily told the other kids that the witch was nice and not scary. The kids learned that they should not be scared of someone just because they look different. They all became friends with the witch and played together. The moral of the story is to not judge someone by how they look.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a special uniform that he loved to wear. One day, he had an idea. He wanted to display his uniform for everyone to see. But first, he needed to find a hidden place to set up his surprise. Tim looked around his room and found a big box. He thought, "This is the perfect hidden place for my surprise!" Tim put his uniform inside the box and closed it. He couldn't wait to show his friends and family. The next day, Tim invited everyone to his house. They all gathered around the big box, excited to see what was inside. Tim opened the box, and there was his uniform! Everyone clapped and cheered. They knew Tim loved his uniform, and they were happy to see it displayed for them. And that's how Tim shared his special surprise with everyone he loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat rice for dinner every night. One day, she went to the park to play on the swings. While she was swinging, she saw a boy who looked very serious. Lily was curious, so she went to meet the boy. He told her his name was Tom and he was looking for his lost toy. Lily offered to help him find it. They looked under the slide, in the sandbox, and even in the bushes. Finally, they found the toy in the grass. Tom was so happy that he gave Lily a big hug. They became good friends and played together every day at the park. From that day on, Lily knew that sometimes when you meet someone new, it can lead to a wonderful friendship.

Lily likes to write. She has a big box of crayons and many sheets of paper. She writes her name, her mom's name, and her dog's name. She writes big and small, red and blue, happy and sad. One day, Lily wants to write a story. She thinks of a story about a princess and a dragon. She writes the first word: "Once". Then she thinks of the next word. But she does not know how to write it. She tries to remember, but she cannot. She feels angry and sad. She asks her mom for help. "Mom, how do you write 'upon'?" she says. Her mom is busy in the kitchen. She says, "Not now, Lily. I'm making dinner. You can write later." Lily does not like this answer. She says, "But I want to write now! Please, mom, help me!" Her mom sighs and comes to Lily. She sees the sheet of paper with the word "Once". She says, "Lily, this is not how you write 'once'. You forgot the 'e' at the end. And you wrote it backwards. This is a stupid way to write." She takes the crayon from Lily and writes "Once" the right way. Lily feels hurt and angry. She does not like her mom's word. She says, "No, mom, you are stupid! This is my story, and I can write it any way I want!" She snatches the crayon and the sheet of paper from her mom. She tears the paper in half and throws it on the floor. She runs to her room and slams the door. Her mom feels sorry and sad. She did not mean to hurt Lily's feelings. She knows Lily is trying to write. She goes to Lily's room and knocks on the door. She says, "Lily, I'm sorry. I did not mean to call your writing stupid. I was just trying to help you. Can I come in and talk to you?" She waits for Lily to answer. She hopes Lily will forgive her and write again.

Tommy and Mummy were having a lovely day. They went to the park and then stopped off at the bakery for a treat. As they walked back to the car, Tommy noticed a man who was eating a meal on the bench. Tommy looked at the man and then looked up at Mummy. "Is he okay?" he asked. Mummy smiled. "Yes," she said. "He's just very hungry and thought it would be nice to have a meal outside today." The man looked up at Tommy and smiled. He said thank you to Mummy for being so thoughtful. Tommy smiled back and waved at the man. He felt happy that his Mummy was being so kind to the man. Mummy took Tommy's hand and they walked back to the car. Tommy looked back one more time and waved goodbye at the man. The man waved back and smiled. Tommy smiled back and thought of how thoughtful Mummy was.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Luna. Luna was a fit cat who loved to play and run. She lived in a big house with her best friend, a little girl named Mia. One day, Mia and Luna found a can of tuna. They both loved tuna very much. Mia said, "Let's pray that we can open this can and share the tuna together!" So, they both closed their eyes and prayed very hard. When they opened their eyes, they saw that the can was open! Mia and Luna were so happy. They sat down and shared the tasty tuna. From that day on, they always remembered to pray and be thankful for the good things in their lives.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy pipe that he liked to play with. The pipe was very popular with all of his friends, and they all wanted to play with it too. One day, Timmy and his friends were playing at the park when they saw two birds fighting in the sky. They all looked up and saw the birds flying around and making lots of noise. Timmy thought it looked like fun, so he pretended to fight with his friends too. After they finished playing, Timmy went home and showed his mom the pipe. She thought it was a nice toy, but reminded him to be careful with it. Timmy promised to take good care of it and put it away in his toy box. From that day on, Timmy and his friends played with the pipe every day. They never fought over it because they knew they could all have a turn. And whenever they saw birds fighting in the sky, they would pretend to fight too, just like Timmy did that day at the park.

One day, a little girl was out in her garden. She looked up at the sky and saw a white nut. It was so bright and shiny! She wondered where it had come from and what it was. The little girl wanted to touch the nut, so she jumped up and reached out for it. But it was too high in the sky for her to reach. She was disappointed. Suddenly, a magical light appeared in the sky. It lit up the nut and the garden. The girl was amazed! She asked the light what it was and why it had shown up. The light said it was there to show her something special. It said the nut was full of wonderful secrets, waiting to be discovered. The little girl felt excited. She couldn't wait to explore the magical nut! She said a big thank you to the light, and went off to look at the nut up close.

Once there was a boy who wanted to go on an adventure. But he had no way of getting out of the house. Then he remembered he had a key! He was so excited that he called for his mom to help him open the door. But his mom was very stubborn. She said he was too little to go outside. The boy was very sad, but he decided to try the key anyway. He put it in the door and turned it. He was so happy when he heard a click! The door opened and he ran out! He had so many fun adventures! But when it was time to go home he couldn't find the key. He looked and looked but it was gone. Soon his mom came looking for him. He was so glad to see her, he called to her. She opened the door and he was so relieved. It turns out that he had dropped the key in the grass!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved orange things. She especially loved wearing her bright orange dress. One day, she asked her mom where a trip to an orange place could be found. "Oh, I know!" her mom said. "We can go to the orange farm and pick oranges right off the trees!" The little girl was so excited that she jumped up and down with joy. So they packed up their bags and hopped in the car. The little girl couldn't believe her eyes when she saw the orange trees! She ran to the nearest tree and picked the biggest and juiciest orange she could find. The little girl had such a wonderful time on her trip that she told all her friends about it. From then on, she knew that the orange farm was always the perfect place to visit.

Lily and Sam were playing with blocks. They liked to create different things with the blocks. Sometimes they made houses, or cars, or animals. "Look, I made a dog!" Lily said, showing Sam her block dog. It had four legs, a tail, and a head with two ears. "That's nice, Lily. But I made something better. I made a rocket!" Sam said, pointing to his block rocket. It had a cone, a cylinder, and four fins. Lily and Sam started to argue. They both thought their block creation was the best. They did not want to share or play together. "Your rocket is silly. It can't fly. My dog is real. It can bark and run." Lily said. "Your dog is boring. It can't go to space. My rocket is cool. It can blast off and see the stars." Sam said. They were very serious and angry. They did not have fun. Then, Mom came in. She saw Lily and Sam fighting over the blocks. She was not happy. "Stop, Lily and Sam. Why are you fighting? You have so many blocks. You can create anything you want. Why don't you work together and make something new?" Mom said. Lily and Sam looked at each other. They felt sorry. They did not want to fight. They wanted to be friends. "Sorry, Lily. Your dog is nice. Can I pet it?" Sam said. "Sorry, Sam. Your rocket is cool. Can I ride it?" Lily said. They smiled and hugged. They decided to create something new with the blocks. They made a dog-rocket. It had a dog head, a rocket body, and a tail that could shoot fire. "Wow, this is awesome!" Lily and Sam said. They played with their dog-rocket. They pretended it could fly to the moon and meet other dogs. They had fun. Mom was happy. She saw Lily and Sam playing nicely with the blocks. She was proud of them. She gave them a kiss and a cookie.

Lily and Ben were eager to play outside. They saw a big barrel in the yard. They wondered what was inside. "Let's open it!" Lily said. "Maybe it has toys or candy!" Ben said. They ran to the barrel and lifted the lid. They saw nothing but water. They felt sad. "Aw, it's just water," Lily said. "Wait, look!" Ben said. He pointed to something shiny in the water. It was a necklace with a star pendant. "Wow, it's so pretty!" Lily said. "Maybe it's magic!" Ben said. He took the necklace and put it around his neck. He closed his eyes and made a wish. "I wish I could fly!" he said. He opened his eyes and jumped. He felt a breeze under his feet. He was flying! "Lily, look! I can fly!" he said. Lily couldn't believe it. She saw Ben flying in the air. She clapped her hands and laughed. "Ben, that's amazing!" she said. "Come on, Lily! You can fly too!" Ben said. He flew down and gave Lily the necklace. She put it around her neck and made a wish. "I wish I could fly with Ben!" she said. She opened her eyes and jumped. She felt a breeze under her feet. She was flying too! "Yay, we can fly!" she said. They flew together in the sky. They felt happy and free. They believed the necklace was magic. They didn't know it was just their imagination.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy blocks. One day, she wanted to make a very big stack. But, the blocks kept falling down. Lily was not happy. Lily's big brother, Tom, saw her trying hard. He wanted to help her. Tom told Lily, "Let me support you." Together, they tried to make the stack. They put one block on top of another. The stack was getting taller and taller. Finally, the stack was very big. Lily and Tom were successful. They were so happy that they could make the big stack. They hugged each other and played with the blocks all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a mop. The mop was very selfish. It did not like to share. It wanted all the water and soap for itself. One day, the mop met a broom. The broom was very kind. The broom wanted to be friends with the mop. The broom tried to encourage the mop to share. The broom said, "Let's clean together. It will be fun!" The mop thought about it. It wanted to have a friend. So, the mop decided to share with the broom. They cleaned the floor together. They had a lot of fun. The mop learned that sharing is good. The mop was not selfish anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a hungry boy. He was looking for something to eat. He noticed a bus and decided to get on. As soon as he got on the bus, he sneezed. All the other people on the bus looked at him. The boy was scared. But then, the people on the bus smiled at him. They were happy he was there! They all started talking to him and gave him something to eat. The boy was so happy that he finished all the food in no time. He thanked the people on the bus and then hopped out to go find more food. The end.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a big slide and a swing. They take turns to go on the slide and the swing. One day, a new boy arrives at the park. He has a red bike. He rides his bike very fast. He does not stop for anyone. He makes Lily and Ben scared. "Who is he?" Lily asks Ben. "I don't know. He is not nice. He goes too fast. He almost hit me with his bike," Ben says. They watch the new boy ride his bike around the park. He does not smile or say hello. He does not share his bike. He only cares about his bike. Lily and Ben decide to go to the other side of the park. They find a sandbox and a seesaw. They have fun playing with the sand and the seesaw. They forget about the new boy and his bike. The new boy sees Lily and Ben. He wants to play with them. He rides his bike to the other side of the park. He stops his bike near the sandbox. He says, "Hi, I am Tom. Can I play with you?" Lily and Ben look at him. They are not sure. He does not look friendly. He does not look sorry. "Maybe," Lily says. "But you have to be nice. You have to slow down. You have to share your bike. You have to say sorry." Tom thinks for a moment. He likes his bike. He likes to go fast. He does not like to share. He does not like to say sorry. He says, "No, thank you. I like my bike. I like to go fast. I don't need to share. I don't need to say sorry." He rides his bike away. He does not look back. He does not make any friends. Lily and Ben shrug. They do not care. They have each other. They have the sandbox and the seesaw. They have fun. They are happy.

Sarah had a new puppy and she was so excited. She loved to feed it and take care of it. One day, Sarah was playing in the backyard and a fake puppy came walking into the garden. It was funny looking and Sarah wanted to feed it. She tried to give the fake puppy her puppy food, but the fake puppy wouldn't eat it. Sarah got angry and started to yell at the fake puppy. The fake puppy didn't move so Sarah stormed inside. Her mom came out and laughed when she saw the fake puppy. She pointed out that it was made out of a toy and was not real. Sarah was embarrassed but she felt better when her puppy came out to play with her. She went back to feeding and playing with her real puppy and forgot all about the fake one.

Mummy had a jolly smile on her face when she put the violin in little Jack's hands. He held it carefully and looked up at Mummy, wondering what he was meant to do. She nodded and said, "Go ahead and play!" Little Jack put the violin to his shoulder and willed himself to make a sound. After a few seconds the room was filled with a beautiful musical melody. Mummy's jolly smile grew even wider and soon she was tapping her feet along with the music. Little Jack looked up, his eyes sparkling with joy. He put the bow up and down, faster and faster, as if he was trying to make all the music out of the world. The violin was singing and Mummy was singing and they were both laughing and smiling. Little Jack put the violin down, still smiling. He felt so proud - he had made something so beautiful. And he knew that with a little bit more practice, he would be able to master the violin!

Once upon a time, there was a pig. The pig lived in a open field. One day, the pig wanted to shout. So, the pig opened its mouth, and shouted. The pig's loud shout echoed in the open field. Then, another pig heard the shout. This pig opened its mouth and shouted too. The two pigs shouted back and forth to each other. Soon, more and more pigs in the open field joined in the shouting. The open field was filled with a lot of loud shouting. The pigs were very happy. They shouted together until the sun went down.

Molly and Bobby were playing together in the park. Molly had a big bowl. She rolled it along the ground and Bobby chased it. It rolled and rolled across the grass. "It's so cold," said Bobby, as he felt the cold air on his face. "Molly, can I roll the bowl?" asked Bobby. "Yes!" replied Molly. Bobby took the bowl and rolled it back to Molly. He laughed as it toppled over and he chased it again. They both ran around and rolled the bowl from one end of the park to the other. They kept rolling it until the sun went down and it was time for them to go home. Molly and Bobby said goodbye and headed off in opposite directions until the next day when they would play again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside and watching the clouds go by. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her supply some food to the animals in the forest. Timmy was enthusiastic to help his mom and quickly gathered some carrots and apples. As they walked through the forest, they noticed a storm was coming. Timmy's mom told him they needed to hurry and finish supplying the food before the storm arrived. Timmy agreed and they continued on their mission. Suddenly, the storm hit and it was very loud and scary. Timmy and his mom tried to run back home, but they got lost in the forest. They were very scared and didn't know what to do. Timmy's mom tried to call for help, but there was no one around to hear them. Eventually, they had to spend the night in the forest. They were cold, wet, and hungry. Timmy was very sad that they couldn't make it back home. The next morning, they were finally found by a search party. Timmy and his mom were safe, but they learned to always be careful when going out in the storm.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and run around. One day, Timmy's mom said, "Timmy, it's time to do some exercise." Timmy didn't want to do exercise, but he knew he had to listen to his mom. As Timmy was doing his exercise, he saw a bird fall from the sky. Timmy said, "Mommy, look! The bird fell down." His mom said, "Oh no, the bird might be dead." Timmy felt sad for the bird. Timmy's mom picked up the bird and they took it to the vet. The vet said the bird was just tired and needed some rest. Timmy was happy to hear that the bird wasn't dead. From that day on, Timmy made sure to always do his exercise so he wouldn't fall down like the bird did.

Once upon a time, there was a charming little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to eat vegetables from the big garden. One day, Remy saw a big, green vegetable that he wanted to eat. But, the vegetable was tied to a tall stick. Remy thought and thought about how to get the vegetable. Then, he had an idea. He called out to his friend, Birdie the bird. "Birdie, can you help me?" he asked. "I want to eat the vegetable, but it is tied up." Birdie flew down and looked at the vegetable. She saw the knot and said, "I can help you, Remy!" Birdie used her beak to untie the knot. The vegetable fell to the ground, and Remy was very happy. Remy and Birdie shared the big, green vegetable. They ate and ate until their tummies were full. From that day on, Remy and Birdie were the best of friends. They always helped each other and shared their food. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, Lily went outside to play, but she forgot her mittens. Her hands were cold and she couldn't play for long. Lily's mom saw her and gave her a pair of mittens. They were soft and warm. Lily was happy and thanked her mom. She put them on and went back outside to play. While she was playing, Lily found a stick. She picked it up and started to twist it around. She did it slow at first, but then she got faster and faster. Suddenly, the stick broke! Lily was sad, but then she remembered her warm mittens and smiled. The end.

Thomas was a very competitive boy. He didn't like to be beaten when it came to games and races. One day, he was walking through the park when he saw a spider. Thomas was scared of spiders, but he wanted to be brave. He hoped he could be brave enough to pick it up. Thomas's friend Sam saw him and said: "Why don't you pick it up, Thomas? It won't hurt you. I'm sure it's nice." Thomas hesitated, but then he slowly picked up the spider. He held it in his hand and admired it. Sam said: "See, you did it! I knew you could be brave. That's very competitive of you!" Thomas smiled and looked proudly at the spider. He was happy he could be so brave. He put the spider back on the ground. As he watched it crawl away, he hoped more brave things would come his way.

Once upon a time, there was a big, attractive cat. The cat was very nice and liked to lead the other animals in the forest. All the animals liked the cat because it was so pretty and kind. One day, the cat saw a small bird that was lost. The bird was sad and scared. The cat decided to help the bird and lead it back to its family. They walked together through the forest, talking and laughing. The bird was very happy to have a new friend. At the end of the day, the cat and the bird found the bird's family. The bird's family was so happy to see their little one safe and sound. They thanked the cat for helping and leading the bird home. The cat felt very proud and happy. The moral of the story is that being kind and helping others can make you feel good and bring happiness to others.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy called Joey. Joey was only three years old and he was very curious. One day, he had been playing around his house when he spotted something on the floor. It was thumb! Joey was so excited. He picked it up and started jumping up and down with it in his hand. Suddenly, Joey noticed something very helpful. It was his big sister, who was smiling at him. Joey knew that she wanted to help him. So he looked at his thumb and smiled back at his sister. Joey's sister showed him how to use his thumb. She showed him how to use it to applaud. Joey was so happy. He started clapping his hands together with his thumb and felt so proud of himself. His parents and sisters could hear the sound of his clapping and came to see what he was doing. When they saw him, they all started applauding him. Joey was so proud. He felt so helpful and important. Joey couldn't stop smiling, and neither could his family. And that's how Joey learned to use his thumb!

Lila and Rani were sisters who lived in a small village. They liked to help their mother cook food for their family. One day, their mother gave them a big orange fruit and told them to rub it on a grater. "This is a carrot," she said. "It makes the food sweet and colorful." Lila and Rani took turns rubbing the carrot on the grater. They watched the orange shreds fall into a bowl. They smelled the fresh and sweet carrot. They wanted to taste it, but their mother said, "No, not yet. We have to add some other things first." Their mother took out a small jar and opened it. She sprinkled some brown powder on the carrot. "This is cumin," she said. "It makes the food spicy and warm." She mixed the carrot and the cumin with a spoon. She smiled and said, "Now we have a salad. It is called gajar ka halwa. It is a special treat for winter." Lila and Rani looked at the salad. They saw the orange and brown colors. They smelled the spicy and sweet cumin. They wanted to taste it, but their mother said, "No, not yet. We have to cook it first." Their mother put the salad in a pot and placed it on the stove. She turned on the fire and stirred the salad. She said, "We have to cook it until it is soft and sticky. Then we will add some sugar and nuts. It will be very yummy." Lila and Rani waited patiently. They heard the salad sizzle and bubble. They smelled the sugar and nuts. They wanted to taste it, but their mother said, "No, not yet. We have to let it cool down first." Their mother turned off the fire and took the pot off the stove. She poured the salad into a big plate and let it cool down. She said, "Now we have a dessert. It is called gajar ka halwa. It is a special treat for winter." Lila and Rani looked at the dessert. They saw the orange and brown colors. They smelled the spicy and sweet cumin. They wanted to taste it, but their mother said, "Yes, now you can. It is ready to eat." Lila and Rani took a spoon each and scooped some dessert. They put it in their mouths and smiled. It was soft and sticky. It was spicy and sweet. It was very yummy. They said, "Thank you, mother. We love gajar ka halwa. It is a special treat for winter."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, she went to bed and fell asleep. She had a dream that she was in a magical land with talking animals and colorful trees. She saw a big castle and wanted to enter it, but the gate was closed. Lily saw a kind and polite rabbit who offered to help her. The rabbit showed her a secret way to enter the castle. They walked through a beautiful garden and found a hidden door. They opened it and went inside. Inside the castle, Lily saw a princess who was very happy to see her. They became friends and had a tea party with the talking animals. Lily was so happy in her dream and didn't want to wake up. But eventually, she did and was sad to leave her new friends. She hoped to enter the magical land again in her dreams.

Lily liked to stretch her lip with her fingers. She thought it was funny to make faces in the mirror. She also liked to stretch her lip when she was bored or angry. She did not know that stretching her lip too much could hurt it. One day, Lily went to the store with her mom. She saw a cheap toy that she wanted. It was a doll with long hair and a pink dress. She asked her mom to buy it for her, but her mom said no. Lily was very angry. She started to cry and scream. She also stretched her lip with her fingers. "Stop that, Lily," her mom said. "You will hurt your lip if you stretch it too much. And you don't need that cheap toy. It will break soon." Lily did not listen to her mom. She kept crying and stretching her lip. She wanted the toy so badly. She did not care about her lip. But then, something bad happened. Lily stretched her lip so much that it tore. She felt a sharp pain and saw blood on her fingers. She was scared and shocked. She stopped crying and looked at her mom. "Mommy, mommy, it hurts!" she said. "My lip is broken!" Her mom hugged her and took her to the bathroom. She cleaned her lip and put a band-aid on it. She also gave her a kiss and said she was sorry. "Lily, I'm sorry you hurt your lip," her mom said. "But you have to be careful with your body. You can't stretch your lip like that. It's not good for you." Lily nodded and said she was sorry too. She learned her lesson. She did not stretch her lip anymore. She also did not want the cheap toy anymore. She realized that it was not worth it. She was happy with her mom and her band-aid.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the forest near their house. One day, they find a big log. They want to make a fort with it. "Let's roll the log to that spot," Tim says. "It will be a good place for our fort." "OK," Sam says. "But it is very heavy. We need something to help us." They look around and see an axe. It belongs to their dad. He uses it to chop wood. "Look, an axe!" Tim says. "We can use it to make the log smaller and lighter." "Good idea," Sam says. "But be careful. The axe is sharp and dangerous." Tim takes the axe and swings it at the log. He makes a big cut. He swings it again and again. He is having fun. "Tim, stop!" Sam says. "You are making too much noise. Dad will hear us and get angry. He will not like us using his axe." But Tim does not listen. He keeps swinging the axe. He is jolly. He laughs and sings. Suddenly, the log splits in two. It rolls down the hill. It goes very fast. It bumps into a tree. It breaks the tree. It keeps rolling. "Oh no!" Tim and Sam say. "The log is out of control. It will hit something or someone. We have to stop it." They run after the log. They try to catch it. But it is too fast for them. They are scared. They shout for help. "Help! Help! Stop the log!"

Sara and Tom were playing in the garden. They saw a big green plant with many sharp points. Sara wanted to touch it, but Tom stopped her. "No, Sara, don't touch it! It is a cactus. It can hurt you!" Tom said. "What is a cactus?" Sara asked. She liked to question everything. "A cactus is a plant that lives in the desert. It does not need much water. It has sharp points to protect itself from animals," Tom explained. "Why does it live in the desert? Why does it not need water? Why does it have sharp points?" Sara asked. She had many questions. Tom sighed. He did not know all the answers. He looked at the cactus and saw a pink flower on top of it. He smiled. "Look, Sara, the cactus has a flower. It is beautiful. Maybe the cactus is not so bad after all," he said. Sara looked at the flower too. She agreed. It was beautiful. She smiled back at Tom. "Maybe you are right, Tom. The cactus is beautiful. But I still don't want to touch it," she said.

One day, Diego was feeling very impatient. He wanted to make something, but he had no tools. So, he asked his mom if he could borrow a hammer. She said yes, and gave him a hammer. He was so excited! He ran outside with his new hammer and started tapping and banging on all the things he could find. He ran around the yard thumping the hammer on anything and everything. Then he looked up and noticed that his neighbor had a fence. He was determined to bang the hammer against the fence. But when he got closer, he started to worry - he realised the fence was too big to hit with the hammer. He was so frustrated and started to cry. He sat on the ground, feeling sad. Suddenly, he heard a voice behind him. It was his neighbor. He was smiling and he was holding a big hammer! He had seen Diego trying to hit the fence and wanted to help. He said he had an extra hammer that he would be happy to give to Diego. Diego was so excited and quickly received the big hammer from his neighbor. After that, he was able to easily hit the fence with the hammer. He had a really great time and was very thankful to his neighbor.

It was time to celebrate! Mommy and Daddy said they had something special to do. They took their daughter to the attic. She was a bit fearful. She held Daddy's hand tightly. When they got to the top of the attic, there was a huge surprise - balloons, cake, and lots of presents! She couldn't believe it. Mommy and Daddy said it was time for her birthday party! She was so excited. She got to play games and blow out all the candles on her cake. It was a fun day of celebrating in the attic. Then they went home with lots of goodies and memories.

Once there was a little girl who loved pushing buttons. She had lots of buttons - some made noise, some lit up, and some moved in funny ways. Her mommy would often encourage her to push more buttons, and the little girl loved it. One day, she was playing with a toy that had lots of buttons on it and her brother wanted to play too. The little girl was very jealous that her brother wanted to play with her toy, but her mommy encouraged her to let him push some buttons too. So the two of them had a lot of fun pressing all the buttons together. At the end of the day, the little girl felt very happy and proud that she had been brave enough to allow her brother to join in her game. She was glad that her mommy had encouraged her to be generous.

Once upon a time there was a jolly beetle. Every day the beetle went out to study. He studied the trees, the flowers and the grass. He looked at their colours, shapes and sizes. Everyday he had a great time studying. One day, the beetle came across a big pond. He wanted to study the pond too, so he hopped up onto a fallen leaf and floated across the surface of the water. Suddenly, he noticed something swimming with him. It was a fish! The beetle was so excited. He studied the fish as it moved through the water. The beetle was so busy studying that he didn't even realise how far he had floated. He was so far away from his home. He knew it was time to go back. The beetle turned around and waved goodbye to the fish before heading home. He thought about his studies with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Kaylee who went for a walk in the woods. She saw an enormous insect, which made her happy. She wanted to catch it, so she ran after it. The insect kept flying away from her, but Kaylee was determined to catch it. She followed it deep into the woods, where it suddenly stopped. Kaylee was excited and said, "I caught you!" But the enormous insect remained still and didn't move. So she stepped closer and closer until she bumped into something. When she looked down, she saw a big bear! The bear stood up, growled and started to chase after Kaylee. She screamed and ran as fast as she could, but the bear was too fast. In the end, itmanaged to catch her. Kaylee was too scared to move and remained still, while the bear dragged her away. The poor girl never returned home.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was very happy living in her nest. One day, Tweety saw a big orange cat trying to catch her. Tweety got scared and flew away to find shade under a tree. The tree protected Tweety from the cat. Tweety was very happy to find shade under the tree. She felt safe and secure. But then, a big storm came and the tree fell down. Tweety's nest got destroyed and she had nowhere to go. She felt sad and alone. Tweety realized that sometimes protection and shade are not enough. She needed a stronger home to protect her from the storm. From that day on, Tweety built a new nest that was stronger and safer. She learned that sometimes bad things happen, but we can always find a way to protect ourselves and be safe.

Once upon a time there was a beautiful pool. It was so big and so deep and so blue. One day, a little boy named Jack was playing by the pool. He wanted to jump in, so he took hold of the edge and jumped in with a big splash. But when Jack got out of the water, he was crying. He had tears streaming down his face. He had torn his shirt when he jumped in the pool. He was so sad. But Jack's mom came and gave him a hug. She wiped away his tears and told him not to worry. She said she would take him to the store and get him a new shirt. Jack smiled and his tears were gone. He was so happy to be able to go back in the beautiful pool. He went back in, jumped and splashed around with a big smile on his face. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl named Lucy. She was very small and very adorable. She was very happy because she had a good life. Every day, Lucy went to the park to play. She would slide down the slide and swing on the swings. But one day when Lucy asked her mom to go to the park, her mom said no. Lucy was sad and asked her mom why. Her mom said, "The park is too busy and there are too many people there. I refuse to take you there. I want your life to be safe." Lucy was disappointed, but she understood and stayed home. Instead of going to the park, Lucy stayed at home and drew pictures with her crayons. She also wrote stories and sang songs. She had fun and it was still an adorable day! The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who lived in the jungle. He had a loud roar that scared all the animals. One day, he met a little squirrel who was climbing an oak tree. "Hello, little squirrel. Why are you climbing that tree?" asked the lion. "I am looking for acorns to eat," replied the squirrel. "That's unusual. Most animals are afraid of me," said the lion. The lion and the squirrel became friends and played together every day. But one day, the lion got very hungry and decided to eat the little squirrel. "I'm sorry, my friend. I'm so hungry," said the lion. The squirrel tried to run away, but the lion caught him and ate him for dinner. The other animals in the jungle were very sad and angry when they heard what happened. They all agreed to stay away from the lion and never play with him again. The lion was very lonely and sad because he lost all his friends.

Leo was a little lion who loved to roar. He roared when he woke up, he roared when he played, and he roared when he was hungry. He roared so loud that all the animals in the jungle heard him. One day, Leo was roaring near a big tree. He saw a bird with bright feathers on a branch. He wanted to play with the bird, so he roared at it. But the bird was scared of Leo's roar and flew away. "Come back, bird! I want to be your friend!" Leo shouted. But the bird did not come back. Leo felt sad and lonely. He wished he had a friend who liked his roar. Then he heard a noise in the bushes. He saw a little monkey with a long tail. The monkey was curious about Leo and came closer. "Hello, lion. What are you doing?" the monkey asked. "I'm looking for a friend who likes my roar. Do you like my roar?" Leo asked. The monkey nodded. "Yes, I like your roar. It sounds strong and brave. Can I hear it again?" Leo smiled and roared as loud as he could. The monkey clapped his hands and cheered. "Wow, that was a great roar! You are a hero, lion!" the monkey said. Leo felt happy and proud. He had found a friend who liked his roar. "Thank you, monkey. You are very patient and kind. Do you want to play with me?" Leo asked. The monkey nodded again. "Yes, I want to play with you. You are fun and friendly. What do you want to play?" Leo thought for a moment. Then he had an idea. "Let's play hide and seek. I will count to ten and you hide. Then I will find you with my roar. OK?" The monkey agreed. He ran to find a hiding spot. Leo closed his eyes and counted to ten. Then he opened his eyes and roared. "Ready or not, here I come!" he said. He followed his roar to find his friend. They played hide and seek for a long time. They had a lot of fun. They became the best of friends. They roared and laughed together. Leo was happy. He had learned that his roar was not scary, but special. And he had learned that a friend who likes you for who you are is a true hero.

Sally was a very busy girl. She liked to organize everything. She liked to organize her toys, her books, and even her wood. But Sally was getting a bit too organized. One day, Sally was organizing her wood. She placed each piece in a very neat pile. But then she had a thought. What if her piles weren't perfect? She started to get frustrated and her feeling were getting more and more bitter. Suddenly, Sally had an idea. She went to the store and bought some colorful string. She used the string to make her pile of wood look even better. She was so happy with the end result! It was definitely more organized! Sally smiled a big smile. She was proud of herself for creating something so neat and organized. She learned that being organized didn't have to be so bitter. Sometimes, it could be a lot of fun!

Once upon a time there was a purple flower. It was in a garden and it bloomed every day. The flower liked to watch the birds and butterflies who came to the garden. One day, the flower looked in the sky and saw a white cloud. It smiled and felt so happy. Suddenly, the flower heard a noise coming from the sink. She looked over and saw that a little frog had hopped inside. The frog was scared and wanted to get out. The flower felt so sorry for the frog so she reached her petals and helped him out. The frog thanked the flower and hopped away. Then a few minutes later, the flower saw the frog back in the garden. He was with his family and friends and they were looking at the flower's bright purple petals. They all admired the flower and smiled. The flower was so happy that she was able to help the frog. From that day on, the flower always bloomed with pride and smiled even when the sun went down.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jane. She was three years old. Jane wanted to find something special and so she decided to go searching. She looked all around her house, peeking into cupboards and checking behind furniture. But she still couldn't find what she was looking for. Just then Jane's mother came into the room. "What are you searching for, Jane?" she asked. "I'm looking for a case, mummy," Jane said sadly. "I can't find it!" "Ah, I know where it is," said Jane's mother. She picked up a pale case from the top of a high shelf. "Here it is," she said with a grin. She handed the case to Jane who smiled brightly. "Thank you, mummy!" said Jane as she opened the case to find lots of her favourite toys inside. She was so happy that she had found her special case!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lola. She always wanted to help people. One day, a funny problem happened in her house. The lightbulb stopped working. Lola took a look at the lightbulb. It was very thin and not giving out any light. She wondered what she should do. Suddenly, she got an idea! She ran to the kitchen to get a ladder. She tried to take down the lightbulb but she was too short. So she asked her mom to help her. Her mom used her mind and came up with a plan.
