She put a box next to the lightbulb, then climbed up the ladder and changed it for a new one. The new lightbulb was much bigger and brighter than the old one. Everyone in the house was very happy! Lola was proud of using her mind to help her family.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went on a walk with his mom in the nature. They saw a lot of trees, flowers and birds. Timmy loved it! Suddenly, they saw a man sitting on a bench. He looked very sad. Timmy asked his mom why the man was sad. His mom explained that the man was deaf and couldn't hear the birds singing. Timmy felt sad for the man too. He ran over to the man and said, "Hello! Do you want to seat with us?" The man smiled and nodded. They all sat together and enjoyed the nature. The man even felt the wind blowing and smiled again. Timmy was happy to make a new friend.

Once there was a boy named Jack. He was honest, but too honest. One day, Jack was playing with his friends when he heard a phone ringing. He decided he should be the one to answer it, because he was honest. When Jack picked up the phone, he heard a loud, angry voice on the other end. It was an old man, yelling at Jack for something he didn't do. Jack was confused, but he was honest. He refused to hang up until the old man stopped yelling. The old man was so angry that he told Jack he would never get his way ever again. Then there was silence. Jack learned his lesson that day. Being honest is important, but sometimes being too honest can cause more harm then good. The moral of the story is: honesty is the best policy, but be careful of how honest you are.

One day, Rita wanted to go to the gym. She asked her mum if she could go. Her mum said it was ok and she could go as long as she promised to look after herself. Rita was so excited! She put on her favourite purple t-shirt and her brightly coloured sneakers and then she took a taxi with her mum to the gym. When they arrived, Rita's mum told her that she had to be careful and stay away from the heavy weights and machinery that the gym had. Rita promised to listen and her mum gave her permission to start. Rita was very happy. She jumped, skipped and crawled all around the gym. Whenever she felt like it, she stopped to do some stretches or hop on the trampoline. Everyone at the gym was impressed with how well she was listening to her mum and staying away from the weights and machines. After a few hours, Rita and her mum said goodbye to everyone at the gym and went home. Rita fell asleep on the taxi ride back and had lots of fun dreams. Every time she thought of the gym and all the fun she had, she smiled from ear to ear. It was a day to remember!

One day, a red bird saw a red envelope on the ground. The sun was shining bright in the sky. The bird picked up the envelope with its beak. The bird flew to its friend, the cat. The cat was sitting under a tree. The bird said, "Look! I found a red envelope. It was shining in the sun." The cat said, "Let's open it and see what's inside." They opened the envelope together. Inside, they found a pretty picture of a rainbow. The bird and the cat were very happy. They put the picture on the tree for everyone to see. The sun kept shining, making the red envelope and the rainbow picture shine too.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved trains and he had a toy engine that he played with every day. One day, Timmy was playing with his engine when his friend Billy came over. "Hi Timmy! Can I play with your engine?" asked Billy. Timmy thought for a moment and then said, "Sure Billy, you can play with it, but you have to be obedient and take good care of it." Billy promised to take good care of the engine and they played together for a while. But then, Billy started to get rough with the engine and Timmy got upset. "Hey Billy, you're not being obedient! You promised to take good care of my engine," said Timmy. Billy realized he had made a mistake and apologized to Timmy. From that day on, Billy learned to be more obedient and take better care of his own toys. And Timmy learned the importance of choosing good friends who keep their promises.

Once upon a time there was a kind, compassionate cheese named Cheese. Cheese was very warm and friendly, but he didn't know many people. One day, Cheese went for a walk in the park and he saw a little girl. He waved hello and the girl smiled back. Cheese felt so happy! Cheese and the girl became fast friends. That evening Cheese asked the girl, "What do you know?" The girl thought for a moment and then said, "I know how to be kind to others and I know how to show compassion." Cheese was so happy that he jumped up and down. The girl and Cheese spent many days together, learning new things and having fun. Cheese taught her how to make cheese sandwiches and the girl showed Cheese how to play tag. They both laughed and enjoyed their time together. Cheese and the girl became very close and together they shared their knowledge and love of cheese. They both learned a lot from each other and they both grew to be much more compassionate and kind. The girl was very glad she met Cheese and Cheese was so grateful that he had a friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big box of colorful blocks. One day, she wanted to make a figure of a cat. She tried to put the blocks together, but it didn't look like a cat. She felt sad. Her mom asked her, "What's wrong, Lily?" "I can't make a cat figure," Lily replied. Her mom said, "Let's mix the blocks up and try again." So they mixed up the blocks and started over. This time, Lily was able to make a cat figure that she was proud of. She was happy again and showed her mom the cat figure. Her mom smiled and said, "Great job, Lily!"

Sara and Tom are playing in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. Sara has a pink dress and Tom has a blue shirt. They are friends and share their toys. One day, they see a big hill with many flowers. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side. They hold hands and start to walk up the hill. They see yellow, purple and white flowers. They smell nice and make them happy. But the hill is steep and slippery. Sara steps on a rock and loses her balance. She falls down and rolls down the hill. She screams and cries. Tom sees her fall and runs after her. He is scared and worried. He reaches her at the bottom of the hill. She is dirty and has a scratch on her knee. She is still crying and holding her dress. Tom hugs her and says, "Don't cry, Sara. You are okay. You are powerful. You can stand up and smile." Sara looks at him and wipes her tears. She smiles and says, "Thank you, Tom. You are powerful too. You are a good friend. You helped me." They hug again and stand up. They look at the hill and decide to go back to the park. They don't want to climb the hill anymore. They want to swing, slide and run. They are happy and safe. They are powerful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain. One day, she went outside and got very wet. She ran inside to her mommy and said, "Mommy, I'm wet!" Her mommy gave her a big hug and said, "Let's dry you off." Lily's mommy took a towel and dried her off. After a minute, Lily said, "Mommy, can we go outside and play again?" Her mommy said, "Yes, but let's make sure to seat on the porch so we don't get wet again." Lily was happy and they went outside to seat on the porch and watch the rain. They had fun even though they were not playing in the rain.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play at the park with her friends. One day, they went to the playground and Lily saw a big slide. She wanted to try it out but she was scared. Her friend, Timmy, said, "Don't worry, Lily! You can do it! You'll fit perfectly on the slide!" Lily felt better and climbed up the ladder to the top of the slide. As she slid down, she saw a toy snake on the ground. She thought it was real but Timmy said, "Don't be afraid, Lily. That's just a fake snake. It's not real." Lily felt silly for being scared of a fake snake. She laughed and played with her friends all day long. They had so much fun together!

Once upon a time, there was a little figure. He was very small and he had no name. One day he decided to take a walk. As he was walking, he lay down on the ground. Suddenly, a little boy came around the corner. He saw the figure lying on the ground and said, "Hello there! Who are you?" The figure said, "I don't have a name, but I'm looking for one. What's your name?" The little boy smiled. "My name is Max," he said. Max lay down next to the little figure and said, "We can be friends! Why don't I call you Little Figure?" The little figure was so excited! He jumped up and said, "I like that! From now on my name is Little Figure!" And so Little Figure and Max became best friends. They would always lay down together and tell stories. Little Figure was very happy to finally have a name.

Once there was a baby chicken named Peepers. Peepers loved to go for a swim in the pond. He always asked his parents if he could go, and they always said yes. One day Peepers was feeling extra brave and jumped into the pond without asking. When he emerged from the water, he was covered in mud. He asked his mom for help. She put him in a big bowl full of warm, soapy water and left him to soak for a few minutes. As the dirt and mud washed away, Peepers felt much cleaner. After his bath, Mom put a big blob of butter on his feathers to help get them back in place. Peepers felt embarrassed that he got so dirty in the first place but he was very happy his mom had helped him. After that, Peepers always asked before jumping into the pond, and if he got muddy he was sure to take a soak in the warm water.

Once upon a time there were three friends. Jack, James, and Susie. They were planning a meeting. Jack said, "Let's have a meeting". Susie said, "Yes, that is a good plan!" So the three friends decided to meet at the park. When they got to the park, it was very hot. But, they still wanted to have their meeting. Jack said, "Let's sit under this tree, so we can stay in the shade and stay cool". That sounded like a good idea, so they all sat down in the shade. Susie said, "Now let's look at what we should talk about at our meeting." James said, "Yes, let's start planning". So the three friends talked and planned their meeting. They decided to talk about new ideas, games, and how they could help each other. They had so many good plans they were excited. When their meeting was finished, the three friends said good-bye. They were all so happy with the plans they made and couldn't wait for their next meeting.

Once upon a time, there was a white squash. It was the biggest squash that anyone had ever seen. Everybody wanted to cut it but no one knew how. One day, a brave little boy came along and said he could cut it. Everyone laughed, but the little boy said he'd give it a try. He picked up a tiny knife and got to work. Everyone was surprised when he actually managed to cut it. The little boy pulled off the top, and inside he found the biggest, juiciest squash he had ever seen! Everyone was so happy and shared it together. The little boy was the happiest of all!

Ben and Mia like to fish with Dad. They have a big pole with a string and a hook. Dad puts a worm on the hook and throws it in the water. Ben and Mia wait for a fish to bite. One day, they go to a new lake. Dad says it is very deep and has big fish. Ben and Mia are excited. They want to catch a big fish. They throw their hooks in the water and wait. Soon, Ben feels a tug on his pole. He pulls hard and sees a big fish. It is shiny and green and has a long mouth. Ben is happy. He says, "Look, Dad, I caught a big fish!" Mia feels a tug on her pole too. She pulls hard and sees a big fish. It is brown and spiky and has a big eye. Mia is scared. She says, "Eek, Dad, I caught a scary fish!" Dad smiles and helps them take the fish off the hooks. He says, "You both did a great job. These are different kinds of fish. Ben's fish is a bass and Mia's fish is a catfish. They are both good to eat. Do you want to keep them or let them go?" Ben says, "I want to keep my fish. It is pretty and I want to show Mom." Mia says, "I want to let my fish go. It is ugly and I don't like it." Dad says, "OK, that is fine. You can choose what to do with your fish. You have to accept that they are different and respect them." Ben and Mia nod. They do what they want with their fish. Then they hug Dad and say, "Thank you, Dad, for taking us fishing. We had fun." Dad hugs them back and says, "You're welcome, Ben and Mia. I love you." They pack up their poles and go home.

One day, a little girl decided to collect some things from her bedroom ceiling. She was worried that she wouldn't be able to get them because the ceiling was too high. Her brother was there to help her, but he wasn't sure what to do. They tried lots of different ideas but none of them worked. Finally, they decided to work together. The little girl climbed on a chair, and her brother stood below her to catch the things she collected. The little girl was grateful that they were able to do it together. She learned an important lesson. When she has a problem, she can always ask her brother for help. They can work together to make things better.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his ball, and he would roll it all around the yard. One day, Timmy's mom said to him, "Timmy, I have a surprise for you!" Timmy was so excited to hear this, he couldn't wait to find out what it was. When Timmy's mom brought out a big box, Timmy's eyes got really big. "Wow, Mommy! What's in the box?" Timmy asked. "It's a present for you, Timmy," his mom said with a smile. "It's a toy car that rolls really fast!" Timmy was so happy and grateful for his generous mom. He couldn't wait to play with his new toy car and roll it all around the house. Timmy hugged his mom and said, "Thank you so much, Mommy! You're the best!"

Once upon a time, there was a yellow bird called Bob. Bob lived in a regular tree close to a lake. Every day he wanted to explore, but he was scared. He wanted something to protect him. One day, he saw something shine in the lake. He flew down to see what it was, and it was a yellow feather! Bob was so excited to find it. He flew back up to his tree and showed the feather to all his bird friends. Bob's friends all agreed that the yellow feather was a sign that he was special and should be protected. That night, Bob put the feather in a special place so he would never lose it. Every day, Bob wore the yellow feather and felt brave. He was no longer scared to explore the world. He had his yellow feather to protect him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to smile and play with his red toy automobile. One day, Tim's mommy told him they were going on a trip. Tim was very excited and wanted to bring his toy automobile along. On their trip, they saw a big hill. Tim's mommy said it would be difficult to go up the hill, but they tried their best. Tim held his toy automobile tightly and smiled as they slowly went up the hill. At the top of the hill, they saw a beautiful view. After they enjoyed the view, it was time to go back down the hill. Tim's mommy told him it would be easier to go down than up. Tim smiled and held his toy automobile as they went down the hill. When they got to the bottom, Tim was so happy that he and his toy automobile made it through the difficult trip.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Harry. Tom and Harry liked to spend time in the garden together. One day, they were discussing what to play when they heard a terrible sound. Tom asked, "What was that noise?" Harry replied, "It sounded terrible. It came from the garden." Tom was scared and said, "Let's go check it out." Harry was brave and said, "Let's go." So they went to the garden. There was a big dog. The dog was barking and growling. Harry said, "It's ok. He looks scary but he won't hurt us." Tom said, "Let's stay back and discuss if we should help the dog or find a grown-up." Harry agreed and they discussed what to do. Finally, they decided to find a grown-up to help the dog. They ran to find a grown-up and saved the poor animal. The end.

Once upon a time there was an adorable little girl. She was so curious and loved learning new things. One day, when she was out with her mom, they came across a beautiful meeting. She had never seen anything so grand! The little girl kept asking her mom what it was, so her mom decided to take her to the meeting. She was so excited to learn what it was all about. When they arrived, everyone was so friendly and welcoming. They were there to feed the hungry animals in the nearby forests. Everyone worked together to collect food and bring it to the animals. The little girl had so much fun helping to feed the animals. She was so proud that she had done something nice to help them. Her mom was so proud of her too. At the end of the day, they hugged goodbye and the little girl went home with a smile on her face. She knew that she had had a very special and lovely day.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor named Jack. He was very charming and everyone liked him. One day, Jack went on a long journey to find a treasure. He sailed on his boat for many days and nights. One night, Jack heard a loud noise. He was surprised and scared. He saw a big storm coming. The waves were very high and the wind was very strong. Jack tried to control his boat, but he couldn't. His boat was going up and down and he was afraid that he would drown. Suddenly, Jack remembered his father's words. His father had told him that he should never give up and always be brave. Jack took a deep breath and tried again. He was able to control his boat and he sailed safely to the shore. Jack learned that he should never give up and always be brave, even when he is surprised by something unexpected.

One day, a little boy named Tim went outside to play. It was cold and he started to shiver. He saw his bike and wanted to ride it. Tim got on his bike and began to pedal fast to get warm. As he pedaled, Tim saw his friend, Sally. Sally was eating something. "What are you eating?" asked Tim. "I am eating a sour candy," said Sally. "Do you want to try one?" Tim nodded and took a candy from Sally. Tim put the sour candy in his mouth. His face turned funny because it was very sour. He laughed and Sally laughed too. They both got on their bikes and pedaled together, enjoying their sour candies and the cold day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved her daddy very much. One day, she saw her daddy bring out some shiny things from a box. She was curious and asked her daddy what they were for. Daddy told her they were decorations for their Christmas tree. Lily was very excited and wanted to help decorate the tree. Daddy lifted her up so she could put the shiny things on the branches. She had so much fun! After they finished decorating the tree, Lily hugged her daddy and said, "Thank you for letting me help decorate the tree, daddy. It looks so pretty!" Daddy smiled and hugged her back, feeling happy that Lily was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a kangaroo who wanted to go on an adventure. She thought and thought about what she should bring, and soon came up with an idea. She would pack her favorite things! The kangaroo started to pack all of her things. She wished she had help. Suddenly she spotted a helpful ant. He had 6 legs, so he could carry more things, and he worked very hard to help her pack. Once everything was packed, the kangaroo put on her backpack, gave the helpful ant a big thank-you hug and hopped off on her adventure. The kangaroo had such a great time on her adventure, she forgot to unpack her bag. But it didn't matter, because it was part of the fun!

Once upon a time, there were two twins who loved to play together. They were always honest with each other and never told lies. One day, they went to the park to play on the swings. After a while, it started to get dark, and their mother called out to them to come home. The twins started to walk home, but they got lost. They didn't know which way to go, and it was getting colder and darker. They tried to find their way back, but they couldn't. Finally, they saw a house with a light on, so they went to ask for help. The person who answered the door seemed nice, but they weren't honest. They told the twins to come inside and wait for their parents. But they didn't call the twins' parents, and they didn't let the twins leave. The twins were scared and wanted to go home, but the person wouldn't let them. They were trapped, and they couldn't escape. The twins wished they had never left the park and closed their eyes, hoping to wake up from this bad dream.

Lily wanted to teach her doll how to drink wine. She saw her mom and dad drink wine sometimes, and they said it was good. Lily found a bottle of wine in the kitchen and poured some in a cup. She brought the cup and the doll to her room. "Look, doll, this is wine. It is a drink for grown-ups. You can try some, but only a little bit, okay?" Lily said to her doll. She held the cup to the doll's mouth and pretended to make her drink. "Mmm, do you like it? It is sweet and sour." But then, Lily heard a knock on the door. It was her mom. She opened the door and saw Lily and the doll with the cup of wine. She was very angry and surprised. "Lily, what are you doing? Where did you get that wine? You know you are not allowed to touch that!" her mom said in a loud voice. Lily felt embarrassed and scared. She dropped the cup and the wine spilled on the floor. She started to cry and hugged her doll. "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to teach my doll how to drink wine. I didn't know it was bad," Lily said between sobs. Her mom sighed and picked up Lily and the doll. She took them to the bathroom and cleaned them up. She also cleaned the floor and threw away the cup. "Lily, wine is not for children. It can make you sick and hurt your body. You should never drink it or play with it. Do you understand?" her mom said in a calm voice. Lily nodded and said sorry again. She felt sorry for making a mess and making her mom angry. She also felt sorry for her doll, who didn't like wine either. Her mom hugged her and said she loved her. She said she was not angry anymore, but she wanted Lily to be careful and listen to her. She said she would teach her about wine when she was older and ready. Lily said she loved her mom too. She said she would be careful and listen to her. She said she would teach her doll something else, like how to sing or dance. Her mom smiled and kissed her. She said she was proud of her for being honest and brave. She said she would like to see her doll sing or dance. Lily smiled and kissed her back. She felt happy and safe. She took her doll and went to her room. She forgot about the wine and taught her doll how to sing a song.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to hear jokes and would laugh and laugh. One day, her friend told her a joke that she didn't understand. It was unknown to her, so she didn't laugh. Lily went home feeling sad and started to weep. Her mom asked her what was wrong, and she told her about the joke that she didn't understand. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. Sometimes we hear things that we don't understand, but that doesn't mean we can't learn and laugh later." Lily wiped her tears and felt better. She knew that she could learn more jokes and understand them too. From that day on, Lily tried to learn new things and never let the unknown make her weep again.

Once upon a time, there lived a naughty lion. He lived in a small forest and liked to play tricks on the animals. One day, the lion's friends thought of a plan. They asked the lion to try and jump over a tall tree. The lion was excited and agreed to try. The lion used all his strength and jumped as high as he could. Unfortunately, he did not succeed. He felt so sad and disappointed. Just then, a small rabbit hopped up to the lion. "I believe in you," said the rabbit. The lion smiled and tried again. He was determined to make it this time. With a big leap, he succeeded! The lion was so proud and happy. His friends cheered and congratulated him. He had made it!

Once upon a time there was a furry monster who lived upstairs. He was very naughty and kept doing bad things. One day, he was caught being very naughty and his parents had to punish him. They were very angry and said he must stay upstairs for a long time without being able to play or have fun. The monster was very sad. He tried to be good, but he didn't know how. So he kept doing naughty things, which made his parents even angrier. One day, his parents brought him to the top of the stairs and said he must stay there without moving for a whole day. The monster was very scared and he begged his parents to let him out, but they didn't. The monster was so scared and sad, he started to cry. He wanted to do something good to show his parents he was sorry, but they wouldn't let him. After a long time, they finally let him out, but he was still punished. The monster was so sad, he never wanted to be naughty again and he never told anyone what had happened. From that day, he was always the best he could be and never misbehaved.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived with her parent. Lily liked to eat sweet things, but she didn't like sour things. One day, Lily's parent brought home some sour candy. Lily tried it, but she didn't like it. She told her parent that the candy was sour and made her worry that she wouldn't like anything sweet anymore. Lily's parent hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. Even though you don't like sour candy, you still like sweet things. We can find other sweet things for you to eat." Lily felt better and hugged her parent back. They went to the store and found some delicious sweet treats that Lily loved. From then on, Lily's parent made sure to ask her if she liked something before bringing it home. Lily was happy and never had to worry about not liking sweet things again.

Anna liked to play dress-up with her dolls. She had many clothes and hats and shoes for them. She wanted to make them look pretty and funny. She liked fashion. One day, she decided to have a fashion show with her dolls. She invited her brother Ben to watch. She put her dolls on a table and gave them names. She said, "This is Lily. She is wearing a pink dress and a yellow hat. She is very sweet. This is Max. He is wearing a blue shirt and a green cap. He is very cool. This is Zoe. She is wearing a purple skirt and a red scarf. She is very smart." Ben clapped his hands and said, "Wow, Anna, you are very good at fashion. Your dolls look great. Can I play too?" Anna smiled and said, "Yes, you can. You can be the judge. You can give them stars. One star is good, two stars is better, three stars is best." Ben nodded and said, "OK, I will be the judge. Let me see your dolls again." Anna showed him her dolls one by one. Ben gave them stars. He said, "Lily, you get one star. You are good. Max, you get two stars. You are better. Zoe, you get three stars. You are the best. You are mighty." Anna was very happy. She hugged her dolls and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a nice judge. I succeed in my fashion show. I am mighty too." Ben hugged her back and said, "You are welcome, Anna. You are a nice fashion designer. You succeed in your fashion show. You are mighty too." They laughed and played with their dolls. They had fun. They were mighty.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily who loved flowers. She would pick them and put them in a vase in her room. One day, she found an ordinary flower in her garden. It was not as pretty as the others, but Lily still liked it. She decided to study it and learn more about it. She read books and asked her mom questions. She found out that even ordinary flowers are special in their own way. From that day on, Lily appreciated all flowers, even the ordinary ones.

Lily was a playful girl who liked to run and jump and sing. She had a new friend at school, his name was Sam. Sam was shy and quiet, he did not know how to play with the other kids. He liked to draw and read and watch the birds. One day, Lily saw Sam sitting alone on a bench. She ran to him and said, "Hi, Sam! Do you want to play with me?" Sam looked up and smiled a little. He nodded and said, "Yes, please." Lily took Sam by the hand and led him to the playground. She showed him how to slide and swing and climb. She said, "This is fun, Sam! You are good at this!" Sam laughed and said, "Thank you, Lily! You are very kind." Lily and Sam played for a long time. They made friends with the other kids and shared their toys and snacks. They had a lot of fun and learned new things. Lily said, "Sam, you are my friend. I like you." Sam said, "Lily, you are my friend too. I like you." Lily and Sam hugged and said, "We are friends!" They were happy and playful. They welcomed each other and taught each other. They had a good day at school.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play together. Today, Tom goes to visit Mia at her house. He brings his toy car and his hat. "Hi, Tom!" Mia says. "Do you want to play with me?" "Yes, please!" Tom says. He puts his hat on the table and his car on the floor. "What do you want to play?" Mia thinks for a moment. She has an idea. "Let's play tea party!" she says. She takes two cups and a pitcher from her toy box. She fills the pitcher with juice. "This is our tea," she says. Tom nods. He likes juice. He takes a cup and holds it out. Mia pours some juice into his cup. "Thank you," Tom says. He takes a sip. The juice is sweet and cold. Mia pours some juice into her cup, too. She raises it to her lips. But then, she sneezes. Achoo! The juice spills out of her cup and onto her dress. She gasps. Her dress is wet and sticky. "Oh, no!" Tom says. He puts his cup down and gets a napkin. He tries to help Mia wipe the juice off her dress. But the napkin is too small. The juice makes a big stain. Mia starts to cry. She does not like her wet dress. She feels sad and messy. "Don't cry, Mia," Tom says. He hugs her. "It's okay. It was an accident. You can change your dress." Mia sniffles. She looks at Tom. He is a good friend. He makes her feel better. She hugs him back. "Thank you, Tom," she says. "You are very nice." Tom smiles. He is happy to help Mia. He likes to play with her. He does not mind the juice. He thinks it is funny. He laughs. "You're welcome, Mia," he says. "You are very nice, too."

Once upon a time, there was a heavy rock. The rock could not move, but it had a voice. It could talk to the animals in the forest. The rock liked to spend time with the animals. One day, a bird came to visit the heavy rock. The rock said, "Hello, bird! I like your voice." The bird was happy and sang a song for the rock. They spent the day talking and singing. As the sun went down, more animals came to see the heavy rock. The rock spent the night talking and laughing with all its friends. The animals loved the rock's voice, and they all had a fun time together.

One day, Mama and Mama's friend, Michelle, decided to go for a walk together. Mama was introducing Michelle to all of their neighbours. First, they came to the mailbox. Then, they stopped at Sally's front porch. Finally, they walked up to a big, tall house. "Ah, this is my house," said Mama. Inside, she opened the large, wooden cabinet and showed Michelle a present. Michelle was very excited, but she was also impatient. "Can I see it? Can I see it?" Mama smiled. "Sure you can!" she said, and handed Michelle a big, colourful box. Michelle opened the box and jumped up and down. She was so happy - she was like a little jumping bean. Mama laughed. "I'm so glad you like it," she said. Michelle agreed. "Me too! It's the best present ever!" Mama and Michelle hugged, and continued on their walk together.

Once upon a time there was a furry motor. It was noisy and it made funny noises. Everyone in the village had never seen anything like it before and they didn't believe it could move. But one day, the furry motor started to hum and rattle. Everyone in the village was amazed and they all cheered! They couldn't believe the motor was moving. The motor zoomed around the village, but it didn't make a mess. Everyone was so happy that they started to laugh and dance. Everyone wanted a ride on the furry motor. In the end, everyone was so happy that they believed the furry motor was magical. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a bright window. The window was in a house and it was so pretty. The window was almost too big to fit in the wall! One day, a little bunny hopped over to the window. He hopped and hopped and came close enough to the window to take a peek inside. The window opened and the bunny hopped into the room. He couldn't believe his eyes! Inside, there were all sorts of colors everywhere. Bright blue, yellow, and red were everywhere. He had never seen so many colors in one place before! He hopped around and explored, discovering all the colors. The bunny was so happy to find such a bright and fun place and he knew he would never forget it. He hopped out of the window and went back to his home, with the colors still on his mind. He would remember it forever, the bright window full of colors.

One day, a little girl named Sue found a penny on the ground. It was a brilliant, shiny penny. Sue was so happy. She wanted to show her best friend, Tom. Sue ran to Tom and said, "Look what I found! It's a shiny penny!" Tom looked at the penny and smiled. He said, "Wow, that's a cool penny! Let's hide it and see if someone can find it." Sue and Tom hid the penny under a big rock. They went to find their friend, Lily, to play the game. They told Lily, "We hid something shiny. Can you find it?" Lily looked and looked. She moved the big rock and saw the penny. "I found it!" she yelled. Sue and Tom clapped and laughed. They all played with the penny together and had a fun day.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They liked to go on the slide, the seesaw and the swing. But sometimes Ben was mean to Lily and teased her. He said she was too slow, too small and too scared. He made her feel sad and hurt. One day, Ben wanted to go on the swing, but Lily was already there. She was having fun and did not want to stop. Ben got angry and said, "Get off the swing, Lily! It's my turn! You are so selfish and boring!" He tried to push her off the swing, but Lily held on tight. She said, "No, Ben! You are being rude and mean! You have to wait your turn and share!" Ben did not listen and kept trying to make Lily get off the swing. He pulled her hair, kicked her legs and shouted at her. Lily started to cry and felt very sad. She wished Ben would stop teasing her and be nice to her. Then, something happened. Ben lost his balance and fell off the swing. He landed on the ground and hurt his knee. He started to cry and felt very sad. He wished Lily would help him and be nice to him. Lily saw Ben crying and felt sorry for him. She got off the swing and went to him. She said, "Are you okay, Ben? Do you need a hug?" She helped him get up and gave him a hug. She said, "I'm sorry you hurt yourself, Ben. But you should not tease me and be mean to me. That's not how friends treat each other. Friends are kind and share and have fun together." Ben felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. You are right. I was wrong to tease you and be mean to you. That's not how friends treat each other. Friends are kind and share and have fun together. Can you forgive me, Lily? Can we still be friends?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Ben. I forgive you. We can still be friends. But you have to promise me not to tease me and be mean to me again. Okay?" Ben nodded and said, "Okay, Lily. I promise. Thank you for being nice to me. You are a good friend." Lily and Ben hugged and smiled. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that teasing and being mean is not fun and can hurt others. They learned that being kind and sharing is fun and can make others happy. They learned that friendship is a precious thing that needs respect and care. They learned that they can be better friends if they treat each other the way they want to be treated.

Once upon a time, there was a squirrel named Nutty. Nutty loved to collect nuts and store them in his treehouse. One day, Nutty's friend, a rabbit named Bouncy, came to visit him. Bouncy said, "Nutty, why are you so restless today?" Nutty replied, "I can't find my favorite nut. I've been searching all morning." Bouncy said, "Don't worry, Nutty. I'll help you find it." They searched high and low until Bouncy finally found the nut. Nutty was so happy that he started to applaud. "Thank you, Bouncy! You're the best friend ever," Nutty said. From that day on, Nutty and Bouncy were the best of friends and they always helped each other when they needed it.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play together. One day, they find a big bottle of shampoo in the bathroom. The shampoo is colorful. It has red, blue, green, and yellow stripes. "Look, Tom, this shampoo is like a rainbow!" Sara says. "Let's play with it!" Tom nods. He thinks the shampoo is pretty. They open the bottle and squeeze some shampoo on their hands. They rub the shampoo on their hair, their faces, their clothes, and the walls. They laugh and make bubbles. But then, Mom comes in. She sees the mess. She is angry. She says, "Sara and Tom, what have you done? This shampoo is not for playing. It is for washing your hair. You have wasted the shampoo and made a big mess. You have to clean up and say sorry." Sara and Tom feel bad. They know they did something wrong. They say sorry to Mom. They help her clean up the bathroom. They wash their hair with water. They learn their lesson. They do not play with shampoo again. They only use it when they need to wash their hair. They understand that shampoo is not a toy. It is a useful thing.

Tim and Mia are playing in the park. They like to go on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They see a big wheel with many colors and lights. It goes round and round very fast. Tim wants to try it, but Mia is afraid. "Come on, Mia, let's go on the wheel. It looks fun!" Tim says. "No, Tim, it is too high and too fast. It will scare me. I don't want to go on the wheel." Mia says. "Please, Mia, don't be scared. I will hold your hand. We can see the whole park from the wheel. It will be fun!" Tim says. Mia thinks for a moment. She likes Tim and she wants to make him happy. She decides to be brave and go on the wheel with him. They get in a seat and buckle up. The wheel starts to move. "Wow, look, Mia, we are going up!" Tim says. Mia feels her tummy go funny. She closes her eyes and holds Tim's hand tight. She hears the wind and the music and the people. She is scared. "Tim, I don't like this. I want to get off. Please make it stop." Mia says. "Don't worry, Mia, it will be over soon. Just breathe and look at me. You are doing great." Tim says. He smiles at her and tries to calm her down. He is proud of her for trying something new. He knows she is scared, but he also knows she is strong. The wheel goes round and round a few more times. Then it slows down and stops. Tim and Mia get off the seat and walk away. Mia feels dizzy and shaky. She is glad it is over. "Thank you, Tim, for holding my hand. You are a good friend." Mia says. "Thank you, Mia, for going on the wheel with me. You are very brave." Tim says. They hug each other and smile. They are happy. They go to the ice cream stand and buy two cones. They lick the ice cream and enjoy the tasty flavors. They forget about the wheel and have fun in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to surf in the ocean with his friends. One day, Timmy saw a big wave coming towards him. He was scared because he didn't think he could match the power of the wave. But then, he remembered his mom telling him to be brave and face his fears. So, Timmy took a deep breath and rode the wave like a brave surfer. After surfing, Timmy went to play with his friends. They were playing a game of matching cards. Timmy was having trouble finding the matching cards, but he didn't give up. He kept trying until he found all the matches. His friends were proud of him for being patient and not giving up. The moral of the story is to be brave and keep trying even when things get tough. Just like Timmy, we can all face our fears and overcome challenges. And sometimes, it just takes a little patience and determination to find the matches in life.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey named Bobo. Bobo loved to eat bananas. One day, Bobo saw his friend Timmy with a big yellow banana. Bobo felt jealous because he wanted the banana. Bobo asked Timmy if he could have the banana, but Timmy said no. Bobo tried to take the banana from Timmy, but they started to fight. Bobo was too strong and he took the banana. But then, Bobo started to feel sick. The banana was bad and made him sick. Bobo learned that it's not good to take things that don't belong to you. He felt bad for what he did and promised to never do it again.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer. The farmer had a farm with many animals. He had cows, pigs, and chickens. The farmer liked to keep his farm clean and organize. One day, a rare bird came to the farm. The bird was very big and very loud. The bird started to make a mess. It knocked over the farmer's things and scared the animals. The farmer did not like the mess and the noise. The farmer tried to make the bird go away. He clapped his hands and shouted, "Go away, bird!" But the bird did not listen. The farmer was sad and did not know what to do. Then, the farmer had an idea. He gave the bird some food. The bird ate the food and became happy. The bird stopped making a mess and making noise. The farmer and the bird became friends. From that day on, the rare bird helped the farmer organize the farm. The farmer was happy, and the farm was clean and peaceful again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his friends at the park. One day, they decided to play soccer. Timmy's team scored a goal, but his friend disagreed and said it wasn't fair. Timmy didn't like when his friend disagreed, but he tried to be nice and said, "Let's keep playing and have fun." They continued to play and Timmy's team scored another goal. This time, his friend agreed that it was a good goal. After playing for a while, Timmy's mom came to pick him up. She was happy to see that he had a clean shirt and shorts. Timmy was proud of himself for not getting too dirty while playing soccer with his friends. When he got home, he told his mom all about the game and how they disagreed about the first goal, but then agreed on the second one.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was very sad. She had a big, scary problem and she didn't know what to do. One day, she saw a mirror in front of her. She looked closely and saw something different in the reflection. It was a kind and compassionate face. She knew that the face could help her save her problem. The girl went close to the mirror and asked for help. The kind face said, "I will help you. I will give you the courage and strength to save yourself." The girl was so happy and felt good. From then on, whenever the girl was scared, she looked in the mirror for help. The kind and compassionate face always gave her the courage to save herself. The girl lived a happy life.

Tim likes to ride his motorcycle. It is red and shiny and makes a loud noise. He knows how to put on his helmet and gloves and start the engine. He likes to go fast and feel the wind on his face. One day, he sees a big hill. He wants to go up the hill and see what is on the other side. He thinks it will be fun and exciting. He speeds up and zooms towards the hill. But the hill is too steep and his motorcycle is too heavy. He tries to push harder, but his motorcycle goes slower and slower. He feels scared and sad. He thinks he will not make it to the top. Then he hears a voice. It is his dad. He is behind him on his own motorcycle. He says, "Don't worry, Tim. I am here to help you. You can do it. Just keep going." Tim feels happy and brave. He listens to his dad and keeps going. His dad gives him a little push and his motorcycle goes faster. He reaches the top of the hill and sees a beautiful view. He smiles and hugs his dad. He says, "Thank you, dad. You are the best. I love you."

Once there was a little boy named Jake. He was very playful. He ran around with his toy car. He liked to zoom around and make car noises. One day, Jake's mom came and said, "Come on now Jake, let's go outside and play in the park!" So Jake and his mom went outside. There was a playground with a swing and a slide. Jake ran ahead and climbed up the stairs. At the top, he saw a handle. He tried and tried to reach it but it was too high. "Can you help me reach the handle, Mom?" asked Jake. His Mom smiled and said, "Sure, I can help you, Jake." She bent down and helped him reach the handle. Once he touched the handle, a surge of happiness ran through Jake. He smiled and he was ready to have some fun. He went down the slide and quickly Up the ladder again. He chuckled as he reached the handle and ran down the slide again. Jake played all day till it was time to go home. He ran ahead with his toy car, feeling happy and proud that he could now reach the handle.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. Jack was a clever boy who loved to play outside. One day, Jack went to the park to play with his friends. They played on the swings and the slide, but then Jack saw a big tree. He wanted to climb it, but he struggled to get up. Jack's friends tried to help him, but they couldn't. Jack didn't give up though. He kept trying and trying until he finally made it to the top of the tree. His friends cheered for him and Jack felt very proud of himself. From that day on, Jack knew that even if he struggled, he could still succeed if he kept trying.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big question in her head. She asked her mommy, "Why is the sky blue?" Her mommy said, "It's because of the sun, dear." Lily then sucked her thumb and thought about it. She didn't understand why the sun made the sky blue. She asked her daddy, "Can you help me understand?" Her daddy said, "The sun shines on the air and makes it look blue." Lily said, "Oh, I see!" But then she tasted something bitter in her mouth. She made a face and said, "Ew, this candy is bitter!" Her mommy said, "That's because it's dark chocolate, sweetie. Some people like it bitter." Lily tried it again and said, "No thank you, mommy. I like my candy sweet."

One day, a cheerful girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. They saw many fun things to do. Lily liked to observe the birds and the trees. She also saw kids playing and laughing. Lily saw a boy with a stamp. She asked the boy, "What is that?" The boy said, "It is a stamp. I use it to make pictures on paper." Lily thought it was fun and wanted to try it too. Lily's mom bought her a stamp. Lily and the boy played with the stamps together. They made pretty pictures and had a lot of fun. At the end of the day, Lily and her mom went home with a big smile.

One day, Sammy saw something very beautiful in the sky. It was a modern rainbow! It had every color of the rainbow in it. Sammy wanted to learn how to make his own rainbow. He asked his Mom, who told him that he could mix different colors together. Sammy liked this idea, so he got to work. He mixed red with yellow to make the color orange. He mixed blue with yellow to make green. He mixed red with blue to make purple. Sammy was so excited with the different colors he was making! Then he mixed all the colors together, just like the rainbow in the sky. When it was done, it looked exactly like the beautiful rainbow he had seen. Sammy was so proud! He had made a modern rainbow all by himself. He thought it was even more beautiful than the one he'd seen in the sky!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved pizza. Pizza was her favorite food. She would always ask her mom to make pizza for dinner. One day, Lily's mom made a pizza for dinner. It smelled so good! Lily was so happy. Her mom encouraged her to eat all of her pizza. Lily ate all of her pizza and it was so yummy. She felt good and happy. From that day on, Lily ate pizza every week and her mom always encouraged her to eat it all up. The end.

Max had a new phone and was so excited to play with it! His best friend, Max saw it and felt jealous. "What is that?" asked Max. "It is my new phone!" Max said. Max wanted a new phone too. "Can I have one too?" he asked his mum and dad. They told him he would have to wait, but then something unexpected appeared. Max's mum had a surprise for Max. It was a phone, just like Max's. Max was so excited, he couldn't believe it. His best friend was so jealous! But he knew he couldn't be too mad because Max had been so lucky.

Once upon a time, there was a little engine named Eddie. Eddie was a dependable engine who liked to help his friends. He was always there when they needed him. His friends loved him very much. One day, a big storm came to the town. The wind blew and the rain fell. Eddie's friend, a small car named Carrie, was stuck in the mud. She was very sad and started to weep. She needed help to get out of the mud. Eddie heard Carrie weeping and knew he had to help her. He went to her and said, "Don't cry, Carrie. I will help you." Eddie pulled and pulled, and soon Carrie was out of the mud. She was very happy and thanked Eddie. They went home together, and everyone was safe and sound.

Anna loved her doll very much. She named her doll Lily and played with her every day. Lily had a pink dress, blue eyes and long hair. Anna liked to brush her hair and make her look pretty. One day, Anna and Lily went outside to play in the garden. Anna was very enthusiastic and ran around with Lily in her arms. She saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. She put Lily on a branch and tried to go higher. But she slipped and fell down. She hurt her knee and it bled. She cried and picked up Lily. But Lily was hurt too. Her dress was torn and her hair was dirty. Anna felt very sad. She ran inside the house and showed her mom her knee and Lily. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Anna. We can heal your knee and Lily. Let me get a band-aid and some water." She cleaned Anna's knee and put a band-aid on it. She said, "There, now your knee will feel better soon. And we can wash Lily's dress and hair and sew her dress. She will look pretty again." Anna smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. Can I help you heal Lily?" Her mom nodded and said, "Of course, you can. You are a good helper. Let's go to the bathroom and get some soap and a towel." They went to the bathroom and washed Lily's dress and hair. They dried her with a towel and combed her hair. Then they went to the living room and sewed her dress. Anna held the needle and thread and followed her mom's instructions. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to hurt you. I love you very much." She kissed Lily and hugged her. Her mom smiled and said, "You did a great job, Anna. Lily looks beautiful again. And I'm sure she loves you too. You are a good friend to her. Now, why don't you go and play with her in your room? And be careful when you climb the tree next time." Anna nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will. Thank you for helping me heal Lily. You are the best mom ever." She took Lily and ran to her room. She was happy and enthusiastic again. She played with Lily and told her stories. She said, "Lily, you are my favorite doll. And we are both healed now. We are both happy." Lily smiled and nodded. They were both happy.

One day, a little girl named Lucy wanted a red waffle. She asked her mom, "Can I have a red waffle, please?" Her mom said, "We don't have red waffles, but I can make you a normal waffle." Lucy was sad. She really wanted a red waffle. She thought, "How can I make a red waffle?" Then, Lucy had an idea! She found some red juice in the fridge. She poured the red juice on the waffle her mom made. But, the waffle was not red. It was just wet and not yummy. Lucy started to cry. She still wanted a red waffle. Her mom heard her cry and came to help. Her mom said, "I have an idea!" She took some red fruit and mashed it up. Then, she put the red fruit on the waffle. Now, Lucy had a red waffle! She was so happy, and the waffle was very yummy.

Once upon a time there was a March. It was a very dull March. On this March, Bob wanted to cover his house. He got some paint and started to cover the walls. He worked hard and carefully. When Bob was finished, he saw that the house was covered in lots of colors! Bob was so happy. He smiled and clapped his hands. His house was so bright! The colors made the dull March look so nice. But when Bob looked outside, he saw that his house was not alone. All the houses on the street were covered in colors too! Bob smiled. Everyone was happy and the street looked even brighter. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She was very hungry. Mia wanted to find something yummy to eat. So, she went for a walk in the park. In the park, Mia saw a big ice-cream truck. The truck had many colors and lots of ice-cream. Mia was happy to see the ice-cream truck. She knew she wanted ice-cream to eat. Mia went to the ice-cream truck and met a nice man. The man gave her a big ice-cream cone. Mia said thank you and ate the ice-cream. It was so yummy! Now, Mia was not hungry anymore. She went home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys in the park. One day, a mean boy came and took Timmy's toy truck. Timmy felt sad and cried. Timmy's mom asked him, "What happened, Timmy? Why are you crying?" "The boy stole my truck," Timmy said. "He hurt my feelings." Timmy's mom hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. We'll get your truck back. Let's go talk to the boy and ask him to give it back." They went to the mean boy and asked him to give Timmy's truck back. The boy said sorry and gave the truck back to Timmy. Timmy felt happy again and hugged his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little player named Tim. Tim loved to play with his ball every day. He would kick it, throw it, and bounce it all around the yard. One day, Tim's ball rolled into the forest. Tim was scared, but he wanted his ball back. He went into the forest and found a big, angry bear. The bear said, "This is my ball now!" Tim was sad, but he had an idea. He said to the bear, "If you give me my ball back, I will be your friend and we can play together." The bear thought about it and decided to give the ball back to Tim. From that day on, Tim and the big, angry bear became friends. They played together every day and the bear was not angry anymore. They had so much fun and all the animals in the forest would come and watch them play.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They saw some flowers and trees that were very pretty and colorful. "Look, mom, the flowers are growing!" Lily said, pointing at a red rose. "Yes, they are, sweetie. Do you know how they grow?" Mom asked. "From water and sun?" Ben guessed. "That's right, and from the soil too. The soil has food for the plants. But too much water can be bad for them." Mom explained. "Why?" Lily wondered. "Because too much water can make a flood. A flood is when water covers everything and makes it wet and muddy. It can hurt the plants and the animals and the people." Mom said. "Oh no, that sounds scary!" Ben said. "It is, but don't worry. We have a safe place to go if there is a flood. We can go to the big hill where the water can't reach us." Mom said. "OK, mom. Can we play some more?" Lily asked. "Sure, but be careful. Don't go near the pond. There might be unknown things in the water." Mom warned. "Unknown things? Like what?" Ben asked. "I don't know, maybe fish or frogs or snakes. Some of them might be friendly, but some of them might be dangerous. It's better to stay away from them." Mom said. "OK, mom. We will stay away from the unknown things." Ben and Lily said. They played some more, but they always listened to their mom and stayed away from the pond. They had fun and learned something new. They loved the park and the flowers and the trees. They hoped there would never be a flood.

Once upon a time, there was a witch who had a garden. The witch wanted to make it even more beautiful, and so she decided to spray it with a special potion. The witch carefully put the potion in her spray bottle, and then went to the garden. She started spraying the potion everywhere, but some of it went in the wrong direction! The wind blew the spray in a special way, and before long a big rainbow was in the sky! Everyone was amazed to see such a beautiful sight! The witch was very happy, and had enough potion spray left for everyone to enjoy. She made it available for everyone to use, so that she could make rainbows in the sky even more often!

Lena and Tom are friends. They like to play pretend. Today they want to be superheroes. They have masks and capes. They run and jump in the park. "Look, Tom, a bad guy!" Lena says. She points to a man with a bag. The man is running away from a shop. He did not pay for the things in the bag. He is a thief. "Let's stop him, Lena!" Tom says. He and Lena run after the man. They shout, "Stop, thief! Give back the things!" The man is scared. He sees the kids with masks and capes. He thinks they are real superheroes. He drops the bag and runs away. Lena and Tom pick up the bag. They bring it back to the shop. The shop lady is happy. She thanks them and gives them a candy each. "You are very brave and kind, kids," she says. "You are true superheroes." Lena and Tom smile. They eat their candy. They are proud and happy. They have fun playing pretend. They are lively and smart.

Mira and Ravi are twins. They like to play with toys and books. But they do not like to share. Sometimes they fight and slap each other. One day, Mira finds a violin in the attic. It is big and shiny. She wants to play with it. She takes it to her room and tries to make sounds. But the violin is hard to play. It makes loud and ugly noises. Ravi hears the noises and comes to see. He sees Mira with the violin. He wants to play with it too. He says, "Give me the violin. It is mine." Mira says, "No, it is mine. I found it first. Go away." Ravi says, "That is not fair. You have to share. Let me try it." Mira says, "No, you will break it. It is delicate. You are clumsy." They start to argue and pull the violin. They slap each other. The violin falls to the floor and breaks. It makes a loud and sad sound. Mira and Ravi stop fighting. They look at the broken violin. They feel sorry and scared. They know they did something bad. They hug each other and cry. They hear their mom coming. They hide the violin under the bed. They hope she will not find out. They say, "We are sorry. We love each other. We will not fight again."

Ben was sad. He had a hard day at school. He did not like his file. His file had many papers with red marks. His teacher said he had to do better. Ben felt bad. He came home and ran to his room. He did not want to talk to anyone. He lay on his bed and cried. He hugged his teddy bear. His teddy bear was soft and warm. He liked his teddy bear. His mom knocked on his door. She opened it and saw Ben. She smiled and sat on his bed. She stroked his hair and kissed his cheek. She said, "What's wrong, Ben? Why are you sad?" Ben showed her his file. He said, "Look, mom. I have many red marks. I am not good at school. I am dumb." His mom shook her head. She said, "No, Ben. You are not dumb. You are smart and kind and brave. You can do anything you want. You just need to practice more and ask for help when you need it. I am proud of you, Ben. I love you." She hugged him and comforted him. She said, "Do you want to read a story with me? I have a new book for you. It is about a boy who goes on an adventure with his teddy bear." Ben nodded. He wiped his tears and smiled. He said, "Yes, mom. I want to read with you. Thank you, mom. I love you too." They went to the living room and sat on the couch. His mom opened the book and read to him. Ben listened and looked at the pictures. He felt happy and safe. He cuddled with his teddy bear and his mom. He forgot about his hard day and his file. He dreamed of his adventure.

Once there was a boy named Jack who loved to do silly things. One day, after finishing his dinner, he found his old wallet and he thought it would be fun to take it outside and play with it. So he ran with it in his hands and thought he was having a wonderful time. Suddenly he heard a voice calling him. When he looked up, he saw Mother, who was looking at him with a stern face. "Jack, what do you think you're doing?", she asked. Jack explained that he was just having a little fun with his wallet. Mother shook her head and said, "We don't believe in playing with wallets. That's silly. You should put it away and come inside the house." Jack nodded and said he was sorry. He put away his wallet, and ran inside. He was still a bit sad but he knew that Mother was right. His wallet was not a toy. He needed to believe in what she said.

One winter day, Jack and his mom were going to celebrate his third birthday. He was so excited he put on his mittens and went outside to play in the snow. Jack found a friend there and they started playing together. His mom was watching from afar, feeling happy and generous. Suddenly, the friend stumbled and the mitten slipped off Jack's hand. Jack said to his mom: "Mommy, my mitten is gone!" She quickly replied: "It's okay. Let's find it!" He looked everywhere but couldn't find it anywhere. His mom then said: "I'm sorry, Jack. We'll have to say goodbye to your mitten. Let's be generous and give a sincere wish for whoever finds it." Jack was sad, but they both celebrated his birthday, even though he had no mitten. Jack learned the importance of being generous and wishing the best to the ones you hold dear.

Tim was very happy. He had a new pair of pants. They were blue and soft and had a big pocket. He wanted to show them to his friends at school. He put them on and ran to the bus. At school, Tim saw his friends. They were playing with blocks and cars and dolls. Tim said, "Look at my new pants! They are blue and soft and have a big pocket!" His friends looked at his pants. They liked them. They said, "Wow, Tim, your pants are very nice! Can we touch them? Can we see your pocket?" Tim said, "Yes, you can touch them and see my pocket. But be careful. Don't make them dirty or tear them." His friends nodded. They touched his pants and looked at his pocket. They said, "Your pants are very soft. Your pocket is very big. You can put many things in it." Tim was very proud. He said, "Thank you, friends. You are very kind. Do you want to see what I have in my pocket?" His friends said, "Yes, yes, please show us!" Tim smiled. He reached into his pocket and pulled out a frog. His friends gasped. They saw the frog. It was green and slimy and had big eyes. It croaked and jumped. Tim said, "This is my frog. His name is Bob. I found him in the pond. He is my friend. He likes my pants. Do you like him?" His friends did not like the frog. They were scared and disgusted. They screamed and ran away. They said, "Ew, Tim, a frog! That is gross! That is not a good thing to have in your pocket! That is not a friend! That is a pest! Go away, Tim, go away!" Tim was very sad. He did not understand. He liked his frog. He thought his friends would like him too. He wanted to play with them. He wanted them to applaud him and his frog. But they did not. They hated him and his frog. They left him alone. Tim cried. He hugged his frog. He said, "Don't worry, Bob. I still like you. You are still my friend. You are not a pest. You are a good frog. You like my pants. They are still blue and soft and have a big pocket." But his pants were not blue and soft and have a big pocket anymore. The frog had peed and pooped in his pocket. The pee and the poop had made his pants wet and smelly and stained. They had also made a hole in his pocket. The hole was big and clear. Everyone could see it. Tim did not see the hole. He did not smell the pee and the poop. He did not feel the wet and the stain. He only felt his frog and his tears. He did not know that his pants were ruined. He did not know that his day was ruined. He did not know that his new pants were the worst pants ever.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Jane. She was feeling very miserable. One day as she was lying in her bedroom, she heard something outside her window. It was a scratching sound. She got out of bed and opened the window to reveal a little cat standing on the window ledge. Jane was so surprised, she asked the cat, "What are you doing outside my window?". The cat replied, "I'm feeling very cold and hungry. Can I come inside your bedroom?". Jane was so happy to see the cat and she quickly opened the window. The cat jumped inside and snuggled up beside Jane. She felt much better with her new friend. From that day onwards, Jane was never so miserable again. The cat remained by her side and was a loyal companion.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely bookcase. It stood in a big room with no friends. The bookcase was sad and wanted to play. One day, a fast car came into the room. The car saw the lonely bookcase and said, "Hi, bookcase! I see you are lonely. Do you want to play with me?" The bookcase was very happy and said, "Yes, I would love to play with you." The car and the bookcase played all day. The car would speed around the room and the bookcase would watch and laugh. They became best friends and the bookcase was not lonely anymore. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a boy, Jack, and a girl, Jane. The two of them decided to go for a walk one day. "Let's go to the park," said Jane. "Yeah, let's go," replied Jack. When the two arrived, they saw something high up in a tree. "What is that?" asked Jack. "It's an arm," Jane said. Jack was worried because he wanted to get the arm out of the tree. "I don't know how we can reach it," he said. Jane then had an idea. "Let's part the branches!" she suggested. So Jack and Jane parted the branches and soon they could reach the arm. They both grabbed it and brought it down. "Hurrah!" they shouted. The two of them had saved the day.

This morning was a beautiful one. The sun was shining and all the animals were awake in the park. One of them was a little puppy. He was so excited to go and explore. He started to sniff around and mark his territory. He was using special smells so he could come back here later. He went around and found a dry patch of grass which he liked. He lay down and made a soft bed for him to sleep in. The puppy started to feel a bit hungry. His nose twitched as he smelled something in the air. Suddenly, he saw a bowl of crunchy treats. He gobbled them up and soon he was full and happy. He laid down again and drifted off to sleep in the warmth of the sun. What a wonderful day it had been!

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to drink. She would go to the river every day and take a sip of the cool, clear water. One day, she decided to go further and explore beyond the river. As she was walking, she spotted something unusual and shiny in the tall grass. She looked closer and discovered it was a suit! The suit was very rare and made of a beautiful sparkly fabric. The little girl was so excited! She had never seen such a wonderful suit before. She quickly put it on and headed off down the path. As she was walking, she grew thirsty. She went back to the river to take a drink. However, the suit was so special that it kept her dry. The girl couldn't believe it! The little girl was so happy to own such a rare and wonderful suit. From that day on, wherever she went, she was always dry-and always had something to drink!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went outside to play with her friends. They played hide-and-seek, tag, and other fun games. Suddenly, Lily saw something very attractive. It was a symbol on the ground that looked like a star. Lily called her friends over to see the symbol. "Look, look!" she said. "See the pretty star?" Her friends came over and looked at the symbol too. "Wow, that's so cool!" they said. But then, something strange happened. The ground began to freeze around the symbol. "Brrr, it's so cold!" Lily said. "Let's go inside and get some hot cocoa." And so, they went inside and warmed up while they talked about the attractive symbol they had found.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a crab walking on the ground. The crab had big claws, but Lily knew it was harmless. "Hello, Mr. Crab," said Lily. "What are you doing here?" "I'm just walking around," replied the crab. "But I'm looking for a place to bloom." "Bloom?" asked Lily. "What does that mean?" "It means to grow and become beautiful," said the crab. Lily thought for a moment and then said, "Oh, I want to bloom too!" The crab smiled and said, "Everyone can bloom, as long as they have a kind heart." From that day on, Lily learned to be kind to everyone she met. And just like the crab, she bloomed into a beautiful person.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ponies and wanted one for her own. One day, she asked her mom, "Can I have a little pony, please?" Her mom said, "Sure, but you have to take care of it and help it grow." Lily was so happy and took good care of her little pony. She fed it and brushed its fur every day. Her pony grew bigger and stronger each day. One day, Lily's friend came over and said, "Wow, your pony is so big now!" Lily replied, "Yes, I helped it grow!" The moral of the story is that if you take care of something, it will grow and become strong. And if you ask nicely, sometimes you can get what you want.

Once upon a time, there was a brave sailor who wanted to unite the world. He wanted everyone to get along. But it was hard. The sailor took a long journey across the sea. He got on his tall ship, full of hope and determination. He encountered lots of storms along his way. But with each one, he stayed strong and kept going. He wanted to find peace for everyone. He wanted everyone to come together and be friends. Finally, after a long, hard journey, the sailor arrived at his destination. Everyone he met was able to unite and be kind to one another. They all shared the same goal now. The sailor felt proud that he was able to bring people together. The end!

Once upon a time, there was a young rabbit who lived in a land full of green grass and tall trees. One day, the rabbit was hopping around when he saw a bird's nest on the ground. The young rabbit felt sad for the little birds who lost their home. He thought about how he could help them, and then he had an idea. He went to collect some soft leaves and sticks and built a new nest for the birds. The young rabbit was happy to see the birds happy in their new home. The moral of the story is that sometimes things get broken or lost, but we can always replace them with something new and better.

Sam and Mia liked to play golf with their dad. He gave them each a small stick and a ball. They went to a big field with holes in the ground. Dad showed them how to hit the ball with the stick and make it go into the hole. Sam was good at golf. He hit the ball hard and far. He made it go into the hole in a few tries. He was happy and proud. He said, "Look, dad, I am great at golf!" Mia was not so good at golf. She hit the ball softly and near. She missed the hole many times. She was sad and angry. She said, "I hate golf, it is too hard!" Sam saw Mia was upset. He wanted to make her feel better. He said, "Don't worry, Mia, you can do it. You just need to practice more. Here, let me help you." He took Mia's stick and ball and showed her how to hold them. He said, "You need to swing the stick like this, and hit the ball like this. Then it will go far and straight." Mia watched Sam and tried to copy him. She swung the stick and hit the ball. But she hit it too hard and in the wrong direction. The ball flew up in the air and hit dad in the head. Dad fell down and said, "Ow, ow, ow!" Sam and Mia ran to dad and said, "Sorry, dad, are you okay?" Dad rubbed his head and said, "I'm okay, don't worry. It was an accident. But you need to be careful when you play golf. You need to look where you hit the ball and not kick it too hard. Golf is a fun game, but you need to follow the rules and be respectful of others." Sam and Mia nodded and said, "We understand, dad. We are sorry we hurt you. We will be more careful next time. We love you, dad." Dad smiled and said, "I love you too, kids. Now, let's go home and have some ice cream. You both did great today."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her family. One day, Lily's mom told her that they were going to celebrate her dad's birthday. Lily was very excited because she loved birthdays. On the day of the party, Lily and her family decorated the house with balloons and streamers. They even put a big sign on the roof that said "Happy Birthday, Dad!" But when Lily looked up at the roof, she saw that it was filthy with dirt and leaves. She pointed it out to her mom and said, "Mommy, the roof is dirty." Her mom replied, "Oh no! We can't have a dirty roof for the party. Let's clean it up." So, Lily and her mom got a ladder and some soap and water. They climbed up to the roof and scrubbed it clean. When they were finished, Lily said, "Wow, the roof looks so much better now!" Later that day, Lily's dad arrived and everyone shouted, "Happy Birthday!" They ate cake and sang songs. Lily was so happy that they were able to celebrate her dad's birthday in a clean and beautiful house.

Lily liked to read novels. She had many novels in her room. She liked to look at the words and the pictures. She liked to make up stories in her head. One day, Lily found a new novel on her bed. It was green and had a big dragon on the cover. Lily was very happy. She wanted to read the novel right away. She opened the novel and started to read. But then, her brother Tom came into her room. Tom was naughty. He liked to take Lily's things and make her angry. He saw the green novel and wanted to have it. "Give me that novel!" Tom said. He grabbed the novel from Lily's hands. "No, Tom! It's mine! Mom gave it to me!" Lily said. She tried to get the novel back. They pulled and pushed and fought over the novel. They made a lot of noise. "Stop it, you two!" Mom said. She heard them from downstairs. She came into Lily's room. She saw them fighting over the green novel. "What are you doing?" Mom asked. She was angry. "Tom took my novel!" Lily said. She screamed. "No, I want it!" Tom said. He screamed. Mom took the novel from them. She looked at the cover. She saw the dragon. "This is not a novel for you. This is a novel for me. It's my novel. I put it on your bed by mistake. It's too scary for you. You can't read it." Mom said. Lily and Tom were surprised. They looked at Mom. They looked at the novel. They felt silly. "Sorry, Mom." Lily said. "Sorry, Mom." Tom said. Mom smiled. She gave them a hug. "It's okay. I have other novels for you. You can read them together. But no more fighting, okay?" Mom said. "Okay, Mom." Lily and Tom said. They went to the shelf and picked out some novels. They sat on the bed and read them together. They did not fight. They did not scream. They were happy.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Lily and Sam. They were playing with a golf ball when Sam started to sneeze. Lily giggled and said, "Oh Sam, why did you sneeze?" Sam replied, "I don't know, it was so silly!" They decided to keep playing with the golf ball and they had lots of fun. Whenever Sam sneezed, Lily would let out a laugh and then they would keep playing. Eventually, they got tired and decided to go home. Before they left, Lily said to Sam "Remember, it's okay to sneeze, even if it's silly!" Then they said goodbye and went on their way.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Benny. Benny loved to explore the forest and find new things to play with. One day, Benny saw a big cave in the distance. He became curious and wanted to check it out. As he walked closer to the cave, he started to feel scared. It was dark and he couldn't see anything inside. But Benny was brave and wanted to see what was inside the cave. Slowly, Benny walked into the cave and saw that it was filled with shiny rocks and crystals. He wasn't scared anymore and spent the rest of the day exploring the cave and collecting rocks to take home. Benny was happy he overcame his fear and found something new to play with.

Sara liked to eat toast with jam for breakfast. She liked to spread the jam with her knife and make it cover the whole toast. She did not like to leave any white spots. She also liked to cut her toast into small pieces and eat them one by one. One morning, Sara was making her toast when she heard a loud noise outside. She ran to the window and saw a big truck with a deep hole in the back. The truck was full of dirt and rocks. Sara wondered what the truck was doing. She asked her mom, who was in the kitchen. "Mom, what is that truck for?" Sara said. "That truck is for digging a new pool in our backyard, honey," Mom said. "Remember, we talked about it yesterday? We are going to have a lot of fun in the summer." Sara nodded. She remembered that Mom and Dad had told her that they were going to build a pool for her and her brother. She was very excited. She wanted to swim and splash and play with her toys in the water. Sara went back to her toast. She finished spreading the jam and cutting the pieces. She was about to take a bite when she heard another loud noise. She looked out the window again and saw the truck dumping the dirt and rocks into the hole. She gasped. She saw something shiny and red in the dirt. It looked like her favorite toy car. The one that Dad had given her for her birthday. "Mom, Mom, look!" Sara cried. "My car, my car! It's in the dirt!" Mom came to the window and saw the car too. She frowned. She remembered that Sara had left it outside yesterday and had forgotten to bring it in. "Oh, Sara, I'm sorry," Mom said. "That was your car. It must have been in the grass and the truck picked it up. We can't get it back now. It's buried under the dirt." Sara felt a big lump in her throat. She felt tears in her eyes. She loved her car. She did not want to lose it. She did not care about the pool anymore. She only wanted her car. She dropped her toast on the plate and ran to her room. She threw herself on her bed and sobbed. She wished she had taken better care of her car. She wished she had not left it outside. She wished the truck had not taken it away. She hugged her pillow and covered her face.
