She did not want to see anything. She did not want to hear anything. She did not want to eat anything. She only wanted her car.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy wanted a new toy, so she went to the toy shop. In the shop, she saw a big bow. She wanted it very much and asked her Dad if she could have it. Her dad said yes, so Daisy was very happy. Daisy dad paid for the bow, and before they left the shop, Daisy hugged it and thanked him for buying it. He smiled as he watched her. Back at home, Daisy played with the bow every day. She loved it and it was very reliable. She could always depend on it to make her smile. Daisy was very glad that her dad had paid for the bow. She would never forget his kindness.

Mum and Dad took their little girl out for a walk. The sky had gone grey and the wind was getting stronger. Suddenly, lightning struck and little girl became scared. "Mum, what was that?" asked the little girl. "It's lightning," said Mum. "But don't worry, we're safe." The wind blew and the sky grew darker. The little girl started to cry, but Mum and Dad tried to cheer her up. Suddenly, lightning struck again, brighter this time and closer. The little girl screamed and Mum and Dad picked her up and ran. They ran and ran until they found shelter. But the lightning followed them and it became too much for the little girl. She closed her eyes and the lightning struck one last time, taking her away. Mum and Dad cried and held each other close, mourning the loss of their little girl.

Lila was a little girl who liked to play in the park. She had a toy lion that she took with her everywhere. She loved her lion very much and pretended it was her friend. One day, she saw a big sign in the park that said "Rare Animals Show". She was curious and wanted to see the rare animals. She asked her mom if they could go, and her mom said yes. They walked to the show and saw many different animals. Lila saw a snake, a monkey, a parrot, and a zebra. She was amazed and happy. Then she saw a real lion in a cage. It was big and yellow and had a long mane. It looked like her toy lion, but much bigger and scarier. Lila wanted to see it closer, so she ran to the cage. Her mom shouted "Lila, wait! Don't go near the lion!" But Lila did not listen. She thought the lion was friendly and wanted to play with her. She reached the cage and said "Hello, lion. Do you want to be my friend? I have a toy lion like you. See?" She held up her toy lion and showed it to the real lion. The real lion saw the toy lion and growled. It did not like the toy lion. It thought it was a rival and wanted to attack it. It jumped at the cage and tried to grab the toy lion. Lila was scared and dropped her toy lion. The real lion caught the toy lion in its mouth and tore it apart. Lila cried and screamed. Her mom ran to her and hugged her. She said "Lila, I'm sorry. You should have listened to me. The lion is not a friend. It is a wild animal. It can hurt you and your toy. You should never go near a wild animal. You should relax and stay safe." Lila learned a hard lesson that day. She lost her toy lion and her trust in the real lion. She realized that not all animals are friendly and that she should obey her mom. She wished she had relaxed and played with her toy lion in the park instead of going to the show. She was sad and sorry. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big red ball. It bounced around all day and made the children very happy. One day, a naughty dog came and bit the ball. The ball got a big knot and couldn't bounce anymore. The children were sad and demanded the dog to say sorry. The dog felt bad and licked the ball to make it better. The children were happy again and played with the ball all day long.

Once there were two frogs who lived in a green closet. Their names were Dave and Lulu. Dave and Lulu were always fighting. Even though they were good friends, they still argued a lot. One day, Dave and Lulu started fighting again. They were hopping around the closet and shouting at each other. Dave wanted to go play outside, and Lulu wanted to stay inside and think. They just couldn't agree. Eventually, Dave decided to take a nap. Lulu was tired too, so she crept over and lay down next to him. As the two friends drifted off to sleep, the quarrel was forgotten. In the morning, Dave and Lulu hopped out of the closet. They went outside and had a wonderful day playing. Even though they fought sometimes, they still loved being friends.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play at the park. They like to go on the slide. The slide is big and fun. One day, Anna is sick. She has to stay at home. She cannot go to the park. She cannot play with Ben. She is sad. She misses Ben. She misses the slide. Ben goes to the park. He looks for Anna. He does not see her. He asks his mom. His mom says Anna is sick. She says Anna has to rest. Ben is sad. He misses Anna. He misses playing with her. Ben decides to go on the slide. He climbs up the ladder. He sits on the top. He looks at the slide. The slide is dirty. There is mud and leaves on it. Ben does not like the dirty slide. He likes the clean slide. He wishes Anna was here. She would help him clean the slide. Ben hears a voice. It is Anna. She says, "Hi, Ben!" Ben looks down. He sees Anna. She is standing by the slide. She is smiling. She says, "I feel better. My mom said I can come to the park. I brought a towel. We can clean the slide together." Ben is happy. He slides down. He hugs Anna. He says, "I missed you, Anna. I missed playing with you. Let's clean the slide. Then we can have fun." Anna and Ben clean the slide. They wipe off the mud and the leaves. They make the slide clean and shiny. They take turns going on the slide. They laugh and have fun. They are happy. They do not miss anything. They have each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the store with her mommy to buy some fruits. When they arrived at the store, Lily saw a toy that she really wanted. She asked her mommy if she could have it, but her mommy said it was too expensive and they couldn't afford it. Lily was sad and started to cry. A nice old lady who was standing nearby saw Lily crying and whispered to her, "Don't be afraid, little one. Everything has a price, but not everything is worth it." Lily stopped crying and looked at the old lady, confused. The old lady continued, "The toy may be expensive, but it won't make you happy for long. You have to learn to be happy with what you have." Lily listened to the old lady and stopped crying. She realized that her mommy was right and that the toy wasn't worth the price. From that day on, Lily learned to be happy with what she had and never asked for expensive toys again. The moral of the story is that sometimes the things we want are not worth the price and we should learn to be happy with what we have.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful cat. The cat was very happy. One day, the cat found a marble. The marble was very pretty. The cat liked the marble a lot. The cat played with the marble every day. The cat was very careful with the marble. But one day, the cat saw a big dog. The cat was scared. The cat started to tremble. The cat ran away from the dog. The cat was still trembling. The cat dropped the marble. The marble broke. The cat was very sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a squirrel living in the forest. Every day, the squirrel would go out and look for food. One day, the squirrel saw something glimmering amongst the trees. When he got closer, he realised it was a recorder. He picked it up and played with it, trying to record different sounds like the birds singing or the wind blowing in the trees. The next day, the squirrel heard the little boy who lived in the nearby village calling out his name. He quickly ran away and hid in a tree, feeling guilty but not sure why. The little boy saw the squirrel and started to follow him. When the boy realised the squirrel was carrying something in his hands, he shouted: "Hey squirrel! Give that recorder back!" The squirrel stopped and looked at the little boy guiltily. He didn't want to give it back, but he knew he had to. He carefully placed it in the boy's hands and the boy smiled. "Thank you, squirrel!" the little boy said. "I'm glad you were honest and gave it back." The squirrel nodded and ran away happily, knowing that he had done the right thing.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the kitchen with Mom. Mom is making a salad for lunch. She has a big green fruit. It is an avocado. "Can I help, Mom?" Sara asks. She wants to cut the avocado. "Sure, sweetie. But be careful. The knife is sharp. You need to lean on the table and hold the avocado with your hand. Like this." Mom shows Sara how to cut the avocado. Ben watches Sara and Mom. He is curious. He wants to taste the avocado. He reaches for a piece on the plate. "Ben, no!" Mom says. "The avocado is not ready yet. It needs some salt and lemon. Wait a minute, please." But Ben does not listen. He puts the avocado in his mouth. He makes a face. He does not like it. It is soft and bland. "Yuck!" Ben says. He spits out the avocado. "This is not good, Mom. This is not a fruit. This is a vegetable." Mom laughs. She hugs Ben. "No, honey. This is not a vegetable. This is a fruit. But it is a special fruit. It is not sweet like an apple or a banana. It is creamy and healthy. Some people like it, some people don't. It's okay if you don't like it. You can try something else." Sara smiles. She likes the avocado. She sprinkles some salt and lemon on it. She takes a bite. She thinks it is delicious. "Can I have more, Mom?" Sara asks. "This is a good fruit. I like it." Mom nods. She gives Sara more avocado. She is happy that Sara likes it. She hopes that Ben will like it too, someday. She thinks that avocado is a good fruit for twins.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went on a walk with her mommy in the park. They saw a big dog with a shiny collar. The dog was wagging its tail and looked very friendly. Lily said, "Mommy, can we go pet the dog? He looks interesting." Mommy said, "Sure, but be careful. You can pet him, but don't lead him away from his owner." Lily went up to the dog and petted him. But after a few minutes, she started to itch. She said, "Mommy, my arm itches. Maybe the dog has fleas." Mommy said, "Let's go wash your hands and put some cream on it. We don't want you to be uncomfortable." Lily and her mommy walked away from the dog, and Lily said, "That was fun! I like petting dogs, but I don't like the itch."

Once upon a time, there was an ancient style of wagon. It had been made many years ago, but it still looked very sharp. It had bright yellow paint, with a wood frame and big, sturdy wheels. One day, a three year old child found the wagon. She was very excited! She ran up to it and began petting it. She liked how glossy and smooth the yellow paint felt. The child wanted to take the wagon for a ride. She looked around, but she could not find anyone to help her. That did not stop her! With determination and practice, she managed to figure out how to move the wagon by herself. The little girl was so happy, she pushed the wagon for a long time around the garden. She loved the feeling of the grass tickling her feet as she rolled around. Finally, she got back to the wagon and stopped. She had enjoyed her magical ride. She looked back at it one more time, admiring its ancient style and how sharp it looked. The child smiled and waved to the wagon as she left. Goodnight, ancient wagon!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her serve lunch. Timmy was happy to help his mom. As they were walking to the picnic area, Timmy accidentally dropped his sandwich on the ground. He felt sorry and picked it up quickly. His mom told him it was okay and they found a new spot to sit and eat. After lunch, Timmy and his friends played a game of tag. They ran around and around until they were tired. Timmy's mom called him over and asked him to help clean up the trash. Timmy served as a good helper and picked up all the trash he could find on the ground. At the end of the day, Timmy felt happy that he was able to serve his mom and the park by cleaning up the ground. He went home with a smile on his face and a sense of accomplishment. The end.

Lily was a 3-year-old who wanted to help out with the housework. She had noticed her mom cleaning the mild cabinet in the kitchen and wanted to help. So she requested something nice, "Mommy, can I clean the cabinet too?" Her mom smiled and said, "I'm sorry, Lily, but it's too complicated for you to do. You might break something if you try." Lily was determined to help. She thought for a moment and then requested something different, "Can I just put away the things in the cabinet?" This request was accepted and her mom showed her where to put everything. Lily worked hard and when she was done the cabinet looked nice and tidy. Her mom complimented her hard work and Lily was so proud. She had conquered the mild cabinet!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the circus. He had a ticket for the circus in his pocket. One day, Timmy and his mommy went to the circus. Timmy was so excited! He held his ticket tightly in his hand. As they walked to their seats, Timmy accidentally dropped his ticket. It fell on the ground and broke into many pieces. Timmy started to cry. His mommy hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. We will go to the ticket booth and get a new ticket." Timmy smiled and felt happy again. They got a new ticket and enjoyed the circus together.

John was playing in the garden. He was looking for something fun to do. Suddenly, he spotted something sparkly in the grass. It was a crystal! He scooped it up and ran inside to show his parents. John held up the crystal and said "look! I found it!" His mom and dad looked amazed. They asked him where he had found it. John pointed at the garden and said "outside". John's parents were very excited. They told him that the crystal was very special and it was made of something called quartz. They said it looked new and very valuable. John realized that this was a very special crystal. He was so happy that he found the new crystal in the garden. He gave it a big hug and smiled. John's mom could see how happy he was and gave him a little hug. She said "this is your crystal now, and you should take care of it forever". John smiled and gave the crystal a special place in his bedroom. John couldn't believe his luck. He was so excited that he gave the crystal a little kiss and went to bed with a big smile.

Ben and Lily are playing with blocks. They like to make big buildings with many blocks. They put blocks on top of blocks, and make towers and walls and bridges. "Look at my building!" Ben says. "It is very high and strong. It can touch the sky!" Lily looks at Ben's building. She thinks it is too high and not strong. She wants to make her building higher and stronger. She takes some blocks from Ben's building and puts them on her building. "Hey, stop!" Ben says. "Those are my blocks! Give them back!" Lily does not listen. She takes more blocks from Ben's building and puts them on her building. Ben's building gets smaller and smaller. Lily's building gets bigger and bigger. "Look at my building now!" Lily says. "It is higher and stronger than yours. It can touch the stars!" Ben is angry. He pushes Lily's building with his hand. Lily's building is not strong. It has too many blocks. It cannot stand. It falls down with a loud noise. Blocks go everywhere. Some blocks hit Lily and Ben. They hurt. "Ow!" Lily says. "That was not nice! You made my building fall!" "Ow!" Ben says. "You took my blocks! You made my building small!" Lily and Ben are both sad and mad. They cry. They do not want to play with blocks anymore. They do not want to play with each other anymore. Mom hears the noise and comes to see. She sees the blocks and the tears. She hugs Lily and Ben. "What happened?" Mom says. "Why are you crying?" "Lily took my blocks and made my building small!" Ben says. "Ben pushed my building and made it fall!" Lily says. Mom looks at the blocks. She sees some blocks are open. They have holes in them. She has an idea. "I'm sorry you are sad and mad," Mom says. "But maybe you can play with the blocks in a different way. Look, some blocks are open. You can put things inside them. You can make boxes and baskets and cars and trains. You can share the blocks and play together. Do you want to try?" Lily and Ben stop crying. They look at the open blocks. They think Mom's idea is good. They say sorry to each other. They take the open blocks and put things inside them. They make boxes and baskets and cars and trains. They share the blocks and play together. They have fun. "Look at our blocks!" Lily says. "They are not buildings, but they are still nice. We can make many things with them!" "Look at our blocks!" Ben says. "They are not high, but they are still strong. We can play with them for a long time!" Mom smiles. She is happy. She sees Lily and Ben are happy too. She sees they learned something new. She sees they are friends again. She says, "I'm proud of you. You are very smart and kind. I love you."

Once upon a time, there was a cold winter day. Mary was walking in the park when she came across a young boy. He was chewing on a pink measure. Mary asked him why he was eating the measure. The boy looked up and said, "My mommy gave it to me, and she said it would measure how much cold I can handle!" Mary was intrigued, so she asked the boy what he was supposed to do next. The boy said, "I'm supposed to chew the measure until it breaks. Then I'll know how much cold I can take!" Mary smiled and said, "That's a great idea! Good luck with the measuring!" The boy happily smiled and continued to chew on the measure. He slowly but surely was able to break it and prove to himself how much cold he could take.

Once upon a time there was a baby bear named Bob. He loved to go outside and explore. One day, he went to an old tree. He felt something soft on the tree's bark. He rubbed it and the bark began to move. It was an original creature! Bob was so excited. He wanted to find out what it was. He followed it into a cave at the bottom of the tree. Inside the cave, he saw a big creature that looked just like the one from the tree. It was a friendly dragon. The dragon offered to take Bob on a magical journey. Bob said yes and the dragon flew away with him. They went high up in the sky and beyond. Bob had so much fun flying around with the dragon. At the end of the day, the dragon brought Bob back to the tree. Bob hugged the dragon and thanked it for the wonderful adventure. The dragon smiled and said goodbye. Bob rubbed the original creature one more time. He said goodbye and went home. He never forgot the magical journey he shared with the dragon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved toys and he always wondered where they came from. One day, he asked his mommy, "Where do toys come from?" His mommy smiled and said, "Toys come from a special place called a factory. That's where they make all the toys you love to play with." Timmy's eyes widened with excitement. "Can we go there?" he asked. His mommy nodded and they went on a trip to the toy factory. When they arrived, Timmy was so proud to see all the toys being made. He saw machines moving and workers busy making toys. Suddenly, the workers revealed a new toy they had just made. It was a shiny red car and Timmy couldn't wait to play with it. He was so happy to have learned where toys come from and he couldn't wait to tell his friends all about it.

The sun was shining in the sky and it was a beautiful day. Mom said, "Lets go exploring". So they set off in search of adventure. As they were walking down the path, they saw a big, colorful tree. Mom said, "Look there! A colorful tree." They walked closer and squealed with delight when they saw a big box filled with colorful balls underneath the tree. "Wow, what a surprise! Lets play!", Mom said. The little girl couldn't contain her excitement. She picked up a bright red ball, hugged it and said, "This is the best day ever". Mom smiled, "I think so too". She said. And off they went, hand in hand, exploring with delight.

Tom and Mia were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big cave near the hill. They wanted to see what was inside, but they were nervous. "Let's go in the cave," Tom said. "Maybe we can find something cool." "I don't know," Mia said. "It looks dark and scary. What if there are monsters or bats?" "Don't be afraid," Tom said. "We can number the steps we take, so we can find our way back. I have a flashlight, too. Come on, it will be fun." Mia agreed, but she was still nervous. They held hands and walked into the cave. They counted one, two, three, four, five steps. The cave was cold and quiet. They saw some rocks and some bugs, but nothing else. "Let's go deeper," Tom said. "Maybe there is a treasure or a secret." "OK, but not too far," Mia said. They counted six, seven, eight, nine, ten steps. The cave was darker and louder. They heard some water and some wind, but nothing else. "Let's go back," Mia said. "I don't like it here. It's too spooky." "OK, OK," Tom said. "Let's go back. We can number the steps again, so we don't get lost." They turned around and walked back. They counted ten, nine, eight, seven, six steps. But then, they saw something that made them stop. It was a big bear, blocking the way out. It was growling and showing its teeth. It looked angry and hungry. Tom and Mia were very nervous. They did not know what to do. They screamed and hugged each other. They wished they never went into the cave. They hoped someone would hear them and help them. They hoped the bear would go away. They hoped they would be safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park to play on the swings and slide. One day, she saw a boy who was sad and crying. She asked him why he was sad and he said he was scared because he had to go to court with his mom and dad. Lily didn't know what court was, so she asked her mom. Her mom explained that court is where a lawyer talks to a judge about what is right and wrong. Lily wanted to help the boy feel better, so she told him that he could be brave and that his mom and dad's lawyer would encourage them to do the right thing. The boy stopped crying and smiled at Lily. He said that he felt better and thanked her for being so nice. As they played together, they saw a disgusting bug crawling on the ground. Lily said "Ew, that bug is disgusting!" and the boy laughed. They became good friends and played at the park every day.

John was searching. He searched high and low, and everywhere he looked, he saw nothing. Then suddenly he spotted something on the icy ground. He rushed forward and looked closer. He saw a head! "What is that?" John wondered out loud. Just then, he heard a voice. It said, "That is my head!" John was very surprised. He looked around and saw a monkey sitting close by. "How did your head get here?" John asked. "I was searching for fruit in the icy forest, and I slipped," said the monkey. "My head came off and rolled away! But you found it. Thank you!" John was happy to help. He carefully picked up the monkey's head and put it back on its shoulders. "Now you can go back to searching for fruit," he said. The grateful monkey thanked John once again and then hopped away, searching for his tasty treat.

Lily wanted to buy a new toy. She saw a big doll with long hair and a pink dress in the shop window. She asked her mom to buy it for her. "Maybe later, sweetie. We have to go to the bank first. It won't take long, I promise." Mom said. Lily was impatient. She did not want to go to the bank. She wanted to play with the doll. She pulled mom's hand and said, "Please, mom, please. I want the doll now." Mom sighed. She looked at her watch. She had to pay some bills at the bank. She did not have much time. She said, "Okay, okay. We'll buy the doll first. But you have to be good and stay with me. The bank is not a safe place for little girls." Lily was happy. She smiled and hugged mom. She said, "Thank you, mom, thank you. You are the best mom ever." Mom and Lily went into the shop. Mom paid for the doll and gave it to Lily. Lily hugged the doll and said, "Hello, doll. I'm Lily. You are my new friend." Mom and Lily left the shop. They walked to the bank. Lily held the doll in her arms. She did not notice the man who followed them. He had a mask and a gun. He wanted to rob the bank. He saw mom's purse. He thought it had a lot of money. He decided to take it. He ran after mom and Lily. He grabbed mom's purse. He said, "Give me that. It's mine now." Mom screamed. She tried to get her purse back. She said, "No, no. Leave us alone. Help, help." Lily was scared. She dropped the doll. She cried. She said, "Mom, mom. What's happening?" The man pushed mom to the ground. He ran away with the purse. He did not see the police car that was coming. The police saw him. They chased him. They caught him. They took him to jail. Mom and Lily were safe. The police gave mom her purse back. They said, "Are you okay, ma'am? We're sorry this happened to you. He's a bad man. He won't hurt you anymore." Mom thanked the police. She hugged Lily. She said, "We're okay, sweetie. We're okay. Don't worry. He's gone now." Lily looked for her doll. She saw it on the sidewalk. She ran to get it. She said, "Doll, doll. I'm sorry I dropped you. Are you okay?" The doll was okay. It had a small tear on its dress. Lily did not mind. She said, "It's okay, doll. You are still pretty. I love you." Mom and Lily went home. They did not go to the bank. They did not need to. They had each other. They were happy.

One morning, Jack woke up feeling adventurous. He shouted for his mum, but she was busy. He put on his shoes and went outside. Suddenly, Jack saw a package at his front door. He was excited, but also a bit scared. He got closer to look. Then, the package called out to Jack! "Hey, little Jack!" it said. "Take me with you on your adventures!" Jack hesitated, then he decided to pick up the package and take it with him. They explored the forest and the beach. Jack and the package had a lot of fun. Then, it started to get dark. "It's time to return home now," said the package. Jack sighed, but he knew it was time to go. He said goodbye to the package and went back home. He returned with lots of stories to tell his mum.

John was a little boy who loved the sea. He often went down to the beach to watch the waves crash against the shore. Every time he went he took his special bucket with him. One hot day John and his bucket headed to the beach. John stopped at the edge of the sand and looked out over the sea. He could feel the heat from the warm sand under his feet. He looked up and saw some big seagulls in the sky. John started digging in the sand with his bucket. He scooped up some sand and threw it into the water. It made a splash. John loved the way it sounded and the way it felt when the water ran through his fingers. Suddenly, a voice called out behind him. "That sand belongs in the sea," it said. John turned around and saw an old man smiling at him. "It belongs here," the old man said, pointing to the endless blue expanse of the ocean. John nodded and smiled. He knew he belonged here too. He belonged at the beach, with his bucket and his sand, feeling the heat of the day and looking out to the sea.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were walking in the woods when they saw a turkey. "Let's get the turkey!" said Jack. Jill was scared so she said, "No. That turkey is too fast. We won't be able to get it." Jack didn't give up and said, "I can get the turkey if I run fast." Jack ran fast, but the turkey ran faster. Then something amazing happened. Jack received help from a friendly animal! The animal ran after the turkey and caught it. Jack was very happy and said, "Thank you for helping me get the turkey." The animal smiled and said, "You're welcome. Now you can enjoy the turkey. Have a good day!" Jack and Jill received the turkey and ran home. They had a wonderful dinner that day and were very happy.

Once there was a little girl named Mia. She was three years old and very curious. She wanted to explore the world and learn new things. Mia's parents wanted to help her learn, so they took her on a trip to a distant port. On their trip they included lots of activities. They took a boat ride out to the big ocean. Mia was so excited to see the dolphins swimming nearby. She even saw some whales in the distance. Next, Mia's parents took her to the beach. She made a sandcastle, collected shells and played in the waves. Finally, they visited the port. Mia was amazed at all the boats and ships. It was like a whole new world! She even got to go on a real pirate ship. Mia was so happy that she was included on the family adventure. It was a distant port she will never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named George. He was very gifted and so proud of it. One day, George was running around the park, proud of his agility. Suddenly, he tripped and fell on his toe. He began to cry out in pain and said to his mom, "It hurts! It hurts!" His mother said, "Don't worry, honey. You're very gifted. Nothing will stop you from playing again soon." After much rest, George was able to walk on his sore toe after a few days. He wanted to show off his newfound talent to his friends, so he started running and jumping again. Unfortunately, George's toe was still not completely healed and as he was running, he suddenly felt a sharp pain and fell down again. George was so sad. He knew he would never be able to jump and run around like before. His mother hugged him and told him, "That's okay. You're still very gifted, even if you can't run and jump like before." But George was heart-broken. He had lost his most cherished gift - the gift of running and jumping freely.

Sam likes to test new things. He likes to touch, smell and taste them. He thinks it is fun and easy to learn. One day, Sam finds a big red fruit in the kitchen. He does not know what it is. He picks it up and feels it. It is round and smooth and heavy. He smells it. It has a sweet and sour smell. He wants to taste it. He bites the fruit with his mouth. He feels a squirt of juice on his tongue. It is very sour and makes him pucker his mouth. He does not like it. He spits it out and makes a face. He says, "Yuck!" Mom sees Sam and laughs. She says, "That is a lemon, Sam. It is not for eating by itself. It is for making lemonade or putting on fish. Do you want to try some lemonade?" Sam nods. He likes lemonade. It is sweet and cold and refreshing. Mom cuts the lemon and squeezes it into a pitcher. She adds water and sugar and stirs it. She pours some lemonade into a cup and gives it to Sam. Sam sips the lemonade with his mouth. He likes it. It is not too sour and not too sweet. It makes him smile. He says, "Yum!" Mom smiles too. She says, "You are a good tester, Sam. You are brave and curious. But be careful, some things are not good for your mouth. Always ask me before you test something new, okay?" Sam nods. He hugs Mom and says, "Okay, Mom. I love you. And I love lemonade."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her crayons. One day, she was drawing a picture of a big, red apple when her mom came in the room. Mom: "Wow, Lily! That apple looks so creative. Can you draw me a picture of a banana?" Lily: "Sure, Mommy! I love drawing fruits." As Lily was drawing the banana, she heard an increase in noise outside. She looked out the window and saw that her neighbors were having a party. She wanted to go join the fun, so she asked her mom if she could go. Lily: "Mommy, can I go play with the other kids at the party?" Mom: "Of course, Lily. Just remember to be safe and have fun!" Lily ran outside and joined the other kids. They were playing games, dancing, and making a lot of noise. Lily loved being creative and coming up with new games to play. She had so much fun at the party that she didn't want to leave when it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went on a trip with her mommy and daddy. They had big luggage with them. Lily was very sleepy in the car. She said, "Mommy, I want to sleep." Mommy said, "Okay, Lily. You can sleep in the car." Daddy drove the car slow so Lily could sleep. After a while, Lily woke up and asked, "Are we there yet?" Mommy said, "Not yet, Lily. We still have a long way to go." Lily said, "Okay" and went back to sleep. Finally, they arrived at their destination. Daddy took the luggage out of the car and they went to their hotel. Lily was so excited to see the big bed in their room. She said, "Mommy, can I sleep now?" Mommy said, "Yes, Lily. You can sleep now." And Lily went to sleep in her big comfy bed.

Once upon a time, a poor hedgehog named Jennifer lived deep in the woods. She was very sad because she wasn't rich like the other animals. One day, as Jennifer was walking, she found a sparkly gold coin. Then she heard a distant voice. "Slide that coin over here," said the voice. Jennifer looked and saw a big, glossy fox. He had a long tail and a golden cap. Jennifer slid the coin towards the fox. "I am very rich," the fox said, "and one gold coin won't make a difference. But why don't you have it? Keep it and do something nice for yourself!" Jennifer's eyes lit up with joy. She said thank you and hugged the fox. From then on, whenever Jennifer needed something, she would spend a few coins and feel rich. She would slide her coins to the shopkeeper and smile. The fox was so pleased that he visited Jennifer from time to time with more coins. Jennifer was happy and the fox's tail wagged in joy. The end.

Anna liked to read books. She had many books in her room. She read them every day. She learned new words and stories. She was happy. One day, Anna went to the park with her mom. She saw a big barrel near a tree. It was brown and round. She wondered what was inside. She ran to the barrel and looked in. "Wow!" she said. "There are books in here! So many books!" She picked up a book. It had a pretty picture of a princess on the cover. She opened the book and read the title. "The Princess and the Pea." "Can I read this book, mom?" she asked. "Sure, sweetie," her mom said. "But be careful. Don't get dirty. The barrel is old and dusty." Anna nodded. She sat on the grass and read the book. She liked the story. It was about a princess who slept on many mattresses. But she felt a pea under them. She was very sensitive. The prince knew she was a real princess. Anna smiled. She wanted to be a princess too. She finished the book and put it back in the barrel. She thanked the barrel for the book. She hugged her mom and went home. She had a new story to remember. She was happy.

Tom and Lily like to play with their toy trains. They have a big track that goes around the room. They make the trains go fast and slow, and make noises like choo-choo and beep-beep. One day, Mom says they have to clean up their track. She says it is time for lunch and they have to put away their toys. Tom and Lily do not want to stop playing. They say, "Please, Mom, can we play a little more?" Mom says, "No, you have to eat now. You can play again after lunch. But you have to clean up your track first. It is too messy and someone can trip on it." Tom and Lily are sad and angry. They do not like to clean up. They think it is boring and hard. They say, "No, Mom, we do not want to clean up. We want to play. You are mean and do not allow us to have fun." Mom says, "That is not nice to say. I am not mean. I love you and I want you to be healthy and safe. Cleaning up is part of playing. You have to take care of your toys and your room. If you do not clean up, you will lose your toys and your track. Do you want that?" Tom and Lily think for a moment. They do not want to lose their toys and their track. They like them very much. They say, "No, Mom, we do not want that. We are sorry for being rude. We will clean up our track now. Can you help us?" Mom says, "Yes, I can help you. I am glad you are sorry and you will clean up. That is very good of you. You are my smart and sweet children. Come on, let's do it together. It will not take long. And then we can have lunch and play some more." Tom and Lily smile and hug Mom. They say, "Thank you, Mom. We love you. You are the best." They start to pick up their trains and their track. They put them in a big box. They make a game out of it. They see who can find the most pieces and who can make the neatest pile. They have fun and they finish quickly. They are proud of their work. Mom says, "Wow, you did a great job. I am very proud of you too. You have a very nice track and very nice trains. You are very lucky to have them. And I am very lucky to have you. Now, let's go and have some lunch. I made your favorite sandwiches and juice. And I have a surprise for you too." Tom and Lily say, "What is the surprise, Mom?" Mom says, "You will see. Come on, follow me." Tom and Lily follow Mom to the kitchen. They are curious and excited. They wonder what the surprise is. They hope it is something fun and yummy. They are happy and hungry. They love their Mom and their track and their trains. They are having a good day.

Once upon a time there was a purple mop. The mop lived in a big, pink room. Every morning the mop would wake up ready for the day! The mop would enjoy the bright sunshine that shone through the window and the birds chirping outside. Then, the mop would be ready to start its day. Every morning it would go over to the floor and start to clean. It felt so nice having the floor all clean. After the mop had finished it would sit back,dance around and sing. The purple mop was so happy and enjoyed its days, it wanted to help out around the house all the time. All the people in the house were so pleased they had the purple mop keeping their floors squeaky clean. The days became so much fun for everyone and the purple mop loved being useful. It was a job it was perfect for! So, the purple mop kept waking up every morning to keep the house clean and everyone happy.

Max was a very stubborn 3 year old. He didn't like to share his things or talk to people. One day, he was at the park and he saw a shoe. It was a nice shoe, so he didn't want to share it with anyone. He decided to take it home with him. When he got home, he put the shoe in his room, but his mom found it. She asked him where he got it, but he didn't want to talk about it. He just locked himself in his room and kept the shoe for himself. His mom was very stubborn, too. She asked him over and over again to tell her where he got the shoe, but Max remained tight-lipped. Finally, his mom had to take the shoe away. Max was very sad, but he knew better than to talk about it.

Young Jenny and her adorable bear were walking in the park. Suddenly the bear sneezed. Jenny smiled and hugged him tightly. Then she noticed something was wrong. The bear started to get smaller and smaller! Soon he was so small that he disappeared! Jenny was very sad and couldn't understand what had happened. Her bear had gone forever! Jenny cried and hugged the air and said goodbye to her lost bear. The end.

Once upon a time there was a clever bunny. His name was Jack. He had a special weapon which he used to protect his friends. One silly day, Jack was out walking in the forest with his friends. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise! What was it? "Let me take a look," said Jack bravely. So he bravely grabbed his weapon and ran off to the source of the noise. He found a giant monster! It was big and very scary. The monster shouted, "I will get you!" But Jack bravely held up his weapon and shouted back, "No, you won't! I will protect my friends!" The monster saw that Jack was brave. He knew that he had met his match! So the monster turned and ran away. Jack had saved the day! His silly weapon had protected his friends from the giant monster. From then on, Jack was a hero.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bird. This bird flapped its wings with incredible speed. It whizzed through the air, faster and faster. The dog, who was watching from the ground, was amazed. "How can the bird go so fast?" he wondered. The bird heard the question and flew back down. It smiled at the dog and said, "It's simple. All I do is practice speed every day!" The dog was inspired by the bird. He thought to himself, "Maybe if I practice speed every day, I can fly too!" The bird smiled. "It won't be easy, but I believe you can do it!" The dog loved the challenge and decided to give it a try. He practiced every day and finally, after a few weeks, he began to fly! The dog and the bird were so excited. At last, they were able to soar around the sky together. They were the fastest friends in the world!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom had a long journey ahead of him, so he got up very early one morning. He packed his bag with a heavy lunch and he began walking down the road. Tom walked and walked until he reached a big hill. He was tired, but he kept walking. As he reached the top of the hill, he saw a little town below. Tom was thrilled to reach the town. When he arrived, the town was very busy. People were walking up and down the roads and lights were twinkling in the houses. Tom had never seen a town before and he was very excited. Tom followed the road until it ended. He was very tired from his long walk, but he was also very happy to have reached the town. He knew he had had a long journey, but he was proud of himself for making it there.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl named Mary. Mary was young and very adventurous. She always wanted to go on new adventures. One day, Mary's parents decided to raise a ranch. Mary was excited to help with the new ranch. Every corner of it was an adventure. Even the work seemed like play to Mary. They bought lots of animals to live on the ranch. Mary fed the poultry and went around to check on all the animals. Everyday, she went around exploring the ranch with her parents. She couldn't believe how big the ranch was. One day, Mary made some new friends on the ranch. The animals were so friendly to her. She was so happy and felt like she was part of the ranch now. She was learning how to care for the animals and was so proud. At the end of the day, Mary's parents looked on at their daughter and the ranch with pride. They celebrated Mary's adventurous spirit and the new beginnings at the ranch. Everyone was so happy and excited for the future.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Worry. Worry was a bitter bird because he did not have many friends. He lived in a big tree with other birds, but he was always sad and alone. One day, Worry met a wise old owl named Wisdom. Wisdom saw that Worry was sad and asked, "Why are you so bitter, little bird?" Worry told Wisdom that he was sad because he did not have any friends. Wisdom thought for a moment and said, "To make friends, you must be kind and share with others." Worry listened to Wisdom and decided to try being kind and sharing with the other birds. Soon, Worry found that he had many friends, and he was no longer a bitter bird. Worry was happy, and he thanked Wisdom for helping him learn how to make friends. From that day on, Worry was always kind and shared with others, and he lived happily with his new friends in the big tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her favorite red hat everywhere she went. One day, Lily went to her grandma's house for lunch. Her grandma made a really spicy soup that Lily didn't like. She made a frown on her face and said, "This soup is too spicy for me." Lily's grandma felt sad that Lily didn't like the soup. She wanted to make her happy, so she asked Lily to take off her hat and put it on the table. Then, she put some yummy fruits in the hat. Lily was so happy and smiled again. She loved the fruits and forgot all about the spicy soup. From that day on, Lily always brought her hat to her grandma's house for lunch.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They loved to play together and explore the woods. One day, they found a shiny rock and both wanted to keep it in their pocket. They started to quarrel and argue about who should keep it. Timmy said, "I found it first, so it should be mine!" Tommy replied, "But I helped you find it, so we should share it!" Their argument got louder and louder until they both felt dizzy. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and saw a big bear coming towards them. They quickly forgot about the rock and ran away as fast as they could. After they were safe, they realized that they were still friends and that the rock didn't matter. They hugged each other and promised to never quarrel again. From that day on, they explored the woods together and always shared their treasures.

Once upon a time, there was a gorilla named George. George was very sad because he lost his favorite banana. He looked everywhere for it but couldn't find it. One day, a little girl named Lily came to the jungle. She saw George and asked him why he was sad. George told her about his lost banana. Lily felt sorry for George and decided to help him find it. They searched everywhere but still couldn't find the banana. Suddenly, Lily had an idea. She asked George to throw a coconut at a tree to see if the banana would fall out. George threw the coconut and, to their surprise, the banana fell out of the tree! George was so happy that he hugged Lily and thanked her for helping him. From that day on, George and Lily became good friends and went on many adventures together.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Bob. Bob was only three, so he didn't know very many big words yet. One day his mom said, "Bob, it's time to find a barber!" Bob said, "What's a barber?" His mom smiled, "A barber is someone who adds a new style to your hair." Bob was frightened. He replied, "No, I don't want a new style. I like my hair the way it is." His mom said, "It's okay, Bob. You don't have to be scared. The barber will add a small change. I think you'll like it." So Bob went to visit the barber. He was still a bit scared, but his mom was right - he liked the new style! He left the barber happy and proud of his fancy new hair.

Molly peeked around the corner. She was so curious about what was on the other side. She was a bit fearful but wanted to take a look anyway. Sweat beaded on her forehead, but Molly was determined. Molly tiptoed around the corner and gasped. There was a great mine in front of her. Molly had never seen anything like it before. She found a door and reached out to touch it. As soon as she touched it, the door flew open. Molly was so scared she almost screamed. But then Molly remembered what her mom had taught her: she should never be fearful. Slowly, she stepped inside the mine, feeling a little braver. The inside of the mine was very dark but Molly could make out little piles of colorful stones. They were shiny and so pretty. She picked one up and put it inside her pocket. Molly had never been so brave before. She peeked around the corner again and smiled as she thought of the shiny stones in her pocket. She couldn't wait to show them to her mom and dad.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl called Bonnie. Bonnie lived by the sea and loved to dive and explore the reef. She had a special knife to cut coral and shells from the reef, but one day Bonnie lost her knife. She was so sad and frightened that she had lost her knife and could no longer explore. That night, she lay awake in her bed, worrying about her knife coming back. But the next day, Bonnie heard something in the distance. She got out of bed and went outside - and there it was - her knife! Sitting under the tree with a big smile on her face, Bonnie realised that it was more important to keep the reef safe and not to cut anything without caution. She gave her knife a loving hug, happy that she was back with her best friend.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toy cars on the floor. They have a big box that they pretend is a garage. They take turns to drive their cars in and out of the box. "Can I have your red car, please?" Ben asks Lily. "No, it is mine. You have your blue car," Lily says. "But I like the red car. It is faster and shinier," Ben says. They start to argue and pull the red car from each other. The car breaks in half and falls on the floor. "Oh no! Look what you did!" Lily cries. "I am sorry. It was an accident," Ben says. They feel sad and sorry. They don't want to play anymore. They sit on the floor and look at the broken car. Mom comes in and sees them. She sees the broken car and the empty box. "What happened here?" Mom asks. "We broke the red car. We were fighting over it," Lily says. "We are sorry, Mom. We were not nice to each other," Ben says. Mom hugs them and says, "It is okay. I know you are sorry. But you have to learn to share and take turns. You have many other toys to play with. And you can fix the red car with some glue and tape." She helps them to pick up the pieces of the car and put them in a bag. She gives them some glue and tape and shows them how to fix the car. "Thank you, Mom. You are the best," Lily and Ben say. They work together to fix the red car. They make it look like new. They are happy and proud. They put the red car in the box and give it a tip. They say, "Good job, red car. You are very brave and strong." They smile and hug each other. They decide to share the red car and the blue car. They play nicely and have fun. They are good friends.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they went to the lake with their mom and dad. They saw many things at the lake: fish, ducks, frogs, and a big furry dog. "Can we pet the dog, mom?" Lily asked. "Sure, but be gentle and ask the owner first," mom said. Lily and Ben ran to the dog, who was sitting by a man on a bench. The dog wagged its tail and licked their faces. They giggled and stroked its fur. "Hello, kids. This is Max. He's very friendly," the man said. "Hi, Max. You're so soft and warm," Lily said. "Can we play with Max, please?" Ben asked. "Of course. He loves to play fetch. Here, take this stick and throw it for him," the man said. Lily and Ben took turns throwing the stick and watching Max run after it and bring it back. They had a lot of fun with Max. But then, something bad happened. Ben threw the stick too far, and it landed in the water. Max jumped into the lake and swam to get it. Lily and Ben watched him, but they did not see him come back. "Where's Max?" Lily asked, worried. "I don't know. Maybe he's stuck under the water," Ben said, worried too. They ran to the edge of the lake and looked for Max. They called his name, but he did not answer. "Mom, dad, help! Max is gone!" Lily cried. Mom and dad heard them and came running. They saw the stick floating in the water, but no sign of Max. "Oh no, where's the dog?" mom asked. "He went to get the stick, but he didn't come back," Ben said. "Maybe he's on the other side of the lake," dad said. "Let's go and see." They followed the shore of the lake, hoping to find Max. They searched and searched, but they could not see him. They were about to give up, when they heard a loud bark. They turned around and saw Max, wet and happy, running towards them. He had the stick in his mouth. "Max!" Lily and Ben shouted. They hugged him and kissed him. "Good boy, Max. You're safe," mom said. "Sorry, kids. I didn't mean to scare you. Max is a good swimmer, but he likes to explore. He found a way out of the lake on the other side. He's a smart dog," the man said. "Thank you for letting us play with Max. He's the best dog ever," Lily said. "You're welcome. He likes you too. Maybe we'll see you again at the lake," the man said. Lily and Ben waved goodbye to Max and the man. They were happy that Max was okay. They learned to be careful when playing near the water. They also made a new furry friend.

Once upon a time, there lived a young girl named Abigail. She was a curious and brave girl who didn't like to follow rules. One day, Abigail was exploring in the forest when she saw a heel lying in the grass. She hadn't seen one before so she was very curious. Abigail picked it up and was about to put it on when a voice stopped her. "What do you think you're doing?" Abigail looked around and saw an old man standing behind her. She knew right away that he was not as friendly as she thought. "I found this heel and was curious," Abigail said. "That heel belongs to me," the old man said. He was very rude and ignorant. Abigail was quick to respond. "Why don't you lay it back down so we can both be happy," she said. The old man was shocked by Abigail's courage. He silently put the heel back on the ground, thanked Abigail for her politeness, then walked away. Abigail smiled and continued to explore the forest with her newfound courage.

Once upon a time there was a dependable frog called Mary. Mary lived in a muddy pond, and every day she would hop around the pond looking for something to eat. One day, Mary saw something strange. It was a little pink kitten, stuck in the mud! She knew she had to rescue it, so she hopped over to the kitten and started to pull it out. Mary kept pulling, and eventually the kitten was free! The kitten gave Mary a big hug and thanked her for rescuing it. Mary was so happy to have helped the kitten! Mary said goodbye to the kitten and continued hopping around her muddy pond. She was glad that she was able to be so dependable and help her new friend. The End

Once upon a time, there was a big, loud lion. He roared all day long and scared all the animals. One day, a little mouse came up to him and asked, "Why do you roar so loud?" The lion said, "It's the truth, I roar because I am king of the jungle." The little mouse didn't believe him, so he asked the other animals. They all said the same thing, that the lion was the king of the jungle. The little mouse was tired from all the talking, so he took a nap. When he woke up, he saw the lion taking a nap too. The little mouse realized that even the king of the jungle needs a nap sometimes. From that day on, the lion roared a little less loudly and the little mouse knew the truth about the king of the jungle.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Zoom. Zoom loved to go fast. One day, Zoom went to the park to play with his friend, a big tree. Zoom and the tree liked to play a game. The tree would shake its leaves, and Zoom would try to dry them with his wind. "Zoom, can you dry my leaves today?" the tree asked. "Yes, I can!" said Zoom. So, Zoom went very fast around the tree, making a lot of wind. The leaves became dry, and the tree was happy. After playing, Zoom was hungry. He saw a delicious apple on the ground. Zoom picked up the apple with his little door and ate it. "Yum, this is delicious!" said Zoom. The tree smiled, happy to see his friend enjoy the apple. And they played together until the sun went down.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a big field. He loved planting seeds in the ground. One day, he found an amazing seed that was different from all the others. It was shiny and sparkly. So, he decided to plant it in the ground. After a few days, a big plant grew from the ground. It was so tall and green. The farmer was very happy and proud of himself. But one day, a big storm came and the lightning struck the plant. The farmer was sad because his amazing plant was destroyed. However, he didn't give up. He planted more seeds and took care of them every day. And soon enough, he had a beautiful garden full of amazing plants. The farmer learned that even if something strikes you down, you can always get back up and try again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a big fountain in the middle of the park. The fountain was very pretty and had lots of water coming out of it. Lily wanted to get closer to the fountain, so she ran over to it. As she got closer, she smelled a smelly smell. It was coming from the water in the fountain. Lily didn't like the smell, but she still wanted to see the fountain up close. When she got to the fountain, she looked at the water and started to clap her hands. She was so happy to see the fountain! Even though it was smelly, Lily thought it was still very pretty. She decided to come back to the fountain every day to see it and clap her hands.

There was a little girl named Lily who loved sweets. She would go to the store with her mommy and pick out all the sweet treats she could find. One day, Lily's mommy told her that she needed to study for her school test. Lily didn't want to study, she just wanted to eat sweets. So, Lily's mommy went to the store alone and left Lily at home to study. But Lily didn't study, instead she sneaked out of the house to go to the store to get some sweets. When she got to the store, she saw a big jar of sweet candy. She stuck her hand in the jar to grab some candy, but she accidentally knocked the jar over and it shattered on the ground. Lily was scared and didn't know what to do, so she ran back home. When her mommy came back from the store, she saw the mess and asked Lily what happened. Lily felt guilty and told her mommy the truth. Her mommy was disappointed and sad that Lily didn't listen to her and study. From that day on, Lily learned that it's important to listen to her mommy and study, and not just think about sweets all the time.

Once upon a time, there were two sister called Jane and Sue. Jane's dress was very dull and plain, but Sue had the most beautiful dress. It was the color of a beautiful summer sky and had gorgeous velvet petals that bloomed in the sun. The dress twirled and sparkled when Sue spun around on the grass. One day, Jane grew very jealous of Sue's dress. She wished she had something as beautiful as her sister. The next morning, Jane got dressed and noticed her dull dress had bloomed with lovely, bright colors. Now her dress was just like Sue's! Jane skipped to school, beaming with joy. When su see saw Jane she gasped with delight and asked if she had gotten a new dress. Jane smiled and said, "Nope, I guess my old one just bloomed!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emily. Emily was three years old and liked to watch the world around her. One beautiful day, she took a walk to the park with her Mommy. As they were walking, Emily noticed a big, round number: zero. Emily's Mommy smiled at her and said: "Emily, let's watch the zero carefully." Emily looked at the zero and saw how it was the smallest number she knew. But even though it was the smallest, it still looked big and important. Emily kept watching. Suddenly, her Mommy said: "Emily, can you count to zero?" Emily said: "Yes, I can! Zero, zero, zero!" Her Mommy smiled and said: "Very careful, Emily." Emily kept counting and looking at the zero until she and her Mommy arrived at the park. Emily smiled and the two of them started to play.

Once upon a time there was a clever mouse. He liked to wander around in the woods and gaze up at the sky. One day, he came across a large hole. He peered inside and saw two rows of bright gold coins. Instantly, greed filled the mouse's heart and he wanted to take them, even though he knew it wasn't his. He quickly gathered the coins and put them all in his pocket. But as he rushed away, a big net fell down from the sky and caught him. The mouse was so scared that he dropped all the coins. A voice spoke up from above, "You think you're clever, and you were clever to find these coins. But it would have been much wiser of you to leave them alone." The mouse was ashamed and quickly ran off. He never forgot the lesson he learned that day and ever since, he was more careful to stick to the right thing instead of giving in to his greed.

Once upon a time, there was a humble man named Jack. Jack lived in a small house with his wife and their cat, Mr. Whiskers. One day, Jack found an old chest in the attic. He opened it and saw a shiny necklace inside. Jack showed the necklace to his wife and said, "Look at this! It's beautiful!" His wife replied, "We should sell it and make some money." Jack agreed and took the necklace to a pawn shop. The pawnbroker looked at the necklace and said, "This is worth a lot of money. I will give you $500 for it." Jack was happy and took the money. But, as he was leaving the pawn shop, the necklace vanished from his pocket! Jack looked around but it was nowhere to be found. He went back to the pawnbroker, but he didn't believe Jack's story. Jack went home empty-handed and sad. When Jack told his wife what happened, she got angry and said, "You should have been more careful with the necklace! Now we have lost all that money." Jack felt terrible and wished he had never found the chest in the first place. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, she saw a big, white snowman. She was happy and said, "Hello, Mr. Snowman! You look so big and tall!" The snowman smiled and said, "Hello, Lily! I am happy to meet you too!" Lily asked, "Mr. Snowman, why are you so cold?" The snowman replied, "I am made of snow, and snow is always cold." Lily thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's put you in a sack and take you inside. Then you won't be cold anymore!" The snowman laughed and said, "Lily, I will melt if you put me in a sack! But thank you for trying to help me." Lily was sad to hear that the snowman would melt, but she understood. She said goodbye to the snowman and went inside to get warm.

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl who lived in a tree. Every Tuesday, the owl would fly to the river to catch fish for dinner. But one day, it started to rain and the owl got wet. So, the owl flew back to its tree to dry itself off. The owl flapped its wings and shook its feathers to get dry. After a while, the sun came out and the owl felt warm again. It decided to wait until next Tuesday to catch fish. From then on, the owl always checked the weather before going out to catch fish.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sleep in her cozy bed every night. One morning, she woke up early because she heard a loud noise. It was her cat, Fluffy, who knocked over a vase. Lily was very upset because the vase was very special to her. Later that day, Lily and her mom went for a walk in the park. They saw a big dog passing by. Lily was scared of dogs, but her mom held her hand tightly and they walked away safely. At dinner time, Lily's dad came home from work. He was very proud of himself because he got a promotion at his job. But Lily was sad because she didn't have a good day. She told her dad about the broken vase and the scary dog. Her dad listened carefully and gave her a big hug. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can fix the vase and I'm proud of you for being brave around the dog." Lily felt much better after talking to her dad. She learned that even when things go wrong, her family will always be there to make her feel better.

Lily was a famous singer. She sang very well and many people liked her songs. She had a big house, a nice car and a lot of toys. But she was not happy. She wanted to have a friend to play with. One day, she saw a boy in the park. He was flying a kite and laughing. Lily liked his kite and his smile. She went to him and said, "Hello, I am Lily. Can I play with you?" The boy looked at her and said, "No, you can't. You are too famous. You don't know how to play. You only know how to sing." Lily felt sad. She said, "But I want to learn how to play. Please, can you teach me? I can share my toys with you." The boy thought for a while. He said, "OK, I will teach you. But you have to promise me something. You have to be my friend for a year. A year is a long time. You can't leave me for another famous person." Lily nodded. She said, "I promise. I will be your friend for a year. And maybe more. What is your name?" The boy smiled. He said, "My name is Tom. Come on, let's fly the kite together." Lily and Tom became friends. They played in the park, in the house, and in the car. They sang songs, told stories, and had fun. Lily was happy. She learned how to play and how to be a friend. Tom was happy too. He had a famous friend who was also a kind friend. They stayed friends for a year and more.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Tim. He liked to explore the world around him. One sunny day, he saw a driver climbing into a car. Tim thought this looked like fun, so he decided to climb into the car too. The driver was a bit surprised to see him. He asked, "What are you doing here?" Tim grinned with a modest smile. He said, "I want to go for a drive!" The driver smiled. "Okay, let's go!" So Tim and the driver drove away. Tim was excited for the adventure. He smiled the whole way! Soon, they arrived back home. Tim waved goodbye to the driver and then he climbed out of the car, ready to explore something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jessica. She was very brave and wanted to try something new. One day, she walked into a long, dark hallway. She was very scared, but she kept walking. At the end of the hallway, she saw a big door. She reached out to open it. Suddenly, the door opened and she saw a room filled with silly things. Jessica was so happy! She started to try them out when she noticed a man watching her. He seemed ignorant but she wasn't scared. Jessica asked the man what he was doing. He said he was just watching and making sure that everyone was having fun. Jessica smiled and said thank you. Jessica spent the rest of the day playing and trying new things. She was so excited! She was happy that she had tried something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and trucks, especially ones with big engines. One day, Timmy's dad took him to a car show. Timmy saw many cars and trucks with big engines. He said to his dad, "I want a car with a big engine like that one." His dad replied, "Timmy, those cars are very modern and expensive. We can't afford them." Timmy was sad, but he didn't give up. He asked his dad, "Can we save money and gain enough to buy a car with a big engine?" His dad smiled and said, "Yes, Timmy. We can work hard and save money to buy a modern car with a big engine." Timmy was very happy and excited to work with his dad to save money for their dream car.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big black dog. The dog is very thin and dirty. It has no collar or tag. "Look, a dog!" Tom says. "Can we pet it?" "I don't know," Sue says. "It might be scared or sick. Maybe it has no home." They go closer to the dog. The dog does not bark or run away. It looks at them with sad eyes. Tom and Sue feel sorry for the dog. "Hi, dog," Tom says softly. "We are Tom and Sue. We want to be your friends. Do you want some food?" Tom has a sandwich in his backpack. He breaks it in half and sets it on the ground. The dog sniffs the food and eats it slowly. It wags its tail a little. "Good dog," Sue says. "You are very hungry. Do you want some water?" Sue has a bottle of water in her backpack. She pours some water in a plastic cup and sets it on the ground. The dog drinks the water and licks its lips. It wags its tail more. "Good dog," Tom says. "You are very thirsty. Do you want to come with us?" Tom and Sue look at each other. They want to help the poor black dog. They think it needs a home and a family. They think their parents might let them keep the dog. "Come on, dog," Sue says. "We will take you to our house. We will give you a name and a bed and a toy. We will love you." Tom and Sue hold out their hands. The dog stands up and walks to them. It lets them pet its fur and scratch its ears. It wags its tail a lot. "Good dog," Tom and Sue say. "You are our dog now. We are your friends." They smile and hug the dog. The dog smiles and licks their faces. They are happy. They walk to their house with the dog. They hope their parents will say yes. They have a new friend.

Lily liked to draw. She had many colors and papers. She made images of her family, her pets, and her toys. She was happy when she drew. One day, Lily felt a tickle in her nose. She tried to ignore it, but it grew bigger and bigger. She knew she had to sneeze. She looked for a tissue, but she could not find one. She did not want to sneeze on her images. She did not want to ruin them. She ran to the bathroom, but it was too late. She sneezed very loud. ACHOO! The sneeze was so noisy that it made her ears hurt. It also made her images fly in the air. They landed on the floor, the sink, and the mirror. Lily was sad. She liked her images. She did not want them to be dirty or wet. She heard a knock on the door. It was her mom. She heard Lily's sneeze. She came to see if she was okay. She saw Lily and her images. She smiled. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. Your images are still beautiful. We can clean them and hang them on the wall. And here is a tissue for your nose. Next time, try to sneeze in your elbow. That way, you won't spread germs or mess up your art." Lily nodded. She said, "Thank you, mom. I'm sorry for the noise. I will sneeze in my elbow next time." She wiped her nose and hugged her mom. She felt better. She picked up her images and showed them to her mom. She was proud of her art. She was happy again.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big box. They pretended the box was a spaceship, a castle, a boat, and many other things. One day, their mom said she had to mail some letters. She asked Lily and Ben to help her put the letters in the box. Lily and Ben were happy to help. They took the letters and put them in the box. But then, they had an idea. "Let's mail ourselves!" Lily said. "Yeah, let's go on an adventure!" Ben agreed. They climbed into the box and closed the lid. They giggled and whispered to each other. "Where do you think we will go?" Lily asked. "Maybe to the moon, or the jungle, or the sea!" Ben said. They waited and waited, but nothing happened. They started to feel hot and bored. "Mom, we're ready to go!" Lily shouted. "Mom, open the box!" Ben yelled. But mom did not hear them. She had gone to the kitchen to make some tea. She did not know that Lily and Ben were in the box. Soon, dad came home from work. He saw the box and the letters on the table. "Looks like mom has some mail to send," he said. He picked up the box and carried it to the car. He did not know that Lily and Ben were in the box. Lily and Ben felt the box move. They were scared and confused. "Dad, stop!" Lily cried. "Dad, we're in here!" Ben screamed. But dad did not hear them. He had turned on the radio and was singing along. He did not know that Lily and Ben were in the box. He drove to the post office and parked the car. He got out and took the box to the counter. He did not know that Lily and Ben were in the box. "Hi, I have some mail to send," he said to the lady. "Sure, let me weigh it for you," the lady said. She put the box on the scale. She was shocked. The box was very heavy. "What's in here?" she asked. "Just some letters," dad said. The lady looked at him suspiciously. She shook the box gently. She heard some noises. "Help!" Lily and Ben shouted. The lady opened the box. She was shocked. She saw Lily and Ben in the box. "What are you doing here?" she asked. "We wanted to mail ourselves," Lily and Ben said. The lady looked at dad. He was shocked. He saw Lily and Ben in the box. "How did you get in there?" he asked. "We put ourselves in," Lily and Ben said. Dad was angry. He took Lily and Ben out of the box. He apologized to the lady. He took the letters and the box and went back to the car. He did not know what to say. Lily and Ben were sorry. They realized they had made a big mistake. They did not want to mail themselves anymore. They wanted to go home. "Mom, we're sorry!" Lily and Ben said. "Mom, we love you!" Lily and Ben said. Mom was shocked. She saw Lily and Ben in the car. She hugged them and kissed them. She was glad they were safe. "What happened?" she asked. "We'll tell you later," dad said. He drove them home. He explained what had happened. He was not happy. He said they had to be more careful and listen to mom. He said they had to share their toys and play nicely. He said they had to be fair. Lily and Ben nodded. They agreed. They learned their lesson. They did not want to mail themselves again. They wanted to stay with mom and dad. They loved them very much.

One sunny day, a small boy called Jack took his kite to the park. He wanted to fly it in the big open space there. Jack took the kite to the park and watched it soar into the bright blue sky. It flew higher and higher, and Jack was so happy. He ran around the park and laughed as the kite stayed in the air. Suddenly, a strong gust of wind blew across the park and the kite started to spin and twirl around in the sky. Jack felt a bit dizzy as he tried to keep up with the kite as it flew around. But, eventually, the wind died down and the kite remained in the same spot in the sky. Jack cheered and clapped his hands. He had done it! He had managed to keep his kite in the air!

Once there was a little girl who wanted to buy a beautiful lion. She asked her Mum if she could buy one, and her Mum said yes, so they went to the animal shop. When they got to the shop there were many animals, but the girl saw a beautiful lion in the corner. She was so excited that she couldn't stop smiling. The shopkeeper said the lion was very friendly, so the girl's Mum bought it for her. They took the beautiful lion home and the girl named it Leo. The girl was so happy. She played with Leo every day and loved him very much. He was the best pet she could ever have asked for.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat that went on adventures. It had a special home called a "port" where it would stay when it wasn't out sailing. The boat had a captain who loved to explore. One day, they went out to sea and saw lots of fish and whales. The captain admired the deep blue water and all the creatures that lived in it. They had so much fun that they sailed back to their port with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was very tidy, so every day he picked up his toys, swept the floors and made his bed. One day, as he was tidying his room, he saw something outside his window. He saw a big white cloud! The cloud said, "Hello Little Boy!" The little boy was so surprised. He looked around, but he couldn't see who was speaking. The cloud said, "I am a friendly cloud! What's your name?" The little boy told the cloud his name and asked, "How can you talk?" The cloud laughed and said, "I can talk because I'm special." The little boy smiled and asked, "What else can you do?" The cloud said, "I can show you wonderful places if you like." The little boy was so excited. He said, "Yes please!" The cloud said, "Hop on my back and I'll take you away!" The little boy climbed on the cloud's back and they flew away. They had so many adventures together, discovering new and exciting places. They even saw a castle in the clouds! The little boy smiled and said, "Thank you, Cloud!" The cloud smiled and said, "You're welcome, Little Boy!" They flew off into the sky to have more adventures together.

Once upon a time there was a bunny called Furry. Furry was very excited and couldn't wait to explore the forest. Furry hopped and hopped until he found a pond. He settled near the edge and started to drink the cool, clear water. Suddenly, Furry saw something oily floating on top of the water. He nibbled the oily thing and it tasted really bad. Furry felt sick and he went to settle on the grass to rest. Unfortunately, the oil had made Furry very sick. As the hours went by, he felt worse and worse. Furry sadly passed away surrounded by the forest he had been so excited about exploring.

Once upon a time, there was a colorful bird named Bobo. Bobo liked to display his bright feathers to all his friends. He would show off his feathers on one side, then the other side. One day, a new bird named Lulu came to the forest. Lulu was not colorful like Bobo. She had only one color. Bobo wanted to display his feathers to Lulu, but Lulu was sad. She did not have bright feathers like Bobo. Bobo had an idea. He shared his colorful feathers with Lulu. They became good friends. All the birds in the forest were happy. The moral of the story is to be kind and share with others.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy's mom came in and said, "Timmy, I need you to clean up your toys. It's your job to keep your room clean." Timmy didn't want to clean up his toys, but he knew it was his job. As he was cleaning, he noticed a disgusting smell coming from under his bed. He said to his mom, "Mommy, something is disturbing me. There is a disgusting smell under my bed." His mom looked under the bed and found an old piece of pizza that had been there for a long time. She said, "Timmy, this old pizza is what's disturbing you. It's so disgusting! Let's throw it away and clean up your room." Timmy was happy to have a clean room and no more disgusting smells. He knew it was his job to keep his room clean and he didn't want anything to disturb him again.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl. She had long hair and a big smile. Every day she went to the park to play. One day she found a bottle of perfume. It was a beautiful bottle with sparkles on it. She wanted to keep it, so she put it in her pocket. On her way home, she came across an ugly monster. It was very scary and the girl was scared. She quickly hid behind a tree and stayed very still. The ugly monster could still smell her perfume. It followed her until she came home safe and sound. From then on, she always remembered to stay away from the ugly monster.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Molly. She was only three years old and loved exploring. One day, Molly was in the park looking for things to touch. She came upon a big, old book lying in the grass. When she opened the book, thick, yellow pages appeared in front of her. She found this very exciting. Molly touched each page, as if it was a special gift. Suddenly, an ugly owl flew down from a nearby tree. The owl said, "Those pages are very special! You need to take care of them." Molly smiled. She said, "I will take care of them! I promise." Molly carefully closed the book and hugged it. She kept it safe and found it exciting to explore the pages whenever she wanted. The end.

Lily was a healthy girl who liked to observe everything. She liked to watch the birds, the flowers, the clouds and the stars. She also liked to observe her friends and learn from them. One day, it was Lily's birthday. She was very happy and excited. She invited her friends to her house for a party. She had a big cake, balloons, games and presents. She wanted to share her joy with everyone. But some of her friends were not very nice. They did not observe the rules of the party.
