They ate too much cake, popped the balloons, cheated in the games and took the presents. They did not say thank you or happy birthday to Lily. They made a big mess and left. Lily was very sad and angry. She felt like her friends did not care about her. She cried and told her mom what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Some people are not very kind or grateful. But you are a good and generous girl. You observe how to be a friend and how to be happy. You have a healthy heart and a healthy mind. And you have other friends who love you and appreciate you. Don't let the bad ones spoil your birthday. You are special and you deserve to be happy." Lily smiled and wiped her tears. She said, "Thank you, mom. You are right. I have other friends who are nice and fun. I will observe who they are and invite them next time. And I will observe how to be a good friend to them too. I love you, mom. And I love my birthday."

Once upon a time, there were two friends. Polly and Jack were very different and never agreed on anything. One day, Polly said, "Let's unite and build a ladder." Jack was embarrassed, but he agreed. The two friends worked in the sun, and then the rain. But their hard work paid off, and soon enough, the ladder was standing tall. The two friends looked at their ladder in amazement. They decided to climb the ladder every day, just to keep it strong. Soon enough, Polly and Jack were closer than ever. They were no longer embarrassing when around each other and always had fun. The two friends were united by the ladder they had built, and that made them the happiest they had ever been.

Once there was a girl. Every day, she would feed the birds. One day, there was an uncomfortable earthquake. The girl jumped in fear. She ran away and hid, but when the earthquake was over, she felt brave. She went out and started to feed the birds again. It felt good to help the birds in spite of feeling uncomfortable. The girl went home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the gym with his mommy. They would run and play together. One day, Timmy's mommy hurt her leg while they were playing. Timmy asked, "Mommy, are you okay?" His mommy replied, "No, my leg hurts." Timmy wanted to help his mommy feel better. He saw a rubber band on the floor and had an idea. He said, "Mommy, watch this!" He took the rubber band and snapped it. His mommy asked, "What are you doing, Timmy?" Timmy replied, "I'm trying to make you feel better. When I snap the rubber band, it makes me feel better. Maybe it will make you feel better too!" His mommy smiled and said, "Thank you, Timmy. You are so sweet." They continued to play and have fun at the gym, and Timmy's mommy's leg started to feel better. From that day on, Timmy always brought a rubber band to the gym to snap whenever someone got hurt.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy was a very miserable girl. She thought her life was unfair. Every day she was sad, and never smiled. One day, Lucy was walking by a bakery and smelled something good. It was a pastry! Lucy felt so happy that she could almost smile. But then Lucy remembered that she didn't have any money with her. She felt so sad and alone. She thought she would never get to have a pastry. Suddenly, the bakery owner opened the door and handed her a pastry. He said he wanted Lucy to be happy again. Lucy was so happy. She smiled and thanked the kind bakery owner. She took a big bite of the pastry and thought about how nice it was to get a special treat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. Every day she would go out to play with her friends. Today, Emma wanted to try something new - pass a crack. She ran to get her friends and said to them, "Let's go pass a crack!" They agreed and they went to the park to play. When they got to the park, they found a healthy crack in the ground. Her friends gathered around the crack and began to pass it back and forth. Every time it went around, Emma would cheer. Then an old man walked by and said, "Good job, kids! Pass that crack as much as you can. It's very healthy for you!" The kids thanked him, and then kept passing the crack around. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a player. He was amazing. He liked to dream. He dreamed of being the best player ever. One day, he went outside and played a game. He was so fast and so good. Everyone was amazed. When he came home, his mum gave him a big hug and told him how wonderful he was. He smiled and went to sleep. Every night he had amazing dreams of being the very best player ever. He was so happy and his dreams kept getting better and better. One day, he became the best player ever just like he had dreamed. Everyone was so amazed and happy for him.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She liked to play in the snow. One day, it started to snow outside. The girl was so excited. She put on her coat and went outside. "Look at all this snow!" she said. But then she got cold and her hands and feet started to hurt. "I should go home and wash," she thought. But then she thought it would be more fun to stay and play in the snow. "No," she said. "That is too foolish." So she went home and washed. Then she put on some warm, dry clothes and went back outside and played in the snow.

Once upon a time, there was a lawyer named Tom. Tom liked to help people. He wanted to make sure everyone was treated fair. One day, a man came to Tom. The man was sad because someone took his toy. Tom wanted to help the man get his toy back. So, Tom went to talk to the person who took the toy. Tom told the person, "It is not fair to take toys from others. Please give the toy back to the man." The person felt bad and gave the toy back. The man was very happy. Tom taught the person that it is important to be fair and not take things from others. Everyone learned to share and be kind to each other. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Millie. She was 3-years-old and very curious. One day, Millie sneaked away and went to explore a nearby bush. Millie forgot about the time and soon her mom called her back home. Millie was embarrassed because she had been gone so long. When Millie got home, her mom decided to cook them a special dinner. She made Millie a yummy bowl of spaghetti and meatballs. Millie ate every bite and was so happy. Millie never ever snuck away to explore another bush again. She was just too embarrassed. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play on her soft carpet in her room. One day, she found a weird toy hidden under her bed. It was a funny looking doll that could display different colors. Lily was so excited to play with her new toy. She placed the doll on her carpet and watched as it displayed a rainbow of colors. She thought it was so cool! As she played with the doll, Lily's mom walked in and saw the weird toy. She asked Lily where she found it and Lily showed her. Her mom explained that the toy belonged to her older sister and had been missing for a long time. Lily was sad that she couldn't keep the toy, but she was happy that she found it and was able to display its beautiful colors on her carpet for a little while.

Once there was a little toddler called Emma. She loved to paint and make things bright and full of colour. One day Emma went to the store to buy some paint. She pointed to the different colours, but she was getting very weak from standing for too long. So Emma's mom scooped her up in her arms and said "Don't worry princess, we will get the paint later". Emma wasn't sure what to do, so she started to cry. But her mom told her "Don't worry, sweetheart. We will get some paint soon and make lovely pictures together." Emma brightened up right away. She knew that soon she would have lots of lovely bright colours to paint with.

Lily and Ben are playing in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They give him a carrot nose and two coal eyes. They are happy and laugh. But then the wind blows hard and cold. It makes the snowman's hat fly away. It makes Lily and Ben shiver. They are not happy and cry. "Let's go home," Lily says. "I'm cold and hungry." "Me too," Ben says. "But what about the snowman? He will be cold too." They look at the snowman. He has no hat and his scarf is loose. He looks sad. Lily has an idea. She takes off her mittens and puts them on the snowman's hands. Ben takes off his boots and puts them on the snowman's feet. "There," Lily says. "Now he is warm and cozy." Ben smiles. He hugs Lily. "You are very gentle and kind," he says. They wave goodbye to the snowman and run home. They have hot chocolate and cookies. They are warm and happy. They win the day.

Tim and Mia like to play in the park. They run and jump and laugh. They see many things in nature: trees, flowers, birds, bugs. They like to pretend they are explorers. One day, they find a big hill. They want to climb it and see what is on the other side. They hold hands and start to walk up the hill. But the hill is very steep and slippery. They slip and slide and fall. They get dirty and tired. "Tim, I don't want to climb anymore," Mia says. "It is too hard and scary." "Come on, Mia, don't give up," Tim says. "We are almost there. I want to see what is on the other side. Maybe there is a treasure or a castle or a dragon." "No, Tim, I want to go back," Mia says. "I want to play on the swings or the slide or the sandbox. They are more fun and safe." Tim and Mia look at each other. They have different ideas. They don't know what to do. They feel sad and angry. Then, they hear a voice. It is their mom. She is calling them from the bottom of the hill. "Tim, Mia, where are you?" she says. "It is time to go home. Come down, please." Tim and Mia look at each other again. They smile. They have a way to end their fight. They both say the same word. "Surrender!" They let go of their hands and roll down the hill. They laugh and scream and enjoy the ride. They land on the grass and hug each other. They are not mad anymore. They are happy. They run to their mom and tell her about their adventure. She listens and smiles. She hugs them and says they are brave and smart. She says she loves them. They go home and have a snack and a nap. They dream of nature and deep hills and treasures and castles and dragons. They are friends. They are explorers.

Once upon a time there was a very good man. The man liked to teach other people. He taught them a lot of things. One day he decided to teach some people how to make things out of leather. He showed them how to cut it with a knife, then he showed them how to sew it together. The people learned very quickly. They made many things out of the leather. Shoes, jackets, bags and lots of other things. They all loved their new things and thanked the man for teaching them. The man was very happy. He taught many other people too. He taught them how to cook, how to play music and even how to use computers. He was happy to have helped so many people. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bossy little boy called Jay. He wanted to belong and he thought the best way to do that was to wear a special veil. He went to the market with his mum to pick out one. At the market, there were veils of all colours, shapes and sizes. Some were sparkly and some were plain. Jay had to choose very carefully. He picked out a veil that was bright and colourful, with lots of patterns. Mum said it was perfect. His mum tied the veil around Jay's neck and he felt so special. He ran around the market with his veil, feeling like he belonged. Everyone eyed him curiously, but he didn't mind. He felt like he was special. They finally went home with the veil and Jay never took it off. Everywhere he went, he wore it proudly. With the veil on, he felt like he belonged. The End

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny was a happy bunny who loved to play in the spring. One day, Benny found some carrots and wanted to eat them. But he needed to add some salt to make them taste good. Benny hopped around looking for some salt, but he couldn't find any. He asked his friend, a bird, if he knew where to find salt. The bird told Benny that he could find some at the farmer's house. So, Benny hopped over to the farmer's house and found some salt. He added it to his carrots and they tasted so yummy! Benny was so happy that he could enjoy his snack in the beautiful spring weather. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Lily. She had a very important poem that her mom gave her. Lily loved the poem so much. She read it every day and night. One day, a big wind came and blew the poem out of Lily's hands. It flew far away. Lily was very sad. She knew she had to protect the poem, so she went on a journey to find it. She looked up and down, left and right, and asked her friends to help her. Finally, Lily found the poem under a big tree. She was so happy! She hugged the poem and promised to protect it forever. From that day on, Lily learned that it is important to take care of the things we love.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play with blocks and dolls. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big slide and run to it. "Me first!" Lily says. She climbs up the stairs and sits on the slide. She is ready to go down. "Wait for me!" Max says. He follows her and tries to get on the slide too. But he is too slow. Lily pushes him away with her foot. "Hey, that's not nice!" Max says. He falls off the slide and lands on the grass. He is sad and angry. Lily slides down and laughs. She thinks she is funny. But then she sees something on her dress. It is gray and sticky. It is bird poop. A bird pooped on her when she was on the slide. "Yuck!" Lily says. She tries to wipe it off, but it only makes it worse. She looks at her dress and feels embarrassed. She starts to cry. Max gets up and sees Lily crying. He is not angry anymore. He feels sorry for her. He goes to her and gives her a hug. "It's okay, Lily. It was an accident. You can get a new dress. Do you want to play with me?" Max says. Lily stops crying and nods. She hugs him back. She is glad he is her friend. They go to their moms and tell them what happened. Their moms help them clean up and get new clothes. Then they go back to the park and play together. They share the slide and have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Molly. She was brave and ready to try new things. One day, she saw a woman in a beautiful garden filled with flowers and buzzing insects. She wanted to go and talk to her but she didn't know what to say. Molly took a deep breath and asked the woman: "What is wisdom?" The woman smiled and said: "Wisdom is inside you, Molly. It will help guide you in life!" Molly was unsure but she was ready to find out more. She asked the woman again: "How do I get wisdom?" The woman said: "The only way to get wisdom is to tear away the things that make it difficult to find it." Molly thought for a moment and then she understood. She said: "Thank you for your wise words!" The woman smiled and nodded. Molly left the garden with a sense of new understanding. She was ready to start tearing away what was getting in the way of her wisdom. She was ready to start her new journey.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to eat ice cream. One day, he was eating his ice cream with a spoon when his mom asked him, "Timmy, can you please be loyal and share some of your ice cream with your sister?" Timmy didn't want to share his ice cream because it was his favorite flavor, but he knew his mom was right. So, he gave his sister a spoonful of ice cream. His sister was happy and said, "Thank you, Timmy! You are so sharp for sharing your ice cream with me." Timmy felt proud of himself for being a good brother and sharing his ice cream. From that day on, he always shared his treats with his sister and became known as the loyal and kind brother in his family.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird in the sky. The bird flapped its wings and flew all around. One day, it flew over a family. The family was very happy and they sang a song. The bird liked it so much that it flew past them again and again. The family thought that the bird liked their song and they allowed the bird to listen. Every day, the bird flew by and listened to the family's song. Each time, the bird became happier. One day, the family decided to no longer allow the big bird to listen. The bird was very sad and flew away. The moral of the story is that it's important to share our joy with others. Allowing people to enjoy the good things we do can bring us and them a lot of happiness.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emily. She loved to go to the park with her dad. Today, though, Emily was feeling very sad. Her dad asked her why she was so sad and Emily said, "My shirt is old and doesn't fit me anymore." Her dad said, "That's okay, Emily. We will go out and find you a new shirt." So they went to the store and Emily picked out a pretty, new shirt. When they got home, Emily said, "I feel better now that I have a new shirt!" Her dad smiled and said, "It's important to replace things when they get old or worn out. That way, we can all stay healthy!" Emily felt very happy and hugged her dad. She said, "Thanks daddy!" And they both smiled, happy to be together.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a yellow ball. The ball is light and soft. They can throw it and catch it. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big slide. Sara wants to go on the slide. She says, "Ben, let's go on the slide. It looks fun." Ben is scared. He says, "No, Sara. The slide is too high. I don't want to go." Sara says, "Don't be scared, Ben. I will go first. You can watch me. Then you can try." Sara gives the ball to her mom. She climbs the ladder. She sits on the slide. She slides down. She laughs. She says, "Whee! That was fun. Come on, Ben. Your turn." Ben looks at the slide. He looks at Sara. He looks at the ball. He wants to play with the ball. He says, "No, Sara. I don't want to go on the slide. I want to play with the ball." Sara says, "OK, Ben. You can play with the ball. I will go on the slide again. Maybe later you will want to try." Sara and Ben are still friends. They play in the park. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a funny monkey named Max. Max loved to joke around and make his friends laugh. One day, Max told his friend Timmy a silly joke. Timmy didn't understand the joke and got mad at Max. Max didn't know that Timmy was ignorant about the joke. Later that day, Max and Timmy were playing in the jungle when they saw a cable hanging from a tree. Max wanted to swing on the cable, but Timmy was scared. Timmy told Max that the cable was dangerous and that they shouldn't play with it. Max didn't listen and started to swing on the cable. As Max was swinging, the cable suddenly broke and Max fell to the ground. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. He ran to get help from the other animals in the jungle. They all came together to help Max and make sure he was okay. Max realized that he shouldn't have ignored Timmy's warning about the cable. From then on, Max promised to always listen to his friends and not ignore them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, especially near the river. One day, Lily's mom asked her a question. "What did you have for lunch?" her mom asked. Lily thought for a moment and then answered, "I had a peanut butter sandwich." Later that day, Lily was playing by the river when she accidentally dropped her favorite toy in the water. She felt so ashamed that she had been careless. But then, her dad came to the rescue and fished the toy out of the river for her. Lily was so happy and grateful that she hugged her dad tightly. From that day on, Lily made sure to be extra careful near the river. And whenever her parents asked her a question, she always made sure to answer truthfully.

Once upon a time, there was a barber named Bob. He had a special job - he provided haircuts for the people in town. Each day, Bob opened his barbershop, and people came to get their hair cut or trimmed. Bob was very careful when he cut the hair. He made sure each person's hair was cutting clean and clear. Bob always made sure to use the right tools and be very patient when giving each haircut. At the end of the day, Bob would close his shop and children would come to watch. They were always excited to see Bob provide haircuts for the people in town. All the children were amazed at how neat and tidy Bob's work was. The end!

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. They enjoy exercise. They run, jump, and kick a ball. They are clever. They know how to share and take turns. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is black and white. It has a long tail. It looks friendly. Anna and Ben want to pet the dog. They run to the dog. They say, "Hello, dog! Can we play with you?" The dog does not like Anna and Ben. The dog is angry. It barks and growls. It shows its teeth. It bites Anna and Ben. They cry and scream. They are hurt. They are scared. A man comes. He is the dog's owner. He says, "Sorry, sorry! My dog is not nice. He does not like children. He is a guard dog. You should not go near him." Anna and Ben are sad and mad. They say, "You are a bad man! You should not have a bad dog! You should keep him away from us!" The man takes the dog and leaves. Anna and Ben go home. They tell their moms what happened. Their moms hug them and take them to the doctor. The doctor gives them medicine and bandages. He says, "You are brave. You will be okay. But you should be careful. Not all dogs are friendly. Some dogs are dangerous. You should always ask before you pet a dog." Anna and Ben learn a lesson. They do not enjoy exercise today. They do not feel clever. They feel sorry and silly. They wish they had not met the bad dog.

Ben and Mia like to play with trains. They have a big train set with tracks and bridges and tunnels. They make the trains go fast and slow and make noises like choo-choo. One day, they see a real train outside their window. It is a steam train, with white smoke coming out of its chimney. It looks old and shiny and loud. Ben and Mia want to see it up close. They ask their mom if they can go to the train station. Mom says yes, but they have to be careful and hold her hand. They put on their coats and shoes and go outside. They walk to the train station, following the steam in the sky. At the train station, they see the steam train waiting on the platform. It is bigger than their toy trains, and has many cars behind it. The driver is wearing a hat and a scarf. He sees Ben and Mia and smiles. "Hello, little ones," he says. "Do you like my train?" "Yes, we do!" Ben and Mia say. "Can we see inside?" "Sure, you can," the driver says. "But only for a minute. We have to go soon." He lets them climb up the steps and shows them the engine. He explains how he makes the fire and the water and the steam. He lets them pull the whistle and hear the loud sound. Ben and Mia are amazed and happy. "Thank you, Mr. Driver," they say. "You are very helpful and kind." "You're welcome, kids," the driver says. "But now you have to go. The train is ready to leave." He helps them down the steps and waves goodbye. Ben and Mia wave back and hold their mom's hand. They watch the steam train go away, with a loud choo-choo and a puff of smoke. They feel sad, but also glad. They have seen a real steam train, and made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite was a stuffed bunny named Mr. Floppy. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to help with a special task. She needed Lily to let their neighbor know that she had a message for her. Lily was very excited to help her mommy. She put on her shoes and got ready to go outside. She walked over to their neighbor's house and knocked on the door. When the neighbor answered, Lily told her that her mommy had a message for her. The neighbor was very grateful and thanked Lily for letting her know. Lily was so happy that she could help her mommy and the neighbor. She went back inside and played with Mr. Floppy, feeling proud of herself for being a good helper.

Once upon a time, there was a brown dog named Max. Max loved to play with junk he found in the park. One day, Max found an old can and started to play with it. He barked and jumped around with the can in his mouth. Suddenly, a little girl walked by and saw Max playing. She clapped her hands and said, "Good job, Max!" Max felt happy and wagged his tail. The little girl continued to applaud as Max continued to play with the can. From that day on, Max would always look for junk to play with in the park. And every time someone would pass by and see him playing, they would applaud and Max would feel proud. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice-cream, especially the green one. Her mommy would take her to the store to buy ice-cream every weekend. One day, Lily and her mommy went to the store to buy ice-cream. They saw a big green ice-cream and Lily was so happy. She asked her mommy if they could buy it. Her mommy said yes and they brought the ice-cream home. Lily loved the green ice-cream so much that she ate it all in one day. She asked her mommy if they could go to the store again to buy more green ice-cream. Her mommy said they could go next weekend. Lily was very excited and couldn't wait to go back to the store to buy more ice-cream.

Once there was a naughty little girl. She was very naughty and always misbehaving. One day she do something very naughty. She took her daddy's tie and put it in the dirt. It began to rot away in the soil. The little girl felt very bad about what she'd done, but it was too late. The tie was ruined and couldn't be fixed. The little girl's daddy was very sad. He had worked very hard to buy that tie, and now it was gone. The little girl knew she had done something wrong and she was sorry. The daddy gave the little girl a big, big hug and said it was alright. He said he still loved her and that she must never do such a naughty thing again. The little girl was very happy and promised to never do anything naughty again. And with that, the tie was forgotten and the little girl was happy once more.

The sun shone brightly in the jungle that day. Bob the monkey was sad. He watched the other animals in the jungle playing together. He wanted to join in the fun, but nobody asked him to play. Suddenly, an elephant stomped into the clearing and roared. He was mad! Everyone else looked scared. The elephant turned to Bob and said, "You need to help me find my lost trunk!" Bob didn't want to help, but he knew he had to. He climbed onto the elephant's back and off they went. But when the elephant couldn't find his trunk, he got even madder! He turned to Bob and slapped him with his trunk. Bob ran off, never to be seen in the jungle again. He was sad. He wished someone had played with him when he had the chance.

Once there was a little girl called Emily, and she was very brave. One day she went on a long walk in the forest, and it was getting dark. Suddenly, she heard scary noises, and she felt a bit scared. Suddenly, a monster appeared! It was big and green, and it had big eyes. Emily was scared, but she didn't run away. She walked up to the monster and said "Hello". The monster said "I'm looking for someone to play with. Will you surrender to me?" Emily thought about it and said "Yes, I surrender". Then, the monster smiled and said "Great! We can play hide-and-seek!" Emily was happy and so was the monster. They played hide-and-seek until it was time to go home. Emily hugged the monster goodbye and said "See you soon!" The monster waved goodbye as Emily walked away. From that day on, Emily was never scared in the forest. She knew that she could always find a new friend if she was brave enough to surrender.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went on a walk with her mommy and daddy. They walked up a big mountain and saw lots of pretty flowers along the way. Lily's daddy said, "Look at the beautiful view from up here!" But Lily thought it was dull because everything looked so far away. She wanted to go back down the mountain and play with her toys. Her mommy said, "Don't ignore the beauty around you, Lily. Look at the flowers and the trees. They are all so pretty." Lily looked around and saw all the pretty things her mommy was talking about. She smiled and said, "You're right, mommy. It's not dull at all. It's beautiful!" And they all continued to walk up the mountain, enjoying the view and each other's company.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Peter. Peter was three years old and loved to explore. One day, he saw something mysterious in the sky. He looked closely and saw that it was a balloon! The balloon was filled with lots of stuff. There were colourful toys, chocolate, and many other things. Peter was very excited! He wanted to see what else was in the balloon, so he ran over to it. He grabbed onto the string and the balloon started to descend. As the balloon came closer to the ground, it started to display all the things inside it. Peter was amazed! He saw many different items he had never seen before. He wanted to touch them, but he couldn't reach them all. So he decided to take some stuff back home with him. When he got home, he showed his family the mysterious stuff he had found in the balloon. They were all surprised to see the kinds of things he had discovered! So, the mysterious balloon filled with stuff displayed lots of wonders to Peter that day. Peter and his family enjoyed talking about all the things he had seen.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived on a farm with her family. She had a pet chicken named Daisy who she loved very much. One day, Lily's brother wanted to play with Daisy too, but Lily didn't trust him because he was always rough with their toys. Lily's brother got angry and took Daisy away from her. Lily was sad and worried about her chicken. She went to her mom and dad and told them what happened. They told her that they trusted her brother to take care of Daisy, but they would talk to him about being gentle. Later that day, Lily's brother brought Daisy back and apologized. He said he didn't know how much Daisy meant to her. Lily forgave him and they all played together. They even cooked a rare chicken for dinner and enjoyed it as a family. From that day on, Lily knew she could trust her brother with Daisy.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little robot named Robby. He was made of shiny metal and he loved to dance around. One day, he went to play with his robot friends, but they didn't want to play with him. They ignored him and it made Robby feel sad. But then, he saw a group of cheerful kids playing nearby. They saw Robby and thought he was cool! They asked him to dance with them and Robby was so happy. They played together all day long and Robby felt loved. From that day on, Robby didn't worry about his robot friends ignoring him. He had new friends who liked him for who he was, even though he was made of metal. And he was always cheerful because he knew he had friends who cared about him. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to bounce. She could bounce higher than anyone else! One day, she saw a yellow pond. She wanted to bounce on the pond so she did. She bounced once, twice, three times and then she heard a splash! The little girl had bounced so hard that she fell into the pond! She was scared at first, but she started to laugh. She swam around, splashed and had lots of fun in the yellow pond. It was so much fun that she started to bounce in the pond. She bounced once, twice, three times. She was so happy and she even taught the frogs how to bounce!

Once there was a bear who was very hungry. He went looking for food but found nothing. Suddenly, he heard someone laughing and saw a path. He followed the path, to see where it would take him. The path became narrower, but then he saw a stream. He was so happy and got down to drink some water. After drinking, the bear looked around and noticed there were some berries growing on the side of the path. He ate them all, until he was full and content. As he followed the path, he began to feel sleepy. He lay down and soon drifted off. When he woke up, he continued his journey, happy and satisfied. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved flowers and always picked them when she was outside playing. One day, she saw a dull flower on the ground and decided to pick it up. Lily showed the flower to her mom and said, "Look, I receive this flower. It's not pretty, but I like it." Her mom smiled and said, "That's nice, Lily. But be careful, sometimes things that look dull on the outside can be dangerous." Lily didn't listen and kept the dull flower in her room. One night, she woke up feeling sick and realized that the dull flower was making her feel bad. She tried to tell her mom, but it was too late. Lily had to go to the hospital and was very sick. From that day on, Lily learned that she should listen to her mom and not pick up dull flowers.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man who used to take a walk every day. One day, he felt an itch on his nose and was about to scratch it when suddenly he spotted a young boy and girl nearby playing tag! The elderly man was quite excited to see the children playing and laughing together, so he decided not to scratch his nose. He watched them as they ran around and he smiled. After a few minutes, the children's mother noticed the elderly man watching the children and asked him why he was there. The elderly man replied, "I'm just here to see how lovely you and your children are behaving." The mother was pleased and thanked him for not scratching his nose while the children were playing. She realized what a kind gesture this was from the elderly man, and she thanked him again before he left. The story has a moral value - it is important to always behave in a kind and courteous way, even when you have an itch.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. Today, they want to bake a cake for their mom. They go to the kitchen and find a big bowl, some eggs, some flour, some sugar, and some butter. They also find a cake pan with a zigzag shape. "Look, Ben, this is an interesting pan. It has many ups and downs. Do you think our cake will look like this?" Anna asks. "Yes, Anna, I think so. Let's try it. We have to crack the eggs, mix the flour, add the sugar, and melt the butter. Then we have to pour the batter into the pan and put it in the oven. Can you help me?" Ben says. "Of course, Ben, I can help you. We are a good team. But we have to be careful. The oven is hot. We have to ask mom to help us with that part. And we have to wait for the cake to bake. It will take some time. Do you want to play a game while we wait?" Anna says. "Sure, Anna, I want to play a game. What game do you want to play? How about hide and seek? You can count to ten and I will hide. Then you have to find me. And then we can switch. OK?" Ben says. "OK, Ben, that sounds fun. Let's play hide and seek. But we have to stay close to the kitchen. We don't want to miss our cake. It will smell good and taste yummy. And mom will be happy. Ready? One, two, three..." Anna says.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very tired and needed a nap. She asked her mommy if she could nap under the big tree in the park. Her mommy said yes and told her to be careful. Lily fell asleep and had a dream about a friendly bunny. The bunny was very compassionate and helped her find her way back home. When she woke up, she saw that her mommy was gone. She looked around and saw a scary man. The man was not compassionate and took her away. Lily was very scared and cried for her mommy. She wished she had never taken a nap under the big tree.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who liked to play together. Their names were Chris and Eric. Chris liked music and Eric liked food. One day, Chris said to Eric, "Let's make a band!" Eric liked the idea, so they got some drums and a trumpet. Chris played the drums and Eric played the trumpet. The next day, Chris said, "Let's make something tasty together!" Eric liked the idea, so they went to the kitchen and made a yummy cake. They also made some yummy cookies. When the tasty treats were ready, the two friends said, "Let's have a band party!" So they brought their music and their tasty treats to the park. Everyone said they played the best music and had the tastiest treats at the party. Chris and Eric had so much fun that they couldn't believe how quickly the day went by. They said, "Let's do this every day!"

Once there was a smelly dog named Bob. He loved to play with his board. One day, Bob saw a little girl named Sue. Sue was sad because she lost her ball. Bob wanted to help Sue. He said, "Come, I will help you find your ball." Sue smiled and said, "Thank you, Bob!" They looked all around the park for the ball. At last, they found the ball under a big tree. Sue was very happy. She said, "You are a good friend, Bob!" Then, they played together with the ball and the board. They had lots of fun and became best friends.

Tommy was a very intelligent boy. He liked to learn new things and solve problems. He had a big book of puzzles that he read every day. He wanted to succeed in everything he did. One day, he saw a red cap on a high shelf in his room. He wanted to wear the cap, but he could not reach it. He tried to jump, but he was too short. He tried to climb, but he was too small. He tried to use a chair, but he was too weak. He felt sad and angry. He asked his mom for help. "Mom, can you get me the cap, please?" he said. His mom smiled and said, "Why do you want the cap, Tommy?" Tommy said, "Because it is red and I like red. And because it is on the high shelf and I want to get it." His mom said, "I see. But you know, Tommy, sometimes you have to work hard and be creative to get what you want. You are a very intelligent boy, and I'm sure you can find a way to get the cap by yourself. Why don't you try again and use your brain?" Tommy thought for a while. He looked around his room and saw his toys. He had an idea. He took his toy truck and his toy crane. He put the truck under the shelf and the crane on the truck. He used the crane to lift the cap from the shelf and bring it down to the truck. He was very happy. He put the cap on his head and said, "I did it! I got the cap!" His mom came back and saw him. She was very proud. She hugged him and said, "Well done, Tommy! You are a very intelligent boy, and you succeeded in getting the cap by yourself. You used your brain and your toys to solve the problem. That's very clever. I love you, Tommy, and I love your red cap." Tommy smiled and said, "I love you too, mom, and I love my puzzles. Can we do some together?" His mom said, "Of course, Tommy. Let's go and have some fun." They went to the living room and did some puzzles together. They had a great time.

One day, Lily and Ben went to the park with their mom. They saw a big slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They wanted to play with everything. "Can we go on the slide, mom?" Lily asked. "Sure, but be careful. There are some holes in the ground. Don't step on them or you might fall," mom said. Lily and Ben nodded and ran to the slide. They took turns sliding down and laughing. They had a lot of fun. But then, Ben saw something shiny in the grass. He ran to it and picked it up. It was a brilliant coin. He was very happy. "Look, Lily, I found a coin! It's so shiny and pretty!" Ben said. "Wow, that's cool! Can I see it?" Lily said. Ben showed her the coin. He was very proud. "Where did you find it?" Lily asked. "Over there, in the grass. Maybe there are more. Let's go and look," Ben said. He ran to the grass again, but he did not watch where he was going. He stepped on a hole and tripped. He fell and hurt his knee. He dropped the coin and it rolled away. "Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. Lily and mom heard him and ran to him. They helped him up and checked his knee. It was bleeding a little. "Are you okay, Ben?" mom asked. "It hurts, mom. And I lost my coin," Ben said. "I'm sorry, Ben. But you should have listened to me. I told you not to step on the holes. They are dangerous. You have to be careful where you walk," mom said. "I know, mom. I was silly. I only cared about the coin. I should have watched where I was going," Ben said. He hugged mom and said he was sorry. Mom hugged him back and said she forgave him. She put a band-aid on his knee and gave him a kiss. Lily gave him a hug too and said she was sorry he lost his coin. She said she would share her toys with him. Ben smiled and thanked her. He said he was lucky to have a mom and a sister who loved him. He said he learned his lesson. He said he would be more careful and not step on holes again. The end. Moral value: The story teaches the value of being careful, listening to advice, and caring more about people than things.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very popular. Her name was Bella. She was always happy and friendly and everyone loved her. One day, Bella was feeling a bit tired, so she decided to relax. She lay down on the couch and imagined she was at the beach. The warm sun was shining and she could feel the sand beneath her toes. It was time for Bella to have a snack so she made a sandwich. It was yummy - it had her favorite fillings inside. She enjoyed it so much that she made another one! After eating her sandwiches, Bella felt much better. She was relaxed and ready to carry on with her day.

Once upon a time there was a happy boy. He loved to explore the world around him. One day he was looking around his backyard and saw a frog. He wanted to take a closer look. So, he bent down to examine it. The frog suddenly began to sing a song. The boy was amazed by the sound and listened very carefully. The song was slow and sweet. He asked the frog, "What is that song?" The frog answered, "It is a song of friendship. It is a sweet reminder that friends can be found in the most unexpected places." The boy smiled and thanked the frog. From then on, he always examined the world around him in hopes of finding more new friends. The end.

John was a loyal dog. He loved his owner and never wanted to leave her side. Every day, their routine was the same. They would go for a walk in the park and then play fetch with a small orange pitched ball. John really enjoyed it. One day, John and his owner went for a walk. When they got to the park, John forgot about his toy. He went running and chasing after birds, forgetting he was supposed to get his ball. His owner tried to remind him but John was having too much fun. But luckily, she remembered to bring the ball. She gave it to John and he was so happy. John ran and ran, chasing after the ball and never forgetting to bring it back to his owner. From then on, the ball never got forgotten. John was always loyal and his owner was so proud of him.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sally. She loved to eat cookies, especially the delicious ones. Today Sally was feeling particularly hungry and ran to the kitchen with excitement. She opened the cupboard and there in the cupboard lay a big plate of delicious cookies. Sally squealed with glee and reached out to take one of the big cookies. She opened up the cookie and savoured the delicious smell. She took a big bite, and grinned as the delicious sweet taste filled her mouth. Sally ate all the yummy cookies, and then lay down on the sofa feeling very happy and satisfied. She was very glad she had decided to lay out and eat the delicious cookies.

Once upon a time, there were two friends Jack and Tom. They were walking through a forest when they saw a blue door. Jack wanted to enter, but Tom said it was a bad idea. But Jack wouldn't listen and he opened the door anyway. Inside the door there were two big men. They were fighting and they were very angry. Jack was scared and quickly closed the door. But it was too late, the men had seen them. All of a sudden, the men burst out of the door. They growled and ran towards Jack and Tom. Jack and Tom were very scared and they ran as fast as they could, but the men were too fast. They caught Jack and Tom and started boxing them. After getting punched many times, Jack and Tom ran away. They never returned to the blue door again. The moral of the story is: always listen to your friends' advice! Even if it's something you don't want to hear, it might be the best thing for you.

Once upon a time there was a strong man. He loved demanding things from others. One day, he saw a little bird perched in a tree. He demanded that the bird obey his command. The little bird didn't know what to do, so she just chirped sadly. The strong man demanded again, and the little bird still didn't understand. He asked one more time, and this time the bird flew away. The strong man was angry! He decided to demand something from the wind. He asked the wind to carry him away from the bird. The result was unbelievable! The wind took him far away, and the bird was safe. The man smiled, happy with the result of his demand.

Once upon a time, there was a big room with lots of things in it. It was all very organized like an organized room. In the middle of the room was an ornament. It shone really brightly. Every morning when the sun came up, the ornament shone even more brightly. One day a small child walked into the room and saw the ornament. She said to it, "What a beautiful ornament. I wish I had something like you." The ornament didn't say anything, but it seemed to be smiling. Soon after the child saw the ornament, she started to explore the room. She found a box full of things and opened it. Inside the box were lots of things that shone just like the ornament. The child was so happy. She said, "All these things are so pretty. Now I can have an ornament just like the one in the middle of the room." The foreshadowing and setup was that the child was enamored of the ornament, and the payoff was that when she opened the box, she found lots of things that shone like ornaments.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved riding the elevator in her building. One day, she saw her neighbor carrying a big bag of candy. "Wow, that looks yummy!" she said. The neighbor smiled and said, "Yes, it is. Do you want to try some?" Lily nodded eagerly and the neighbor gave her a piece of candy. "This candy is heavy," Lily said. "How much does it weigh?" The neighbor replied, "It weighs about one ounce." Lily was fascinated by the weight of the candy and asked the neighbor to weigh other things in the elevator. They had a fun time weighing different items and guessing their weights. From that day on, Lily loved riding the elevator even more because she knew she could weigh things in it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat popcorn while watching his favorite movie. One day, Tim's mom said, "Tim, it's time to clean up your toys." Tim replied, "I want to watch my movie first." His mom said, "Okay, but you need to clean up after the movie is finished." Tim agreed and turned on his movie. As he ate his popcorn, he watched the characters march across the screen. Tim thought to himself, "I want to be independent like them." After the movie, Tim got up and marched to his toy box. He picked up his toys and put them away. His mom was very proud of him for being independent. Tim smiled and said, "Can we have more popcorn now?" His mom laughed and said, "Of course!" And they enjoyed another bowl of popcorn together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a special teddy bear that she loved very much. One day, she was playing with her teddy bear and accidentally broke its handle. She was sad and didn't know what to do. Lily's mommy told her to be careful when playing with her toys so they wouldn't break. Lily felt bad and wanted to fix the handle on her teddy bear. She didn't know how to fix it, so she decided to pray for help. Suddenly, a kind fairy appeared and saw Lily's broken teddy bear. The fairy used her magic wand to fix the handle and make it as good as new. Lily was so happy and thanked the fairy for her help. From that day on, Lily was more careful with her toys and always remembered to pray when she needed help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing songs all day long. Her mommy told her that if she sang a lot, she would lose her tooth. Lily didn't want to lose her tooth, so she stopped singing. One day, Lily's mommy saw that her tooth was wiggling. She told Lily that she would soon lose her tooth. Lily was scared, but her mommy said that the Tooth Fairy would come and leave her a surprise. The next morning, Lily woke up and found a shiny coin under her pillow. She was so happy! She sang a song to thank the Tooth Fairy. Her mommy smiled and said, "Your messy room is now clean. You sang a song and got a prize. That's a good setup and payoff!" Lily didn't understand what that meant, but she was happy that she got a surprise and could sing again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to sing and dance with her friends. One day, Lily's favorite band came to town. They were very popular and everyone wanted to see them. Lily and her friends went to the concert and sang along to all the songs. But then, Lily's little brother started to cry because he was scared of the loud music. Lily hugged him and sang softly to him until he stopped crying. After the concert, Lily and her friends went to meet the band. They took a picture with the band and got autographs. Lily was so happy that she cried tears of joy. From that day on, Lily and her friends talked about the concert and the popular band all the time.

Once upon a time there was a sad little bird. He was feeling lonely on this day and there was nobody around. He looked everywhere, but could not find anyone to play with him. He flew up high in the sky and let out a loud, sad cry. He was hoping that someone might hear him, but there was only silence in the air. Just then, a friendly voice called out from above. It belonged to a nice, kind cloud. "Don't be sad little bird" said the cloud. "Come fly with me and I will provide you with some joy and fun today". The bird eagerly flapped it's wings and flew up above. He was no longer feeling lonely, and the cloud was able to bring him some joy. They spent the day together, playing games, chasing each other and singing songs. The bird was filled with happiness and thanked the cloud for providing him with such a wonderfully fun day. From then on he would never be lonely, for he had made a new, special friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very lonely because he didn't have any friends. He wanted to find a job so that he could meet new people and make friends. One day, Timmy's mommy suggested that he should go to the park and look for a job there. Timmy thought it was a good idea and went to the park. At the park, Timmy saw a man who needed help picking up trash. Timmy asked the man if he could help him and the man said yes. Timmy was very happy because he made a new friend and got a job helping the man. From that day on, Timmy went to the park every day to help the man and he made lots of new friends. He was no longer lonely and was very happy that his mommy suggested he go to the park to find a job.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside and look up at the sky. She loved the sky because it was so big and blue. One day, Lily's mom asked her to clean her room. Lily didn't want to clean her room, so she didn't. Her mom warned her that if she didn't clean her room, she wouldn't be able to go outside and look at the sky. Lily didn't listen to her mom and went outside anyway. But when she looked up at the sky, she saw that it was filthy with dark clouds. Lily felt sad that she couldn't see the blue sky anymore. She realized that she should have listened to her mom and cleaned her room. She went back inside and cleaned her room right away. When she was done, she looked out the window and saw that the sky was blue again. She felt happy and thanked her mom for reminding her to clean her room.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who lived in a small village. One day, there was a big earthquake that shook the ground and made everything wobble. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. His dad told him that everything will be okay and that they just need to be careful. After the earthquake, Timmy saw that his friend Billy's house was destroyed. Billy was crying and sad because he lost all his toys and clothes. Timmy wanted to help his friend, but he didn't know how. He asked his dad what he can do to make Billy feel better. His dad told him that sometimes, the best thing we can do is just be there for our friends and accept them for who they are. Timmy didn't understand what his dad meant by "accept", but he knew that he wanted to help Billy. So, he went to Billy's house and sat with him. They talked about the earthquake and how scary it was. Timmy made Billy laugh by doing silly faces and making funny noises. Timmy learned that being there for someone is important and that we should never judge others for their mistakes. His dad told him that it's foolish to think that we are better than others just because we have more things or because we didn't experience the same things they did. Timmy promised himself that he will always be there for his friends and accept them for who they are.

Tim and Mia were very happy. They were going to fly in a big plane with their mom and dad. They had never flown before and they wanted to see the clouds and the sky. They got on the plane and found their seats. They put on their seat belts and waited for the plane to start. They heard a voice on the speaker. It was the pilot. He said, "Hello, everyone. Welcome to flight 123. My name is Jack and I am your pilot today. We are ready to take off. Please sit back and enjoy the ride." Tim and Mia looked at each other and smiled. They were excited to hear the pilot. They wondered what he looked like and how he could fly the plane. They wanted to meet him and say thank you. The plane moved faster and faster on the ground. Then it lifted up in the air. Tim and Mia looked out the window and saw the houses and cars get smaller and smaller. Then they saw the clouds and the sun. They were amazed by the view. They clapped their hands and laughed. After a while, the pilot came on the speaker again. He said, "We are almost at our destination. We will be landing soon. I hope you had a good time on the plane. Thank you for flying with us." Tim and Mia wanted to say something to the pilot. They asked their mom and dad if they could. Their mom and dad said yes and took them to the front of the plane. They knocked on the door of the cockpit. The pilot opened the door and smiled. He was wearing a red hat and a red jacket. He looked very nice. "Hello, Tim and Mia. I'm glad you came to see me. Did you enjoy the flight?" he asked. "Yes, we did. It was fun and beautiful. You are a great pilot. Thank you for flying the plane," Tim and Mia said. "You're very welcome. I'm happy you liked it. You are very brave and polite. Do you want to see the buttons and the wheels?" the pilot asked. "Yes, please. Can we?" Tim and Mia asked. "Sure. Come in and have a look. But don't touch anything, okay?" the pilot said. "Okay. We won't touch anything," Tim and Mia said. They went inside the cockpit and saw the buttons and the wheels. They were very curious and asked the pilot many questions. The pilot answered them and showed them how he flew the plane. Tim and Mia learned a lot and had a lot of fun. They smiled and thanked the pilot again. They gave him a hug and a high five. The pilot smiled and hugged them back. He said, "You're very welcome. You are very smart and sweet. Maybe one day you can be pilots too." Tim and Mia liked that idea. They said, "Maybe we can. That would be cool." They went back to their seats and told their mom and dad what they saw and learned. Their mom and dad were proud of them and happy for them. They said, "You are very lucky and adventurous. We love you very much." Tim and Mia said, "We love you too." They landed safely and got off the plane. They waved goodbye to the pilot and the plane. They smiled and looked forward to their next adventure.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lulu. Everyday, she went on a walk with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lulu stumbled upon a shiny object in the grass. It was a microscope! Lulu picked up the microscope and looked through it. She could see tiny bugs and ants up close. She was so excited and proud. Mommy and Daddy said that the microscope was very safe. Lulu knew that it was very special and she had to take good care of it. Later that night, Lulu was having dinner with her mommy and daddy. Mommy said to Daddy, "Should we get Lulu her own microscope for her birthday?" Lulu shouted with glee, "Yes please!" Everyone laughed at her enthusiasm. Mommy and Daddy said that they would make sure to find a safe microscope for Lulu's birthday present. Lulu couldn't wait to have her very own microscope!

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jake and Sue, who lived in a tiny universe. One day, Jake thought it would be fun to test their universe. He picked a sour apple and asked Sue to take a bite. As Sue bit into it, something magical happened. The universe changed! Suddenly, there was a huge playground with lots of fun. Jake and Sue explored the playground, trying out different rides and having so much fun. After a while, Jake and Sue knew the test was a success and the playground was their own special universe. They had lots of fun that day and now whenever they want, they can test their universe by picking a sour apple.

One day, a little boy named Tim was very eager. He wanted to go to the park today. He told his mom, "Mom, can we go to the park today?" Mom smiled and said, "Yes, we can go today." At the park, Tim saw his friend, Sue. Sue said, "Hi, Tim! I am happy to see you." Tim said, "Hi, Sue! I am happy too." Tim and Sue played on the swings and the slide. They had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, Tim told Sue, "I will see you soon." Sue said, "Yes, see you soon." Tim told his mom about Sue. He mentioned how much fun they had at the park today. Mom was happy to hear that. They went home and Tim was very tired but happy.

Once upon a time there was a butterfly. He was so pretty and perfect that everyone loved him. The butterfly wanted to find a new home, so he started to look. He saw lots of places, but none seemed quite right. Then, he saw a perfect spot underneath a microscope. "Yes!" he said. "This is it!" He flew underneath the microscope and started to settle down. But then, he relalized that he was stuck! No matter how much he fluttered and tried to move, he could not yield. The butterfly was so sad. He stayed underneath the microscope forever, trapped and alone.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty workman. He was strong, and worked very hard all day long. But one day he found a task that was too much for him. The workman stopped to rest on the side of the work. He was very tired! Then he saw a little ant. The workman asked the ant, "Do you have any ideas on how to finish my work? It's too much for me to do on my own!" The ant replied, "It may take time and hard work, but if you try hard to yield, you can do it. " The workman smiled and thanked the ant. He knew he had a lot of work to do, but he said that even he could do mighty things with a lot of hard work and effort. The workman continued his work, and with each task he completed, he felt stronger. He kept going until he had finished the task! He smiled with pride, realizing that there was nothing too hard or too big for him. The moral of the story is that with a lot of hard work and effort, even the mighty can yield when faced with a challenge.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, while playing hide and seek, Lily's friend Tommy vanished. Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. Lily ran to her mommy and daddy and told them what happened. Her daddy said, "Let's go find Tommy. We will ask the lawyer who lives next door if he saw anything." The lawyer was very honest and told them that he saw Tommy playing near the lake. They rushed to the lake and found Tommy safe and sound. Lily was so happy that her friend was okay. From that day on, Lily and her friends never played near the lake again.

Tommy loved to watch the parade. He liked the big drums, the shiny cars, and the funny clowns. He wanted to be in the parade too. He asked his mom if he could join the parade. He said, "Mom, can I be in the parade? Please, please, please!" His mom smiled and said, "Maybe, Tommy. But you have to be brave. The parade is very loud and long. You have to walk a lot and wave to the people. Are you sure you want to do that?" Tommy nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I want to be brave. I want to be in the parade. I can walk and wave and smile. Please, mom, let me be in the parade." His mom hugged him and said, "Okay, Tommy. You can be in the parade. But you have to stay with me and hold my hand. And you have to listen to the parade leader. He will tell you what to do and where to go. Do you understand?" Tommy said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will stay with you and hold your hand. I will listen to the parade leader. Thank you, mom. You are the best mom ever." Tommy and his mom went to the parade. They wore matching hats and shirts. They joined a group of other kids and parents. They walked and waved and smiled. Tommy had so much fun. He felt very brave. He was in the parade. He was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny carrot. Bunny carrot was thick and bouncy. He was always smiling and his yellow teeth shone in the sun. One day, bunny carrot hopped down the road and met a friendly squirrel. The squirrel was very happy to meet bunny carrot and smiled at him. Bunny carrot thought it was so cool to make a new friend, so he hopped back home. He ran to the garden and grabbed a carrot as a present for his new friend. The next day, bunny carrot brought the carrot to the squirrel. The squirrel was so excited! He smiled at bunny carrot and thanked him for the gift. The two friends became best friends and every day, they would play together and share carrots. They were so happy and would always smile at each other.

One day, a little girl named Sally went to the park with her mom. Sally's mom had a big purse. Inside the purse, Sally found a small, dull rock. She picked it up and showed it to her mom. "Look, Mommy! I found a rock!" said Sally. Her mom smiled and said, "That's a nice rock, Sally. But be careful not to pinch your fingers with it." Sally played with the rock all day. She held it tight in her hand so she wouldn't lose it. But when it was time to go home, Sally felt a pinch on her fingers. "Ouch!" she cried. Her mom looked at her hand and saw the pinch. "I'm sorry, Sally," she said. "Let's put the rock back in the purse so it doesn't hurt you again." Sally agreed and put the rock back in the purse. She felt better now that the rock was safe and her fingers didn't hurt anymore. Sally and her mom walked home, holding hands and talking about their fun day at the park.

Once there was a little girl. She was only three years old and very adventurous. One day, the girl's mommy said, "Let's go to the park!" The little girl was so excited. She jumped up, grabbed her mom and said, "Yippee! I'm ready!" When they got to the park, the little girl wanted to explore. But she saw a large seat and was very fearful. She stopped and asked, "Mommy, what's that big seat?" Her mom smiled and said, "It's a swing. It's fun to swing, but you have to stay on the seat to be safe. Don't quit until I say it is time to." The little girl nodded. She got up on the seat cautiously and held on tight. She swung back and forth, laughing with delight. And soon, when it was time to go, the little girl quit the swing with a big smile.

Lily is a giraffe. She has a very long neck. She can eat leaves from the tall trees. She likes to be with her friends in the savanna. They are all giraffes too. One day, Lily sees a new animal. It is small and brown. It has a short neck and a long nose. It is an elephant. Lily is curious. She wants to say hello. She walks to the elephant. The elephant is friendly. He says hello to Lily. He tells her his name is Sam. He says he is looking for water. He is thirsty. He asks Lily if she knows where to find water. Lily nods. She knows where to find water. There is a big lake near the trees. She tells Sam to follow her. She leads him to the lake. Sam is happy. He thanks Lily. He drinks some water. He splashes some water on his nose. Lily and Sam become friends. They talk and play. They learn about each other. They find out they have some things in common. They both like to eat plants. They both like to be kind. They both think their necks are important. Lily's neck helps her reach the leaves. Sam's neck helps him drink the water. They are proud of their necks. They are proud of their friendship. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her fragile toy dolls. One day, she saw a big closet in her room. She had never seen it before. Lily was very curious about the closet. Lily opened the closet and saw many pretty dresses. She also found a soft, warm blanket. Lily thought it would be fun to lie down on the blanket with her toy dolls. She took the blanket out of the closet and put it on the floor. Lily played with her dolls on the blanket for a long time. She pretended they were having a tea party. After a while, Lily felt very tired. She remembered the warm blanket and decided to lie down on it. She fell asleep and had sweet dreams. When Lily woke up, she saw her mommy standing by the closet. Her mommy smiled and said, "I put the blanket in the closet for you to find. I knew you would love it." Lily hugged her mommy and they played with the dolls together.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Ben. He was playing by the beach, looking for fun. He could see the ocean in the distance. He spotted something in the sand and decided to have a glance. Ben crouched down and gazed at the ground. There in the sand was a big, round shell. He picked it up and admired its beautiful shape. Ben jumped to his feet and ran to the edge of the shore. The sky was pretty gloomy. He peered down the beach. He saw a lady in the distance. She was gazing out to sea. He decided to go and meet her. When Ben arrived, he said hello. The lady smiled and asked "What do you have there?" Ben proudly held up the shell and said, "I found this shell by the shore." The lady smiled and said, "It's a very special find. You should keep it safe." Ben smiled and thanked the lady. He put the shell in his pocket and ran back to the beach. Every time Ben looked at his shell, he thought about the lady by the sea and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a shiny box that she loved to play with. One day, she took her box to the park and showed it to her friend, Tommy. Tommy was glad to see the box and asked Lily if he could play with it. But Lily said no because she didn't want anyone else to touch her special box. This made Tommy sad, and he walked away. Later that day, Lily went home and put her box on her dresser. She went to bed and fell asleep. In the middle of the night, she woke up to a loud noise. She saw that her box was gone! She was so sad and didn't know what to do. The next day, Lily went back to the park and saw Tommy playing with her box. She was so glad to see it again! Tommy had found the box on the ground and had taken it home to keep it safe. Lily thanked Tommy and they played together happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat salad for lunch every day. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to hurry up and finish her salad because they needed to go to the park. Lily replied, "But mommy, my tummy hurts. I can't eat my salad too fast." Mommy said, "Okay, take your time. But we need to hurry so we can play before it gets dark." Lily tried her best to eat her salad as quickly as she could without getting hurt. When she finished, she said, "I'm ready, mommy! Let's go play!"

Once upon a time, there was a kind little girl who wanted to explore the sea. She put on her red swimming costume and headed to the beach. The sun was shining and the water was calm. As she got closer to the sea, she noticed a dolphin in the distance. She was so happy to see it! But before she could get in the water, she remembered what her mum had told her: "Behave, little one". "I promise to behave," she said aloud. She slowly stepped into the warm water and started swimming towards the dolphin. She wanted to get closer, so she came up with a plan. She decided to stay quiet and get as close as she could. The dolphin became curious and came right up to her. The little girl was so excited she wanted to swim with the dolphin, but she remembered what her mum had said. She stayed quiet and calmly watched the dolphin. The dolphin looked at her and then swam away. The little girl was so happy, she had managed to behave. She learned a valuable lesson that day - if we want something, we must stay quiet and be patient.

Lily liked to read big books with many words. She had a dictionary that helped her learn new words. She was very independent and did not need help from anyone. One day, a big dog came to her garden. It barked and ran towards her. Lily was scared and ran to her house. She grabbed her dictionary and held it tight. The dog followed her and scratched at the door. Lily shouted, "Go away, dog! You are not nice!" Her mom heard her and came to see what was wrong. She saw the dog and opened the door. She told the dog, "Shoo, shoo! This is not your home!" The dog ran away and Lily hugged her mom. She said, "Thank you, mom! You protected me from the dog!" Her mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily! I'm proud of you for being brave and independent. And I'm glad you love your dictionary. It's a very useful book."

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She wanted to bake something for her family. So, she went to the market to buy some ingredients. At the market, she saw some yummy food. The market was hot, but she was brave and kept going. She bought some flour, eggs, sugar and butter. With her ingredients she went back home. Back home, she mixed the ingredients and put them in the oven. Her mommy showed her how to do it. Soon, the kitchen smelled yummy. She had made a delicious cake! Everyone was so happy and ate it all up. The girl was proud that she had been able to bake a cake.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a dream to visit a distant crystal. Every day she would ask her parents if they could go on a visit. Lucy's mummy and daddy said they would try to go, but they were very busy. Lucy felt sad and cried. One morning, Lucy's parents took her on a special visit. She was very excited! They rode in a car for a long time until they arrived at the crystal. It was so beautiful, with sparkly colors in the air. But Lucy saw a problem. A big dog was guarding the crystal and it wouldn't let Lucy get close. Lucy was afraid and started to cry. Suddenly, the dog stopped barking and wagged its tail. Lucy realized the dog was her friend, not her enemy. She petted the dog and gave it a hug. The magical crystal was finally in Lucy's reach. She touched it and made a wish. Her visit to the distant crystal was a dream come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside on her porch. Her porch was big and green, just like the grass. One day, Lily saw her friend, Timmy, racing down the street on his bike. "Hi Timmy!" Lily shouted. "Hi Lily!" Timmy shouted back. "Can I race with you?" Lily asked. "Sure!" Timmy said. So, Lily got on her tricycle and they raced down the street. Lily's porch was the finish line. Timmy won the race, but Lily didn't mind. She was just happy to have fun with her friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little mole. The mole lived in a hole in the ground. One day, the mole wanted to jump out of the hole, but it was too high. The mole tried and tried, but it couldn't jump high enough. Then, the mole saw a bitter apple on the ground. The mole thought, "Maybe if I eat the bitter apple, I will be able to jump higher." So, the mole ate the bitter apple. After eating the bitter apple, the mole felt stronger. It jumped and jumped, and finally, it was able to jump out of the hole. The mole was so happy to be out of the hole and see the sunshine. From then on, the mole ate bitter apples every day and became the best jumper in the whole forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. She loved to feel the soft grass under her feet and listen to the birds singing. One day, she went for a walk in the forest with her mom. They saw many beautiful trees and flowers. Lily said, "Mom, nature is so pretty!" Suddenly, they saw a butterfly appear out of nowhere. Lily was so happy and said, "Mom, look! The butterfly appeared!" Her mom replied, "Yes, Lily. Sometimes beautiful things appear when we least expect them." As they continued their walk, they saw a small bird that had fallen from its nest. Lily's mom said, "Let's help the bird and put it back in its nest." They carefully put the bird back in its nest and watched as it snuggled up with its siblings. Lily said, "Mom, it feels good to help nature." From that day on, Lily learned that even small acts of kindness can make a big difference in nature. She always looked for ways to help animals and plants. And sometimes, beautiful things would appear as a reward for her kindness.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Ann. She was three years old and loved playing outside. One day, Ann wanted to try something new. She took a ball out of her toy cupboard and went outside. Ann set off on an adventure with her ball. Ann was walking along when she heard a noise. She looked around and saw that a baby rabbit was stuck. Its foot was stuck in a tight hole. Ann did not want the rabbit to be in trouble. Ann carefully reached down to try and take the rabbit out. She had to pull very hard but with lots of determination she eventually got the rabbit out. Ann was very happy. The rabbit hopped off into the fields and Ann took her ball home.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. They were called Jack and Jill. They both loved to explore and loved having adventures. One day, the two friends were walking through the woods when they came across a shiny crystal. It was so beautiful that they wanted to take it home with them. Jill said, "Let's take it home. It will be so useful!" Jack agreed. But when they tried to pick it up, nothing happened. They both looked at each other, puzzled. Then, Jack had an idea. He turned the crystal around and suddenly it glowed. The crystal then began to lift up and float in the air. The two friends were so excited! The crystal took them on the most magical journey. The crystal flew very high in the sky, over the trees and flowers. After an hour or so, the crystal descended and landed in front of a beautiful castle. Standing at the castle gates was an old man. He smiled and said, "Welcome, brave adventurers! I am the King." Jack and Jill thanked the King for his hospitality. He then gave them a special gift - the magic crystal he had been guarding. "You are both very brave, and this crystal will be very useful to you in your adventures," the King said. He smiled and waved goodbye as Jack and Jill turned and flew away with their new crystal.

Sam and Mia were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food for their toys. Sam found a big white thing in the fridge. He did not know what it was. "Look, Mia, what is this?" he asked, holding the white thing. Mia looked at it and smiled. She knew what it was. It was a cauliflower. Her mom sometimes cooked it for dinner. "It is a cauliflower, Sam. It is a kind of flower that you can eat. Do you want to try it?" she said. Sam was not sure. He did not like flowers. They smelled funny and tasted bitter. He shook his head. "No, thank you. I do not like flowers. They are not good for food. They are good for looking," he said. Mia shrugged. She liked cauliflower. She thought it was crunchy and sweet. She decided to make a dish with it. She took a pot and filled it with water. She put the cauliflower in the pot and set it on the stove. She turned the knob to make the fire. "Be careful, Mia. The fire is hot. It can hurt you," Sam warned. Mia nodded. She was serious. She knew how to be safe in the kitchen. She had watched her mom many times. She put on an oven mitt and a apron. She looked like a real chef. "I know, Sam. I am careful. I am making cauliflower soup. It is yummy. Do you want some?" she offered. Sam looked at the pot. He saw the water boiling and the cauliflower getting soft. He smelled something nice. He was curious. Maybe cauliflower was not so bad after all. "Maybe I will try some. But only a little bit," he said. Mia smiled. She was happy. She liked to share her food with her brother. She took a spoon and a bowl. She scooped some soup and gave it to Sam. She watched him taste it. Sam was surprised. The soup was warm and creamy. It had salt and pepper and butter. It was not bitter at all. It was good. He liked it. "Mmm, this is good, Mia. You are a good chef. Thank you for the soup," he said. Mia beamed. She was proud. She had made a good dish with cauliflower. She had made her brother happy. "You are welcome, Sam. I am glad you like it. Do you want some more?" she asked. Sam nodded. He did want some more. He had changed his mind about cauliflower. He thought it was a good flower for eating. He thought Mia was a good sister for cooking. He thought they were a good team for playing. He was happy.

Sara and Ben are playing with blocks. They want to build a big tower. Sara puts a blue block on top of a red block. Ben puts a yellow block on top of a green block. They take turns to add more blocks. "Look, our tower is so high!" Sara says. She is happy. "Yes, it is!" Ben says. He is happy too. But then, a cat comes into the room. The cat is cute, but it is also curious. It sees the tower and wants to touch it. It jumps on the table and paws at the blocks. "Meow!" the cat says. "Oh no!" Sara and Ben say. The tower falls down. The blocks make a loud noise. Sara and Ben are sad. They frown. "Bad cat!" Sara says. She is angry. "Go away!" Ben says. He is angry too. The cat does not understand. It thinks they are playing. It purrs and rubs against them. It wants to be friends. "Sorry, cat," Sara says. She is not angry anymore. "It's okay, cat," Ben says. He is not angry anymore either. They pet the cat.
