The cat is happy. It licks them. "Maybe we can build another tower later," Sara says. "Or we can play with the cat," Ben says. They smile. They have a new friend. They forget about the tower. They have a different victory.

Molly was a helpful 3 year old who liked to help others. One day, she saw a sad woman in the park and wanted to help her feel better. Molly went over to her and offered her a sandwich. The woman smiled and was grateful. The extra food helped the woman to heal and feel better. Molly was so pleased to know that she could help someone else to heal. She found that it made her very happy. She decided that whenever she saw someone who needed help, she wanted to be sure to offer it. She could tell when people were sad and wanted to help however she could. Molly thought that food was a great way to help heal somebody. She was always looking for ways to help, and she knew making sandwiches was one of her specialties! Whenever someone needed help, she was always happy to help however she could. With a helpful, kind heart and a tasty sandwich, Molly was able to help others heal.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the park with his friends. One day, while playing hide and seek, Timmy discovered a shiny coin on the ground. "Wow, this coin is mighty cool!" Timmy exclaimed. Later that day, Timmy went to the store to buy some candy with his coin. While he was counting his coins, the store owner noticed the shiny one. "Where did you discover this coin?" asked the store owner. Timmy told him about finding it in the park. The store owner smiled and said, "You are very lucky, Timmy. This is a rare and valuable coin!" Timmy was so happy to hear this news. He decided to keep the coin safe and sound. He knew that he had discovered something special and he was proud of himself. From that day on, Timmy always kept his eyes open for new discoveries, hoping to find something as mighty as his shiny coin.

Once upon a time there was a small flag. The flag wanted to surprise something, so it started to flutter. It moved up and down, but it wasn't fast enough. So it thought of a plan. It asked two birds to help it. The birds were happy to help and flapped their wings quickly. The small flag flew high and far. It was so excited and it waved to the sky. Everywhere it went, it brought a surprise. The small flag was now the most famous flag in the world. It made many people happy. So it kept flying until it was tired. Then it rested on a tall tree with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a kind judge. The judge lived in a big house with many rooms. The judge liked to help people. One day, a girl came to the judge. She had a problem. She needed to get a gift for her friend, but she did not know what to get. The judge thought it was an easy problem to solve. The judge told her, "Give your friend something that makes her happy." The girl went to the store and found a pretty doll. She knew her friend would love it. She gave the doll to her friend, and her friend was so happy to receive it. The girl thanked the judge for helping her. They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat dinner with her family every night. One day, her mom made her favorite food, spaghetti with meatballs. It smelled so delicious that Lily's tummy started to growl. As they were eating, Lily accidentally dropped her fork on the floor. She tried to pick it up, but it was too slippery. Suddenly, her brother came over and tried to grab it, but he accidentally stepped on it and it snapped in half. Lily was sad because she loved that fork, but her mom told her not to worry. She gave her a new fork and said that dinner was still delicious, even without the old fork. From that day on, Lily learned that accidents happen, but it's important to enjoy the good things in life, like a yummy dinner with her family.

Once upon a time there was a gifted girl who loved to make things. She always used her scissors to cut paper, fabric and more. One day she was playing in the garden and she saw a carrot. She decided to use her scissors to cut it. But it was too hard and the scissors snapped. The girl was so sad that she couldn't cut it. She had to leave the carrot there in the garden. She put away her scissors, wishing she had been more gifted. The end.

Once upon a time there was an old house. One day, a small boy with a big heart came to visit his new home. He knew it was very special and he wanted to explore. So, off he went. He walked into the living room and saw something strange. On the wall was a mysterious film. He couldn't read the words, but he could feel the film trembling. He gasped - it was alive! He stepped closer and saw the film shaking. He noticed small creatures running and jumping around on the screen. He laughed and clapped his hands - it was so exciting! He wanted to join in the fun. Quickly, he stepped closer and tried to touch the film. Suddenly, it stopped trembling and everything was still. He looked around and saw that all the creatures had gone. But as he was about to leave, something mysterious happened. He heard a little whisper coming from the film and a new creature appeared. They both smiled and the film started to tremble once more.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who loved blueberries. One day, he saw a big blueberry bush and he ran over to it. He was so excited! He grabbed a big plump blueberry and he bit into it. The sweet juice filled his mouth. He ate a few more of the blueberries and soon the bush was empty. He laughed as he licked his fingers. Then, he heard a noise. It was a strange sound. The young boy looked everywhere to find out where it was coming from. Finally, he saw a big green frog, tucked away in a corner of the bush. The frog croaked at the boy and the boy said "Oh hello! I'm sorry I ate all the blueberries". The frog didn't seem angry though. The frog jumped up right next to the boy, and before the boy knew what was happening, the frog had bit him on the hand! The boy gasped and ran away, holding his hand which now hurt. He looked back and saw the frog hopping away, looking proud of itself. The boy never forgot the lesson he learned that day - even the youngest creatures can bite!

Once upon a time there was a ranch filled with animals. Every day the farmer, Mr. Smith, went out to take care of them and make sure they were safe and happy. One day, as Mr. Smith was walking through the ranch, he heard a noise coming from one of the pens. To his surprise, there was a little rabbit hopping about the pen. Mr. Smith said to the rabbit: "What are you doing here?" The rabbit, feeling a bit guilty, replied "I was looking for some food. I was carted away from my home. Can you please help me?" Mr. Smith was moved by the rabbit's story and said he must serve him right away. Mr. Smith took the rabbit home and fed him a delicious meal. After eating, the rabbit felt much better and the two became friends. From then on, Mr. Smith would feed the rabbit every day and the rabbit was happy to stay at the ranch. Mr. Smith knew that he did the right thing - it was only natural to serve and take care of one who needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet bunny named Benny. Benny was very cute and Lily thought he was adorable. One day, Lily found a penny on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to Benny. Benny didn't know what a penny was, but Lily enjoyed showing it to him. Lily and Benny played together all day. They ran around the yard and had lots of fun. When it was time for bed, Lily gave Benny a big hug and said, "I love you, Benny. You're my best friend." Benny wiggled his nose and snuggled up next to Lily. They fell asleep, dreaming of all the fun they would have together tomorrow. The end.

Once upon a time there was a poor man. He wanted a better life, but nothing seemed to happen. One day he went for a walk. He saw a tip next to a tree. He was very excited and started to pick it up. Suddenly, something very good happened! The tip was filled with money! The man was overjoyed and ran home to tell his family. He used the money to buy food and clothes, and they all lived happily ever after. The End.

Once there was a clever rabbit called Judy. One day Judy saw a big tree. She wanted to cut it down, so she could make a house. But she couldn't find a saw, so she looked around for something else to use. Suddenly, she saw a little frog called Fred. Judy had an idea. She asked Fred if he could help her to cut down the tree. She smiled and said, "Can you make me a saw?" Fred thought for a moment. Then he said, "Yes I can!". He clapped his hands and the biggest saw appeared. Judy was very happy and clapped her hands too. They cut down the tree and Judy was able to make a nice house. Judy was very thankful for Fred's help and thanked him for being so clever. The moral of this story is that if you are clever and think outside the box, you can achieve your goals.

Sara and Ben went to see a show with their mom and dad. They saw many people on the stage. Some people sang songs, some people danced, and some people told jokes. Sara and Ben liked the show very much. They clapped their hands when the people did something good. That is called applaud. One lady on the stage had a big hat with flowers on it. She sang a song about a rainbow. Sara and Ben liked her song. They wanted to tell her. After the show, they saw the lady outside. She was talking to some other people. Sara and Ben ran to the lady. They said, "Hello, lady. We liked your song. You have a nice hat." The lady smiled. She said, "Thank you, Sara and Ben. You are very polite. I'm glad you enjoyed the show." She gave them each a flower from her hat. Sara and Ben were happy. They thanked the lady and gave her a hug. Then they went back to their mom and dad. They told them about the lady and the flowers. Mom and dad said, "You are very lucky. The lady is very kind. You should always be polite to people who make you happy." Sara and Ben nodded. They agreed. They liked being polite.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, Lily noticed that her nose was getting cold. "Mommy, my nose is icy!" she said. Her mommy replied, "Oh no! You need to wear your mask to keep your nose warm." Lily put on her mask and continued to play in the snow. She built a big snowman and pretended to have a snowball fight with her imaginary friend. As the sun began to set, Lily's mommy called her inside. "It's time to go in for dinner," she said. Lily smiled and said, "Okay mommy, but can we come back outside tomorrow and play in the snow again?" "Of course, we can," her mommy replied. "But next time, we'll make sure you have a warmer coat."

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their mom. They saw a big truck with a sign that said "Zoo". They ran to the truck and looked inside. They saw many cages with animals. "Look, a lion!" Tom said, pointing to a cage with a big yellow cat. "Wow, he is so big and loud!" Lily said, hearing the lion roar. They moved to the next cage. It had a gray animal with a long nose and big ears. "What is that?" Lily asked. "That is an elephant," mom said. "He can spray water with his nose." "Can we see him do that?" Tom asked. Mom nodded and took them to the front of the cage. She pressed a button and the cage door opened. The elephant walked out and looked at them. He lifted his nose and sprayed water on them. "Wow, he revealed his trick!" Lily said, laughing and getting wet. "Ha ha, that was fun!" Tom said, wiping his face. The elephant smiled and went back to his cage. Lily and Tom thanked him and waved goodbye. They went to see the other animals in the truck. They had a great day at the park.

Jenny liked to look at the magazines in the store. She liked the pictures of the animals and the toys and the dresses. She asked her mom if she could have one. Her mom said no, they were too expensive and they had to go home soon. "But mom, please, just one!" Jenny begged. She saw a magazine with a big pink pony on the cover. She loved ponies. She reached for it and tried to pull it out of the rack. "Jenny, stop that!" her mom said. She grabbed her hand and pulled her away. "You are making a mess and you are being rude. You have to promise me you will not do that again." Jenny felt embarrassed. She saw some other people looking at her and shaking their heads. She did not like it when people were mad at her. She wanted to make her mom happy. She nodded and said, "I promise, mom. I will not do that again." Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Thank you, Jenny. I love you. You are a good girl. Maybe next time we can get a magazine from the library. They have many nice ones there." Jenny felt better. She loved her mom too. She said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. Let's go home." They walked out of the store, holding hands. Jenny forgot about the pony magazine. She was happy to be with her mom.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Bob. He was a brave boy, but one day he felt scared. It was raining outside and he was afraid. He had never seen rain before. But then he saw something pretty. It was a rainbow! He liked the rainbow because it was colourful and he wasn't scared anymore. It reminded him that the rain was only temporary. He went outside and looked up. He saw lots of raindrops falling from the sky, but he wasn't scared anymore because he knew the rainbow was waiting for him when the rain was done. After a few minutes, the rain stopped and the pretty rainbow was in the sky! Bob smiled happily and he wasn't scared anymore. He felt brave and he knew he could face rain again whenever it happened. The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the market with her mom. They were looking for some potatoes to make dinner. Lily noticed a great big potato on the shelf, and she asked her mom to buy it. Her mom said yes, and they took it home. When they got home, Lily's mom started cooking the potato. Lily was so excited to eat it because it looked so great. But when they cut it open, they noticed that it was rotten inside. They couldn't eat it, and they had to throw it away. Lily was sad because she really wanted to eat the potato. But her mom told her that sometimes things that look great on the outside can be bad on the inside. The moral of the story is to always be careful and not judge things by their appearance.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Tara. She was only 3 years old, but was really smart. Every day, she would go to school and learn new things. Today, Tara was in math class. She faced a hard problem and it made her feel a bit dizzy. Then, her teacher encouraged her not to give up. She said that math is important and it helps Tara to grow and become smarter. Tara eventually solved the problem, and she felt so proud! As she continued to learn more and more math, her teacher kept encouraging her. This story teaches us an important lesson. Whenever we face something difficult, it can be helpful to get some encouraging words. This encourages us to never give up and reach our goals.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance to jazz music. One day, she went to a jazz concert with her mommy and daddy. The music was so brilliant that Lily couldn't stop moving her feet. Suddenly, a big boy pushed Lily and she fell down. She started to cry because her knees hurt. Her mommy and daddy were angry at the big boy for hurting their little girl. But then, the big boy said sorry and helped Lily up. They settled their conflict and enjoyed the rest of the concert together. From that day on, Lily and the big boy became friends and danced together to the brilliant jazz music.

Once upon a time, there was a little oyster named Bobby. Bobby was brown and lived in the ocean with his family. One day, the sun came out and started to shine on the water. Bobby saw the sun and thought it was very pretty. Bobby wanted to see the sun shine on him, so he opened up his shell. When he did, a shiny pearl fell out! Bobby was so happy because he had never seen anything so shiny before. Bobby showed his shiny pearl to all of his oyster friends and they were amazed. They had never seen a pearl that shiny before. From that day on, Bobby loved when the sun would shine on him because it made his pearl sparkle and shine too.

Once upon a time, the sky hang a big bunch of grapes. The grapes looked so brilliant and juicy. All the animals wanted it very much. One hot day, the animals gathered together and started to plan to get the grapes. The tiger said: "I will jump up and reach the grapes!" The monkey said: "I can climb up the tree and hang onto the branch!" But then the fox said: "Wait. I have a brilliant idea. Let's all work together! We can make a big tower out of our bodies and then one of us can reach the grapes." So the animals worked together and made a big tower. The tiger jumped up and grabbed the grapes. Everyone cheered for the fox's brilliant idea. The animals enjoyed the grapes and had a great time.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy staff. Its name was Clumsy. Tom and Jill had never seen a staff like Clumsy before. They fed Clumsy some nice treats and wanted to play with it. Jill wanted to hold Clumsy, so Tom gave it to her. But Clumsy was so clumsy that it slipped out of Jill's hands and fell on the ground. Tom and Jill were sad when the clumsy staff was broken. So the two friends decided to make a new staff for Clumsy. They took some sticks and tied them together. Tom and Jill painted it beautiful colors and called it "New Clumsy". Then they gave it back to the clumsy staff. From that day forward, Clumsy was never clumsy anymore. Tom and Jill were happy and enjoyed playing with New Clumsy!

Once there was a little dog named Jack. He was so little and helpless, he could only crawl around. One day, Jack decided to explore the world around him. He started to climb up the stairs, but suddenly he saw something strange in the corner - a big pile of spaghetti! He just couldn't resist trying it. Jack started crawling closer and he could smell the delicious spaghetti. He was about to eat it when suddenly he heard a voice: "No, Jack! You can't eat this spaghetti!" It was Jack's mommy. She had found him trying to eat spaghetti and she knew he was too little to do it on his own. Jack was so embarrassed and he crawled away, feeling so helpless. His mommy smiled and said, "Don't worry, Jack. I'll make you your own plate of spaghetti for dinner later. You can have it then!" Jack was so happy and he crawled away to find something else to do. He never forgot that day, and he still loves spaghetti to this day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved ice-cream so much. One day, he saw an ancient ice-cream truck. The truck was very old and slow, but it had a big sign that said "Ice-Cream". Tim went to the truck and said, "Hi, can I have ice-cream, please?" The ice-cream man looked at him and said, "Sure, little boy. Here you go." Tim took the ice-cream and started to eat it. But it did not taste good at all. It tasted very bad. Tim screamed, "Yuck! This ice-cream is bad!" The ice-cream man just laughed and said, "I am sorry, little boy. The ice-cream is too old." Tim was very sad and walked away. He did not get to enjoy his ice-cream that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red wagon with four big wheels. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park to play. Timmy wanted to bring his wagon, so he rolled it all the way to the park. At the park, Timmy saw a man who was deaf. The man couldn't hear anything, but he was very nice. Timmy wanted to share his wagon with the man, so he let him roll it around the park. The man smiled and thanked Timmy for being so kind. After playing with the wagon, Timmy and the man sat on a bench and watched the other kids play. Timmy was happy to have made a new friend, even if he couldn't hear very well. They rolled the wagon back home together, and Timmy promised to visit the man again soon.

Anna and Ben were playing in the sand with their buckets and shovels. They made a big castle with towers and walls and a moat. They were very happy and proud of their work. But then a big dog came running and jumped on their castle. He broke the towers and the walls and made a big mess. He also bit Anna's bucket and made a hole in it. Anna and Ben were very sad and angry. They shouted at the dog to go away. "Bad dog! Bad dog! You broke our castle and our bucket! Go away!" they cried. The dog did not listen. He wagged his tail and barked. He thought they were playing with him. He ran around and kicked more sand on their castle. Anna and Ben felt helpless. They did not know what to do. They looked for their mom and dad, but they were far away on the beach. They wished they could fix their bucket and their castle. Then they saw Lily, their friend from the kindergarten. She was walking with her mom and her bucket. She saw Anna and Ben and the dog and the mess. She felt sorry for them. "Hi, Anna and Ben. What happened?" she asked. "A big dog broke our castle and our bucket. He won't go away. We are very sad," Anna said. "That's not nice. Do you want to play with me? I have a bucket. We can share it and make a new castle," Lily said. Anna and Ben smiled. They liked Lily. She was very kind. They nodded and said yes. "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend," Ben said. Lily's mom called the dog and took him away. He was not a bad dog, just a playful one. He did not mean to break their things. Anna and Ben and Lily took their buckets and shovels and went to a new spot. They made a new castle, bigger and better than before. They had fun and forgot about the dog and the mess. They were happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a special button. When she used the button, something amazing would happen. One day, the little girl decided to try out her button. She put her finger on top of the button and pushed it. Suddenly, an amazing thing happened - the button lit up in beautiful colors. The little girl was so excited by what the button had done. She used the button ever day and saw something new and amazing each time. Soon, the little girl realized that the button held a very special power. She used the button to play games and make wonderful music. The little girl was delighted with the power of her button. She was determined to keep using it and explore the amazing things it could do.

Once upon a time, there was a man who had a big axe. The axe was very flexible and could cut through anything. One day, the man went into the forest to chop some wood. He swung his axe and it hit a tree. Suddenly, the axe flew out of his hand and hit him on the foot. He cried out in pain. A little girl who was walking in the forest heard the man crying. She went over to him and asked what happened. The man told her that his axe had hit him on the foot. The little girl said, "You should be careful with your axe. It's very dangerous." The man said, "You're right. I will be more careful from now on." But the man didn't listen to the little girl. He picked up his axe and started chopping again. This time, the axe flew out of his hand and hit him on the head. He cried out again, but this time he didn't get up. The little girl ran to get help, but it was too late. The man had died from his injuries. The little girl cried and cried because she was sad that the man had died.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Mary. Mary was very rich and very happy. She had lots of nice things, but sometimes she was sad because she was ill. One day, Mary's mom said to her, "We need to go to the doctor and get you some medicine, Mary." Mary was scared but nodded her head. At the doctor's, Mary was given some medicine. She didn't like it very much because it tasted bad. But, the doctor said it was very important to take the medicine so she did. When she got home, Mary's mom hugged her and said, "See, dear? I told you the medicine would make you feel better." Mary was glad. She felt much better and she was happy again. She hugged her mom and said "Thank you for getting me the medicine. Now I'm not sick anymore!" The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in her backyard. One day, she saw a big gate. It was shiny and new, and it looked like it could keep anything out. Lily wanted to open the gate and see what was on the other side. But her mom warned her that it was hot outside and she should wait until it was cooler. Lily didn't want to wait, so she went outside anyway. She tried to open the gate, but it was stuck. She pulled and pulled until finally, she heard a loud tear. The gate had ripped right off its hinges! Lily felt bad for breaking it, but she also felt brave for trying to open it. From then on, she always listened to her mom's advice and waited until it was cooler outside before playing.

One day, a tall boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw a big tree with a hook on it. Tim thought it was a fun place to play. He ran to the tree and said, "I want to play here!" As Tim played, he met a small girl named Sue. Sue looked at the hook and said, "We can hang our bags on it!" They both hung their bags on the hook and played together all day. They had a lot of fun. Later, the sky turned dark. Tim and Sue knew they had to hurry home. They grabbed their bags from the hook and ran back to their houses. When they got home, they told their moms and dads about the fun they had at the big tree with the hook. They couldn't wait to play there again.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers. The older brother was naughty and liked to push the little brother around. He thought it was fun to push his brother around and never stopped. Every time the older brother pushed the little one, the little brother would cry. He did not like it that his brother was naughty. He wanted his brother to stop. One day the little brother had enough of the pushing and decided to fight back. He pushed back hard! The older brother was not expecting it and fell down. He laughed and said, "You're really strong little brother!" The little brother was happy that his brother had learned his lesson. He also learned that it was important to stand up for himself. From then on, he kept pushing back whenever his brother got naughty.

Timmy liked to play with his toy lion. He made it roar and jump on his bed. He pretended he was a brave hunter who could catch the big lion. He had fun with his lion every day. One day, Timmy had to go to the doctor. He was scared of the doctor. He thought the doctor would hurt him with a needle. He did not want to go. He took his lion with him. He hoped his lion would protect him. At the doctor's office, Timmy met a nice nurse. She smiled at him and said hello. She asked him his name and what he liked to play with. Timmy showed her his lion and said he liked to roar. The nurse said she liked lions too. She said they were strong and brave, but also harmless and friendly. She said she had a lion sticker for him. The nurse gave Timmy the sticker and put it on his shirt. She said he was a good boy and he could roar as much as he wanted. She said the doctor would not hurt him, but only check him and make him feel better. She said she would be with him all the time. Timmy felt less scared. He liked the nurse and the sticker. He roared with his lion and smiled at the nurse. He said thank you and followed her to the doctor. He was still a little nervous, but he knew his lion and the nurse were with him. He was a brave hunter and a good boy.

Once upon a time there was a clever bear. He wanted to measure how high the ceiling was in his cave. He looked around, but he didn't have anything that he could use. He thought and thought, but he still couldn't figure out how to do it. Just then he had a brilliant idea. He got some string from a nearby tree and tied it to the floor. He slowly pulled the string up and measured how high it went. When he reached the ceiling, he stopped. The bear smiled, he had measured the ceiling perfectly! He was very happy. He thanked his cleverness for helping him to find a way. The end.

Little Sam had a very special treasure. It was a tiny necklace made of shiny stones. The necklace never left him, he always wore it around his neck. Every day, he put on his shiny treasure and went on an adventure. He played with his friends in the park and ran around the school grounds. He was never lonely. But one day, Little Sam had no one to play with. His friends were all busy, so he was all alone. He felt so lonely and sad. He looked at his necklace, and it suddenly seemed to twinkle brighter. It suddenly reminded him of good times with his friends, and it made him feel not so lonely anymore. Little Sam never went anywhere without his treasure again. He wore it everyday and felt safe and happy.

Sara loved to paint. She had many colors and brushes and papers. She liked to paint flowers and animals and rainbows. She was happy when she painted. One day, her big brother Tom came home with a new basketball. He wanted to play with it outside. He saw Sara's paintings on the table. He did not like them. He said they were silly and ugly. He took one of them and ripped it. He threw it in the trash. Sara was very sad. She cried and ran to her room. She felt miserable. She did not want to paint anymore. Tom felt bad. He knew he was mean to Sara. He wanted to say sorry. He went to her room and knocked on the door. He heard Sara sniffing. "Sara, can I come in?" he asked. "No, go away!" Sara said. "Please, Sara, I want to talk to you. I'm sorry I ripped your painting. It was wrong of me. You are a good painter. Your paintings are beautiful." Sara opened the door a little. She looked at Tom. He had a big smile and a surprise. He gave her a new paper and a new brush. He also gave her his basketball. "Here, Sara, these are for you. I want you to paint something for me. Maybe you can paint a basketball. Or anything you like. And you can play with my basketball too. I can teach you how to bounce it and throw it. Do you want to try?" Sara smiled too. She took the paper and the brush and the basketball. She hugged Tom and said thank you. She felt happy again. She wanted to paint and play. Tom and Sara went outside. They painted and played together. They had fun. They were nice to each other. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a humble kangaroo. He lived in a small forest and liked to roll through the grass. Every day he would go for a nice roll and take in all the sights and smells around him. He had some good friends he would roll with, like a rabbit, an elephant, and a monkey. One day while they were rolling through the grass, they came across a big hill. It was so big and so high that they had no idea how they would ever get to the top. But the kangaroo had an idea. He said to his friends, "Let's all roll together, and we'll make it to the top." So they all lined up and started to roll. As they rolled, they went higher and higher, until they finally made it to the top. At the top, they could see all the way across the forest. It was so beautiful, and they all felt so proud. From then on, whenever the kangaroo and his friends wanted to see a nice view, they would come back to the top of the hill and roll together.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play with their toys and make funny noises. One day, they find a big box in the living room. It has a bow and a tag that says "For Tim and Kim, from Mom and Dad". "What is in the box?" Tim questions. He wants to open it and see. "We have to wait until tomorrow. It is a surprise for our birthday," Kim says. She knows the rules. But Tim is curious. He tries to shake the box and listen. He does not hear anything. He tries to peek under the bow and the tape. He does not see anything. "Come on, Kim. Let's open it. Just a little bit. Mom and Dad will not know," Tim says. He gives Kim a wink. He thinks he is clever. Kim shakes her head. She does not want to spoil the surprise. She likes surprises. She also likes to follow the rules. "No, Tim. We have to wait. Mom and Dad will be sad if we open it. They worked hard to get us something nice," Kim says. She tries to stop Tim from touching the box. But Tim does not listen. He pulls the bow and the tape. He opens the box. He looks inside. He gasps. "What is it? What is it?" Kim questions. She is worried. She hopes Tim did not break anything. Tim does not answer. He is too shocked. He stares at the box. He sees a big, fluffy, white bunny. It has long ears and a pink nose. It looks at Tim and Kim. It makes a funny noise. "Surprise!" Mom and Dad say. They come into the living room. They see Tim and Kim and the bunny. They smile. "Happy birthday, Tim and Kim! We got you a new friend. His name is Fluffy. He likes to hop and cuddle and eat carrots. Do you like him?" Mom says. Tim and Kim do not know what to say. They feel happy and guilty and scared and excited. They look at Mom and Dad and Fluffy. They hug them all. "Thank you, Mom and Dad. We love Fluffy. He is so cute and funny. We are sorry we opened the box. We were curious. We will take good care of him," Tim and Kim say. Mom and Dad laugh. They are not angry. They understand. "It's okay, Tim and Kim. We know you were curious. We are glad you like Fluffy. He is a special gift for our special twins. We love you very much. Happy birthday!" Dad says. Tim and Kim smile. They feel happy. They have a new friend. They have a surprise. They have a funny story to tell. They have a good birthday.

One day, two children were walking in the park. One of the children called out, "Look! There is so much ice over there!" The other child said, "Let's cover it and make it a big slide!" The first child said, "That's a great idea!" The two children ran to the ice and started to try and cover it. They pushed and tugged, but it was too heavy. As they kept trying, the ice started to crack. Suddenly, there was a loud noise and the ice broke apart, and the children tumbled down. As they looked around, they saw that the ice had all broken up and gone away. The heavy ice was now gone. The two children looked at each other in shock and sadness. They had hoped to make a nice slide but in the end, their plan had gone wrong.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted little girl. Every day, she rose early and went to the fields to help harvest wheat. Her friends came along to help her, and they all had a lot of fun. One day, when they were done gathering the wheat, the little girl called out to her friends, "Let's make a big tower out of the wheat!" Everyone cheered and said it was a great idea. So they all worked together to build the tower. They rose one wheat stalk at a time until it was as tall as they were! They were so proud of their tower and they all cheered when it was done. The little girl then smiled and said, "Together, we really can do anything!" Her friends agreed, and they laughed as they ran off to play.

Once upon a time there was an cool dragon. It loved to explore and fly around the world. One day it came across a peaceful village and decided to settle there. It made its home in a cave near the village. Everyone was very excited to have a dragon living close by! The dragon was so friendly and kind, it helped the villagers with all sorts of tasks. It flew high up in the sky to collect clouds for rain, and loved playing hide and seek with the children. On hot days it cooled down the village by blowing a gentle breeze. The villagers were so happy to have their dragon friend. They even threw a special party for it! The dragon had a wonderful time, and settled back in its cave when the night ended. The dragon and the villagers became good friends. And to this day, he still visits the village, bringing cool winds and fun adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard and find treasures. One day, she found an old box full of junk. She didn't think much of it and left it there. The next day, Lily's mom asked her to help make some cookies. They got all the ingredients out and Lily saw the box of junk. She remembered that there was a spoon inside that she could use to stir the cookie dough. So, they opened the box and found the spoon. But, they also found an original recipe for chocolate chip cookies! Lily and her mom followed the recipe and made the most delicious cookies they had ever tasted. Lily was so happy that she found the box of junk and they were able to make something so yummy. From then on, she always looked for hidden treasures in her backyard.

One day, there was a unique toilet. It was special because it could wash itself. Every time the toilet was used, it would automatically give itself a good wash. The 3 year old was amazed by this special toilet and took a closer look. He was so intrigued he even took a seat! As soon as he sat on the toilet, it began to wash itself. It sparkled so much the 3 year old couldn't believe his eyes. From that day on, the 3 year old always wanted to sit on the unique toilet and watch it wash itself. He was fascinated every time!

Tim likes to read books. He has many books with pictures and words. He can read some words by himself, but not all. He likes to ask his mom or dad to read with him. One day, Tim wants to read a book about sport. He likes sport. He likes to run and jump and kick a ball. He finds a book with a big ball on the cover. He thinks it is about sport. He opens the book and sees many words. He does not know the words. He feels frustrated. He goes to his mom and says, "Mom, can you read this book with me? It is about sport. I like sport." His mom looks at the book and smiles. She says, "Tim, this book is not about sport. It is about math. It has numbers and shapes and problems. It is too hard for you right now. You can read it when you are older." Tim is confused. He says, "But it has a ball on the cover. Why does it have a ball if it is not about sport?" His mom says, "The ball is a sphere. A sphere is a shape. It is a math word. The book uses the ball to teach you about spheres and other shapes." Tim does not like math. He does not want to learn about spheres and other shapes. He wants to read about sport. He says, "I don't like this book. I want a book about sport. Do you have a book about sport?" His mom says, "Yes, I do. I have a book about soccer. It has pictures and words that you can read. Do you want to read it with me?" Tim says, "Yes, please. I love soccer. Thank you, mom." He gives his mom a hug and they go to the couch to read the book about soccer. Tim is happy. He likes to read books with his mom.

Once upon a time there was a weird delivery man who was driving his truck. He was going far and wide to deliver packages. One day he came to a big hill that was too tall for his truck to get up. He stopped to think and suddenly he got an idea! He found a screw and with the help of the screw he fixed his truck. Now the truck could drive up to the big hill! He was so happy and continued to deliver his packages. He was proud of himself for using his brain to solve the problem. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat cauliflower, but her mommy didn't like it. One day, Lily went to the store with her mommy and saw a big, beautiful cauliflower. She asked her mommy if they could buy it and her mommy said no. Lily was sad and started to cry. A kind old lady saw her crying and asked what was wrong. Lily told her about the cauliflower and the old lady said she had some at her house. She gave Lily a piece of cauliflower and Lily felt so happy. She said "thank you" to the old lady and ran back to her mommy. When they got home, Lily's mommy was dizzy and felt sick. They had to go to the hospital and it turned out the cauliflower was bad. Lily felt so sad and wished she had listened to her mommy. From then on, Lily always listened to her mommy's advice.

Once upon a time, there was a mechanic named Dave. He loved his job and enjoyed fixing things for people. One day, Dave got a very special job - he had to fix an orange truck. When Dave arrived at the garage, he couldn't believe his eyes. The truck was so orange! Dave was excited to get started on the job. But as he began to work, Dave realized it was a hard job. He worked and worked, but still the truck wouldn't work. Dave became discouraged, and was starting to give up. He thought to himself, "I don't think I can fix it!" Just then, Dave heard the voice of his friend, who said, "Don't give up, Dave! If you try hard enough, you can do anything!" With new determination and courage, Dave worked harder. In the end, he was able to fix the truck. He proved to himself that if you don't give up, and if you keep trying, you can achieve anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her rubber duck in the bathtub. One day, she accidentally dropped her rubber duck and it went down the drain. Lily was very sad and started to cry. Her mommy asked her what was wrong and Lily said, "My duckie is gone, mommy. I hope we can get it back." Mommy tried to get the rubber duck out of the drain, but it was stuck. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. We can't get it out." Lily was still sad, but then her mommy had an idea. She said, "Let's go to the store and get a new rubber duckie for you to play with." Lily's face lit up with joy and she said, "Yay! Thank you, mommy!" They went to the store and picked out a new rubber duckie for Lily to play with in the bathtub. She was very happy and said, "I love my new duckie. Thank you, mommy."

Lily liked to read books. She had many books in her room. She read about animals, colors, shapes, and stories. She read every day with her mom or dad. One day, Lily went to the pool with her mom. She saw other kids playing in the water. She wanted to play too, but she was nervous. She had never been in the pool before. She did not know how to swim. Her mom saw that Lily was nervous. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will help you. You can wear this floaty. It will keep you safe and happy in the water. You can also bring your book. You can read it on the side of the pool or in the water." Lily liked that idea. She put on her floaty and took her book. She followed her mom to the pool. She sat on the edge and dipped her feet in the water. It was cold and wet, but it felt good. She opened her book and read it. She saw a picture of a fish. She smiled. She looked up and saw her mom in the water. Her mom waved at her and said, "Come on, Lily. The water is fun. You can read and swim at the same time. I will be with you. You can do it." Lily felt brave. She closed her book and put it on the ground. She slid into the water and held her mom's hand. She kicked her legs and moved her arms. She felt the water splash on her face. She laughed. She liked the pool. She was not nervous anymore. She was happy.

Lily liked to play with her dolls in the garden. She had a big dollhouse with many rooms and furniture. She also had a small vase with pretty flowers that she put on the table. One day, a friendly bird came to visit her. The bird was blue and yellow and had a sweet song. Lily smiled and said hello to the bird. She gave it some seeds and water from her dollhouse. The bird liked Lily and stayed with her. The next day, Lily wanted to play with the bird again. She went to the garden and looked for it. She saw it on the fence, but it did not fly to her. It looked sad and tired. Lily wondered what was wrong. She noticed that the vase with the flowers was empty. The water had dried up and the flowers had wilted. Lily felt sorry for the bird. She realized that the bird needed fresh flowers to be happy. She ran inside and asked her mom for some new flowers. Her mom gave her a bunch of roses and helped her fill the vase with water. Lily thanked her mom and ran back to the garden. She put the vase on the table and called the bird. The bird saw the roses and perked up. It flew to the vase and smelled the flowers. It sang a happy song and rubbed its head on Lily's cheek. Lily hugged the bird and smiled. She was glad that the bird was happy again. They played together until the sun began to rise.

Joey was a lucky boy. He had many toys to play with and lots of fun! One day, Joey opened his toy box and what did he find? A shiny new toy car! Joey was so excited. He opened up the car and found a key inside. He put it inside the car and opened and closed the doors. He was very happy! He spent all day playing with the car and having lots of fun. What a lucky boy!

John and his family were on vacation. They wanted to explore the sea, so they requested a dependable yacht. They were so excited! The yacht was big and brightly coloured. It was ready to sail on the waves. John's dad was a captain, so he knew how to sail the yacht. He took everyone on a journey around the island. John and his siblings all had turns steering the yacht. Everyone was having fun! At the end of the day, John's dad asked if everyone knew how to sail the yacht. Everyone nodded yes. They said good-bye to the dependable yacht and made plans for their next adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl. She had a very nice, safe house, where she kept all of her most prized treasures. Every day, the girl would go outside and play. One day, she heard a disturbed noise. She was scared, but tried to stay safe. The girl looked around and discovered something. Hidden in the bushes was a prize! It was a big, shiny box, and it glinted in the sun. The girl was so excited, she took it home and opened it. To her surprise, inside was a big, sparkly doll. She was so happy, she hugged it and put it in her safe house with the rest of her prized treasures. The girl was so relieved that nothing had disturbed her safe house, and all of her treasures were safe. The end.

Once there was a young woman. She was going to the river to do her washing. As she walked, the sun shone happily and birds chirped in the trees. When she got to the river, she took off her shoes and socks. She rolled up her trousers and carefully stepped into the cool water. She washed her clothes, splashing and singing. Suddenly, a little 3-year-old boy came running down to the water's edge. He had heard the happy singing, and he was curious to see who was singing. The young woman stopped washing her clothes and smiled at the little boy. She reached out her hand and said, "Hello, I'm washing my clothes. Would you like to join me?" The little boy smiled and nodded. Together, the woman and the boy tossed stones into the river and sang happy songs until all of the clothes were clean and dry.

Ben and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But today, Mom says they have to help with the laundry. She gives them a big basket of dirty clothes and tells them to take it to the washing machine. Ben and Lily do not want to do laundry. They think it is boring and hard. They want to play with their toys. They hope Mom will forget about the laundry and let them play. They walk slowly to the washing machine. They see a big pile of clean clothes on the sofa. They have an idea. They put the basket of dirty clothes on the floor and start to throw the clean clothes in the air. They pretend they are snowflakes and catch them with their hands. They laugh and have fun. Mom hears them and comes to see what they are doing. She is not happy. She sees the clean clothes all over the floor and the dirty clothes still in the basket. She says, "Ben and Lily, what are you doing? You are making a mess. You are supposed to do the laundry, not play with it. Now you have to pick up all the clothes and put them back where they belong. And then you have to do the laundry. No more playing until you finish." Ben and Lily are sad. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We did not want to do the laundry. We wanted to play. We thought laundry was easy. But it is not. It is hard and boring." Mom says, "I know, laundry is not fun. But it is something we have to do. It is part of being a family. We all have to help with the chores. If we do them together, they will be easier and faster. And then we can have more time to play. Come on, I will help you. Let's do the laundry together. And then we can play with your toys. OK?" Ben and Lily nod. They say, "OK, Mom. Thank you. We will help you. We will do the laundry together. And then we can play." They pick up the clothes and put them back where they belong. They take the basket of dirty clothes to the washing machine. They help Mom put the clothes in and press the buttons. They watch the clothes spin and make bubbles. They think it is a little bit fun. They hope the laundry will be done soon. And then they can play.

Once there was a boy called Tim. He was three years old and very honest. He wanted to do something special, so he decided to raise his hand. He raised it high to show everyone he wanted to say something. Everyone looked at him and smiled. Then Tim began to raise his eyebrows and he closed one eye and winking. Everyone was surprised and laughed. They thought this was very funny. Tim kept raising his eyebrows and winking. He kept going until he started to giggle. Everyone around laughed too, and a few people started to wink back. Soon, everyone was winking and raising their eyebrows! It was so much fun! Tim was so happy, for he had done something special and it made all the people smile.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to collect rocks. They have a big box of rocks at home. They want to find more rocks. They go to the park with a bag. At the park, they see many rocks. Some are big, some are small, some are shiny, some are dull. They run to the rocks and start to fill their bag. They are happy. But Tim is clumsy. He trips over a rock and falls. He hurts his knee. He cries. Sam hears him and runs to him. He sees Tim's knee is bleeding. He says, "Are you okay, Tim?" Tim says, "No, I'm not okay. I hurt my knee. It's bad. I want to go home." Sam says, "Don't worry, Tim. I'll help you. Here, take my hand. We'll go home together. We can come back another day to collect more rocks." Tim says, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good friend. I'm sorry I was clumsy." Sam says, "It's okay, Tim. Everyone is clumsy sometimes. The important thing is to help each other when we are hurt. That's what friends do." They walk home slowly, holding hands. They still have their bag of rocks. They are still happy. The moral value of the story is: Friendship is more valuable than collecting things. Friends should help each other when they are in trouble. Being clumsy is not a bad thing, as long as you learn from your mistakes.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to swing on the swings and slide on the slide. They also liked to hang from the monkey bars and pretend they were monkeys. One day, they saw a new thing in the park. It was a big rope with a loop at the end. It was hanging from a tree. Lily and Tom wondered what it was for. "Maybe it is for jumping," Lily said. "Or for flying," Tom said. They decided to try it. Lily went first. She put her foot in the loop and pulled the rope. She felt the rope lift her up. She felt happy and excited. "Look at me, Tom! I am flying!" she shouted. Tom clapped his hands and cheered. He wanted to try it too. He waited for Lily to come down. But Lily did not come down. She was stuck. The loop was too tight around her foot. She could not get it off. She started to cry. "Help me, Tom! I am stuck!" she cried. Tom ran to the tree. He tried to pull the rope. But the rope was too high and too strong. He could not reach it. He felt scared and worried. "Help! Help!" he yelled. A man heard them. He was walking his dog in the park. He saw Lily and Tom. He saw the rope. He knew what it was for. It was not for playing. It was for catching animals. It was a trap. He felt angry and sorry. He ran to the tree. He had a knife. He cut the rope. He freed Lily. He lifted her down. He checked her foot. It was red and sore. But it was not broken. He felt relieved and glad. "Are you okay, little girl?" he asked. Lily nodded. She hugged him. She thanked him. She felt safe and grateful. Tom hugged Lily. He hugged the man. He thanked him too. He felt happy and thankful. The man smiled. He told them to be careful. He told them not to play with the rope. He told them it was dangerous. He told them it was a trap. He felt kind and helpful. Lily and Tom felt guilty. They knew they did a bad thing. They knew they should not have played with the rope. They knew they could have been hurt. They felt sorry and ashamed. They said sorry to the man. They said sorry to each other. They said sorry to the animals. They felt sorry and sorry. They learned a lesson. They learned to be safe. They learned to be smart. They learned to be good. They felt better and better.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to play golf with his friends. One day, Mittens got very angry when he lost a game of golf. He wanted to destroy the golf course. But then, Mittens remembered something his mommy had told him. She said that it's not nice to destroy things when we're angry. Mittens thought about it and realized that it was true. Instead, Mittens apologized to his friends for being a sore loser and they forgave him. Mittens learned that it's important to be a good sport and to control our anger.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the garden. They had a big box of toys and they could build anything they wanted. One day, they decided to build a castle with blocks and a sword with sticks and tape. "Look at my sword!" Ben said, holding up his stick. "It is long and sharp. I can fight the bad guys with it." "Wow, that is a good sword!" Lily said, admiring his work. "Can I try it?" Ben thought for a moment. He liked his sword very much, but he also liked Lily. She was his friend and she always shared her toys with him. He decided to be generous and let her use his sword. "Okay, you can try it," he said, handing her the stick. "But be careful, it is very strong." "Thank you, Ben, you are very generous," Lily said, smiling. She took the stick and pretended to swing it around. "I am a brave knight, too. I can help you protect the castle." They played together for a long time, having fun and making noises. They built a big castle with blocks and put a flag on top. They used their sword to fight the bad guys and save the princess. They were happy and proud of their work. They were good friends and good builders.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his ball and run in the park. One day, Spot saw a big camera on the grass. Spot was curious and wanted to see what the camera was for. Spot's friend, a little girl named Sue, came over and said, "Spot, I want to take a picture of you with this camera. But you need to improve your pose. Can you sit and smile for me?" Spot nodded and tried his best to sit still and smile for Sue. But as Sue was about to take the picture, a naughty cat named Whiskers jumped in front of the camera. Whiskers wanted to be in the picture too! Spot and Whiskers started to argue about who should be in the picture. Sue said, "Stop! We can all be in the picture together. Let's be friends and share." Spot and Whiskers agreed, and they all posed for a friendly picture together.

Lily and Ben were excited to go to the lake with their dad. They liked to swim, splash and play with the fish. They also liked to find logs and sticks to make boats and rafts. "Look, dad, I found a big log!" Ben shouted, dragging a long piece of wood to the shore. "Can we make a boat with it?" "Sure, Ben, that's a great log for a boat. Let's see if we can find some rope and a sail," dad said, smiling. Lily ran to help Ben with the log. She saw a blue towel and a stick nearby. "I have an idea, Ben. We can use this towel as a sail and this stick as a mast. Then we can tie them to the log with this rope," she said, holding up the items. "Wow, Lily, you are very smart. That's a good idea. Let's do it," Ben said, nodding. They worked together to make the boat. They tied the rope around the log and the stick. They attached the towel to the stick with some knots. They made sure the boat was strong and stable. "Are you ready, Ben?" Lily asked, holding the boat. "Yes, I'm ready, Lily. Let's send our boat to the water," Ben said, grabbing the other end of the boat. They lifted the boat and carried it to the edge of the lake. They counted to three and pushed the boat into the water. The boat floated and the wind blew the sail. "Look, dad, look! Our boat is sailing!" Lily and Ben shouted, jumping and clapping. "Wow, you two, you made a wonderful boat. I'm very proud of you. Let's watch it go," dad said, hugging them.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny who lived in a big meadow. One day he was feeling sad so he lay down in the grass and closed his eyes. He was alone and he wished he had somebody to give him a gentle hug. Suddenly, a little bird with a bright yellow beak flew by and winked at the bunny. It said, "Cheer up! Everything will be alright." The bunny felt better and smiled. The bird sat by the bunny and they talked until the sun started to set. Before they said goodbye, the bird said to the bunny, "Remember, you always have friends here in the meadow if you ever feel sad." The bunny lay back in the grass and waved goodbye with a gentle smile.

One day, a mole was digging in the ground near the house. He was looking for something to provide him with food, but he wasn't having much luck. Just then, the mole heard a noise coming from inside the house. He peeked through the window to see the family inside. "Mama, I'm hungry," said the little girl, who was three years old. "I know, my love, I'll provide you with something to eat," said Mama. The mole was desperate to get inside the house and get some of the food, so he decided to try and sneak in while they weren't looking. He scurried to the back door and began to dig a tunnel. It was quite quiet at first, but the mole began to get a bit loud as he dug and Mama heard him. She rushed outside and scolded the mole. "No, no mole! You can't be here!" The mole was very scared, but he apologized and quickly ran away. The little girl felt sorry for the mole and offered him some of her food. Mama allowed it, and the mole was very thankful. "Thank you for providing me with food," said the mole before he ran off. Mama and the little girl smiled, glad that they could put the conflict behind them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big bag that she loved to carry around with her everywhere she went. One day, she went to the park and saw a new friend playing on the swings. Lily wanted to say hello, but she was shy. Her mom saw her feeling shy and said, "Why don't you introduce yourself to your new friend?" Lily thought that sounded like a good idea, so she walked over to the swings and said, "Hi, my name is Lily. What's your name?" Her new friend said, "My name is Sarah. Nice to meet you!" They started playing together and had so much fun. Lily's bag was very powerful because it had all her favorite toys inside. She shared her toys with Sarah and they played for hours. From that day on, they were the best of friends and Lily never felt shy again when meeting new people.

Once there was a generous farmer. He liked to count things. He would count the animals on his farm. He counted the chickens, the pigs and the cows. "One, two, three," he sang. He liked to count the vegetables in his garden too. "One, two, three, four," he chanted. He was very pleased with all the things he had to count. One day, the generous farmer went to the market. The market was full of food and he had lots to count. He started to count the apples and then he counted the oranges. He counted the carrots, the potatoes and the onions. He was smiling and counting his way around the market. He was so happy that he forgot to buy anything! But that was alright. The generous farmer was happy with the things he got to count. He was thankful that he was able to count all the wonderful things at the market. He was grateful for being able to count.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who had a very special stuffed bear named Teddy. Teddy was always with Lily, and she loved him very much. One day, Lily and her family went on a trip to the beach. While they were playing in the sand, Lily accidentally dropped Teddy and he got lost in the waves. Lily was very sad and cried for Teddy. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we'll find him." But Lily was worried that they would never find Teddy and he would be wasted in the ocean forever. A kind man saw Lily crying and asked what was wrong. Lily told him about Teddy and how she missed him very much. The man promised to help find Teddy and said he was a reliable friend. After searching for a while, they found Teddy washed up on the shore. Lily was so happy and hugged Teddy tightly. "Thank you for helping me find Teddy," she said to the man. "You're a reliable friend too!"

Once upon a time, there was a big wall. It was so big that nobody could climb over it. One day, a little boy wanted to see what was on the other side of the big wall. He tried to climb it, but he couldn't. He asked his friends to help him, but they couldn't climb it either. They all shrugged their shoulders and went home. The little boy didn't give up. He went back to the big wall every day and tried to climb it. One day, he found a small hole in the big wall. He peeked through the hole and saw a beautiful garden on the other side. He was so happy! He went back to his friends and told them about the garden. They all wanted to see it too, but they couldn't fit through the small hole. The little boy shrugged his shoulders and went back to the big wall. He found a way to make the hole bigger and soon all his friends could see the beautiful garden too. They were all so happy that they had found a way to see what was on the other side of the big wall. From that day on, they went to the garden every day and played together.

Mama and Papa had a plan. They wanted to find the perfect pupil for their family. Mama and Papa looked far and wide until they found open arms that welcomed them. The family visited the kind family. The little girl was so happy to welcome them and shared her toys. Mama and Papa were so pleased they knew they had found the perfect pupil. Mama and Papa never forgot the family's open arms that greeted them. Whenever they met someone, they showed an open heart. Their plan always working out, they knew by showing kindness they would always find the right pupil. Moral of the story: By being open and kind you will always find the right answer.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy store where he would supply toys to his friends. He loved to share and make his friends happy. One day, Tim got a new toy. It was a model car, and it was very pretty. Tim thought it was the best toy he had ever seen. He wanted to show it to all his friends and let them play with it too. Tim made sure the model car was safe for his friends to play with. He checked it carefully and made sure there were no sharp parts that could hurt anyone. Then, he invited his friends over to see the new toy. They all played together and had lots of fun. And Tim was happy because he had shared his special toy with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little island in the middle of the sea. The island had many trees, animals, and a big mountain. One day, a flexible snake named Slinky came to the island to rest. Slinky met a friendly bird named Chirpy on the island. Chirpy said, "Hello, Slinky! Why are you here?" Slinky replied, "I am here to rest. I am very tired from swimming in the sea." Chirpy said, "You can rest in my tree. It is very nice and safe." So, Slinky and Chirpy became good friends. They played and rested together on the island. They were very happy and had lots of fun. And they lived happily ever after on their little island.

Once there was a little girl named Joy who lived in a big, green field. Every day, she would go out and explore with her friends. One day, Joy noticed an old vine growing in the grass. It had big, green leaves and lots of purple grapes. She was so enthusiastic about it! Joy asked her friends if they wanted to help pick the grapes. But her friends just complained and said that it would take too much work. So, Joy decided to do it on her own. She worked hard, picking all of the ripe grapes off the vine. It took a while, but eventually, she filled a basket with lots of delicious purple grapes. Joy was so happy that she had done it by herself. Although it was hard work, Joy enjoyed picking the grapes. From then on, she visited the vine every day and was always enthusiastic to pick more grapes.

Once upon a time there was a cold morning and Amy was getting ready for school. She grabbed her heavy winter coat, hat and scarf and was ready to go. "Mom, what are you doing with my scarf?" asked Amy. "I want to put a bit more colour in your outfit. It will look great," replied Mom. So Amy started wearing the bright, colourful scarf that Mom had given her. She was so excited and couldn't wait to show her friends at school. Once she reached her school, Amy ran to her friends and they started to play hide and seek in the playground. They had lots of fun running around and playing games. At the end of the day, Amy thanked Mom for giving her the scarf. She was so excited to wear it and start playing with her friends. It was such a wonderful gift and she was sure it was going to keep her warm in the cold winter days.

Once upon a time there was a green frog. He was very happy jumping around in his pond. One day he heard a loud splash. When he looked up he saw a big, red fish slapping its tail in the water. The big fish was trying to catch some bugs. The frog was scared. He tried to jump away but the fish was too fast. The fish slapped its tail right on the frog's skin. The frog was so shocked he jumped straight out of the water into the grass. The frog was relieved. He looked back at the pond but the fish had gone. He was safe, but very tired. He decided to have a nap in the green grass and thanked the lucky stars that he still had his own skin.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was very restless and wanted something to do. So he decided to go to the park. When he arrived at the park, he saw a big, round, sausage. It was big enough for him to hug. So he grabbed it tight and hugged it. He smiled, feeling happy that he had something to hug. He hugged it so much until he was tired. When he was tired, he sat down. He felt cozy with the sausage by his side. He closed his eyes and felt very peaceful. He fell asleep with the sausage still in his arms. When he woke up, the sausage was still there. He smiled and gave the sausage one final hug before he went home.

Once upon a time, there was a big ostrich named Ollie. Ollie loved to paint. One day, he found some bright colors to play with. He was so happy! Ollie went to his friend, the little bird named Billy. "Look at my bright colors!" said Ollie. "Let's paint together!" Billy was excited too. They started to paint the trees and the grass with the bright colors. But then, Ollie got an idea. "Let's paint the sun!" he said. Billy thought it was a bad idea, but Ollie didn't listen. He took the bright colors and painted the sun. Suddenly, the sun was not happy. It got too hot, and the bright colors started to melt. The trees, the grass, and even Ollie and Billy were all covered in the melted colors. And that is why you should never paint the sun. The end.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a truck that sold ice cream. Sara wanted a cone with chocolate and Ben wanted a cone with vanilla. They ran to the truck and asked for their cones. The man gave them what they wanted and they paid with their coins. Sara and Ben were happy with their cones. They licked them and smiled. They sat on a bench and enjoyed their ice cream. But then a big boy came. He had no cone. He looked at Sara and Ben and said, "Give me your cones. I want them." Sara and Ben were scared. They said, "No, these are our cones. We bought them with our money. Go away." The big boy was angry. He tried to grab their cones. He was selfish. He did not care about Sara and Ben. Sara and Ben raised their cones high. They did not want to lose them. They shouted, "Help, help! This boy is mean. He wants to take our cones." Some people heard them. They came to see what was wrong. They saw the big boy and the small children. They scolded the big boy and told him to leave. The big boy ran away. He was ashamed. He had no cone and no friends. Sara and Ben were safe. They thanked the people who helped them. They hugged each other and finished their cones. They were not selfish. They shared their ice cream and their happiness.

Once upon a time there was a cute girl called Daisy. She liked to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she found a daisy growing in the grass and thought it was beautiful. She decided to pick the daisy and take it home to show her parents. When Daisy got home, she showed her parents the daisy and they thought it was really cute. Her mom helped her make a daisy crown for her to wear. Afterwards, Daisy went outside to play. She twirled around in the sunshine and picked more daisies to make a pretty daisy chain. When she was finished, she showed her new daisy chain to her parents. They thought it was very cute and clever. So the next time you see a daisy, remember Daisy and how much fun she had playing with it.

Once there was a little boy who was very frightened. He was holding his mom's hand tight and shaking. As they walked down a long hall in a big building, he asked, "Where are we?" His mom told him, "We are in a hospital. We are here to talk to the doctor." The little boy wasn't sure what to do. He kept on holding his mom's hand, but he kept on feeling scared. When they reached the doctor's office, his mom told him to wear a mask and she put one on too. The little boy was so frightened he couldn't speak. He just put on the mask and followed his mom inside. The doctor asked the little boy to show her his hands and he slowly held them out. She examined them and said they looked healthy. The little boy felt a bit better and his mom smiled at him. He knew everything was going to be alright. They thanked the doctor and the little boy noticed that he wasn't scared anymore. He ran out of the office and his mom smiled again! The little boy was so happy and he knew that everything would be okay.

John was walking in the park one day. His Mommy had sent him to get some fresh air. As he walked, he heard a funny noise. It sounded kind of like someone calling out. John looked around and saw two birds, one was blue and the other was yellow. The blue bird was calling out 'Come with me, come with me!' John kept walking until he saw a pot of jam by the side of a tree. It was blueberry jam, he was sure of it! He knew that the blue bird wanted him to follow it to get some of the jam. He was so excited! He started walking towards the tree, and the blue bird called out again. When he got to the tree, the bluebird was there, too. The bird said 'Taste the jam!' John felt the jam and noticed that it was sweet. He smiled and said 'Thank you' to the bird. The bluebird smiled. It said 'You're welcome. I knew you would like it. Now, call for me if you ever need help!' John nodded and the bird flew away. John was so happy to have found the sweet jam. He knew he could always call the bluebird if he ever needed help.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were very important to each other. One was a little boy, and one was a little girl. They liked to play together, running and having fun. One day, the two friends found something special - two matches. They were so excited to find something that united both of them. The little girl said, "we can use this to keep our friendship together". The little boy was so happy, he wanted to do something special with the matches. So they each made a special wish on their own match. Then they put the two matches together and created a spark. The little girl said "This is how we stay united." And so, the two friends stayed together forever, forever linked by their special matches. They both knew that their friendship was very important!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect shiny rocks and pretty flowers from the park. One day, she met a boy named Max who was playing with his toy cars. Max: "Hi, what are you doing?" Lily: "I'm collecting rocks and flowers. Do you want to help me?" Max: "Sure, that sounds fun. I have a big network of toy cars at home. Do you want to see them?" Lily: "Yes, please! I'm careful with toys." Max took Lily to his house and showed her his collection of toy cars. They played together for a while and had a great time. Lily was happy to have made a new friend and to have seen Max's amazing collection.

Tommy wanted a dream. So, he went to the dark room. He closed his eyes, and made a wish. He wished for a toy train with lots of tracks. He opened his eyes and he saw a very big box. He was excited! He opened the box and there was the toy train! He started to play with it, making it go round and round the tracks. Then, he heard a noise. It was coming from outside. It was the postman with a letter. He opened the letter and it said his dream had come true! Tommy was so happy. He smiled and said, "My dream came true!" He hugged the toy train tight and thanked his lucky stars. His dream was real!

One day, a little girl went outside to examine the world. When she looked up, she saw an unusual rainbow above her. She had never seen anything as beautiful as the rainbow before. She admired the bright colours and knew she had to get a closer look. She jumped up and down and waved her arms around until she was close enough to touch the rainbow. The little girl was so excited to feel the rainbow. She examined it carefully and noticed something special. Not only were the colours of the rainbow beautiful but they had the most remarkable smell. She could smell the sweet smell of rain and the fresh smell of grass. The little girl felt so lucky to experience something so wonderful and unusual. She wanted to look at the rainbow forever, but eventually the sun went down and the rainbow disappeared. She knew that she would never forget her magical moment and she would treasure it forever.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their ball. One day, they see a big zigzag on the grass. It is a snake. The snake is sleeping in the sun. "Look, a snake!" Ben says. He wants to touch it. He is not careful. "No, Ben, don't!" Anna says. She is scared. She knows snakes can bite. She tries to stop him. But Ben does not listen. He runs to the snake. He disturbs it. The snake wakes up. It is angry. It hisses and coils. It shows its teeth. "Help, help!" Ben cries. He is sorry. He runs back to Anna. Anna hugs him. She is glad he is safe. The snake slithers away. It wants to be alone. Anna and Ben learn a lesson. They should not disturb animals. They should be careful and respectful. They should listen to each other. They should play with their ball instead.

One day, Mommy and Jamel went to the store. It was a big place with many people and things to buy. Jamel was very excited! He saw a new player in the store. It was shiny and blue. Mommy asked Jamel if he wanted it and he nodded yes. She smiled and bought the player for Jamel. On the way home, Jamel couldn't stop smiling. He was so happy to have his new player. When they arrived home, Jamel ran to his bedroom, eager to see what it could do. He opened the box and looked inside. He took out his new player and pushed all the little buttons. He was amazed at all the things it could do! That night when Mommy tucked Jamel into bed, he was still smiling. He was so happy to have his new player and looked forward to playing with it the next day.

Lily was a little girl who loved to play with her toy cars. She had many cars of different colors and sizes, but her favorite one was a red car that could zoom very fast. She liked to zoom her car on the floor, on the table, and on the sofa. One day, Lily was zooming her car in the living room, when she saw her mom come in with a big bag. "What is that, mom?" Lily asked, curious. "It's a surprise for you, Lily," her mom said, smiling. "Do you want to see what's inside?" "Yes, yes, yes!" Lily said, excited. She put down her car and ran to her mom. Her mom opened the bag and took out a big, clear ball. Inside the ball, there was a tiny town with houses, trees, and roads. It was a snow globe. "Wow, mom, it's so pretty!" Lily said, amazed. She took the snow globe and shook it gently. She saw the snowflakes fall and cover the town. "It's a special snow globe, Lily," her mom said. "Look, there's a button on the bottom. If you press it, something magical will happen." Lily pressed the button and heard a soft music play. She looked closer and saw that the cars in the town started to move. They zoomed along the roads, honking and flashing their lights. "Mom, the cars are zooming like my car!" Lily said, delighted. She watched the cars zoom and zoom, and felt happy. "I'm glad you like it, Lily," her mom said, hugging her. "It's a gift for your birthday. Happy birthday, my sweet Lily." "Thank you, mom, I love you," Lily said, hugging her back. She held the snow globe in her hands and smiled. It was the best birthday ever.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was so excited when she found a shell on the beach. It was small, round, and white with a modest pink pattern on it. Lucy ran up to her dad and asked to keep the shell. Her dad smiled and said yes. She was so happy! Every day Lucy would take the shell out of her pocket and look at it. It reminded her of the day she found it. One day, she wanted to make the shell even more special so she asked her dad if they could paint it. He said it was a great idea and so together they painted it with purple and blue swirls. Lucy was so excited to have a shell with a design she had made herself! From that day on, whenever she looked at her special shell, she was reminded of the special day they had spent together.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He liked to play games with his friends. They were very competitive and always wanted to win. One day, they decided to have a race to see who was the fastest. The old man tried his best, but he was very slow. His friends all ran ahead of him. But then, something magical happened. The old man's granddaughter came to watch the race. She ran up to him and gave him a big kiss on the cheek. Suddenly, the old man felt like he could run faster than ever before. He started to catch up with his friends. They were all amazed at how fast he was going. In the end, the old man won the race! His friends were happy for him and they all hugged and laughed together.

Sara and Tom were playing in the garden. They saw a big hole in the ground. It was a well. Sara wanted to look inside. "Can we see the water?" she asked Tom. "I don't know. Maybe. Let's try," Tom said. They went to the well and looked down. It was very dark. They could not see anything. "Maybe there is a fairy in the well," Sara said. "Or a monster," Tom said.
