John was so excited to start painting! He grabbed his brush and some paints and went outside with his mom. John's mom showed him a big white wall and she asked him to paint it. John was so amazed. He was ready to start painting the wall and the paints made it look so beautiful! After painting, John heard a music coming from nearby. He looked around and saw a man playing a flute. John liked the music so much and asked his mom if he could play it. John's mom said that it was available for him to play. John was so happy to learn how to play the flute. He practiced playing it every day till he got very good. John's mom was so proud of him!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Abby. She was three years old and she liked to play at night. One night, Abby wanted to go outside, so her mom gave her a flashlight. She was so excited! She held it tightly as she opened the door and stepped outside. Suddenly, it was very dark. Abby felt embarrassed and scared, but she held the flashlight up and shone it around. The light made everything better and much brighter. Abby began to explore. She found the furry cat hiding in the bushes, and the big bird sleeping in the tree. Everywhere she looked, the flashlight made things easier to see. Abby had so much fun exploring with her flashlight. It made her feel brave and not scared anymore. Later she went back inside, still holding the flashlight tightly. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the rain. One day, Timmy found a plastic toy in the mud. It was wet and dirty, but Timmy didn't mind. He took the toy inside to show his mom. "Look, Mommy!" Timmy said as he held up the toy. "I found it outside in the rain. It's all wet!" Timmy's mom smiled and wiped the toy clean. She put it on a shelf to display it. Timmy was so happy that his toy was now dry and on display for everyone to see.

Once there was a boy named Jack. He liked to run and play outside. One day, Jack was playing and he saw something move. He looked closer and it was his own shadow. Jack laughed and tried to catch it, but it was too fast. So Jack decided to try a different way of catching it. He waited and stood very still. Suddenly he saw it again and made a very big, slow move to frighten it. The shadow jumped and Jack laughed. He reached out to try and catch the shadow and it moved away again. Jack wasn't giving up! He chased his shadow again and when he got close enough, he reached out and gave it a big slap. The shadow was caught and Jack celebrated.

Billy was very upset when he saw the ice cream cone. His best friend had just bought it and he hadn't! Billy wanted the cone badly, but he had no money to buy one. Suddenly, he came up with an idea. He lied to his friend and said he had money to buy his own. Reluctantly, his friend gave him the cone. At first, Billy was very happy. He loved the taste of the ice cream and it made him forget all his troubles. But then his friend asked Billy to give the cone back. Billy denied it. He told his friend that he had paid for it. His friend was angry. He shouted at Billy and called him a liar. He said that he would never talk to him again. The cone felt heavy in Billy's hands as he watched his best friend walk away. He was very upset and knew he had made a big mistake.

Once there was a little boy named Ryan and all he wanted for his 3rd birthday was to try something new. His mom and dad agreed and decided to take him out for lunch. At the restaurant, they ordered some soup. "I try," said Ryan enthusiastically. His parents smiled and handed him the spoon. Ryan tasted it, and his eyes grew wide with wonder. "It taste yummy!" he exclaimed. After they had finished eating, they paid the bill and Ryan's dad gave the waiter a tip. "What's a tip?" Ryan asked. "A tip is a way to say thank you for a job well done," his dad explained. Ryan and his parents left the restaurant feeling dependable. He had learned a new word and tasted something for the first time. It was a special birthday, indeed!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat oranges because they were juicy and sweet. One day, Timmy went to the store with his mom and saw an incredible toy car. He really wanted it, so he begged his mom to buy it for him. His mom said no because they didn't have enough money. Timmy was sad and regretted asking for the toy car. As they walked home, Timmy saw a man who looked very hungry. Timmy remembered that he had an extra orange in his backpack, so he gave it to the man. The man was very grateful and thanked Timmy for his kindness. Timmy felt happy that he could help someone and forgot about the toy car. From that day on, Timmy learned that helping others was more important than having things.

One day, a little girl named Jenny was walking in the woods. She loved playing hide and seek with her friends. Suddenly, Jenny heard something unfamiliar. It sounded like a strange noise. She wanted to know what it was. Jenny began to search for the noise. She looked here and there, but nothing was to be seen. As she moved further into the woods, the sound became louder. Soon enough, Jenny saw something shiny. It was hidden behind a tall tree. She knew she had found the sound. Jenny ran to the hidden thing. It was a quick squirrel, who was scurrying around trying to collect as many nuts as possible. Jenny laughed and watched the squirrel as it gathered its nuts. Then, she went back to searching the woods with her friends.

Sara and Ben are young. They like to play in the park. They see a big swing. Sara says, "I want to swing, Ben. Can you push me?" Ben nods and says, "OK, Sara. I will push you. But you have to hold on tight." Sara climbs on the swing and holds on tight. Ben pushes her gently. Sara feels the wind in her hair. She feels happy. She says, "Wee! This is fun, Ben. Thank you for pushing me." Ben smiles and says, "You're welcome, Sara. You are a good sister." They swing for a long time. They see the birds and the trees. They hear the children and the dogs. They feel the sun and the breeze. The park is peaceful. Sara and Ben are peaceful. They love to swing. They love each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish called Melody. She lived in a tank with lots of colourful stones, plants and other fish. Every morning she liked to take a bath. One day Melody was swimming around the tank, when suddenly she noticed a hidden door. She swam closer, and heard a voice coming from the door. "Hello Melody," the voice said. "I'm a secret mermaid. Would you like to come and explore with me?" Melody was very excited and said yes. She followed the mermaid through the hidden door and into a beautiful hidden garden filled with sparkly plants, rocks and pools of water. The mermaid smiled at Melody. "Now it's time to take a bath," she said. "Jump in the water and enjoy!" Melody splashed around and laughed. She had never had such an exciting bath before! When she was finished, the mermaid thanked her for coming and said goodbye. Melody was sad to see her go, but she knew she would always remember this special hidden bath.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Sammy. Sammy was very shy and always hid when other animals came near him. One day, Sammy was walking in the forest when he saw a big peanut on the ground. He was very hungry but he was too shy to take it. Just then, a friendly rabbit named Benny hopped over to Sammy. "Hi Sammy, what's wrong?" asked Benny. Sammy explained that he was too shy to take the peanut even though he was very hungry. "Don't worry," said Benny, "I'll help you." Benny picked up the peanut and gave it to Sammy. Sammy was very happy and thanked Benny. From that day on, Sammy wasn't as shy anymore and he made lots of new friends. The moral of the story is that sometimes we need a little help from our friends to make good things happen.

Once upon a time, there was a thin ball that liked to bounce. The ball had a friend named Speed. Speed was a fast car. They liked to play together in the park. One day, Speed and the thin ball decided to have a race. Speed went fast, and the thin ball bounced high. They raced to the big tree in the park. The thin ball bounced higher and higher, while Speed went faster and faster. In the end, Speed won the race. The thin ball was happy for his friend. They both had a fun day. After the race, they went home to rest. They knew they would play together again soon.

The sun was shining brightly as Mark went for a walk in the forest. He looked around, taking in all the colors of the trees and the sound of singing birds in the air. Suddenly, a white rabbit hopped across his path. Mark followed the rabbit, determined to make sure it wouldn't get lost in the forest. The rabbit stopped at a bush and the curious Mark moved closer to see what was under it. "Wow, what is it?" he said out loud. The rabbit looked up at him and then hopped away, revealing a sparkling, white stone behind the bush. Mark carefully moved closer, his eyes wide with wonder. What could it be? He picked it up and held it in his small hands. It was smooth and cool to the touch. As he was looking at it, he heard a small voice behind him. "It is a special stone," the voice said. Mark stopped and looked around. Underneath a tree, he saw an old fairy. She smiled at him and said, "That is a special stone that holds all of your hopes, dreams and wishes. Carry it with you, always." Mark thanked the fairy and put the stone in his pocket. He knew it would always be there to reveal his special wishes.

Once upon a time, there was a girl playing in the garden. She had a cloth in her hands and she was poking at some flowers. Then suddenly she heard a voice coming from behind her. "Don't be so careless," said the voice. She turned around to see an old lady standing there. The girl was scared and dropped the cloth. "I'm sorry," said the girl, lowering her head. The old lady smiled and picked up the cloth. She gently patted the girl's head and said, "It's alright. Just don't be so careless when playing with things." The girl nodded and thanked the old lady for her advice. From that day forward, the girl was more careful when playing with things.

Once there was a little girl named Lily. She was very lucky, and she knew it. She saw all the things she could do and all the places she could go with her luck. One summer day, Lily walked into the kitchen and saw something that made her smile. Sitting in the corner was a big freezer - filled with ice cream! Too excited to contain her joy, she jumped up and down, clapping her hands. "Oh, look at all the ice cream I can have!" she said. "Who's that lucky?" Then Lily saw her mom standing in the room. "Where did you get this freezer, Mommy?" she asked. Her mom smiled. "I found it at the store. It's a new model and it was on sale, so I decided to buy it!" Lily admired her mom for her clever idea. "Wow, you are so lucky, Mommy! I'm glad you got it." Lily's mom leaned down, placing her hand on Lily's shoulder. "Yes," she said, "I'm very lucky. But you are lucky too, Lily. You have me as your mom and that is even luckier than this freezer." Lily laughed, knowing that her mom was right. She hugged her mom tightly and they both admired the new freezer in their kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Max. Max loved to play catch with his friends. One day, Max was playing catch with his friend Jack when Jack threw the ball too hard and it went over the fence. Max was sad because he couldn't catch the ball. Max went to get a spoon from his house. He thought he could use the spoon to get the ball back. When Max got back to the fence, he tried to catch the ball with the spoon. But the spoon was too small and the ball was too big. Just then, Max's cheerful neighbor came over and saw what was happening. She said, "Don't worry Max, I can help you catch the ball." The neighbor got a ladder and climbed over the fence. She caught the ball and gave it back to Max. Max was so happy and thanked his neighbor. From that day on, Max always remembered to be cheerful and helpful to his friends.

Once there was a little girl who was very fearful. One night she heard a loud noise coming from her bedroom. It sounded like something was inside her room. She didn't want to look, but she was very curious. So she slowly opened her bedroom door and peeked in. Inside she saw a big, scary computer. It was making strange noises and flashing all sorts of colors. The little girl was so scared, she quickly shut the door and ran into her mom's room. Her mom hugged her tightly and asked her what was wrong. The little girl told her mom about the scary computer, and her mom said it must just be a dream. So, the little girl and her mom snuggled together and went back to sleep. The next morning, when the little girl opened her bedroom door, the computer was gone. She smiled, relieved that it was all just a dream.

Once upon a time, there lived two friends. They were very excited to have a dance party. So, they went to a big house. It was an unusual house because it had lots of colorful decorations everywhere. They put on their dancing shoes and began to dance. They twirled, jumped and spun around the house. They danced to the music that came out of the windows. They didn't want it to end, but it was time to go home. So they said goodbye to the unusual house and left with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a blue bird named Polly. She was kind and every morning she sang a happy song. One day, Polly flew down to the market and saw something strange - a man selling poison! She flew closer and asked him, "What is that?". The man replied, "This is poison. It can make you very sick. I'm selling it so you be careful". Polly flew away quickly and was worried. She told all her animal friends what the man said. But no one else believed her. "It's probably just medicine!", they said. Days passed and Polly did not forget what she saw. She warned the others again and again. "The man will hurt you if you're not careful!", she said. One day, Polly flew back to the market and saw something terrible. The man was selling his poison to all of Polly's Animal friends! She was so angry that she swooped down and used her wings to push the poison away. The man was angry and yelled at Polly, "What do you think you're doing?!". Polly replied, "I'm protecting my friends from your bad poison! You can't sell it here!". The man quickly ran away and never sold his poison again. Polly was a hero, and all her friends lived happily ever after!

One sunny day, Tim and his dog, Spot, went for a walk in the park. They saw a big tree with a long branch. On the branch, there was a pretty bird. The bird was singing a happy song. Tim smiled and said, "Hello, bird!" The bird looked at Tim and nodded its head. "Hello, Tim!" said the bird. Tim was very happy to talk to the bird. He asked, "Can you teach me your song, bird?" The bird nodded again and said, "Yes, it's easy!" Tim and the bird sang the happy song together. Spot wagged his tail and danced around them. They all had a fun time in the park. When it was time to go home, Tim waved goodbye to the bird. "Thank you for teaching me your song!" he said. The bird nodded one last time and flew away.

One day, a beautiful fish with a big bow on her head was swimming in the water. The fish's name was Bella. She saw a big scale on the ground. Bella wanted to play with the scale, but she was scared. She did not know what it was. Bella swam around the scale, looking at it from far away. She saw her friend, Bob the crab, and asked him, "What is this big thing?" Bob said, "It is a scale. We can play with it, but we need to be careful." Bella and Bob played with the scale, but they did not know that there was a mean shark nearby. The mean shark saw Bella and Bob playing with the scale. He wanted the scale for himself. The shark came closer and closer to Bella and Bob. When they saw him, they were scared. But Bella was brave. She swam fast and hit the shark with her big bow. The shark was surprised and swam away. Bella and Bob were safe, and they played with the scale all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a rich man. He had lots of nice things. One day, he wanted a new hedge in his garden. He asked for everyone to come and help build it. But the day was sunny, and everyone was enjoying the weather. They all delayed helping the rich man. So the man decided to do it on his own. He worked very hard, and he managed to build a big and beautiful hedge. The rich man was very happy with his hedge. All his friends admired it, and they were sorry they had delayed helping him. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly motor. The motor hummed and whirred and it churned away, day after day. One day, a little boy was so excited when he saw the motor. He wanted to see what the motor could do. He hopped up on it and grabbed the handle. He yanked it hard and the motor started to spin. Faster and faster it went until it began to yield and the motor started to slow down. As the motor grew slower and slower, the boy felt a warmth inside his heart. He was so happy that the motor had yielded. The little boy ran up to his friends to show them the jolly motor. The made time to visit the motor every day after school and they danced around it, giggling and having fun. It had become the most popular and jolly spot in the village, even after the little boy's parents told him that he had to stop visiting the motor. But, no one can stop the joy and jolliness that the motor spread throughout the town, even still to this day.

Once upon a time, there was a big cable. It was red and strong. One day, it started to zoom. It went up and down, and around and around. It was such a fun ride! Next, a big truck came. It had a lot of special tools. The people in the truck worked hard to make sure the cable was ready to go. When they finished, the cable was nice and tight. Everyone was so excited, because they knew the cable was done. So they all cheered, "Woohoo! Ready, set, go!" Everyone clapped as the cable started to zoom away. As the cable went away, the people waved goodbye. They all said, "Have fun, cable! Zoom off and enjoy!" And the cable zoomed off away into the bright blue sky.

Lila and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But sometimes they fight over the toys. One day, Lila wants to play with the train, but Ben has it. Lila tries to take it from him, but Ben holds it tight. "Give me the train!" Lila says. "No, it is mine!" Ben says. They pull and tug at the train. The train is heavy and hard. It hurts their hands. They yell and cry. Mom hears them and comes to their room. "What is going on here?" Mom asks. "They are fighting over the train!" Lila and Ben say at the same time. Mom looks at the train. It is broken. The wheels are off and the smokestack is bent. Mom is sad and angry. "You broke the train!" Mom says. "That was a gift from Grandma. She loves you and wanted you to share it. How could you do this?" Lila and Ben feel bad. They know they did something wrong. They look at the floor and say nothing. Mom shakes her head. "You need to learn to play nicely and use your words. Fighting is not a good language. It only makes things worse. Now you have no train and no fun. Go to your beds and think about what you did. And shut the door behind you." Lila and Ben nod. They pick up their toys and go to their beds. They shut the door. They are quiet. They wish they had not fought over the train. They wish they had said sorry and shared it. They miss their mom and their grandma. They hope they can fix the train and make them happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play in her backyard with her toys. One day, Lily saw her neighbor, Mr. Smith, walking by. He looked very sad. She asked him what was wrong, and he said that someone had cut down his favorite tree. Lily felt bad for Mr. Smith. She knew that cutting down trees was not good. She decided to help him feel better. She went inside and made him a card. She drew a picture of a new tree that she would plant for him. When Lily gave Mr. Smith the card, he smiled and thanked her. He said that her kind gesture made him feel better. From that day on, Lily and Mr. Smith became good friends. They would often play together in the backyard and talk about how bad it was to cut down trees. They even planted a new tree together.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Bouncy. Bouncy was always very enthusiastic about going for walks and playing with his friends in the park. One day, after a long play session, Bouncy ran away, chasing a butterfly he had seen. The little dog ran so far and for so long that even he became tired. He stopped to take a break and looked around. He realized he had gotten himself lost. Bouncy tried to find his way back home, but he just couldn't remember which way he came from. He was looking around, when he saw a big paw reach out from under a bush. Bouncy was frightened at first, but then he saw a big friendly face looking at him with a big smile. It was a big friendly bear! After a chat, the bear told Bouncy the way back home. Happy and relieved, Bouncy returned home. His family was so happy to see him. "Welcome home, Bouncy!", they said, and the enthusiastic little dog quickly went back to playing with his friends in the park.

One day, a little boy named Tim and his friend Sue went to play outside. They saw a big red car on the street. They wanted to touch the car, but they knew they should ask first. Tim looked at Sue and she nodded, so they both went to find the car's owner. They found the owner, a kind old man, who was sitting on a bench. They asked him if they could touch the car. The old man smiled and said yes. Tim and Sue were so happy! They ran to the car and touched it gently. Suddenly, a big dog came running and barked at them. Tim and Sue felt guilty because they thought they did something bad. The old man came and told the dog to stop. He said it was okay, and they didn't do anything wrong. Tim and Sue smiled and thanked the old man. They knew they had to be more careful next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to eat pasta. One day, she saw a big bowl of pasta on the table. Mia was very happy and wanted to eat it all. But when Mia took a closer look, she saw that the pasta was fake. It was not real pasta, but a toy. Mia was sad because she really wanted to eat pasta. She showed the fake pasta to her mom and asked for real pasta. Mia's mom smiled and said, "I will make you real pasta for dinner tonight." Mia was very happy and played with her fake pasta toy until dinner time. When it was time to eat, Mia enjoyed her real pasta and shared it with her family.

Anna liked to play in the garden with her dad. He showed her how to plant seeds in the soil and water them every day. He said that soon they would grow into green plants that they could eat or smell. One day, Anna saw a tiny sprout poking out of the soil. She was very happy and ran to tell her dad. "Look, look, dad! A seed is growing!" she shouted. Dad smiled and came to see. "That's wonderful, Anna. You did a good job taking care of it. Do you know what kind of plant it is?" he asked. Anna shook her head. She did not know the names of many plants. Dad pointed to a picture on the seed packet. "It's a sunflower, Anna. It will grow very tall and have a big yellow flower that looks like the sun. Do you like sunflowers?" Anna nodded. She liked yellow and she liked the sun. She wondered how big the flower would be. "Can I pick it when it grows?" she asked. Dad shook his head. "No, Anna. We don't pick sunflowers. We thank them for being beautiful and giving us seeds. The seeds are good for us and for the birds. We can share them with our feathered friends. Do you like birds?" Anna nodded. She liked birds and their songs. She wanted to share with them. She looked at the sprout and said, "Thank you, sunflower. I can't wait to see you grow and meet the birds."

Once upon a time, there was a black cave. Inside the cave lived two friends, a mouse and a bat. The mouse was very brave and always wanted to explore. One day, the mouse wanted to see what was outside the cave. He poked his head out and saw a beautiful, blue sky. He was so excited that he wanted to explore further, so he opened the cave door. Suddenly, there was a loud hissing noise. The mouse looked worried and asked the bat, "What is that noise?" The bat replied, "That's the sound of oxygen leaving the cave. We need to close the door quick or we won't be able to breathe." So the mouse and the bat quickly closed the door and the noise stopped. The mouse and the bat both breathed a sigh of relief. From then on, they promised to always close the door to keep the oxygen inside the cave.

Once there was a boy and he had a helmet. He loved his helmet and he had a lot of fun with it. He went outside and hung his helmet from a tree. He thought it was funny to put it there. But then a big bird came along and grabbed the helmet with its beak. The boy was sad, but then he thought of a plan. The boy asked his friends to help him. They all got together and put some string around the bird's feet. They tied the string to a tree, so the bird couldn't fly away. Then, the boy was very brave and he got close to the bird. He took his helmet back. The bird was a little bossy, but the boy was happy to have his helmet back. His friends cheered him on and they all went back inside to play. They hung up their helmets and had lots of fun. They learned a lesson that day: never be bossy or do something wrong or bad things might happen.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to paint. He enjoyed creating lots of pictures with his paint. One day, Jack was very excited and asked his mum if he could paint a cake. His mum said yes so she found a big bowl and filled it with flour. Jack stirred it with a spoon until it was a soft and squishy mixture. Then Jack got out the paint. He mixed a yellow paint to make a golden colour. He painted the cake with the golden colour. Next he mixed green paint to make a mint colour. He painted the leaves and stalks. Then it was time for the taste. Jack asked his mum if he could lick the spoon to try some of the cake. His mum said "Yes, please be polite!" So Jack licked the spoon with a polite face. It tasted sweet and delicious! Jack was very proud of his painted cake!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys in the kitchen while her mom cooked. One day, Lily's tummy started to rumble and she felt very hungry. "Mommy, I'm hungry!" Lily said. "I know, sweetie. I'm almost done cooking," Mommy replied. Just then, a man knocked on the door. He was selling fruits and vegetables. "Hello, would you like to buy some fresh fruits and vegetables?" the man asked. "Yes, please!" Mommy said. "Lily, do you want to help me pick out some yummy fruits and vegetables to eat?" Lily nodded and they went outside to buy some food. They were both very happy and excited to eat their healthy snacks.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little dog named Spot. He lived with his family near a big wood. Spot loved to play and run in the wood with his friends. One day, while Spot was playing, he saw a big, mean cat coming near his friends. Spot wanted to help his friends, so he ran to warn them. He barked, "Stay away from the big, mean cat!" Spot's friends heard his warning and ran away from the big, mean cat. The cat tried to catch them, but they were too fast. The cat got mad and tried to hurt Spot, but Spot was brave. Spot barked and barked at the big, mean cat. The cat was scared of Spot's loud bark and ran away. Spot's friends came back and thanked him for being brave and warning them. They played in the wood for the rest of the day, happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and read books. One day, her mom took her to the store to buy a new book for her shelf. Lily saw a beautiful book with a picture of a princess on the cover. She pointed at it and said, "Mommy, I want that one!" Her mom bought the book and they went home. Lily put the book on her shelf and read it every night before bed. One night, as she was reading, she noticed a small crack in the wall behind her shelf. The next day, Lily's dad came to fix the crack. As he was working, he found a hidden door behind the shelf! They opened the door and found a treasure chest filled with gold coins and jewels. Lily was so happy and pointed at the treasure, saying, "Look, Mommy, it's beautiful!"

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot had a red collar around his neck. One day, Spot's owner decided to travel to a faraway place and brought Spot along. On the way, Spot felt very thirsty and drank all the water from his bowl. But his owner forgot to refill it. Spot's belly was empty and he felt very sad. After a long journey, they finally arrived at their destination. Spot was very happy to see a big yard to play in. But as he ran around, he got tangled in his collar and couldn't breathe. His owner was not around to help him and Spot couldn't escape. Sadly, Spot passed away. This is why it's important to always check that your pet's collar is not too tight and to never leave them alone for too long.

Once upon a time, there was a big, green park. All the children in the neighborhood liked to play there every day. One day, while they were all playing, they noticed a big, red wagon in the corner of the park. The children were all very curious and wanted to know what was inside the wagon, so they went to take a look. Inside the wagon, they found a big, yellow ball. They all took turns chewing on it and saw that it was super soft. Suddenly, a loud crash sounded and the children all started to get scared. But then, they saw a huge wreck of a truck right where the children had been playing a few minutes earlier. The truck was really shattered and bits of the truck were all over the ground. Thankfully, no one had been hurt and the children were safe. The children took the big, yellow ball they had found in the wagon and decided to keep it as a reminder of the time they had a close call but stayed safe!

Once upon a time there was a blue whale. The whale lived deep in the beautiful ocean. The ocean was a very safe and happy place for the whale. Every day the whale would swim around, enjoying the fresh and clean water. But what the whale really loved was the oxygen. The oxygen made it happy and it felt great! The whale wanted to show its gratitude and so it served the other ocean animals. It shared its oxygen with them, making sure everyone was healthy and happy. The whale was so kind! The other animals were so grateful to the blue whale. They thanked it and praised it every day. They were happy to have such a noble creature living in their ocean. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who had a big boo-boo on his knee. He went to the doctor's office and sat in the waiting room with other sick kids. Timmy was very patient and waited for his turn to see the doctor. When it was finally Timmy's turn, the doctor gave him a little pill to make the boo-boo go away. Timmy took the pill and felt much better. He thanked the doctor and went home with his mom. Later that night, Timmy started to cry. His knee hurt again and he couldn't sleep. His mom tried to help him, but the little pill didn't work anymore. Timmy cried and cried until his mom took him back to the doctor. The doctor said that Timmy needed a big operation to fix his knee. Timmy was scared, but his mom told him it would be okay. The next day, Timmy went to the hospital for the operation. The doctor put him to sleep and fixed his knee. When Timmy woke up, he felt much better. But he had a big bandage on his knee and couldn't play outside for a while.

Once upon a time there was a kind bear. He was very generous. He had beautiful soft hair. He gave his tasty honey to all the animals in the forest. Every morning he would go around to their homes and share the honey with them. The animals all liked his honey very much. They would lick and taste it. It was so delicious! One day a little rabbit came out from her burrow. She saw the kind bear giving out honey. She asked the bear if she could have some too. The bear was so generous. He gave her a big spoonful of the honey. The little rabbit was so happy. She made sure to take extra care to taste it. She loved the taste of the sweet honey. The generous bear smiled and said, "Enjoy!" The end.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends; one was a pig called Percy and the other was a rabbit called Ralph. They loved playing in the garden together. One day, they decided to do something special. So, they ran around the garden together, covering all sorts of things with leaves. Percy made a leafy blanket and Ralph covered the garden stool with them. They had so much fun! Then, Ralph hopped to the pond and noticed that it was getting a bit filthy. He wanted to find a way to clean it. Suddenly, he remembered an old bucket he had seen in the shed earlier. He quickly hopped to the shed, grabbed the bucket and went back to the pond. Together with Percy, they covered the pond with water from the bucket. They kept doing this until the pond was clean again. By the time they were done, the sun was setting and it was time for them to go home. The two friends were very proud of their hard work and had a great time.

Lily and Sam went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. Lily liked the lions best. They were big and fierce and had loud roars. Sam liked the monkeys best. They were funny and playful and had long tails. "Can we try to feed the monkeys?" Sam asked Mom. "Sure, we can try," Mom said. "But we have to be careful and follow the rules." Mom bought some nuts from a machine and gave some to Sam and Lily. They walked to the monkey cage and saw the monkeys swinging and jumping on the ropes and trees. "Hello, monkeys!" Sam said. "Do you want some nuts?" He threw a nut to a monkey. The monkey caught it and ate it. Then it made a happy noise and threw a nut back to Sam. "Wow, the monkey is playing with me!" Sam said. He threw another nut and the monkey did the same. Lily wanted to try too. She threw a nut to another monkey. But the monkey did not catch it. It bounced off the cage and hit a lion on the head. The lion was angry. It roared very loud and showed its teeth. Lily was scared. She ran to Mom and hugged her. "Sorry, lion!" Lily said. "I did not mean to hit you!" The lion calmed down and licked its paw. It did not want to hurt Lily. It was just surprised. "It's okay, Lily," Mom said. "The lion is not mad at you. But we have to be more careful when we try to feed the animals. They are not like our pets. They are wild and fierce." Lily nodded. She learned her lesson. She still liked the lions, but she liked the monkeys more. She and Sam gave the rest of the nuts to the monkeys and thanked them for playing with them. Then they went to see the other animals in the zoo. They had a lot of fun.

Mira loves to sing. She sings in the morning, she sings in the afternoon, she sings at night. She sings to her toys, she sings to her mom, she sings to her dad. She sings happy songs, she sings sad songs, she sings silly songs. One day, Mira goes to the market with her mom. She sees many things there. She sees fruits, she sees flowers, she sees bread. She also sees vegetables. She sees carrots, she sees potatoes, she sees tomatoes. She likes vegetables. She likes to eat them and she likes to sing about them. She picks up a tomato and sings, "Tomato, tomato, you are red and round. Tomato, tomato, you make a juicy sound." She picks up a carrot and sings, "Carrot, carrot, you are orange and long. Carrot, carrot, you make me strong." She picks up a potato and sings, "Potato, potato, you are brown and rough. Potato, potato, you are good enough." But then, she sees a vegetable she does not know. It is green and thin and has many leaves. It looks fragile. She asks her mom, "Mom, what is this vegetable?" Her mom says, "That is a celery, Mira. It is crunchy and fresh. Do you want to try it?" Mira nods. She takes the celery and sings, "Celery, celery, you are green and thin. Celery, celery, you are new to me. Celery, celery, I wonder how you taste. Celery, celery, I will not waste." She bites the celery and smiles. She likes it. She sings, "Celery, celery, you are yummy and fun. Celery, celery, you are my new friend. Celery, celery, I will sing to you again. Celery, celery, you are the best vegetable ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a guard dog named Max. Max was big and furry, and he loved to play with Lily. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk in the park. They saw a group of people having a party. Lily asked Max, "What are they doing?" Max barked, "They are celebrating!" Lily and Max went closer to see what was happening. They saw balloons, cake, and lots of happy people. Lily asked Max, "Can we celebrate too?" Max wagged his tail and barked, "Yes, let's celebrate!" Lily and Max joined the party and had lots of fun. After the party, they went back home. Lily's mom asked her, "Did you have a good time?" Lily replied, "Yes, we celebrated with our friends!" Her mom smiled and said, "That's normal for a party."

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was so excited to go on a special trip. She was going to meet a deep statue. The next morning Lucy's mom drove her to the park. When they arrived, the statue was so tall. It was so deep, Lucy was scared. But then she said to herself, "It's okay, I can do this!" She slowly and carefully walked up to the statue. She was so close! She reached out and touched the statue. It felt so cold and wet. Lucy was so proud that she had met the deep statue. She shouted and jumped for joy. She looked up to the sky and whispered a thank you to the statue. Lucy felt so brave, she knew she could do anything! She hugged her mom and skipped off home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time there was a team. They were spread all over the world. They were very excited to start their work together. But then something boring happened. Every day all the team members had to do the same chores. Wash the dishes, vacuum the floors, and sweep the yard. The tasks were boring and tiring and the team was not happy. One day the team decided to do something different. They all spread out and started looking for exciting things to do. They went to the park, explored a cave full of spiders, and built giant sandcastles on the beach. The team was having so much fun that they decided to keep spreading out to discover new things. They explored mountain tops, swam in lakes, and jumped in puddles. The team had the best adventures together and they were never bored again.

Once upon a time, there was an amazing orange. It was a special orange, because it could repeat everything it heard. One day, a three year old boy came across the orange. The boy was so excited. He said "Hello orange!" and the orange said "Hello!" right back. The little boy couldn't believe it. He kept talking so the orange could repeat the words over and over again. He asked the orange to sing a song, so the orange sang "Twinkle, twinkle little star". The boy was so amazed that he sang right along with the orange. The boy and his orange had so much fun together. Each day they played and talked. The little boy was so happy. He loved his amazing orange.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden. One day, while she was playing, she found a lime. It was green and round, and it smelled good. Lily's friend, Max, came to play with her. Max saw the lime and said, "Wow, that's a big lime! Can I have a piece?" Lily gave Max a slice of the lime. Max took a bite and said, "This lime is so sour! I don't like it." Lily realized that Max didn't like the lime. She said, "That's okay, Max. Not everyone likes limes. Maybe you'll like something else." Max smiled and said, "Thanks, Lily. You're a good friend." Lily and Max continued to play in the garden, picking flowers and chasing butterflies. They had a fun day together, and Lily was happy to have a friend like Max. She realized that even if they didn't like the same things, they could still have fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little hurricane named Harry. Harry was always restless. He liked to spin and spin all day long. He would dance in the sky, and the clouds would laugh with him. But sometimes, Harry would spin too fast and make a big mess. One day, Harry met a bird named Betty. Betty was very good at managing things. She knew how to keep her nest clean and her eggs safe. She saw Harry spinning and making a mess, so she decided to help him. Betty taught Harry how to spin just the right amount, so he didn't make a big mess anymore. Harry was so happy that he could still spin and dance without causing trouble. Now, Harry and Betty are the best of friends, and they dance in the sky together every day.

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play with their club. Their club is a big stick that they found in the park. They pretend that their club is a sword or a magic wand. One day, they go to the park with their club. They see a big slide. They both want to go on the slide first. They start to quarrel. "I want to go first!" Ben says. "No, I want to go first!" Sam says. They pull and push each other. They are angry and loud. They forget about their club. A girl sees their club on the ground. She picks it up. She thinks it is a nice stick. She runs away with it. Ben and Sam stop quarreling. They look for their club. They cannot find it. They see the girl with their club. They run after her. "Hey, that is our club!" Ben shouts. "Give it back!" Sam shouts. The girl is scared. She does not want to give back the club. She feels uncomfortable. She does not like to make Ben and Sam sad. She does not know what to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play outside in the grass and eat carrots. One day, Benny found a big hole in the ground. He hopped inside and found himself underground. It was dark and scary, but Benny was curious. He saw lots of bugs and worms crawling around. It was easy for Benny to catch them and eat them. He liked it underground because it was cool and quiet. Benny decided to keep this secret underground place to himself. Every day, Benny would sneak away to his secret underground spot. He would play and eat bugs until it was time to go home. Benny loved his secret spot and was happy to keep it all to himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. Jane was three years old and loved to explore the world around her. One morning, Jane decided to test something new - she closed her eyes, stuck out her thumb and tried to touch her nose. Unfortunately, Jane was not successful and did not manage to touch her nose on her first try. Jane was very upset and tried again, but still couldn't do it. She tried a few more times, but to no avail. Jane's mum saw how upset her little girl was, so she held Jane's thumb for her and guided it to her nose. On the fourth try, Jane was able to touch her own nose. She was so excited and quickly opened her eyes, so surprised that she had done it. Jane was so happy she had managed to test something new and she was sure that she could do it again.

One day, Tom and his mum went to the park. They brought a kite that was in need of repair. As they were walking, Tom started to dream about the beautiful kite being back in the sky. Suddenly, he heard his mum say, "Let's try to repair it here, Tom." Tom was excited. He watched as his mum started to work hard on the kite. She used a long string and some tape. After some time, the kite was ready. Tom couldn't believe his eyes. He said, "The kite looks so nice, mum!" His mum replied, "Yes, it looks like an image in the sky now. All we need to do is wait for the wind to pick it up and take it high." Tom smiled. He knew his dream was finally going to come true.

Ben and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were monkeys and swing on the vines. The vines were hairy and green and strong. "Look at me, Mia!" Ben said. "I can swing very high and fast!" "You are a good monkey, Ben!" Mia said. "But I am hungry. Can we have some bananas?" "OK, Mia. I will serve you some bananas. You wait here and I will go to the kitchen." Ben said. He let go of the vine and ran to the house. Mia waited on the vine. She saw a big yellow bird fly by. She said hello to the bird, but the bird did not answer. She saw a red flower on the ground. She wanted to smell the flower, but she did not want to leave the vine. Soon, Ben came back with two bananas. He peeled one and gave it to Mia. He peeled the other and ate it himself. "Thank you, Ben. You are a nice monkey." Mia said. "You are welcome, Mia. You are a sweet monkey." Ben said. They ate their bananas and smiled. They were happy monkeys on the vine.

Mummy was in the living room. She was putting on her pretty clothes for an important meeting. Suddenly, she noticed something naughty. "Bizzy," Mummy said sternly, "why are you bowing in my clothes?" Bizzy was a three-year-old girl. She had been playing in Mummy's closet. She pointed to a bow that had fallen on the floor. "That bow was pretty," Bizzy said pleadingly. Mummy sighed. She picked up the bow and put it back in the closet. "You must be careful with my clothes," Mummy said. "And no more bowing, okay?" Bizzy nodded solemnly. She knew she had been naughty. From then on, she was extra careful around Mummy's clothes. But every now and then, she would take out the bow and give it a big, twirly bow.

Once upon a time, there was a big sheep. The sheep had an enormous amount of wool. Every day, the sheep would wander around the fields and eat grass. Then, the sheep would go to sleep. One day, a little girl came to the field. She saw the sheep and said, "Wow, your wool is so big!" The sheep replied, "Yes, I know. I repeat this every day." The little girl wanted to touch the wool. She reached out and felt how soft it was. The sheep was happy to be petted. From then on, the little girl would come to the field every day and repeat the same thing. She would pet the sheep and feel its enormous wool.

Once, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved playing in the rain. One day, when it was raining, Lucy went outside and spun around in the rain. The cool water soaked her and she laughed and twirled around. But later, the rain stopped and it made Lucy sad. She wanted to keep playing in the rain. So Lucy stomped her feet and said, "Where is the rain?" Then, Lucy heard a voice speaking. It said, "It's the season for rain, but now it's dull outside. Don't worry, the rains will come again soon." Lucy smiled and waited for rain. When the rain did come again, she ran outside and spun around again in the rain. She felt so happy when she was soaked in the rain!

Once upon a time, there was a group of delicate butterflies. They loved to wander around the garden and smell the pretty flowers. One day, they met a little girl named Lily. "Hello, butterflies!" said Lily. "Can I play with you?" "Of course!" said the butterflies. Lily laughed and chased after the butterflies as they wandered around the garden. They flew up high and then landed on a delicate flower. "This is so much fun!" said Lily. The butterflies were happy to have a new friend to play with. They continued to wander around the garden together, enjoying the sunshine and the beautiful flowers.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pastel colors. One sunny day, Lily went to the park to draw a big tree. She sat on the dry grass and started to draw. Then, a little boy named Tim came to the park. He saw Lily drawing and wanted to join her. "Can I draw with you?" Tim asked. Lily smiled and said, "Yes, but promise to be careful with my pastel colors." Tim and Lily drew together all day. They made a big, beautiful picture of the park with the pastel colors. They were very happy and became good friends. They promised to draw together again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a tray. She was only three years old and it was her favorite thing. She used the tray to carry her toys wherever she went. But one day, something bad happened and the tray was destroyed. The girl felt so sad. She cried and couldn't stop. She wanted her tray back, but it was gone. Her mom saw her tears and said, "Let's make a new tray!" The girl was happy and excited. So the mom and daughter worked together to make a new little tray. Together, they painted it in different colors and decorated it with cute stickers. When it was done, the little girl was so happy. She hugged her mom and thanked her for the new tray. It was even better than the old one! Now she could carry her toys wherever she went.

Once there was a little girl named Daisy who was very lonely. One day, Daisy was playing in her garden when suddenly she started to tremble. She looked around, but she couldn't see anything that would make her afraid. But then she noticed something sparkling on the ground. It was a beautiful bracelet! She was so excited; she picked it up and put it on her wrist. But then, to Daisy's surprise, the bracelet started to tremble. At first, Daisy was scared. But then she realised that the bracelet was shaking because it was lonely and wanted a friend too. So Daisy held the bracelet and both of them stopped trembling. Daisy was so happy, she had a friend! From then on, Daisy and her bracelet were the best of friends, and neither of them ever felt lonely again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl walking down the street. She was looking for something. Everywhere she went she asked people if they could help her, but they all said no. She kept walking until she came to a big, organized house. She stopped in front of the house and asked if anyone could solve her problem. Someone came to the door and said yes. The little girl was so happy! She followed the person into the house, and they showed her how to solve her problem. The little girl thanked them and went back home. When she was walking down the street, the little girl felt proud that she had solved her problem. She knew now that if she ever had a problem in the future she could always come to this organized house and find a way to solve it.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, Tom has a new toy. It is a zebra. It is black and white and soft. Mia sees the zebra and wants to play with it. She asks Tom, "Can I play with your zebra, please?" Tom says, "No, it is mine. You have your own toys." Mia feels sad and angry. She thinks Tom is not a good friend. She tries to take the zebra from Tom. They pull and tug and shout. "Stop it!" says Mom. She comes and takes the zebra from them. She says, "You are both being difficult. Sharing is caring. If you want to play with the zebra, you have to take turns. Tom, you can give the zebra to Mia for five minutes. Then Mia, you can give it back to Tom for five minutes. Do you understand?" Tom and Mia nod. They say, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, friend." They hug and say, "Thank you." They play with the zebra and other toys. They have fun and are happy. They learn to share and be kind.

Once upon a time, there was a normal car. The car could talk and had many friends. One day, the car went to the park to play with its friends. They played hide and seek, and the car was very good at hiding. At lunch time, the car's friend, a little bird, was hungry. The car wanted to help, so it decided to feed the bird. The car went to find food for the bird. It found some yummy seeds and gave them to the bird. The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you, car!" After they ate, the car and the bird played more games. They had a fun day at the park. When it was time to go home, the car said goodbye to its friends. The car went back to its normal life, but it always remembered the fun day at the park with its friends.

Once upon a time there was an ancient track. Nobody ever used it, because it was hidden by trees and bushes. One day, a big black cat came to the track. He looked around, walked a few steps, then stopped. He seemed to like the track very much! He went back to his home and told all his friends to come and visit the track. He said it was the best place ever! Soon, all the animals from all over the forest started to visit the track. They were so excited to play together in this place that had been forgotten for so long. The animals decided to do something special. They wanted to make sure the track stayed their secret forever. So, they decided to lock it. They snuck out one night and put a big lock on the track. Now no one else could find it but the animals. They had their own secret ancient track!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a small, fluffy dog named Max. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk in the park. The sun was shining, and the birds were singing. Suddenly, Max saw a big, loud truck. He was frightened and ran away. Lily looked around and could not find Max. She felt very sad and began to weep. "Max, where are you?" she cried. A kind boy named Tom saw Lily and asked, "Why are you weeping?" Lily told Tom about Max and how he ran away. Tom said, "Don't worry, I will help you find Max." They searched together, and soon they found Max hiding in a quiet corner of the park. Lily hugged Max and said, "I'm so happy we found you!" From that day on, Lily, Max, and Tom became the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Tom. Tom always wanted his bed to be perfect for a good night's sleep. Every night, he would make sure his sheets were tucked in and smooth. But one night, Tom had to make the bed himself. He was very upset. He complained loudly. "It's so difficult to make the bed!" Tom's mum heard him complaining and she came to help him. She said, "Let me help you with your sheets. We can do them together." Tom smiled and thanked his mum. With their help, the bed was made quickly. Tom settled in for a good night's sleep and was happy. He knew that his bed would always be perfect as long as his mum was around.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her toy car. One day, Lily's dad gave her a big box and said, "We're going to load up the car and go on an adventure!" Lily was so excited to go on an adventure with her dad. She put all her toys in the car, but she noticed that her toy car was running out of power. "Oh no!" she said. "My car needs more power!" Her dad smiled and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I have something that will help." He took out a needle and carefully inserted it into the toy car. Suddenly, the car became more powerful than ever before! Lily was amazed and they drove off on their adventure.

Sara was very happy today. She was going to visit her aunt Lily, who lived in a big house with a garden. Sara loved her aunt Lily, who always had fun games and yummy snacks for her. When Sara and her mom arrived at the house, they rang the bell. Aunt Lily opened the door and gave them a big hug. "Hello, Sara! Hello, mom! I'm so glad you're here!" she said. "Hello, aunt Lily! We're happy to see you too!" Sara and her mom said. Aunt Lily led them to the living room, where she had a surprise for Sara. She pointed to a big box wrapped in colorful paper. "This is for you, Sara. Do you want to open it?" she asked. Sara's eyes widened. She loved surprises. She nodded and ran to the box. She tore the paper and lifted the lid. Inside, she saw a beautiful doll with long hair and a pink dress. "Wow! Thank you, aunt Lily! She's so pretty!" Sara exclaimed. "You're welcome, Sara. I'm glad you like her. She's very special. She can talk and sing and play with you. She's your new friend," aunt Lily said. Sara picked up the doll and hugged her. She pressed a button on her back and the doll said, "Hello, Sara. I'm Daisy. I'm happy to meet you." "Hello, Daisy. I'm Sara. I'm happy to meet you too," Sara said. She looked at her aunt Lily and smiled. She was the best aunt ever. She had the best surprises ever. She was always available for Sara. Sara loved her very much.

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Benny. Benny was very hungry and wanted to eat some honey. He went to a hive to get some honey, but the bees were angry and stung him. Benny was very sad and his ears felt deaf. Benny decided to ask his friend, a bird named Billy, for help. Billy flew to the hive and distracted the bees while Benny ate some honey. Benny was very happy and thanked Billy for helping him. From that day on, Benny and Billy were best friends and they always shared their food. Benny never went to a hive again without asking for Billy's help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and toys. One day, she was having a tea party with her teddy bear when her mommy came in. "Would you like some tea, Mommy?" Lily asked. "Yes, please. Thank you for serving me," Mommy replied. Lily poured some tea into a cup and passed it to her mommy. Mommy took a sip and said, "This tea is delicious. You are such a graceful hostess." Lily smiled and continued to serve her mommy tea and biscuits. They had a lovely time together at their tea party.

Once upon a time, there was a sheep named Wooly. Wooly was very fluffy and had lots of wool. One day, Wooly was playing with his friends when he saw a fox peeking from behind a tree. Wooly knew that the fox wanted to eat him and his friends. Wooly tried to warn his friends, but they didn't believe him. So, Wooly decided to be brave and face the fox himself. He walked up to the fox and asked him to leave them alone. The fox laughed and said that he was very hungry and needed to eat. Wooly was very graceful and didn't want to fight, so he came up with a plan. He told the fox that if he waited a little while, he could bring him some delicious carrots to eat instead. The fox agreed and waited while Wooly went to get the carrots. When Wooly came back, he threw the carrots as far as he could and the fox ran after them. Wooly and his friends ran away as fast as they could and were safe. From that day on, Wooly's friends listened to him and they all played together happily ever after.

Lily was a little girl who liked to touch everything. She touched the flowers, the toys, the books, and the cat. She wanted to know how they felt and what they did. One day, she saw a big bowl of ice on the table. The ice was pink and shiny and looked very pretty. Lily wanted to touch the ice and see what it was. She climbed on a chair and reached for the bowl. But when she touched the ice, it was very cold and hurt her hand. She cried out and dropped the bowl. The ice spilled on the floor and made a mess. Lily's mom came and saw what happened. She was not happy. She picked up Lily and said, "Lily, you should not touch things that are not yours. You could get hurt or break something. You should ask before you touch." Lily felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to see the ice. It was so pink and pretty." Mom said, "I know, Lily. But the ice was not for you. It was for the cake. The pink ice was sugar and water and color. It made the cake look nice and sweet. But it was also very cold and hard. It was not good to touch. Next time, you should wait and ask me. I will tell you what things are and if you can touch them or not." Lily nodded and said, "OK, mom. I will wait and ask you. I don't want to get hurt or make a mess." Mom said, "That's good, Lily. I love you. Now let's clean up the ice and make a new cake." Lily said, "I love you too, mom. And I love cake. Can I help you make it?" Mom said, "Yes, you can. But only touch what I give you, OK?" Lily said, "OK, mom. I will be careful." And they hugged and smiled and made a new cake.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Amy and she was three years old. She loved to go to the playground. Amy's favorite thing to do at the playground was to go down the slide. She would climb up the steps and sit down on the slide. Then with a big smile, she would push off and go down the slide. She would giggle all the way down. But, one day, the slide was too slippery. With one careless push, she rose up into the air, higher than she normally did. She was so surprised that she couldn't help but to giggle with delight. But then she landed with a thud in the sand! Amy was okay though, and she was excited to go down the slide again and again. The End.

Tom likes to write. He writes with a crayon on paper. He writes his name, and his mom's name, and his dog's name. He writes big and small and fast and slow. He likes to write when the sun goes down. He likes to see the colors in the sky. He calls them sunset. One day, Tom wants to write outside. He takes his paper and crayon and goes to the yard. He sees a big fence. He thinks the fence is boring. He wants to write on the fence. He climbs on a chair and reaches the fence. He writes his name in red. He thinks it looks nice. But the fence is not his fence. It is the neighbor's fence. The neighbor is mean. He has a big dog. The dog is dangerous. It barks and growls and bites. The dog sees Tom on the chair. The dog runs to the fence. It jumps and snaps at Tom. Tom is scared. He drops his crayon and paper. He falls off the chair. He runs to his house. He cries for his mom. Mom hears Tom cry. She comes to the door. She sees Tom and the dog and the fence. She is angry and worried. She yells at the dog and the neighbor. She hugs Tom and takes him inside. She tells him he was wrong to write on the fence. She tells him he was lucky the dog did not catch him. She tells him he should never go near the fence again. She tells him the fence is dangerous. Tom is sorry. He says he is sorry to his mom and the neighbor and the dog. He says he will not write on the fence again. He says he will only write on paper. He says he will be careful and good. He says he loves his mom and his dog and his sunset. He says he does not love the fence. He says he is happy to be safe. He says he wants to write a new story. He asks his mom for a new crayon and paper. Mom smiles and gives him a new crayon and paper. Tom writes a new story. He writes about his mom and his dog and his sunset. He writes happy and nice and slow. He likes to write.

Once there was a boy named Jim. He was only 3 years old and he loved to eat yogurt. He always asked his mom to give him some yogurt to eat. Today, however, his mom did not give him any. "Why won't you give me any yogurt?" he asked his mom. His mom said, "I'm sorry, Jim. I don't have any yogurt right now. It's all gone." Jim was so sad. He did not understand why there was no yogurt anymore. Suddenly, he smelled something terrible. He ran to the kitchen to look and he saw that the yogurt was all spilled on the floor. It had gone bad and was now stinky. Jim was very sad and angry. "Who spilled the yogurt?" he yelled. His mom shook her head and said, "I'm sorry, Jim. I guess it was just a terrible accident." Jim was still very sad, but at least he knew what happened. His mom gave him a big hug and said, "Don't worry, Jim. You can come with me to the store and we can buy some more yogurt." That made Jim happy again and he smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very smart and loved to study. He always did his homework and listened to his teacher. One day, Timmy's mom made him some hot soup for lunch. "Yum! This soup is hot," said Timmy, blowing on his spoon. "I'm glad you like it, Timmy," said his mom. "Have you been studying for your spelling test tomorrow?" "Yes, Mom! I've been studying every night," replied Timmy. "That's great to hear, Timmy. Keep up the good work!" said his mom, giving him a pat on the back. Timmy smiled and continued to enjoy his hot soup, feeling proud of himself for being a smart student.

Tom is a boy who likes to use his bike. He uses his bike to go to the park, to the shop, and to his friend's house. He likes to ride fast and do tricks on his bike. One day, Tom sees a big hill near the park. He wants to use his bike to go up the hill and down the other side. He thinks it will be fun and exciting. He tells his friend Ben to watch him. Tom pedals hard and starts to go up the hill. He feels strong and happy. He is almost at the top of the hill when he hears a loud pop. His bike has a flat tire. He stops and falls off his bike. He feels sad and angry. Ben runs to help Tom. He says, "Don't worry, Tom. I have a pump in my backpack. We can use it to fix your tire. Then you can try again." Tom smiles and says, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. Can you help me walk my bike to the park? Then we can use the pump and try the hill again." Ben nods and says, "Sure, Tom. Let's go. I think you can be successful and go up and down the hill. You are brave and smart." Tom and Ben walk to the park with Tom's bike. They use the pump to fix the tire. Then they go back to the hill. Tom uses his bike to go up and down the hill. He feels proud and happy. Ben cheers for him. They are both successful and have fun.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they found a big, hairy dog. The dog was friendly and wagged its tail. Lily and Tom wanted to pet the dog, but they were afraid. "Let's make a promise," Lily said. "We will pet the dog together. You go first, then I go." "OK," Tom said. He was brave and walked to the dog. He reached out his hand and touched the dog's fur. The dog licked his hand and made a happy sound. Tom smiled and said, "See, he is nice. Your turn, Lily." Lily nodded and took a step. But then she saw the dog's teeth. They were big and sharp. She got scared and ran away. She tripped and fell on the ground. She hurt her knee and cried. Tom heard her cry and ran to her. He saw her knee was bleeding. He felt sorry for her and hugged her. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I broke our promise. I should have stayed with you. Are you OK?" Lily sniffed and said, "It's OK, Tom. You didn't mean to. I was silly and ran away. My knee hurts, but I'll be OK." They heard the dog bark and looked up. The dog was still wagging its tail. He came to them and licked their faces. He was not mean, he was just playful. Lily and Tom laughed and petted the dog. They made a new promise: to be friends with the dog and each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to do experiments in his lab. He had many weird things in his lab like a big green frog and a shiny blue rock. One day, Timmy's mom came into the lab and said, "Timmy, it's time to finish your experiment and clean up your lab." Timmy replied, "Okay, Mommy. I will finish soon." Timmy worked very hard and finally finished his experiment. He was so proud of himself! He showed his mom the cool thing he made in his lab. His mom was very happy and said, "Good job, Timmy! Your lab looks clean now."

Once upon a time, there was a caterpillar who was looking for a peaceful place to rest. He walked and he walked until he found a big, green leaf. It was the perfect spot! He settled himself on the leaf and was just about to have a peaceful nap when he heard a loud noise. It disturbed him and he looked up to see what was causing it. He saw a little boy playing with a ball. The caterpillar was sad that his peace had been disturbed. He was just about to leave when the boy noticed him and picked up the caterpillar gently. The boy smiled and put the caterpillar in the grass. The caterpillar felt much better now that he was in a peaceful place. He had a wonderful nap and soon he was on his way.

Ben likes to balance things on his head. He thinks it is fun and funny. He can balance a book, a hat, a ball, and even a spoon. He likes to show his mom and dad how good he is at balancing. One day, he finds a big box in the living room. It is a new television for the family. Ben wants to see what is inside the box. He opens it and sees the television. It is shiny and black and has a lot of buttons. Ben thinks it looks like a toy. He takes the television out of the box and puts it on the floor. He tries to turn it on, but nothing happens. He thinks maybe it needs batteries. He looks for batteries in the kitchen, but he cannot find any. He sees a banana on the table. He thinks maybe the banana can make the television work. He peels the banana and puts it in the back of the television. He goes back to the living room and tries to turn on the television again. Still nothing happens. He is disappointed. He thinks maybe the television is broken. He decides to balance it on his head instead. He lifts the television and puts it on his head. It is very heavy and hard to balance. He walks around the living room, trying to keep the television on his head. He does not see his mom coming in the door. She sees Ben with the television on his head and the banana in the back. She is shocked and angry. She yells at Ben to put the television down. Ben is scared and loses his balance. The television falls off his head and crashes on the floor. It breaks into pieces. Ben starts to cry. His mom is very upset. She tells Ben he is in big trouble. He has to go to his room and think about what he did. He cannot play with the television anymore. He is very sorry. He wishes he did not balance the television on his head. He wishes he did not put the banana in the back. He wishes he listened to his mom and dad. He learns a hard lesson. Balancing is fun, but not with a television.

Tom and Ann are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big box near the slide. They want to know what is inside. "Let us lift the box and look," Tom says. He tries to lift the box, but it is too heavy. He grunts and pulls, but the box does not move. "Let me help you," Ann says. She pushes the box from the other side, but it is still too heavy. They both get tired and sit on the grass. "Maybe we can open the box," Tom says. He sees a strip of tape on the box. He pulls the strip, but it is stuck. He pulls harder and harder, but the strip does not come off. "Let me try," Ann says. She pulls the strip from the other end, but it is also stuck. She pulls harder and harder, but the strip does not come off. They both pull the strip together, but it is still stuck. They pull so hard that they fall on the grass. They look at the box and see a big sign on it. The sign says: "Do not open. This box is full of rocks." Tom and Ann feel foolish. They laugh at themselves and go to play on the slide. They forget about the box and have fun.

Sara was a new girl in the class. She did not know anyone. She felt sad and lonely. She wanted to play with the other kids, but they did not let her. "Go away, Sara. You are not our friend. You do not belong here," they said. Sara ran away and hid behind a tree. She cried and wished she had a friend. Tommy saw Sara crying. He felt sorry for her. He liked to play with everyone. He did not like to see anyone sad. "Hi, Sara. I am Tommy. Do you want to play with me?" he asked. Sara looked up and saw Tommy. He had a big smile and a clean shirt. He looked nice and friendly. "Really? You want to play with me?" she asked. "Sure. You are welcome to play with me. I have a ball and a truck. We can share them," he said. Sara smiled and wiped her tears. She felt happy and hopeful. She followed Tommy to the playground. They played with the ball and the truck. They had fun and laughed. The other kids saw Sara and Tommy playing. They felt curious and jealous. They wanted to join them. "Hey, Sara. Hey, Tommy. Can we play with you?" they asked. Sara and Tommy looked at each other. They remembered how the other kids were mean to Sara. "What do you think, Sara? Should we let them play with us?" Tommy asked. Sara thought for a moment. She remembered how Tommy was nice to her. She wanted to be nice too. "Okay. They can play with us. But they have to be nice and share. They have to say sorry for being mean," she said. The other kids nodded and said sorry. They joined Sara and Tommy. They played with the ball and the truck. They had fun and laughed. Sara was not sad and lonely anymore. She had a friend and a group. She felt like she belonged. She felt welcome.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite shoe that was different from all her other shoes. She wore it everywhere she went. One day, while playing outside, she lost her special shoe. She looked everywhere for it but couldn't find it. Lily was very sad because she missed her shoe. She asked her mom and dad to help her find it, but they couldn't find it either. Lily cried and cried because she loved that shoe so much. Days went by, and Lily had to wear her other shoes. They were not the same as her special shoe, and she didn't like them as much. She still missed her special shoe and wished she could find it. One day, while walking to the park, Lily saw her special shoe in the middle of the street. She ran to get it, but a car came and hit her. She was hurt very badly, and her special shoe was ruined. Lily never got to wear her special shoe again, and she missed it every day.

Once there was a man, who was feeling very sad and empty. He thought and thought about what to do and finally, he had an idea. He went out and bought a candle. He lit it and said out loud, "Oh great candle, send my sadness away!" Suddenly, a gust of wind blew and extinguished the flame of the candle. This made the man very angry and he started shouting. He shouted and shouted and suddenly, the wind started to blow again. This time it engulfed the man, sending him away to a faraway land, never to be seen again. The candle remained, burning no longer, and the man's sadness never found an escape and he was gone forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with clay and make things with her hands. One day, she made an unusual clay creature that had many legs and big eyes. Lily's mom saw the clay creature and said, "Wow, Lily! That's so cool! Can you perform a little show with it?" Lily smiled and took her clay creature to her room. She made a little stage out of a shoebox and put her creature on it. Then, she pretended to be a singer and sang a song for her clay creature. The clay creature danced along and the audience (Lily's mom and dad) clapped and cheered. After the show, Lily's mom said, "That was amazing, Lily! You're so creative and talented!" Lily was so happy and proud of herself. She knew she would make more unusual clay creatures and perform more shows for her family.

Once upon a time, a little bird was flying through the sky. His wings were so big and strong, he could go wherever his heart desired. He was so excited for his adventures! One day, as he was flying by, he spotted something that made him slow down. It was a group of animals, surrounding one small, shy hedgehog. The hedgehog was saying funny things and everyone was laughing and clapping. The bird was so amazed by the hedgehog's courage, he flew down and applauded too. The hedgehog was so surprised and happy that the bird was clapping too. He began to fly circles around the animals, who laughed and clapped even more. Then the birds whooshed up into the air and flew to his nest in the tree. From then on, the little bird and the hedgehog were bestest friends. They would fly together around their favorite meadow, playing and singing songs. Whenever one of them was feeling scared, the other would give them a nudge and remind them that they weren't alone. Whenever the little bird flew back to his nest, he always ended his day with a kind, gentle applause for his new friend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sam. She had a drum that she loved to play. One day, her brother and her started to quarrel. They shouted, screamed and banged the drum! The noise was so loud that their mum came to see what was happening. She scolded them and told them to stop, but they just kept on quarreling. Mum had an idea. She said they should play the drum together, and make a happy sound. So they did! They banged the drum in a lively way and made a beautiful, lively sound. The quarreling stopped and they heard the sound of happiness. They smiled and mum was happy, too. They all enjoyed the sound of the drum and made wonderful music together.

Once there was a generous girl who wanted to make her mommy a dress. She found some pretty fabric and asked her mommy how to stitch it together. Her mommy told her to count the stitches carefully when sewing. The girl got to work, looking for the silver needle her mommy had given her. She counted each stitch carefully and soon she was done! Her mommy put on the dress, which made the girl smile. It fit perfectly! Her mommy thanked her for the dress. She said that it was so generous of her to make her a dress. The girl was very proud and hugged her mommy tight. She was so happy that she had made something as special as a dress. She couldn't wait to count more stitches and make more generous gifts!

Jill liked to play with snow. She made snowballs and snowmen with her friends. She wore a pink hat and a pink coat and pink gloves. She was very popular and everyone wanted to be her friend. One day, a new girl came to the park. Her name was Kate. She had a blue hat and a blue coat and no gloves. She looked cold and sad. Jill felt sorry for her and wanted to help her. "Hi, I am Jill. Do you want to play with me?" Jill asked. "Hi, I am Kate. I want to play, but I have no gloves. My hands are very cold," Kate said. "That's okay. You can lend my gloves. They are very warm and pretty," Jill said. She took off her gloves and gave them to Kate. "Thank you, Jill. You are very nice," Kate said. She put on the gloves and smiled. Jill and Kate played with snow. They made snowballs and snowmen and had fun. Jill was happy to share her gloves with Kate. But then, something bad happened. Kate saw some other kids playing with a sled. She wanted to try it too. She ran to the sled and jumped on it. She did not ask Jill or the other kids. She did not say goodbye. She just took the sled and the gloves and slid down the hill. "Hey, that's not fair! That's our sled! And those are my gloves!" Jill shouted. But Kate did not hear her. She did not care. She just kept sliding and laughing. She did not give back the sled or the gloves. She was very mean and selfish. Jill was very sad and angry. She had no gloves and no sled and no friend. She felt cold and lonely. She cried and went home. She wished she never met Kate. She wished she never lent her gloves. She learned a hard lesson. Not everyone is nice and honest. Some people are bad and greedy. She had to be careful who she trusted.

Mary was so happy. She was playing amongst the trees and the birds were singing. Suddenly, a folder fell from the sky. She picked it up and opened it. There, in the folder, she saw a beautiful red hat! Mary put on the hat and ran around playing. Everyone was laughing and having so much fun. Suddenly a voice shouted out: "I want that hat! Give me the hat." It was an ugly monster. Mary stopped running and looked frightened. The monster wanted her hat! Mary thought for a minute, before she said: "I'm sorry.
