She felt happy because she owned two things she loved - something sweet and something soft. She fell asleep with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was playing outside in her garden. She saw a bee flying around and felt scared. She went to her mommy and said, "Mommy, there is a bee. I am afraid." Her mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. Bees are our friends. They help flowers grow." Lily felt better and said, "Oh, I understand. Bees are helpful." Suddenly, the bee flew close to Lily and made a loud buzzing sound. Lily got alert and said, "Mommy, the bee is making a loud noise." Her mommy said, "Yes, that means the bee is busy collecting nectar from flowers." Lily asked, "What is nectar?" Her mommy explained, "Nectar is a sweet juice that flowers make. Bees include it in their honey." Lily smiled and said, "I like honey. Thank you, bee!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He loved going on adventures and playing outside. One day, he found a colourful cloth laying on the ground. John thought that the cloth was so pretty and he wanted to keep it. He decided to hide it in his pocket so that nobody else would find it. After hiding the cloth, John went on playing. Suddenly, John's mom came running up to him. She said, "John, where is my red scarf? I can't seem to find it anywhere!" John smiled and said, "I have it! I found a colourful cloth and I hid it in my pocket because I wanted to keep it!" John's mom laughed and said, "Well, it looks like you have a new scarf now!" John was very happy and ran off to find more adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Annie. Every day she would go to the park to play, and she had lots of fun. Today, Annie wanted to play a new game. She found a special tree with a swing on it, and she sat down in the swing. As she began to swing, she said loudly "I'm going higher and higher!" She said it over and over again. Annie kept on swinging for a really long time, but eventually she got tired. She looked around the park and noticed a very nice watch in the sun. She loved the watch and wanted to take it home. She reached out to pick it up, but it was too high for her to reach. So, Annie decided to use her own special trick and she said "I'm going to get that watch!" She said this for a few minutes and then she went really high up in the swing. As she got to the highest part of her swing, she managed to grab the watch. She was so happy, she said it over and over again! Annie was so tired after the whole adventure, but she finally had the watch. She put it around her neck and went home. She wanted to show everyone her new watch and so she repeated "look what I got!" with a big smile on her face. The End.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Ruby. One day, Ruby met a very nice dog. She was very excited and gave him a pat on the head. As she did this, a tray of food fell from the table. The dog was so hungry that he ate all the food in the tray. Ruby felt sad that the dog was so hungry, so she decided to try to help him. As she was thinking, she realized that she didn't know how to care for the dog. She felt quite ignorant but she was determined to take care of the dog. She went inside and searched the drawers until she found a food tray. She filled it up with delicious food and a bowl full of water. She gave it to the dog, and he was so happy he ate it all. Ruby felt very happy that the dog was now happy and well-fed. From then on, Ruby and the dog were great friends. Every day the dog would meet Ruby at the door, excited for the tray of food. She never forgot how ignorant she felt when she first met the dog, but she learned that it is always worth trying to help others in need.

John and his mom were walking in the fields. It was a warm and sunny day. Suddenly, John saw a hut. He ran toward it and said, "Mommy, look at the hut! Is it open?" His mom said, "Yes, John. Let's go in and explore it." When they entered the hut, John felt excited. He saw chairs, a table and toys. He ran around, exploring every corner of the hut. After a while, John felt tired. He said to his mom, "Mommy, can we share this hut with others too?" His mom answered with a smile, "Yes, John. That's a very good idea. We can share the hut with all our friends and have lots of fun!" John learned a valuable lesson from his mom. It's important to always share and be kind to others, even if it's just a simple open hut.

Lila and Tom are playing with their toys in the living room. Lila has a new laser that makes bright lights and sounds. Tom has a car that can move by itself. Lila likes her laser, but she also wants to try Tom's car. "Can I play with your car, Tom?" Lila asks. "No, it's mine. You have your laser, I have my car," Tom says. "But I want to play with both. Your car is so cool. It can go fast and turn and beep," Lila says. Lila is envious of Tom's car. She thinks it is more fun than her laser. Tom does not want to share his car. He thinks it is better than Lila's laser. They start to argue and tug at the car. The car falls to the floor and breaks. The wheels come off and the battery pops out. "Oh no, look what you did!" Tom cries. "I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to break your car," Lila says. They hear their mom coming. She sees the broken car and the laser on the couch. "What happened here?" she asks. They tell her what happened. She is not happy. She tells them to say sorry to each other and to share their toys. They say sorry and hug. They decide to play with the laser and the car together. They fix the car with some tape and glue. They take turns making the laser shine and the car zoom. They have fun and forget to be envious. They are happy to have each other and their toys.

Mama was having a lot of trouble with her car. It wouldn't start, and the engine made funny noises. "What's wrong mama?" asked the 3 year old child. "My car is broken," replied mama. "Can you repair it?" Mama smiled. "I sure can, with some help." The little girl helped mama take the broken pieces of the car to the repair shop. They worked together to get the car fixed. Finally, after a few days, mama got the car back in working order. "Hey look mama! The car is fixed!" the little girl said excitedly. Mama gave her a big hug. "Yes, we fixed it together. Now we can go anywhere we want!"

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Pete. Pete loved to explore the forest around his home, but he was always careful to lock the doors of his nest so he could stay safe. One day, Pete decided to go explore a new part of the forest and he forgot to lock his nest. While he was out, a big and dangerous fox came by and saw the door unlocked. He opened it and saw that Pete wasn't home. The fox quickly went inside and started to mess with all of Pete's things. He moved things around, ate all of Pete's food, and soon the nest was a total disaster. When Pete came back and saw the mess, he was sad and scared. "What happened here?" he asked the fox. The fox just smiled and said, "I wanted to show you the dangerous result of not locking the door of your home". Then he ran away. Pete quickly ran to his parents, who had seen the whole thing, and told them what happened. His parents hugged him and taught him a good lesson: always lock the doors of your home, otherwise you are in danger. Moral of the story: Always lock your doors, because there can be dangerous results if you don't.

Once, there was a poor family who lived in a small house. They didn't have much, but they were happy. Mum and Dad worked hard to make sure they had enough to live on. Every morning they all had breakfast together, which included toast and juice. They were often very tired, and so the family had to make their juice last for a few days. They would add some water to the juice, which made it stretch further. Today the family were very lucky. Someone had left a large carton of juice on their doorstep. Now they had plenty of juice to drink every day. They were so happy that their prayers had been answered. The family thanked the kind person for their lovely gift. Now they could share their juice with others less fortunate than them.

Once upon a time, there was a kind duck. The duck lived on a farm. The duck had a friend, a little girl. The little girl loved to eat waffles. She would share her waffles with the duck. One day, the duck found a big egg. The duck lay next to the egg to keep it warm. The little girl saw the duck and the egg. She was happy and waited for the egg to hatch. After some days, the egg hatched. A baby duck came out. The baby duck was very cute. The little girl fed the baby duck waffles too. They all played together and had fun. The kind duck and the little girl learned that sharing and caring for others made them very happy.

Jane was trying to find a game to play. She looked through her toy box and found nothing that matched the game she wanted to play. Suddenly, she had an idea. She took a few pieces of paper and wrote a few words down. Jane cut the pieces of paper and spread them around the floor. Jane stepped back, and with a quiet voice announced the game. "The game is called Match!" Everyone was quiet, as if the silence was waiting for Jane to start the game. Jane nodded, and thus began the game! Everyone had to find two pieces of paper that matched each other. The game was going well, and the room was filled with laughter. But it didn't last! Jane's little brother stepped in and made the silence suddenly become very clear. He had no idea what everyone was doing, so he decided to mix up all the pieces of paper. Jane was frustrated. All the pieces of paper were now in a big jumbled mess! She waited a few moments and watched her brothers carefully, trying to decide what to do next. After a few moments, she figured it out. Jane took a deep breath, and started helping her little brother put the pieces of paper back in order. After a few minutes, Jane and her little brother had managed to put all the pieces of paper back into the original order. She laughed with relief, and gave her brother a big hug. They had solved the problem and everyone enjoyed

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. Jack was only three years old and he loved to explore. One day he was walking around his house when he noticed something very big and unusual. What he saw was a huge hall with lots of things inside. He wanted to go inside, so he opened the door and stepped inside. Jack was amazed. Everywhere he looked there were shelves full of interesting things. There were toys, books and games of all shapes and sizes! Jack couldn't believe his eyes. He wanted to explore more so he started running around, touching everything he saw. He looked and looked until he found a special toy he wanted to take home. He couldn't reach it, but he found a chair and stood on it to get to it. Finally he was able to store the toy in his pocket and couldn't wait to show his mom and dad what he found. Jack was so proud of himself and couldn't wait to come back to this huge hall.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Carla who loved to catch bugs. She would catch all kinds of creepy crawly bugs in the garden. One day she noticed a bright blue bug and she decided she wanted to catch it. She ran around and around the garden but the bug was too fast! She chased the bug until she was all out of breath. Suddenly, a big white napkin landed on the blue bug! Carla cautiously picked the napkin up and carefully opened it; and there it was, a beautiful blue bug! She was so excited! Carla sat in the garden to enjoy her catch. But soon, she realized that it wasn't as exciting as she thought it was going to be. She looked around for something else to do but all she could find was an old, boring tree. Carla approached the tree and asked, "Hey, tree. Do you have anything fun to do?" The tree said, "I may not look like it, but I'm full of surprises. Come and take a closer look and see what you can catch!" Carla was delighted and soon she was collecting leaves and petals, she made herself a colourful crown, and she even caught a butterfly! She had a great time exploring the tree and the garden with her new found treasures.

Once upon a time, there was a tall fox who lived in the forest. She was very curious, and every day she liked to study the forest animals. One day, she asked a rabbit who was hopping by, "Do you know what I study every day?" The rabbit looked up and said, "No, I don't know, what do you study?". The fox replied, "I like to study the animals that live in the forest. I like to find out how they live and what they do." The rabbit said, "That sounds very interesting! I wish I could study too." The fox smiled and said, "You can. Just come with me tomorrow, and I will show you how to study the animals in the forest". The rabbit was very happy and the next day they both went off together to study the animals in the forest. They had lots of fun, and they both learnt a lot.

One day, a little boy named Tim lost a tooth. He was very happy because the tooth fairy would come at night. Tim put the tooth under his pillow and went to sleep. In the dark, a tiny fairy named Lily came to save the tooth. She looked under the pillow and found it. But it was so dark that she could not see well. Lily bumped into a toy and made a loud noise. Tim woke up and saw Lily. He said, "Who are you?" Lily said, "I am the tooth fairy. I came to save your tooth." Tim smiled and went back to sleep. In the morning, he found a shiny coin under his pillow.

A little boy named Marky was travelling with his mom to visit his grandma. Marky asked his mom a lot of questions about where they were going. Mom said: "We are going to grandma's house." Marky asked: "What should I bring?" Mom said: "Pack your bag with some toys and some clothes that fit." At the airport, they put their luggage on the conveyor belt. Marky asked: "Where is my bag?" Mom said: "It is over there. See the bag that is fit for a boy?" Marky looked around and found his bag. He was so excited. He now had a bag just like mom. Mom said: "Let's go!" Marky grabbed his bag and ran off with a big smile on his face. He was so excited for their visit to grandma's house.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She lived in a house full of amazing things. Every day she explored her house and discovered something new. One day, Lucy found a cherry tree in her garden. She saw the cherry tree had lots of sweet, red fruits. She didn't know what it was, so she asked her mother. Her mum said, "That is a cherry tree. Do you want to try one of the cherries?" Lucy was so excited. She plucked a juicy cherry off the tree and ate it. It was the most amazing thing she had ever tasted. She knew she loved cherries and wanted to eat them every day. Mum said, "Cherries are very special, so we won't pick them all. We will just pick a few, so that the cherry tree can grow lots more fruit." So every day Lucy would head out into the garden, pick one or two cherries, then she'd run inside and enjoy a delicious snack. She knew that cherries were amazing and always looked forward to picking them.

Once upon a time, there was a pale girl who liked to play with her friends. One day she received an invitation to a special event. She was excited and couldn't wait to go! When she arrived she saw all of her friends there. But something felt wrong. Suddenly, the bad guy appeared. He was angry and said that nobody was allowed to leave. He took away the invitation from the pale girl. Everyone was scared, but the pale girl was brave. She tried to fight back against the bad guy. In the end, the bad guy won. He shouted at everyone to never come back. The pale girl was sad. She wanted to be with her friends, but it was too dangerous. The bad thing had happened and everyone had to go home.

One day, a curious cat named Kitty went for a walk. She saw a big puddle on the ground. Kitty wanted to play with the puddle. She jumped in and splashed the water. The water went up and down, and Kitty laughed. A little dog named Spot saw Kitty playing in the puddle. He came running to the puddle and said, "Can I come play too?" Kitty said, "Yes, come play with me!" So, Spot jumped into the puddle with Kitty. They splashed and played together. After a while, they got tired and went back home. Kitty and Spot became good friends. They played in the puddle every day and had lots of fun. Their moms and dads were happy to see them happy. And that is the story of Kitty and Spot, the curious friends who loved to play in the puddle.

John wanted to do something special. He kneeled down on the ground in the bright sunshine and closed his eyes. He reached out to the ground and felt around until he found a smooth lemon. He held it carefully in his hand and was amazed by how heavy it was. He smelled it, feeling the sweet and tart scent enter his nose. John wanted to share the lemon with his family and he ran inside to show them. Inside, he found his mom and dad. He offered his lemon to them with a big smile. They both laughed, but felt excited about what John had done. It was not normal for a three-year-old child to find a lemon in someone's backyard. John was happy he found the lemon and felt proud he could share it with his family. Everyone gathered around and they enjoyed the crunchy and juicy lemon.

Jimmy and Tom were walking along the street, looking around. Suddenly, they heard a loud sound. It sounded like a trumpet. They both looked around to find out where the noise was coming from. Finally, they saw a group of people. They were playing instruments on the side of the street. Tom said, "Let's join them!" Jimmy was a bit scared. He said, "But I don't know how to play the trumpet." Tom said, "That's ok, it's easy! Just watch what I do." Tom stepped up to the dead trumpet and started to play. Jimmy watched carefully. After a few minutes, Jimmy started to join in. Soon enough, Jimmy and Tom were both playing their own trumpets. They were both so proud of themselves. The people around them clapped and cheered for their music. Jimmy and Tom were so excited! They carried on playing their trumpets until it got dark.

Once there was a little bunny called Bob. Bob was very restless and he loved to explore. He found a pen on the floor and he wanted to play with it. Suddenly, Bob heard his mother's voice. She said, "No, Bob! That pen isn't for playing - don't bite it!" But Bob still wanted to bite the pen. He squished it with his cheeks and his teeth were very close. Just then, Bob felt a big pain on his nose. He jumped back and he saw his mom. She said, "Bob, I told you not to bite the pen." Bob realised that he should have listened to his mom. He learnt that he should not bite things that don't belong to him. He never bit the pen again. The moral of the story is that we should always listen to our parents and not take things that don't belong to us.

Once upon a time on a summer day, there was a mom and dad playing with their little girl. Suddenly, a storm cloud came over the sky and it started to rain. The rain was like lightning and the little girl was sad. Mom and Dad asked, "What's wrong?" The little girl said, "I wish the weather could improve". So Mom and Dad thought of a way to cheer her up. They said, "Let's create a rainbow and when we do, the weather will get better!" The little girl was so happy and grabbed some colors. She quickly painted a rainbow and when she finished, the sky cleared up and the sun started to shine again. Mom and Dad said, "See, you can improve things that are sad!" The little girl smiled and they all enjoyed the sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Kathy. Kathy was three years old and liked to play all the time. One day, Kathy went to the park. She found a nice spot to sit down and began to play. She played for a long time, until she heard someone calling her from across the park. Kathy turned around to see her mom. Her mom said, "Kathy, it's time for lunch. Let's go get some food!" Kathy got up and followed her mom to the cafe. Inside, the cafe was very organized. Kathy and her mom each chose something to eat and then went to sit at a table. Kathy ate her food. She was very happy and soon she and her mom went back to the park to play. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy. He lived in a big house with his family. The boy was very regular and liked to play a lot. One afternoon, he heard a knock at the door. He ran to answer it and was so excited to see who it was. He opened the door and invited the person in with a big welcome. It was his best friend Henry. The boy and Henry said hello and hugged each other. They were so happy to see each other again. The two boys decided to have a regular game of catch. They played for a long time and laughed until their sides hurt. When it was time for Henry to go home, the boy gave him a big hug and welcomed him back anytime. The boy and his family waved goodbye as Henry walked home.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play with toys. One day, they went to the shop with their moms. The shop had many toys. Lily saw a big orange ball. She wanted the ball. "Mom, can I have the ball?" Lily asked. "Sorry, Lily, we don't have money for the ball. Maybe next time," Mom said. Lily was sad. She looked at Ben. Ben had a small green car. He liked his car. "Ben, can I play with your car?" Lily asked. "Sure, Lily, you can play with my car. But be careful, it has many parts. Don't break it," Ben said. Lily took the car. She played with it. She liked the car. She wanted the car. She forgot about the ball. She forgot about Ben. "Mom, can I have the car?" Lily asked. "No, Lily, that's Ben's car. You have to give it back to him. It's not nice to take things that are not yours," Mom said. Lily was angry. She did not want to give back the car. She ran away from Mom. She ran to the door. She tried to open the door. But the door was locked. She could not get out. "Help! Help!" Lily cried. Ben heard Lily. He ran to her. He saw the car in her hand. He saw that the car was broken. Some parts were missing. Some parts were on the floor. "Lily, what did you do to my car? You broke my car! You are a bad friend!" Ben said. Lily was scared. She was sorry. She did not mean to break the car. She wanted to say sorry to Ben. But Ben did not want to talk to her. He took his car and went to his mom. He did not want to play with Lily anymore. Lily was alone. She was sad. She wished she had listened to Mom. She wished she had been nice to Ben. She learned a lesson. She learned that being greedy and selfish is wrong. She learned that being honest and kind is right. She hoped that Ben would forgive her. She hoped that they could be friends again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emma. She was really scared because she had to take a test today. She felt so scared that she wanted to run away and hide. But she bravely stepped into the room where the test was. She was nervous and her heart was thumping fast. She was so frightened that she didn't even touch the test paper. She just sat there, shaking in her chair. Suddenly, someone came in and put their hand on her shoulder. It was her teacher. The teacher smiled and said, "don't be scared, Emma. You can do this!" Her teacher's hand was warm and comforting. Emma bravely picked up the test paper and answered all the questions. She had done it! She couldn't believe it! At the end of the day, Emma was so proud of herself. She had conquered her fear of tests and she knew in future she could take any test without being frightened.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old and loved to use her imagination. One day, Amy's mom told her she had to go to bed. But, Amy wanted to stay up and play. She tried to resist her mom, but her mom was very strong. So, Amy moved to her room. Amy was confused. She had her head in her lap and thought about what to do. Should she obey her mom or should she keep playing? Then, suddenly, an idea came to her! She quickly got up and went back to the living room. She told her mom that she would obey, but that she just wanted to say one more thing before going to bed. Amy's mom agreed and Amy said, "Let's make a deal. I will go to bed now, but can we spend the whole day together tomorrow?" Amy's mom smiled and said yes! She was so proud of Amy for resisting her when it wasn't easy. Happy, Amy ran off to bed, ready for the fun day together the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a big, lazy octopus. It lived in a big box, filled with fun things to play with. Everyday, the octopus would reach in and pull out a surprise. One day, the octopus heard a noise coming from outside the box. It saw some people carrying it away from its home. The octopus was afraid, but it soon realized that the people were actually helping it. The people unpacked the box and set the octopus free. The octopus felt excited! It was so happy to finally explore all the new places around it. The octopus happily spent the day exploring and playing. As it watched the sunset, the octopus felt so content and relaxed. It went to its special spot and watched as the stars twinkled in the night sky. The lazy octopus was so thankful to the people who unpacked it and gave it a chance to explore the world. The octopus gave them a big, sticky hug and said thank you.

Once upon a time, there was a funny monkey named Bobo. Bobo loved to play all day in the big tree. One day, Bobo saw a big banana on the ground. He was very happy and wanted to eat it. Bobo had a friend, a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to watch Bobo play. Bobo showed Timmy the big banana. Timmy kneeled down to look at it. He told Bobo, "Wait, don't eat it yet. I have an idea!" Timmy ran to his house and came back with a rope. He tied the rope to the big banana. Timmy and Bobo pulled the rope together. The big banana went up, up, up into the tree. When they let go, the banana swung back and forth like a swing! Bobo and Timmy laughed and took turns swinging on the big banana. They had so much fun playing together. And at the end of the day, they shared the big banana as a tasty treat. Bobo was happy he waited to eat the banana, because it made the day even more special.

Tom liked to perform tricks for his friends. He had a red hat, a long stick and a shiny knife. He would wave the stick and say magic words, then pull out the knife and cut a rope or a fruit. His friends would clap and cheer for him. One day, Tom wanted to perform a new trick. He saw a big pumpkin in the garden and thought it would be fun to cut it with his knife. He took the pumpkin and put it on a table. He waved his stick and said his magic words. Then he grabbed his knife and tried to cut the pumpkin. But the pumpkin was too hard and the knife was too weak. Tom pushed and pushed, but the knife did not go in. He pushed harder and harder, but the knife only bent and broke. Tom felt sad and angry. He threw the knife and the stick on the ground and started to cry. His friends saw him and ran to him. They hugged him and said it was okay. They said they still liked his tricks and he was a good performer. They said they could help him find a new knife and a new stick. They said they could also help him carve the pumpkin and make a funny face on it. Tom smiled and thanked his friends. He felt better and happy. He said he was sorry for being mad and he wanted to share the pumpkin with them. They all agreed and went to the kitchen. They carved the pumpkin and made a funny face on it. They also made pumpkin pie and pumpkin seeds. They ate and laughed and had fun. Tom was glad he had such good friends. He decided to perform a new trick for them next time, but with a softer fruit.

Anna and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. They had a jar with some ants and worms inside. "Look, Ben, I found a big beetle!" Anna said, holding up a shiny black bug. "Wow, let me see!" Ben said, reaching for the beetle. But as he touched it, the beetle opened its wings and flew away. Anna and Ben screamed and ran away from the beetle. They bumped into a rock and fell down. They looked up and saw something on the rock. It was a lizard. It had green scales and a long tail. It stared at them with its small black eyes. "Ah, a lizard!" Anna said, panicking. She did not like lizards. She thought they were disgusting and scary. "Shh, don't move. Maybe it will go away," Ben said, trying to be brave. But the lizard did not go away. It opened its mouth and showed its sharp teeth. It hissed and flicked its tongue. "Help, help!" Anna and Ben shouted, crying. They wanted their mom and dad to come and save them from the lizard. They heard footsteps and saw their mom and dad running towards them. They picked them up and hugged them. "What's wrong, sweeties? What scared you?" their mom asked, worried. "The lizard, the lizard!" Anna and Ben said, pointing at the rock. Their mom and dad looked at the rock and laughed. They saw the lizard, but it was not a real lizard. It was a toy lizard. Someone had left it on the rock as a joke. "It's okay, it's not a real lizard. It's just a toy. See?" their dad said, picking up the toy lizard and showing it to them. Anna and Ben looked at the toy lizard and felt silly. They realized they had been afraid of nothing. They laughed too and hugged their mom and dad. "Sorry, we were silly. We thought it was a real lizard," Anna said. "It's okay, we all get scared sometimes. But you don't have to be afraid of lizards. They are not disgusting. They are just animals. They won't hurt you if you leave them alone," their mom said. "Really? Can we see a real lizard?" Ben asked, curious. "Sure, maybe we can find one in the garden. But don't touch them, just look at them. They are very interesting and beautiful," their dad said. "Okay, let's go find a real lizard!" Anna and Ben said, excited. They put the toy lizard back on the rock and went with their mom and dad to look for a real lizard in the garden. They learned that lizards were not so bad after all. They had fun and forgot about the beetle.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. But today it is raining. They are sad. "Let's go to your house, Lily," Ben says. "Maybe we can find something fun to do there." "OK, Ben," Lily says. "But we have to be quiet. My baby brother is sleeping." They run to Lily's house. They take off their wet shoes and coats. They go to Lily's room. Lily has many toys and books. "Look, Ben," Lily says. "I have a new story book. It has pictures of animals and colors. Do you want to read it with me?" "Yes, Lily," Ben says. "That sounds fun. Can you bring it to the bed? We can sit on the pillows and read." Lily brings the story book to the bed. She opens it and shows Ben the first page. It has a picture of a red bird. "This is a bird," Lily says. "It can fly and sing. It is red. Red is my favorite color. What is your favorite color, Ben?" Ben thinks for a moment. He looks at the other pages. He sees a yellow duck, a blue fish, a green frog, and a brown bear. "I like all the colors, Lily," Ben says. "But I think I like blue the best. Blue is the color of the sky and the water. They are dry and nice. Not like the rain." Lily nods. She turns the page. She sees a big rainbow. It has all the colors. "Look, Ben," Lily says. "This is a rainbow. It comes after the rain. It is beautiful and bright. Maybe we can see one later, when the rain stops." Ben smiles. He likes the rainbow. He likes the story book. He likes Lily. They read the story book together. They forget about the rain. They are happy.

John was very excited. He was going to the park with his mom and his dog, Daisy. Daisy had a leash on so she wouldn't run away. John's mom held the leash and lead Daisy to the park. When they got there, they took off the leash and Daisy ran around and around. She was so happy! John was happy too. He ran around with Daisy and they had lots of fun. But then it started to rain. John and Daisy had to go home. Daisy was not happy with that. She made a lot of noise and whimpered. She was very miserable. John's mom lead the way home. She put the leash back on Daisy and they walked slowly home. Daisy wasn't happy at all, but she knew she had to listen. Finally, they made it home. Daisy ran off to her bed and John knew she was exhausted from the long walk. John was sad that their fun day ended so soon, but he was happy to be home with his mom and Daisy.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy cat. The cat didn't like to play or cuddle. He just sat around all day looking unhappy. One day, a little boy came to play with the cat. The boy wanted to make the cat happy, so he asked the cat if he wanted to design a toy together. The cat didn't want to design anything, but the boy was persistent. They started to work on the toy, but the cat was not interested. He just sat there and watched the boy. The boy worked hard on the toy, but the cat didn't like it. He thought it was a waste of time. The boy was sad that the cat didn't like the toy. He left the toy with the cat and went home. Later that day, the cat accidentally knocked the toy over and it broke. The cat felt bad that he had broken the toy and felt even grumpier than before. The story ended sadly, but the boy learned that not everyone wants to design things and that it's important to respect other people's feelings.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable rocket. It was always ready to fly. One day, the rocket's owners wanted to take it on an adventure. They wanted to use it to explore the sky. They all yelled with excitement when they saw that the rocket was ready to blast off. When the rocket blasted off, it flew higher and higher into space. Everyone was cheering and yelling as it grew farther and farther away. Then, suddenly, the dependable rocket stopped. It looked like it was stranded! The owners wondered what was wrong. Then, they saw a tiny shoelace wrapped around the rocket. It was causing it to get stuck! Everyone yelled with delight when they saw the little shoelace and knew that the dependable rocket could now be freed. The owners quickly untied the shoelace and the dependable rocket continued its journey. It soared through the sky and was never stuck again. Everyone was happy that their dependable rocket was ready for more adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. The elephant had a long trunk that it used to pick up things. The elephant was very dependable and always helped its friends. One day, the elephant saw a sad little bird. The bird had lost its nest and didn't know what to do. The elephant smiled at the bird and said, "Don't worry, I will help you." The elephant used its trunk to pick up some sticks and made a new nest for the bird. The bird was so happy and thanked the elephant for being such a good friend. From that day on, the bird and the elephant were the best of friends and always helped each other.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved her rubber. Every day she found special ways to play with it. She would make it into perfect shapes and pretend it was a little ballerina. One day she brought it to the park. She was so excited to show off her rubber! As she happily skipped around, a little doggie came up to her. He looked so friendly and cute, so she asked "Can I pet you?" The doggie barked a little and started to lick her hand. She was so happy and gave him a big hug. Suddenly, the doggie gave her a surprise by biting her rubber! The little girl was very shocked, she cried and said "No, no, why did you bite my rubber?!" The doggie just cocked his head to one side and looked sad. The little girl felt bad and said, "It's ok, I forgive you!" Then they played together, just like old friends. And from then on, the doggie had the most perfect rubber toy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He was very busy. Jack wanted to go to the beach to play in the sand. He also wanted to get some shrimp. When Jack got to the beach, he was so excited. He started to make a sandcastle. He worked hard to make it perfect. While Jack was busy building his sandcastle, he found some little shrimp. He picked one up to look at it. It was so funny! He needed to get more shrimp so that he could play with them. Jack looked all around the beach for another shrimp. Finally, he found what he needed. He was so happy to have found two shrimp. He quickly put them in a bucket and ran off to have some fun. Jack spent the whole day playing with his two shrimp. He had so much fun! He wasn't busy anymore. By the end of the day, Jack was tired but he was also very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her friends at the park. One day, they decided to have a race to see who was the fastest. They were very competitive and ran as fast as they could. But then, Lily fell down and hurt her knee. She started to cry, but her friend Sarah came over to comfort her. Sarah gave her a hug and said everything would be okay. Then, Lily's mom came with a rod to help her walk. They all went home together, and Lily felt much better knowing she had such caring friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to watch his daddy shave with his razor in the morning. One day, Timmy asked his daddy if he could shave too. Daddy said, "No, Timmy. You are still too little. But when you grow up, you can shave like a big boy." Timmy was sad, but he understood. He waited and waited until he was big enough to shave. Finally, the day came when Timmy was a big boy. He asked his daddy for his razor and his daddy said, "Okay, but be careful. Razors are sharp." Timmy shaved and shaved until he finished. When he was finished, he looked in the mirror and said, "Wow, I look fine!" His daddy smiled and said, "You did a great job, Timmy." Timmy felt so proud of himself and couldn't wait to shave again.

Once there was a little girl who was very excited. She was getting a new dress with number. She was wearing her dress outside when she saw a hairy dog. The girl said "Hello" but the dog didn't answer. The dog just kept looking at her with its big eyes. She asked the dog if it wanted to come and play with her. The dog shook its head and walked away. The girl then went back to the house and put on her dress. She was very happy to wear the new dress with the number. She went outside and tried to find the hairy dog. She looked for the dog for a long time, but it seemed to have disappeared. Finally, she saw it again. This time, the dog was lying down in the shade. The girl went closer and asked if the dog wanted to be her friend. The dog wagged its tail and said yes. From then on, the little girl and the hairy dog were very good friends. They played and ran around together every day. What a great friendship they had!

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Lucy. She was only three years old but she was very brave. One day, Lucy noticed a parade going past her house. She was very excited and wanted to join in. When Lucy asked her mom if she could take part in the parade, her mom said, "No, it's too expensive. We can't afford it." Lucy was very sad and she decided to hide so that she wouldn't be seen. She found a cheap box and got in it. Moments later, she heard music playing. She peeked out of the box and saw that the parade was still going! Lucy was so excited and she quickly rushed out of the box to join in the parade. She had the best time and was having so much fun! When the parade was over and Lucy returned home, she asked her mom, "Can I join the parade again next year?" Her mom laughed and said, "Yes, but only if you don't hide this time!"

Mum and Dad brought home a big hoop for Maria. She was so excited! She sat down on the floor and watched as Mum and Dad placed the hoop around her. "Wow, it so big!" said Maria. "Yes, it is big and fun," said Mum. Mum showed Maria how to count as she jumped through the hoop. She was a bit clumsy, but she was very happy. "One, two, three!" Maria said, counting each time she jumped through the hoop. Mum and Dad watched and smiled. They were so proud of Maria. She had so much fun that it was hard to take her away from the hoop. The next day, Maria asked Mum and Dad to bring out the hoop again. They quickly set it up and Maria began counting and jumping all over again. "One, two, three!" she said, smiling all the while.

Once upon a time there was a cute little girl named Daisy. Daisy had a glove that she liked to play with. She used to mix everything with it. She mixed sand and dirt and even food. One day, Daisy tried to mix mud and water with her glove. It didn't work very well, because it was too sloppy. Daisy got mad and threw the glove into the mud. She started to cry, because it was her favorite glove. But then something amazing happened! A little frog hopped out of the mud and gave her the glove back. It was all cleaned off and looked like new. Daisy was so happy! She hugged the frog and thanked him for cleaning her glove. And from then on, Daisy was always careful when she mixed things with her glove. She always made sure it was clean, and she still plays with it today.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet lived in a cozy nest on top of a chimney. The chimney kept Tweet warm in the winter. One day, a big storm came. The wind blew so hard that it knocked Tweet's nest off the chimney. Tweet was very sad and cold. She wanted to prevent this from happening again. Tweet decided to build a new nest that was more reliable. She worked hard all day and finally finished her new nest. But that night, a fire started in the chimney. The fire was too big and it burned down the whole house. Tweet's new nest couldn't prevent the fire from hurting her. Tweet was very scared and didn't know what to do. She flew away and never went back to her old home. The end.

One day, a generous lady happened to be walking in the woods. All of a sudden, she stumbled upon an old scale on the ground. She thought to herself, "What can I use this old scale for? Maybe it will come in handy one day!" Meanwhile, not too far away in the woods, there was a 3-year-old boy who was lost. He had been walking around for hours, searching for a way back home. He soon saw the lady, and he ran up to her, asking for help. The lady kindly listened to the boy's story, and with a generous smile, she pulled out the scale from her bag. She then said to the boy, "Maybe this scale can help you find your way back home!" The boy was delighted, and he thanked the lady with a grin. He then set off in the woods and the scale felt heavier and heavier, until it suddenly felt lighter! The boy soon realized that the scale was leading him back home - like a magnetic force! The boy made it safely back home, and soon learned that the generous lady who had helped him was none other than his grandmother! He then thanked her profusely for her generous act of kindness that day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big teddy bear that he loved to carry around with him everywhere he went. One day, Timmy and his teddy bear went for a walk outside. The ground was covered in ice and it was very icy. Timmy slipped and fell down, hurting his leg. But his teddy bear was there to help him up and carry him back home. Timmy was happy to have his teddy bear to help him when he needed it. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and a little boy. The mom had a plan to go to the park. "Let's make popcorn and go to the park," said the mom. The little boy was happy and they began to make popcorn. The boy warned his mom,"Be careful with the fire. Don't touch it." The mom listened and made sure the fire was safe. Soon, the popcorn was ready and it smelled yummy. The little boy took a big sniff and laughed. At the park, they put the popcorn on a picnic blanket and the little boy noticed some people nearby had some food that smelled disgusting. He warned his mom, "Don't eat that, it looks yucky." The mom smiled at her little boy, then they shared their popcorn and had a fun day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red cap that he loved to wear every day. It made him feel happy and powerful. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. He was having so much fun that he didn't notice when his cap fell off his head. Timmy didn't realize he had lost his cap until he got home. He looked everywhere for it, but it was nowhere to be found. Timmy missed his cap so much that he cried himself to sleep that night. The next day, Timmy went back to the park to look for his cap. But it was gone forever. Timmy was so sad and couldn't stop crying. He missed his cap and felt powerless without it. The end.

Tom and Lily were going to the zoo with their mom. They were very excited to see the animals. Mom said they had to take the subway to get there. The subway was a big train that went under the ground. "Can we sit by the window, mom?" Lily asked. "Sure, honey. Maybe we can see some lights or tunnels," mom said. They got on the subway and found a seat. Tom looked out the window, but it was very dark. He felt bored. "Mom, when will we get to the zoo?" he asked. "Soon, sweetie. The subway is very fast," mom said. She took out a book from her bag and said, "Do you want me to read you a story?" Tom nodded. He liked stories. Mom opened the book and said, "This is a story about a lion who lived in the jungle. He was very brave and strong, but he had a problem. He had no friends. He was very lonely. One day, he met a mouse who was very small and scared. The lion decided to help the mouse and they became friends. The mouse was very grateful and said, 'Thank you, lion. You are very kind. Can I recommend something to you?'" "What did the mouse recommend?" Lily asked. "You'll see," mom said. She continued reading. The mouse said, "You should go to the zoo. There are many animals there who are looking for friends. Maybe you can find someone who likes you and wants to play with you." The lion thought that was a good idea. He said, "Thank you, mouse. You are very smart. I will go to the zoo and see if I can make some friends." He said goodbye to the mouse and started walking to the zoo. He was very curious and hopeful. As mom read the story, the subway stopped at a station. The doors opened and a loud voice said, "This is the zoo station. Please exit here for the zoo." Tom and Lily looked at each other and smiled. They grabbed their mom's hand and ran out of the subway. They couldn't wait to see the animals. "Wow, mom, that was incredible!" Tom said. "The story and the subway were both amazing!" "Yes, they were, honey," mom said. "And maybe we'll see the lion and his friends at the zoo. Who knows?" They laughed and walked to the zoo entrance. They were ready for a fun adventure.

Lily liked to cook with her mom. She had a hat that was red and wide. It was her cook hat. She put it on when she helped mom in the kitchen. One day, mom said, "Lily, do you want to cook some cookies with me?" Lily nodded and smiled. She loved cookies. She ran to get her hat and apron. Mom gave Lily a bowl and a spoon. She said, "Lily, can you stir the flour and the sugar and the butter?" Lily said, "Yes, mom, I can stir." She stirred the mix with her spoon. It was hard and sticky. Mom said, "Good job, Lily. Now we need to add some eggs and some milk and some vanilla." She cracked the eggs and poured the milk and the vanilla. Lily stirred again. The mix was soft and smooth. Mom said, "Now we need to make some balls with the mix and put them on the tray." She showed Lily how to roll the mix with her hands and place them on the tray. Lily copied her. She said, "Mom, this is fun. I like to cook with you." Mom said, "Me too, Lily. You are a great helper. Now we need to put the tray in the oven and wait for the cookies to bake." She opened the oven and slid the tray inside. She said, "Lily, can you set the timer for 15 minutes?" Lily said, "Yes, mom, I can set the timer." She pushed the buttons on the timer. It beeped. Mom said, "Now we can clean up and wait for the cookies to be ready. Do you want to read a book with me?" Lily said, "Yes, mom, I want to read a book with you." She took off her hat and apron and put them away. She hugged mom and said, "Mom, I love you. You are the best cook." Mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the best daughter." They sat on the couch and read a book together. They smelled the cookies. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to play outside. One day, Jack went to the park to play on the swings. He loved to swing high up in the sky and feel the wind in his hair. Suddenly, Jack heard a voice. It was his friend, Lily. "Hi Jack, do you want to play with me?" asked Lily. Jack replied, "Yes, let's play together!" Lily had a new helmet on. Jack thought it looked very cool and brave. "Wow, Lily! Your helmet looks so cool and brave!" said Jack. Lily smiled and said, "Thanks, Jack! Do you want to try it on?" Jack put on the helmet and felt very brave. They played together on the swings and had so much fun. Jack felt happy to have such a brave friend like Lily.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing with her toys in the living room when she saw her mommy put a cookie in the cupboard. She wanted the cookie, so she went to the cupboard to get it. But when she opened the cupboard, the cookie was gone! It had vanished into thin air! Lily was very sad that she couldn't find the cookie. But then her mommy came over and saw her looking in the cupboard. "Don't worry, Lily," she said. "I put the cookie in a different place. Let's go find it together!" They looked all around the kitchen, and finally found the cookie on the counter. Lily was so happy! She took a big bite of the cookie and it was very dry, so she drank some milk to help it go down. From then on, she always made sure to ask her mommy where she put the cookies so they wouldn't vanish again.

Once upon a time, there was a worm. He was a very special worm because he was unique. One day, the worm was picking some food from the ground. He was eating some yummy leaves and grass. Suddenly, something special caught the worm's eye. He noticed a bright, sparkly rock nearby. It was so beautiful that he had to pick it up. He was so excited! He held it in his hand for a few moments, then he carefully put it safely in a little hole in the ground. The worm liked the sparkly rock so much, that he went back every day to pick it up again. He would lay down in the grass and he'd look at it and enjoy its beauty. He thought it was the most special thing in the world. The friends of the worm were so impressed by the unique rock, that they started picking up special objects of their own. They kept their special objects in the same hole in the ground as the sparkly rock. The worm was very proud of his special rock and he liked that he could share this unique treasure with his friends. They all enjoyed picking up new things, looking at them and having fun.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toys, but he was sad because his favorite toy was missing. He looked everywhere for it, but he couldn't find it. One day, Timmy saw a big lab with lots of cool things inside. He went inside to look for his toy, but everything was dirty and messy. Timmy tried to clean up, but he accidentally knocked over a candle and started a fire. The fire burned the lab and Timmy was scared. Luckily, the firefighters came and put out the fire. Timmy was sad that he burned the lab, but he was happy when he found his toy. He promised to always be careful with fire and to keep things clean.

Once upon a time, in a charming little town, there lived a boy named Will. He loved to play outside with his friends, and they would run and laugh all day long. One sunny day, Will and his friends were playing near a big tree. They saw a small cat stuck high up in the branches. "Oh no!" said Will. "The cat needs help!" His friends agreed, and they all tried to think of a way to save the cat. Will had an idea. "Let's kneel down and make a ladder with our backs!" he said. So, Will and his friends kneeled down and helped each other climb up. They made a strong ladder for the cat to climb down safely. "Thank you," said the cat, as it jumped down onto the soft grass. Will and his friends were happy that they could help and continued to play and have fun.

Once upon a time there were two friends - Jack and Jill. They were out for a walk in the park. Suddenly, Jack saw a vase on the ground. He asked Jill, "What is that?" Jill said, "It's a vase." Jack ordered Jill to pick it up and put it somewhere safe. So Jill picked up the vase and looked at it closely. She was very sad. Jack asked, "Why are you so sad?" Jill replied, "I think someone dropped it, and it's broken." Jack said, "I'm sure they would be glad if they could have it back. Let's ask them if they know who owns it." So they searched and searched until they finally found the vase's owner, a little old lady. When she saw the vase, she was so happy and hugged them both, thanking them for finding it. Jack and Jill were glad that their search had been successful and the little old lady was happy too. Everyone was happy in the end.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jack and Jill. They always agreed on things and spent lots of time together playing. But then one day, they started to disagree. Jack wanted to go outside and play in the park, but Jill wanted to stay in and read a book. Jack and Jill argued for a long time about what to do. Finally, they decided to ask their tutor for help. The tutor was very wise and had a wide knowledge. The tutor told Jack and Jill that it wasn't good to always disagree. He said that if they took turns doing what each was most interested in, they could still be friends and have lots of fun. Jack and Jill agreed with the tutor and decided to share their time together, so they could be friends forever.

Lily was a curious girl who liked to explore. Today, she went to the park with her mom and saw a big pond with ducks and fish. She wanted to see them closer, so she ran to the edge of the pond and leaned over. "Be careful, Lily!" her mom called. "Don't fall in the water!" Lily nodded, but she was too busy looking at the ducks and fish. She saw a shiny coin at the bottom of the pond and reached for it. But as soon as she touched it, it vanished! "Where did it go?" Lily asked, surprised. "It was a magic coin, Lily," a voice said behind her. Lily turned around and saw a man with a long beard and a hat. He was holding a wand and smiling. "Who are you?" Lily asked, curious. "I'm a magician, Lily. I like to make things vanish and appear. Do you want to see some more magic?" the man asked. Lily nodded, excited. She liked magic. The man waved his wand and made a balloon, a flower, and a rabbit appear. He gave them to Lily and she thanked him. "You're welcome, Lily. But remember, magic is not always what it seems. Sometimes, things that vanish can come back, and things that appear can disappear. Be careful what you wish for, Lily," the man said, and winked. Then, he vanished too, leaving Lily with the balloon, the flower, and the rabbit. Lily was amazed and happy. She ran back to her mom and showed her the gifts. "Wow, Lily, where did you get these?" her mom asked. "From a magician, mom. He made a coin vanish and then he gave me these. He was very nice, but he said magic is not always what it seems. What does that mean, mom?" Lily asked. Her mom looked puzzled and curious. She did not see any magician in the park. She wondered if Lily was making up a story or if she really met a magic man. She hugged Lily and said, "I don't know, Lily. But I'm glad you had fun today. Let's go home and have some cookies, okay?" Lily agreed and smiled. She liked cookies. She also liked magic. She wondered if she would see the magician again. She hoped so. She had many questions for him. She was a curious girl.

Once upon a time there was a gifted girl called Daisy. Daisy loved playing with her toys and wanted to record them every day. She had a special chain that she used to tie all of her toys together at the end of each day. One day, Daisy was playing with her dolls when she had a wonderful idea. She wanted to record all of her dolls on video and save them forever! She got her dad's camera and started to make a movie of her dolls dancing and singing. Daisy was so excited to record her dolls - it was like she was making her own movie! When Daisy had finished recording, she put all of her dolls back in a line and used her special chain to tie them together. The video was saved forever, and Daisy could watch it any time she liked. Everyone was so happy with Daisy's movie, and they all said she was so gifted!

Once upon a time, in a land full of trees, there was a little cherry tree. The cherry tree was very sad because it did not have any friends. All the other trees were big and strong, but the cherry tree was small and weak. The cherry tree was envious of the big trees. One day, the cherry tree felt a tickle in its branches. It was a little spring wind. The wind told the cherry tree not to be sad. The wind said, "You are special because you have sweet cherries that everyone loves." The cherry tree started to feel a little better. As time went on, the cherry tree grew more and more cherries. All the animals in the land came to eat the cherries and play under the cherry tree. The cherry tree was happy because it had many friends now. The cherry tree learned that being different can be a good thing. And they all lived happily ever after.

Sam and Tom are friends. They like to play outside. They have many toys. They have balls, cars, dolls, and books. One day, Sam and Tom want to play with their toys. But their toys are messy. They are everywhere. Sam and Tom cannot find their favorite toys. "Let's organize our toys," Sam says. "We can put them in boxes. Then we can find them easily." "OK," Tom says. "That is a good idea. You take the balls and the cars. I take the dolls and the books." Sam and Tom start to organize their toys. They put them in different boxes. They work hard. They are happy. When they finish, they look at their toys. They are neat and tidy. They can see all their toys. "Wow, we did a good job," Sam says. "Now we can play with our toys." "Yes, we can," Tom says. "But first, let's go for a jog. We need some exercise." "OK," Sam says. "Let's go for a jog. But where is your hat?" Tom touches his head. He is bald. He has no hair. He lost his hat yesterday. "I don't have a hat," Tom says. "But I don't mind. I like being bald. It is cool." Sam smiles. He likes Tom. He does not care if he is bald. He is his friend. "OK, let's go for a jog," Sam says. "But be careful. The sun is hot. It can hurt your head." "OK, I will be careful," Tom says. "But you be careful too. The ground is hard. It can hurt your feet." Sam and Tom laugh. They hold hands. They go for a jog. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy bear. He didn't like to play, he just liked to be alone. One day, he decided he wanted to try something new. He decided to the swing in the park. He hopped onto the swing and pushed off the ground. He whooshed back and forth, feeling happier than before. As he was swinging, he spotted something soar through the sky - it was a missile. He got excited and decided to try to grab the missile. He jumped off the swing and ran to the sky, but he was too slow! The missile kept flying higher and higher, until it was out of sight. The grumpy bear was sad. He had missed the missile. He shuffled back to the swing, but suddenly felt much happier. Even though he had missed the missile, he realized that the swing was fun. And he never stopped swinging again!

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, they found a big bag full of old toys in the attic. They were very happy and took the bag to their room. "Look, Sam, there are so many toys here! Cars, trains, dolls, puzzles, and more!" Tim said. "Yes, Tim, they are very fun! Let's try them all!" Sam said. They opened the bag and took out the toys. Some of the toys were broken or dirty, but they did not care. They played with them for a long time, making noise and mess. But then, Tim's mom came to their room. She was not happy. She saw the bag and the toys and said: "Tim, Sam, what are you doing? These toys are not yours. They belong to your grandpa. He gave them to me when I was little. They are very special and old. You should not play with them like that. You should be careful and respectful. Look, you broke some of them and made them dirty. How do you think your grandpa would feel?" Tim and Sam felt bad. They did not know the toys were so important. They said: "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We just wanted to play. We did not mean to hurt the toys." Tim's mom said: "I know, boys. But you should always ask before you take something that is not yours. And you should treat things with care and love. These toys are part of our family history. They have memories and stories. They need to be restored and cleaned. Do you want to help me do that?" Tim and Sam nodded. They wanted to make up for their mistake. They said: "Yes, mom. We want to help. We want to restore the toys and make them nice again. We want to learn about them and their stories. We want to make you and grandpa happy." Tim's mom smiled. She said: "Thank you, boys. That is very kind and patient of you. I am proud of you. Come on, let's go to the attic and find the tools and materials we need. And then, I will tell you some stories about these toys and how your grandpa and I played with them when we were little." Tim and Sam followed their mom. They felt sorry, but also curious and excited. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect and value the things that belong to others. They learned to restore and care for the things that are old and special. And they learned to listen and enjoy the stories that connect them to their family.

Ben and Mia were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many apples. They wanted to taste the apples. They ran to the tree and picked some apples. "Look, this apple is red and shiny!" Ben said. He bit the apple. He made a face. "Yuck! This apple is sour and hard!" Mia laughed. She looked at her apple. It was green and smooth. She bit the apple. She smiled. "Mmm! This apple is sweet and juicy!" Ben was confused. He looked at Mia's apple. He wanted to taste it. He asked Mia, "Can I have some of your apple?" Mia nodded. She gave Ben some of her apple. Ben tasted it. He liked it. He said, "You are right! This apple is good!" They heard a voice. It was their mom. She called them, "Ben! Mia! It's time to go home!" They ran to their mom. They showed her their apples. They told her about the tree. Mom smiled. She said, "You found a knot tree! A knot tree has two kinds of apples. Some are red and sour, some are green and sweet. You can tell by the color." Ben and Mia were surprised. They did not know that. They said, "Wow! A knot tree is cool!" Mom said, "Yes, it is. But remember, always wash your apples before you eat them. They might have dirt or bugs on them." Ben and Mia nodded. They washed their apples. They ate them on the way home. They were happy. They liked the knot tree. They wanted to come back to the park and taste more apples.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. They had a lovely wagon that they shared. They took turns to pull the wagon and put things in it, like rocks, leaves and toys. They had fun with their wagon. One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They wanted to go down the hill with their wagon. Lily said, "Let's go, Ben! It will be fast and fun!" Ben said, "OK, Lily! But we have to be careful. The hill is steep and the wagon is heavy." They pushed their wagon to the top of the hill. They climbed in and held on tight. Lily said, "Ready, Ben?" Ben said, "Ready, Lily!" They let go of the brakes and the wagon started to roll down the hill. At first, they laughed and screamed with joy. The wagon was fast and fun. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They saw the trees and the flowers and the birds. They were happy. But then, the wagon went too fast. It bumped and shook and rattled. It went out of control. Lily and Ben were scared. They tried to stop the wagon, but they couldn't. They saw a big rock in their way. They shouted, "Help! Help!" But no one heard them. No one came to help them. The wagon hit the rock and crashed. Lily and Ben flew out of the wagon and landed on the ground. They were hurt and bleeding. They cried and cried. Their lovely wagon was broken and smashed. Their rocks, leaves and toys were scattered and lost. They had no fun with their wagon. The moral of the story is: Be careful when you play with your wagon. Don't go down a big hill with your wagon. It can be dangerous and hurt you. Listen to your parents and follow the rules. They know what is best for you.

Once upon a time there was a smart girl called Jane. Jane asked her parents for money every day. Her parents said, "No! You have to work for your money!" One day Jane asked her friend Molly, "Do you have money?" Molly said, "No, but I want money. How can I get money?" Jane said, "You can be smart and work. Then you will get money!" Molly said, "Ok, let's work together!" So the two of them started working together. After a few weeks they had some money. Molly and Jane were very happy! They had lots of fun spending their money.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and going outside to play in the sun. One day, Lily's mom asked her to deliver a package to their neighbor. Lily was so excited to help her mom. She grabbed the package and ran outside. The package was wrapped in brown leather and she held it tightly in her little hands. As she walked to the neighbor's house, she saw some kids playing with a ball. They asked her to play with them, but she said she couldn't because she had to deliver the package. When she arrived at the neighbor's house, she knocked on the door. The neighbor opened the door and said, "Thank you for delivering this package, Lily. You are such a good helper." Lily felt proud and happy, not ashamed like she had felt earlier when she couldn't play with the other kids.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved cookies. One day, he thought of a brilliant idea. He wanted to sell cookies to his friends. Tim asked his mom to help him make cookies. They made many yummy cookies. Tim put the cookies in a big box. He was ready to sell them. Tim went to his friends' houses. He said, "I have cookies to sell!" His friends were happy. They bought cookies from Tim. Tim was very proud of his brilliant idea. And they all enjoyed the yummy cookies together.

Once there lived two brothers. One was named Shaun and one was named Joe. They were very different, but they always got along. One day Joe was feeling nervous. He was looking for something, but he didn't know what it was. So, he went to find his brother Shaun and asked for help. Shaun was very clever and thought he might be able to solve the mystery. So, Shaun and Joe went to search for the answer. They went to a nearby well and chose the biggest copper coin they could find. They dropped it inside and waited to see what would happen. After a few moments, a message came out of the well and told them the answer they had been looking for. Joe was so excited and Shaun felt very proud of himself for helping his brother solve the mystery. They hugged each other happily and continued on their way. The brothers enjoyed the rest of their day and never forgot how they solved the mystery with the help of the well.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug. The bug loved to fly. One day, the bug saw a net. The net was big and harsh. The bug wanted to see the net, but it was scared. The bug flew near the net. The wind blew the net. The net moved fast. The bug was very scared. It flew away from the net. The bug did not want the net to hurt it. The bug found a nice tree. The tree was far from the net. The bug was happy. It could fly and play without the harsh net. The bug lived happily in the tree.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy called Bob. He had long, curly hair and likes to wander around the park. One day, Bob went to the park and found a big chain. He thought it was very interesting and wanted to learn more about it. So, he followed the chain around the park and tried to see where it would take him. Eventually, the chain led him to a big tree. Under the tree, there was an obedient puppy. The puppy looked up at Bob and wagged its tail. Bob smiled and said hello. The puppy was so happy to meet Bob and followed him around the park. They ran and played together until sunset. As the sun went down, Bob took the chain and put it around the puppy's neck. The puppy was obedient and walked after Bob. Bob and the puppy went home. They wandered back through the park, holding hands. Bob knew the puppy was in good care.

Ben and Lily are friends. They like to play together. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big truck. The truck has a sign. The sign says "Popcorn". "Look, popcorn!" Ben says. "I like popcorn. Do you like popcorn, Lily?" "Yes, I do. Popcorn is yummy. Can we have some, mom?" Lily says. Their moms nod and smile. They give them some money. Ben and Lily run to the truck. They see a man. The man has a big machine. The machine makes popcorn. The popcorn pops and pops. It smells good. "Hello, kids. Do you want some popcorn?" the man says. "Yes, please!" Ben and Lily say. The man gives them two bags. One bag is white. One bag is yellow. "This is original popcorn. It has salt and butter. This is cheese popcorn. It has cheese and more butter. Which one do you want?" the man says. Ben and Lily look at the bags. They think hard. "I want the original popcorn. It looks good." Ben says. "I want the cheese popcorn. It looks different." Lily says. They take their bags and say thank you. They go back to their moms. They sit on a bench. They open their bags. They eat their popcorn. They share with their moms. They are happy. "This popcorn is delicious. Thank you, mom." Ben says. "This popcorn is tasty. Thank you, mom." Lily says. Their moms hug them and kiss them. They are proud of them. "You are welcome, Ben. You are welcome, Lily. You are very good kids. You are original kids." their moms say.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, they were playing hide-and-seek when Lily couldn't find her friends. She looked all around but they were nowhere to be seen. Suddenly, she heard her friends shout her name. They were hiding behind the exit sign near the playground. Lily was so happy to find them. She ran towards the exit sign, and her friends opened their arms to give her a big hug. From that day on, Lily always made sure to check behind the exit sign when playing hide-and-seek with her friends.

Jojo was walking through the woods when he stumbled across a crab. He bent down and looked at it closely. It was walking in a straight line and looked so clean. He gasped with delight. "Look at you, you're the most cleanest crab I've ever seen!" The crab heard Jojo and stared at him. It said: "Thanks. I try to keep clean by washing every day." Jojo smiled and said: "I want to support you. What do you need?" The crab thought for a moment and said: "I need food to help me get stronger. Do you have anything to give?" Jojo dug into his pocket and found a few bits he had found earlier. He said: "Here you go!" The crab was so happy and thanked Jojo as it scurried away. Jojo smiled to himself and thought 'I'm glad I could help.'

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mommy asked her to come to the grocery store with her. Lily was very happy and excited to go. When they got there, they saw a big mess on the floor. Lily's mommy said, "Oh no, this is messy. We need to be careful not to slip and fall." Lily said, "I can help clean it up!" But her mommy said, "No, it's not safe for you. I'll take care of it." As they were walking down the aisle, Lily saw a toy she really wanted. She asked her mommy if they could buy it, but her mommy said they didn't have enough money for it. Lily was sad and started crying. Her mommy hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we can save up for it next time." Lily felt better and they continued shopping. When they got home, Lily helped her mommy put away the groceries. She felt happy that she could help and that they had a nice time together.

Once upon a time there was an old girl. She was very happy. She loved to race! Every morning she would get up bright and early and race around the garden. She laughed and smiled as she jumped and skipped. One day, the old girl decided she wanted to race even faster. She ran and ran and ran as fast as she could. The wind whipped through her hair. She felt so alive! Eventually, though, the old girl started to grow tired. She stumbled and slowed down until she could go no more. She looked around and smiled. She had raced all around the world! The old girl collapsed, content and happy. She had raced - and she had won!

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a cart. He was very worried because he had to load it with lots of heavy boxes. He asked his dad to help him. "No problem," said his dad, in a kind voice. "I'll help you load the cart." The boy was relieved and smiled. He and his dad put all the boxes in the cart. The boy felt proud. He had done it with his dad's help. He knew the load would be too much to manage on his own. The cart was now full of boxes. His dad said, "Ready to go!" The boy and his dad pulled the cart together, off to the market they went!

One day, it started to rain outside. All around, the trees, the flowers and the grass were getting wet and washed clean. Inside the house, a little three year old boy watched out of the window with his big eyes. His mama said that it was nice to hear the rain. The boy went running through the house until he arrived in the kitchen. It was so big and modern. There were big white cupboards, a big table in the middle, and a tall fridge. The boy liked looking in the cupboards and opening and closing the fridge. He put his small hands inside and pulled out the food. The boy's mama smiled, looking at her little boy in the modern kitchen. She said he should help her make dinner, so he put on an apron and started to help. They enjoyed their time together in the kitchen, listening to the sound of the rain outside.

Once there was a family who had a little girl called Grace. Grace loved playing on the board with her toys every day. One day, she wanted to play with her toys but her parents said it was time for a nap. Grace sighed and went to her bed. When she was about to sleep, her mummy came over and gave her a kiss. She asked Grace to always be patient and gentle. Grace nodded "Yes, Mummy". Her mummy replied with a gentle smile, "I will always remind you". Grace felt better with the reminder from her mummy. She closed her eyes and drifted off to sleep. When she woke up, she was excited to play with her toys on the board again. She smiled and happily ran off to play.

Once upon a time, two little boys were playing in a park. They were looking at the different plants and tossing a ball around between them. Suddenly, one of the boys, who was feeling very naughty, slapped the other boy on the back. The other little boy turned around and said, "Why did you slap me? That wasn't very nice!" "Because the plant I wanted to look at was more organized," said the naughty boy. The other little boy just stared in confusion. He didn't understand why being organized made it okay to slap someone. The naughty boy said, "Look, it's okay to slap someone sometimes, but only if they're behaving in an organized way." He didn't sound too sure of this himself, but the other little boy still just stared. Then, the naughty boy said, "Let's go look at the other plants. The one I wanted to see was really organized!" And he smiled, hopping off to see the other plants in the park. And the two little boys had a fun day, without any more slaps.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a deer. The deer was very dull. He did not like to play with the other animals. One day, a rabbit came to the deer and said, "Why are you always so dull? Come play with us!" The deer replied, "No, I want to sleep all day. I do not like to play." The rabbit felt sad and went away. The other animals did not like the dull deer. They thought he was not fun to be around. One day, a big storm came to the forest. The wind was strong and the rain was heavy. All the animals ran to find a safe place to hide. The dull deer was still sleeping. The rabbit saw him and said, "Wake up, deer! There is a big storm. We need to find a safe place to hide." The deer woke up and followed the rabbit. They found a big cave to hide in. All the animals were safe inside the cave. The storm went away, and the sun came out. The deer was happy that the rabbit had helped him. From that day on, the dull deer learned the importance of having friends. He started to play with the other animals and became a happy deer. The moral of the story is: having friends is important, and we should always be there for each other.

Sam was getting ready to go to school. He opened his drawer and took out his blue shirt. He quickly put it on and looked in the mirror. He looked organized and smart. But when he went to school his friends started to laugh. He didn't understand why. He was embarrassed. Then he realized his shirt was on inside-out! Sam quickly turned it around. He was so embarrassed but he felt better when his friends stopped laughing. He knew it was important to always be organized so this wouldn't happen again. He put the shirt back in his drawer and made sure it was correctly facing forward. With his shirt now on the right way around, Sam was ready to start a great day at school.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to play in the park. One day, she saw a big image of a monster. She was scared and she started to cry. Her mum came and asked her, "What is wrong, my little one?". The girl showed her the image of the monster and told her, "It scared me." Mum gave her a hug and said, "It's okay, my child. It's just a picture, and it can't hurt you." But the little girl was still shaken and very frightened. She wanted to go home, so they went back. Once they reached home, the girl asked to leave the light on at night. She was afraid the monster in the picture might scare her in her dreams. Mum and the girl said goodnight and the little girl tried to sleep, although she was still scared. From that night on, the image of the monster continued to haunt her dreams.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with toys. They have a big box of toys. They have cars, trains, dolls, balls and a plane. The plane is red and blue. It has wings and wheels. It can fly in the air. One day, Tom and Sam decide to play with the plane. They want to make it fly. They take the plane out of the box. They put some toys inside the plane. They load the plane with cars, trains, dolls and balls. They say, "The plane is full. It is ready to fly." They look for a place to fly the plane. They see a tall tree in the yard.
