They think, "The tree is tall. It is good for flying." They run to the tree. They hold the plane in their hands. They count, "One, two, three, go!" They throw the plane in the air. But the plane is too heavy. It has too many toys inside. It does not fly. It falls down. It hits the tree. It breaks into pieces. The toys fall out of the plane. They scatter on the ground. The plane is ruined. The toys are dirty. Tom and Sam are sad. They cry. They say, "Our plane is broken. Our toys are dirty. We are sorry. We are bad." They pick up the pieces of the plane and the toys. They put them back in the box. They go inside the house. They do not play with the plane anymore. They have no fun. They have a bad day.

Sammy was at the park and wanted to play. He saw a pale spark in the sky. It was very pretty and Sammy wanted to add it to his collection. He tried to reach it but it was too far away. He asked his dad for help and his dad got a big ladder. They carefully climbed the ladder and soon Sammy was close enough to add the spark to his collection. He was so happy and thanked his dad for his help. Then he ran back to the park, spark in hand to share his new treasure with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She was very frustrated because she could not play outside. Every day when the sun came up, she looked out the window longingly, wishing she could go out and explore. One day, Sarah's mother came up to her and said, "Sarah, the sun is shining! Would you like to go outside and explore?" Sarah was so excited. "Yes!" she said, and her eyes lit up with excitement. She jumped up and ran out of the house. As Sarah explored, she noticed the sun was shining and the birds were singing. She felt so happy and free, but suddenly a little worm crawling on the ground caught her eye. She wanted to pick up the worm and explore it, but it suddenly wriggled away. Sarah was frustrated, and a tear rolled down her cheek. Why couldn't she explore the worm, she thought. She yelled out to her mom, who heard her from inside the house. Her mother came out and comforted her. "It's ok Sarah. You can come back tomorrow and see if the worm is still there, ok?" Sarah smiled and wiped away her tears. She was no longer frustrated, and went inside feeling happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with bubbles. She would blow and blow until she made a big, beautiful bubble. One day, Lily met a little boy named Max. Max was very fearful of bubbles. He didn't like them because they popped and disappeared. Lily asked Max if he wanted to play with her and the bubbles. Max was scared at first, but Lily showed him how to blow the bubbles gently. Max became less fearful and started to enjoy playing with the bubbles too. The moral of the story is that sometimes we can be scared of things, but if we try them out, we might become less fearful and even enjoy them.

Lily likes to exercise. She likes to jump, run, and dance. She is very flexible. She can bend her legs and arms in many ways. She can touch her toes and make a bridge. One day, Lily wants to exercise with her mom. But her mom is busy. She has to work on her computer. She tells Lily to play by herself. Lily is sad. She wants to exercise with her mom. Lily has an idea. She takes her mom's yoga mat and puts it on the floor. She says, "Mom, look at me. I can exercise like you." She starts to do some poses. She stretches her arms and legs. She balances on one foot. She twists her body. Her mom looks at her and smiles. She says, "Lily, you are amazing. You are so flexible. You can exercise very well." She closes her computer and joins Lily on the mat. She says, "Let's exercise together. I can learn from you." Lily is happy. She hugs her mom and says, "Thank you, mom. I love you. I love to exercise with you." They exercise and have fun. They do not leave the mat until they are tired. They are both flexible and happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their toys. They saw an old man sitting on a bench. He had a long beard and a hat. He was holding a book. "Who is he?" Lily asked Ben. "I don't know. Maybe he is a wizard," Ben said. They walked closer to the old man. He smiled at them and said hello. "Hello, sir. What are you reading?" Lily asked. "I'm reading a story about a brave and honest knight who saved a princess from a dragon," the old man said. "Wow, that sounds exciting. Can you tell us the story?" Ben asked. "Sure, I can. Come and sit with me," the old man said. He pointed to a picture in the book. It showed the knight riding a horse and holding a sword. "This is the knight. His name is Arthur. He was very brave and honest. He always helped people who were in trouble," the old man said. He pointed to another picture. It showed the princess in a tower and the dragon breathing fire. "This is the princess. Her name is Gwen. She was very kind and beautiful. She was trapped in the tower by the dragon. The dragon was very mean and greedy. He wanted to keep her for himself," the old man said. He pointed to the last picture. It showed the knight fighting the dragon and the princess cheering. "This is the end of the story. Arthur fought the dragon and wounded him with his sword. The dragon ran away and never came back. Arthur freed Gwen from the tower and they hugged each other. They were very happy and grateful. They became friends and lived happily ever after," the old man said. Lily and Ben clapped their hands and cheered. "That was a great story. Thank you, sir," Lily said. "Yes, thank you. You are very nice and smart," Ben said. The old man smiled and said, "You're welcome, children. You are very polite and curious. I'm glad you liked the story. It's one of my favorites." They talked for a while and then said goodbye. Lily and Ben went back to their toys and pretended to be knights and princesses. They had a lot of fun. The old man watched them and smiled. He was happy too.

Ben was a little boy who loved to joke. Every day, he would laugh and make funny noises. He had a lot of fun with his family and friends. One day, the family had an event. Ben was excited to go and see what it was all about. But when he got there, he was in for a big surprise. Everyone was telling jokes and having a great time. Ben wanted to join in too. But he was feeling a bit scared and unsure of himself. He didn't want to make a joke and make it wrong. So, he stood there silently. Then, one of Ben's friends noticed him and asked if he wanted to tell a joke. Ben was relieved and he started to smile. He was about to tell a funny joke, when he felt a bitter taste in his mouth. It was a sour lemon. Ben had been holding it in his hand the whole time and he had forgotten about it. Everyone started to laugh and clap for the funny ending to Ben's story. Ben was so happy that he had made everyone laugh. From then on, he was always ready to tell a joke.

Once upon a time, there was a playful prince. He loved to run and jump and play all day. One day, he wanted to add more fun to his day, so he invited his friends to come and play with him. They played games and had a lot of fun together. As they played, the prince noticed that one of his friends was feeling sad. He asked her what was wrong and she said that she lost her toy. The prince wanted to help her, so he added his favorite toy to her collection. She was so happy and grateful that she gave the prince a big hug. From that day on, the prince learned that adding kindness and love to the world can make everyone happy. He continued to play with his friends and always looked for ways to add more joy to their lives. The end.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Julia. She lived in a small town near the sea. One day, dark clouds formed in the sky. Julia saw lightning and heard thunder. She was scared, but she was brave and wanted to see the storm closely. Julia went outside and noticed a big, dangerous tree. On the very top of the tree sat a bird. Suddenly, she heard the bird chirping. "What are you doing up there?" asked Julia. "I'm scared of the lightning," said the bird. "It's too dangerous for me to fly away." Julia reached up and grabbed the bird gently. "Don't worry," she said. "I will keep you safe." The bird smiled and said, "Thank you." Just then, Julia felt a sharp bite on her arm. She looked down and saw a tiny yellow snake. "That's a dangerous snake," said the bird. "He wants to bite you." Julia quickly put the bird back in the tree and ran away. She had been brave, but now she was safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved watching TV, especially her favorite show about a friendly dinosaur. One day, Lily's mom bought her a new, comfortable couch to sit on while she watched her shows. As Lily sat on her new couch, she noticed something strange on the TV screen. The colors were all mixed up and the picture was blurry. She tried to fix it herself, but she couldn't figure it out. Lily decided to ask her mom for help. Her mom noticed the problem right away and fixed the TV for her. Lily was so happy and grateful that she gave her mom a big hug. From then on, Lily enjoyed watching her shows on her comfortable couch with a clear TV picture.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to play outside. He saw a big mattress in the yard. It was a brilliant color, like the sun. Tim was very happy and ran to the mattress. He jumped on the mattress and played all day. He played games like bounce, roll, and pretend. The mattress was so much fun. Tim's friends came to play too. They all laughed and had a great time. As the sun went down, Tim and his friends were tired from playing. They said goodbye and went home. Tim went inside and told his mom about the brilliant mattress. He could not wait to play again tomorrow.

Peggy was feeling bored so she decided to go outside to explore. As soon as she stepped outside, she saw something disgusting. It was a big tuna flopping around in the mud. It was so gross! Peggy screamed, "Ewwww!" She wanted to get away from the slimy fish. Suddenly, a friendly voice said, "Don't be frightened little one. That tuna won't hurt you." Peggy looked around and saw a kind looking old lady standing nearby. She asked, "Why is the tuna so yucky?" The old lady smiled and said, "It got stuck in the mud pit. That's why it looks so disgusting. It needs help getting out. Would you like to help?" Peggy was so excited! She ran over to the tuna and pulled it out of the mud. "There you go little tuna," she said as she smiled. The tuna swam away happily. Peggy thanked the old lady for helping her. She said, "It was so nice of you to be kind to the poor tuna!" The old lady replied, "Anytime, my dear. Now you have to go before your mom gets worried." Peggy waved goodbye to the old lady and ran back home, feeling excited and happy. She had saved the disgusting tuna!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. Jack was very excited because his parents were taking him on a new adventure. They were going to sail on a big boat! Jack packed his bag and ran to the boat. He was so excited that he forgot to take his stuffed toy out of the closet. Jack and his parents said good-bye and began to sail away. The boat bobbed up and down in the water, and they saw lots of new sights. When they returned, Jack ran to his closet to find his stuffed toy. He was so happy when he saw it. Jack and his family had a wonderful new adventure together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very brave, and she wanted to explore. One day she decided to take a walk. She entered a dark room. All of a sudden a bright light turned on. The little girl was very surprised. She realized the light came from a bulb hanging from the ceiling. The bulb was very loud. It made a buzzing sound and the little girl was not sure if she liked it. She touched the bulb and it got even brighter. She was amazed! The little girl decided to explore the room and see what else she could find. She was very happy she was brave enough to enter. The end.

Once upon a time, in an ordinary little town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim was very hungry. His stomach made loud noises. He wanted to eat something yummy. Tim saw a big apple tree. He asked his friend, Sam, "Can you please help me get an apple?" Sam agreed and helped Tim climb the tree. They both picked apples and ate them. But the apples were not ordinary apples. Soon, Tim and Sam felt sick. Their stomachs hurt a lot. They cried out, "Oh no! What did we eat?" They did not know that the apples were bad apples. In the end, Tim and Sam were still sick. They learned a lesson to not eat apples from that tree again. Their ordinary day turned into a very bad day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a nosy cat named Tom. Tom loved to watch what everyone was doing. One day, Tom saw two little birds having a fight over a toy. "Stop!" Tom said to the birds. "Why are you fighting?" The first bird said, "I found the toy first, but he insists on taking it away from me!" The second bird said, "No, I found it first! You are trying to take it away from me!" Tom thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea. Let's share the toy. You can play with it in the morning, and you can play with it in the afternoon." The two little birds agreed to share the toy, and they stopped fighting. Tom was happy that he could help his friends. From that day on, the birds and Tom played together and shared all their toys. And Tom learned that being nosy can sometimes be helpful.

Once upon a time, there was a good painter who was walking near a hill. Suddenly, she felt the ground shaking and she was scared. The painter asked a 3 year old child nearby,"What's happening?" The child smiled and said "Don't worry, it's just the trees shaking. They like to shake and dance!" The painter was relieved and thanked the child for reassuring her. She said "You are so good! Thank you for telling me the truth." The child grinned and thanked the painter in return. She said "You're welcome, painter. I see you're a good painter too." And they both went on their merry ways.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and watch cartoons on his modern TV. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a present. It was a big, shiny present with a pretty wrap on it. Timmy was so excited to open the present, but when he did, he didn't like what was inside. It was a shirt that he didn't like. Timmy's mom asked him why he didn't like the shirt, and Timmy just shrugged his shoulders. Later that day, Timmy saw a homeless man on the street who didn't have any clothes to wear. Timmy remembered the shirt his mom gave him and realized that he could give it to the homeless man. Timmy felt happy that he could help someone in need and learned that sometimes things may not seem important, but they can be helpful to others.

One day, Tom and Tim went to the park. They saw a big melon on a table. Tim said, "Let's see who can eat the melon faster!" They both wanted to win, so they were competitive. Tom started eating the melon very fast. Tim paused and looked at Tom. He thought of a plan. Tim said, "Tom, look! A big bird is taking your toy!" Tom stopped eating and looked away. While Tom was looking for the bird, Tim ate the melon very fast. When Tom looked back, the melon was gone. Tim smiled and said, "I won! The bird was not real. I tricked you!" Tom was sad but learned that he should not always believe what others say.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a clumsy boy named Tom. Tom liked to play with his toy chain. One day, Tom had a question for his mom. He asked, "Mom, can I go play with my chain outside?" His mom said, "Yes, Tom, but be careful. Don't lose your chain." Tom was happy and ran outside to play. He swung his chain around and around. But because Tom was clumsy, the chain flew out of his hand and into a big tree. Tom was sad and had another question for his mom. "Mom, can you help me get my chain from the tree?" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, Tom. Let's get a long stick and try to get it down." They found a long stick and used it to get the chain back. Tom was happy again and said, "Thank you, Mom!" From that day on, Tom tried to be less clumsy when playing with his chain.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. He loved to play. He had lots of toys to choose from, but his favorite was the black missile. Every day, Joe would play with the black missile. He would run around the house, flinging the missile up in the air and chasing after it. He imagined he was a brave knight, on a grand adventure. One day, something amazing happened. Joe climbed a tree and filled the black missile with glitter. When the wind blew, the glitter sparkled in the sun. People passing by were mesmerized by the show and would stop and watch. Joe was so proud of his creation and kept playing with the black missile until the sun went down. The black missile was Joe's favorite toy and he will always remember his magical adventure.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jack. She was four years old and loved playing outside. One day, Jack went outside to play. Suddenly, she saw something pink in the grass. She went over to investigate and saw it was a beautiful butterfly. She wanted to know its name, so she asked, "What is your name?" The butterfly replied with a fine answer: "My name is Pinky". Jack was so excited. She asked, "Can I touch you?" Pinky said yes, so Jack carefully touched it. Pinky fluttered away and Jack waved goodbye. Jack felt so happy and went inside with a big smile on her face.

Tom and Lily liked to bounce on the big bed. They jumped up and down and laughed. They made funny faces and noises. They did not hear Mom call them for dinner. "Tom, Lily, come and eat!" Mom said again. She was angry. She smelled something bad. She went to their room and saw smoke. There was a fire in the trash can. Tom and Lily had played with matches and made ash. "Tom, Lily, what did you do?" Mom shouted. She grabbed them and ran out of the room. She called Dad and the firemen. They came and put out the fire. They checked the house and said it was safe. "Tom, Lily, you were very naughty," Dad said. "You could have burned the house and hurt yourselves. You should never play with matches. They are dangerous. Do you understand?" Tom and Lily nodded. They were scared and sorry. They hugged Mom and Dad and said they were sorry. They promised to be obedient and not play with matches again. Mom and Dad forgave them and hugged them back. They said they loved them and were glad they were safe. They gave them dinner and tucked them in bed. They kissed them good night and said they were proud of them for telling the truth. Tom and Lily fell asleep and dreamed of bouncing on the big bed.

The big Lion roared loud and harsh. He was the King of the jungle and wanted everyone to know it. Everyone in the jungle was scared of the loud roar, except for the little fox. He had a saw in his hand, and thought he could cut down the lion with it! The little fox ran towards the lion and began to saw, but the lion just roared even louder. The saw was no match for the King of the Jungle. He blasted out a roar that was so loud and so harsh, it made the fox drop his saw and run away. The lion was victorious. He knew that he was powerful and no one could stand up against him! He roared with joy, and the animals of the jungle knew he was the king once again.

One sunny day, a little boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. Tim saw a big, red cherry on a shelf. He wanted to add the cherry to his ice cream. Tim asked his mom, "Can I have the cherry, please?" His mom looked at the price and said, "Oh no, this cherry is too expensive. We can't buy it today." Tim was sad, but he understood. Later, Tim and his mom went to the park. They saw a cherry tree with many cherries. Tim's mom said, "Look, Tim! We can pick cherries here for free!" Tim was very happy. They picked cherries and added them to their ice cream. They enjoyed their ice cream with cherries under the tree, and it was a perfect day.

Once upon a time, there was a big, smelly animal. His name was Joe and he was a funny-looking animal. One day, Joe wanted to play a game. He found a special puzzle. He picked it up and started to play. He struggled to put all the pieces together. He would get stuck, but he kept trying to figure it out. Finally, he struck the last piece in and the puzzle was finished! Joe was very happy. He jumped up and down and cheered. It felt great to finally solve the puzzle. Joe wanted to play it again, but he was too tired. He laid down and fell asleep with a smile on his face.

Lily and Ben are young twins who like to play in the park. They have a big red ball that they can kick and throw. One day, they see a new slide in the park. It is shiny and blue and has a zip at the end. Lily and Ben want to try the slide. They run to the slide and climb the steps. Lily goes first. She sits on the slide and pushes herself down. She feels the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She smiles and laughs as she goes faster and faster. She reaches the zip and flies off the slide. She lands on the soft grass and rolls over. She is happy and proud. Ben watches Lily and claps his hands. He wants to have fun too. He sits on the slide and pushes himself down. He feels the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He smiles and laughs as he goes faster and faster. He reaches the zip and flies off the slide. He lands on the soft grass and rolls over. He is happy and proud too. Lily and Ben hug each other and giggle. They love the slide. They want to go again. They run to the steps and climb them. But then they see a big boy on the slide. He is older and taller than them. He has a mean face and a loud voice. He says, "This is my slide. Go away. You are too young and small." Lily and Ben are scared and sad. They don't want to fight. They just want to play. They look at each other and hold hands. They say, "Please, can we share the slide? It is fun for everyone." The big boy shakes his head and says, "No. This is my slide. You can't have it." He reaches out and pinches Ben on the arm. Ben cries out and lets go of Lily's hand. He rubs his arm and tears fill his eyes. Lily is angry and brave. She says, "That is not nice. You hurt my brother. You are a bad boy. You can't pinch people. You have to be kind and fair." She reaches out and pinches the big boy on the nose. The big boy yelps and lets go of the slide. He rubs his nose and tears fill his eyes. Lily and Ben run to the slide and sit on it. They push themselves down and feel the wind and the sun. They smile and laugh as they go faster and faster. They reach the zip and fly off the slide. They land on the soft grass and roll over. They are happy and proud again. They look at the big boy and say, "Sorry, we pinched you. But you pinched us first. You have to be nice and share. The slide is for everyone. Do you want to play with us?" The big boy nods and says, "Sorry, I pinched you. I was mean and selfish. I have to be nice and share. The slide is for everyone. Yes, I want to play with you." Lily and Ben smile and say, "OK. Let's be friends. Let's have fun." They run to the steps and climb them. They sit on the slide and push themselves down. They feel the wind and the sun. They smile and laugh as they go faster and faster. They reach the zip and fly off the slide. They land on the soft grass and roll over. They are happy and proud together.

It was a sunny day, and the sea was calm. Bob and his father had just put up the sail on their boat. "Alright, let's set sail!" Bob said happily. His father nodded. As the boat was gliding across the water, Bob asked, "What are we looking for?" "We are looking for fish," his father replied. Suddenly, Bob's fishing line jerked. He gasped in excitement. "I think I struck one!" he said. His father smiled as he helped him to reel in the fish. It was a big one! But Bob's excitement soon faded. As he pulled the net closer, he saw that there was another fish already in the net. "It was already there," he said sadly, feeling ignorant. His father nodded. "It looks like we weren't the only ones looking for fish today," he said.

John was very organized. Every morning he would bring his carpet to school. On the carpet were many special toys. They were kept in a special way so they were easy to find. At recess, John would unroll the carpet. All the children would gather around. Everyone loved to play the games. John would organize a game of tag and the children would laugh and giggle as they ran around. John would also organize a hide and seek game. Everyone would hide behind the carpet. Then, when the seeker found them, they would all burst into laughter. At the end of the day, John would roll up the carpet and take it home, looking forward to the next day when he could bring back his favorite carpet again.

Once upon a time, there was a colorful butterfly flying in the garden. The butterfly had many colors like red, blue, and yellow. The butterfly was happy because it could fly wherever it wanted. Suddenly, the butterfly saw its sister sitting on a flower. The sister butterfly was sad because she couldn't fly like her sister. The colorful butterfly stopped and asked her sister what was wrong. The sister butterfly said she wished she could fly like her sister. The colorful butterfly said, "Don't worry, I will teach you how to fly!" And so, the colorful butterfly taught her sister how to fly, and they flew together happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a bright alert blue bird who lives on top of a tall tree. One clear day, the sun was shining so brightly that the bird could no longer stay awake. So, the bird paused for a moment and decided to take a nap in the sun. Suddenly, the bird was awoken with a loud noise. It was the sound of thunder! The blue bird spread its wings wide and flew to an empty branch just as the sky was getting grey. Cautiously, the bird looked around and saw a storm building up in the sky. The bird then paused again, as if it was building up the courage to fly to safety. With one flutter of its wings, the bird set off, faster and faster, trying to catch up with the dark clouds. The storm was getting bigger and bigger and it was getting windier and windier. Finally, the bird managed to stay ahead of the storm and landed safely on a tree in a sunny spot on the other side. The blue bird was happy that it had made it in time, and it watched the storm fly away with its bright alert eyes.

Once, there was a very important bell. Everyday, the bell would ring loudly. Everyone in the village heard the bell. It was a sign that something special was happening. One day, the bell rang and everyone gathered around the village square. The mayor of the village said that today was a special day. He included everyone in a special game. Everyone was so excited and happy. The mayor said to stay very quiet and to all close their eyes when the bell rang again. Everyone followed the mayor's instructions and the bell rang again. When the bell stopped ringing, everyone opened their eyes and the mayor held up a big box full of surprises! Everyone who was included was so happy. They all laughed and cheered for the surprises. From then on, the bell was very important to the village. It was always a sign that something special was happening and that everyone was included in it.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fat cat named Max. Max liked to eat a lot of food, especially fish. One day, Max's owner was making a cake and Max wanted to help. His owner let him mix the batter with a big spoon. Max liked mixing the batter because it was fun. After they mixed the batter, Max's owner poured it into a pan and put it in the oven. Max sat by the oven, watching the cake bake. When it was done, Max's owner cut a big slice and gave it to Max. Max ate it all up and licked his lips. He was happy to have helped make the cake.

Once there was a brave man. He had an axe and he was always very alert. One day, he felt a little worried. So he grabbed his axe and ran into the dark woods. He was very brave, but he was also very scared. He felt the trees around him, swaying in the wind. He felt his heart racing. He was so alert and focused, looking for any signs of danger. Suddenly, he heard a noise! He couldn't believe his ears. He gripped his axe tightly and felt ready to take on anything. He was brave and alert. He had made it through the dark woods and now he felt proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He went to the hospital to see his grandpa who was sick. When he got there, he saw a nurse who was wearing a white outfit. The nurse looked confused because she didn't know where to go. Timmy asked her if she needed help, but she just shrugged her shoulders. Timmy decided to show the nurse where his grandpa's room was. They walked down the long hallway and finally found the room. Timmy's grandpa was happy to see him and gave him a big hug. The nurse was happy too and thanked Timmy for helping her. After visiting with his grandpa, Timmy and the nurse walked back to the front of the hospital. The nurse was no longer confused and Timmy felt proud that he could help her. As they said goodbye, the nurse gave Timmy a big smile and a high five. Timmy felt happy and knew that he had made a new friend.

One day, a mama and dad lay an infant in their bed. The infant was so small and cute, everyone thought it was crazy. The mama and dad were so excited to see the beautiful little infant in their home. The infant loved to sleep in its bed, but it wasn't very good at it. It would lay there, wiggle around and make silly noises. Everyone would laugh and say it was so crazy. Every morning, the infant would wake up and the mama would lay it in her lap. The infant would laugh and smile and giggle as the mama sang to it. It was so happy, it seemed crazy. Then one day, the infant started growing up and no longer wanted to be layed down. It wanted to walk, run and play instead. The mama and dad were so proud, but they still thought it was kind of crazy.

Lila and Rani were sisters who liked to play in the forest. They made spears from sticks and stones and pretended to hunt animals. One day, they saw a big rabbit hopping near a bush. They wanted to catch it for their dinner. "Let's test our spears," Lila whispered to Rani. "You go left and I go right. We will throw our spears at the same time." Rani nodded and they crept closer to the rabbit. They counted to three and threw their spears. But the rabbit was clever and saw them. It jumped away and ran into the bush. "Oh no, we missed!" Lila said. "The rabbit is too fast and smart." "Maybe we can trick it," Rani said. "Look, there is a carrot on the ground. We can use it as bait." Rani picked up the carrot and placed it near the bush. She hid behind a tree and waited. Lila hid behind another tree and held her spear. They hoped the rabbit would come out and eat the carrot. Soon, they heard a rustle in the bush. The rabbit poked its head out and sniffed the air. It saw the carrot and licked its lips. It hopped out of the bush and moved towards the carrot. "Now!" Rani shouted. She and Lila threw their spears again. This time, they hit the rabbit and it fell to the ground. "Yay, we got it!" Lila cheered. "We are good hunters!" They ran to the rabbit and picked it up. They were proud of their spears and their clever plan. They took the rabbit home and cooked it for their dinner. They shared it with their family and told them their story. Their family praised them and said they were brave and smart. Lila and Rani smiled and hugged each other. They loved to play in the forest.

Tom and Mia love to ride the waves at the beach. They have a big board that they share. They take turns to lie on the board and paddle with their arms. When they see a good wave, they push the board fast and slide on the water. One day, they see a very big and powerful wave. It is taller than a house. Tom wants to ride it, but Mia is scared. She says, "No, Tom, that wave is too big. It will hurt us. Let's wait for a smaller one." But Tom does not listen. He says, "I can do it, Mia. I am brave and strong. You are a baby. Watch me ride the wave." He paddles hard and catches the wave. Mia watches from the shore. She sees Tom go up and down on the board. He looks happy and proud. But then, the wave breaks and crashes on him. He falls off the board and disappears in the foam. Mia screams, "Tom, Tom, where are you?" She runs into the water and looks for him. She is very worried and sad. She thinks, "I should have stopped him. He was too silly and reckless." After a few seconds, she sees Tom's head pop up. He is coughing and spluttering. He looks scared and sorry. He says, "Mia, Mia, help me. I can't find the board. The wave was too big. I was wrong. You were right." Mia swims to him and hugs him. She says, "It's okay, Tom. I'm here. I'm glad you are safe. Don't do that again. Let's ride the small waves together. They are more fun and less dangerous." They swim back to the shore and find the board. They dry themselves and hug again. They say, "We love each other. We love the waves. But we have to be careful and smart." They learn their lesson and have a happy day.

Clarissa was feeling very grumpy as she watched the soldiers walk by. "What's wrong?" Her mother asked. "Why don't you play with them in the garden?" Clarissa shook her head, "No. I don't like the soldiers." But her mother smiled and said, "Maybe you'll change your mind. Come and play with them in the garden". So Clarissa went outside. She thought about running away but everything inside her was telling her to give them a chance. As she stepped out of the house, the soldiers saw her and called her name. Clarissa was still feeling grumpy so instead of walking toward them, she ran away and started to weep. The soldiers were startled by her reaction but they followed her anyway and finally caught up to her. "What's wrong?" Asked one of the soldiers. Clarissa wiped her eyes and said, "I was just thinking that sometimes you have to give people a chance". And with that, the soldiers welcomed her as a friend and she learned that soldiers were not so scary after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He was out playing with his friends in the park when he saw a big, red brick. He wanted to have the brick, so he hopped off his swing and ran to get it. But when he got there, Jack realized he couldn't pick up the brick - it was too heavy! He started to yell for help, but no one heard him. Just then, a brilliant girl walked by. Her name was Lucy. She saw Jack trying to pick up the brick and came over to help him. She said to him, "I can lift that brick for you. No problem!" Jack said, "Thank you!" He was embarrassed that he couldn't pick up the brick, but was so glad Lucy was there to help him. She easily lifted the brick, handed it to Jack, and walked away with a smile. Jack was so happy. He picked up the brick and ran to show his friends. He had a brilliant plan all along - they were going to have a brick race!

Anna and her mom went to the grocery store. They needed to buy food for dinner. Anna liked to help her mom. She put apples, carrots, and cheese in the cart. "Can we get cookies, too?" Anna asked. "Maybe later, sweetie. We have to get some bread and milk first," her mom said. They walked to the other side of the store. Anna saw a big display of balloons. They were red, blue, yellow, and green. They looked so pretty and fun. Anna wanted a balloon. "Mom, can I have a balloon?" Anna asked. "Sure, honey. You can pick one," her mom said. Anna ran to the balloons. She grabbed a red one. It had a string attached to it. She pulled the string and the balloon flew up in the air. Anna laughed. She pulled the string again and the balloon came down. She did it over and over. She spun around with the balloon. She felt happy. But then she felt dizzy. She stopped spinning. She felt sick. She let go of the string. The balloon flew away. "Mom, I don't feel good," Anna said. Her mom came to her. She saw the balloon floating away. She saw Anna's pale face. She hugged her. "I'm sorry, baby. You spun too much. You need to sit down and rest," her mom said. She took Anna to a bench. She gave her some water. She rubbed her back. "It's okay, Anna. You'll feel better soon. I love you," her mom said. Anna nodded. She felt sorry for losing the balloon. She felt sorry for being dizzy. She loved her mom. She closed her eyes. She hoped to feel better soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat oatmeal every morning for breakfast because it made her strong. One day, Lily's friend Timmy came over to play. Timmy wanted to eat oatmeal too, but Lily didn't want to share. She didn't accept that Timmy wanted some oatmeal too. Later that day, Lily's mom made some cookies. She told Lily that she could have one cookie, but she wanted more. Lily didn't accept that she could only have one cookie. She took more cookies when her mom wasn't looking. But then, Lily got a tummy ache from eating too many cookies. She realized that it's not good to be greedy and not share. She learned that it's important to accept when you can't have everything you want.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She lived in a nice house and she was very fair. One day, the little girl found a magic mirror. She picked it up and it offered her a special gift. The magic mirror said, "If you look into me every morning, I will make you even fairer." The little girl was very excited. So every morning, the girl looked into the magic mirror. She said hello to the mirror and it always answered with a smile. Every day the little girl grew fairer and fairer. She was the happiest little girl in the world. She was so fair that everyone was amazed. The little girl thanked her magic mirror. The mirror smiled and said, "It's been nice to help you. Now be sure to keep looking in me every morning." And so the little girl kept looking in her magic mirror every morning. And she stayed fair and happy ever after.

Molly and her family were having a lot of fun on their holiday. Her mum and dad were always smiling and Molly really liked that. They were playing in the park, looking at the trees and playing tag. Molly was very calm when she was playing. She was happy and was smiling a lot. She called out to her mum and dad, "Let's go down to the beach!" Molly's mum and dad smiled at each other and said "Sure thing." They all packed up and went to the beach. When they got there, Molly had big fun. She went swimming, dug in the sand and made sandcastles. Her dad and mum also had fun, playing with Molly and laughing. At the end of the holiday, Molly was very happy. She had had a lot of fun, and that made her smile. Her mum and dad smiled too, and they all enjoyed the calm and peaceful atmosphere.

Tom and Sue are twins. They share a room and a crib. They like to play with their toys and books. But when it is night, they have to go to sleep. One night, Tom does not want to sleep. He wants to stay up and read his book. He says to Sue, "Sue, let us sack the crib. We can make a tent with the blanket. Then we can read under the light." Sue thinks this is a fun idea. She says, "OK, Tom, let us sack the crib. But we have to be quiet. Mom and Dad will be mad if they hear us." They sack the crib. They pull the blanket over the bars. They crawl under the blanket. They turn on the light. They read their book. But they do not hear Mom and Dad coming. Mom and Dad open the door. They see the tent. They see the light. They are not happy. They say, "Tom and Sue, what are you doing? You should be sleeping. It is late. You have to go to school tomorrow. Sack the crib right now. Turn off the light. Go to sleep." Tom and Sue are scared. They say, "Sorry, Mom and Dad. We just wanted to read. We will sack the crib. We will turn off the light. We will go to sleep." They sack the crib. They turn off the light. They go to sleep. They dream of books and tents.

Once upon a time, there were two friends: Petey and Libby. Libby was always very fit, she loved to run and play and stay active. Petey on the other hand was very lazy, he loved lying around and eating all sorts of foods. One day Libby and Petey were having lunch together. Libby had a big bowl of delicious, healthy vegetables and Petey had a large plate of pasta. Libby said to Petey, "That looks really yummy, but if you eat too much pasta you won't grow fit like me!" Petey thought about this. He knew Libby was right. So the next day, and every day after, he ate a healthy balanced diet and got fit with Libby by doing lots of exercise. The moral of the story is: Eating a healthy, balanced diet, will help you grow fit!

Once upon a time there was a naughty musician. He liked to eat a lot of food. Every day, the musician would eat yummy snacks and delicious treats. One day, he went to get some chocolate cake. He was so naughty that he ate too much and it made him sick. He was not happy. He ran to the park and saw a big tree. He sat down and thought about what he had done. He knew he shouldn't have eaten so much chocolate cake. Then he saw a bird eating a juicy worm. The musician smiled and decided to be a little more careful with his food. He vowed to eat just enough and not too much. From that day on, the musician was more careful with the food he ate. He was still naughty but he was careful not to eat too much. The end.

Bunny was a little rabbit who loved to hop around the meadow. He liked to explore new places and meet new friends. One day, he saw a big pond with shiny water and green plants. He wanted to hop closer and see what was inside. But Frog, who lived in the pond, did not like strangers. He saw Bunny hopping near his home and croaked loudly. "Who are you and what do you want?" he asked in a grumpy voice. Bunny was scared and anxious. He did not know how to answer Frog's question. He thought Frog might be angry or mean. He wanted to hop away, but he also wanted to be polite. He said in a small voice, "I am Bunny and I just want to look at the pond. It is very pretty." Frog was surprised by Bunny's answer. He realized that Bunny was not a threat, but a curious and friendly visitor. He felt sorry for being rude and decided to be nice. He said in a softer voice, "I am Frog and this is my home. You can look at the pond, but be careful not to fall in. The water is deep and cold." Bunny was relieved and happy. He thanked Frog and hopped closer to the pond. He saw fish and ducks and water lilies. He asked Frog many questions and learned a lot. Frog answered patiently and shared his knowledge. They became friends and had fun. The moral of the story is: Don't judge someone by their appearance or voice. Be kind and respectful to others and you might make a new friend.

Once upon a time, two friends, Tom and Ben, were planning an outing to the opera that evening. Tom was very excited to go and was hopeful to see all the wonderful things the opera had to offer. Ben wasn't as optimistic as Tom. He said to Tom, "We don't have enough money for the opera. How can we see the show?" Tom replied, "Don't worry, I have an idea. I hope we can get into the opera. I have a friend who works there. She is a generous person, I'm sure she will help us." So, Tom and Ben walked over to the opera. When they arrived, they knocked on the door. To their surprise, the door opened and it was Tom' friend. She smiled and said, "Oh, you two wanted to go to the opera. Come in, I think I can help you." Tom and Ben were very happy to have been welcomed into the opera. Little did they know, it was about to be one of the most incredible nights of their lives!

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the backyard. They have a big tent that their dad made for them. They pretend it is a castle or a spaceship or a cave. One day, they see a new family move in next door. They have a little girl named Lily. She is shy and does not talk much. Sara and Ben want to be her friends. They go to the fence and say hello. Lily looks at them and smiles. She sees their tent and says, "Wow, that is a nice tent. I wish I had one." Sara and Ben are happy. They say, "Thank you. We like our tent. Do you want to play with us? You can come inside and see our toys." Lily nods and follows them. They show her their dolls, cars, books and puzzles. They play together and have fun. Lily is playful and laughs a lot. She likes Sara and Ben. Sara and Ben admire Lily. They think she is smart and kind. They ask her, "Do you want to be our friend?" Lily says, "Yes, I do. You are very nice. Can I come back tomorrow?" Sara and Ben say, "Of course. We are glad you are our neighbor. We can play every day." They hug and say goodbye. They go back to their houses. They are happy. They have a new friend.

Once upon a time, in a big lake, there was a brown kayak. The brown kayak liked to roll in the water all day long. It was very happy when it could roll and splash in the lake. One day, a little boy named Tim came to play with the brown kayak. Tim and the brown kayak rolled in the water together. They laughed and had a lot of fun. The sun was shining, and the water was warm. After a while, it was time for Tim to go home. He said goodbye to the brown kayak and gave it a big hug. The brown kayak was sad to see Tim go, but it knew they would play together again soon. So, the brown kayak kept rolling in the water, waiting for the next fun day with Tim.

Here is one possible story, but there are many other ways to write it. Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big maze made of tall plants. They wanted to play in the maze. Mom said, "Be careful, don't get lost. I will wait for you here." Ben and Lily ran into the maze. They had fun finding new paths and hiding from each other. But soon they realized they did not know how to get out. They started to feel scared and sad. They called for mom, but she did not hear them. They saw a sign that said, "Exit this way." They followed the sign, hoping to see mom. But the sign was a trick. It led them to a dead end. There was a camera and a speaker. A voice said, "Ha ha, you fell for it. This is a modern maze. It is a prank. You are on TV. Everyone can see how silly you are." Ben and Lily felt very embarrassed. They wanted to cry. They wished they never went into the maze. They wished they stayed with mom. They did not like the modern maze. They did not like the prank. They did not like the voice. They did not like the TV. They did not like anything.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jay who was very shy. Every day he would go to the park and play by himself. One day, while he was playing he heard a giant roar. He was so scared he ran to hide behind a big tree. He peeked around the tree and saw a giant. The giant had bright blue eyes, and he was smiling at Jay. Jay was still a bit scared, but he bravely walked over to the giant and said, "Hello!" The giant said, "Hi! My name is Sam. It's nice to meet you!" Jay smiled back and said, "My name is Jay. It's nice to meet you too!" The giant and Jay became good friends after that. They would always meet at the park to play games and talk. Jay was no longer shy and he had made a new best friend.

Once there was a little girl who loved pink. All of her favourite clothes were pink and she loved to play with pink toys. One day, her mom took her to the ice cream shop. The little girl was so excited when she saw the different flavours of ice cream in the shop. She immediately chose the pink ice cream. The ice cream was so tasty and the little girl enjoyed eating it very much. She ate a big scoop. Then she had another scoop and enjoyed it even more. The little girl loved pink ice cream and she asked her mom if she could have it again tomorrow. Her mom said yes, and the little girl couldn't wait!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she found a caterpillar on a leaf. The caterpillar was very friendly and Lily liked him a lot. She decided to keep him as her pet. Every day, Lily would visit her caterpillar friend and give him leaves to eat. One day, Lily forgot to visit her friend. She felt sad and worried that he might be hungry. She told her mommy, "I remember my caterpillar friend. I need to go see him!" Lily ran outside and found her caterpillar friend. He was happy to see her and they played together. From that day on, Lily always remembered to visit her friendly caterpillar friend.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Bella and Anna. They were always together and they adored each other. One night, Anna suggested they go to the opera. She had never been before and she was very excited. But Bella was fearful. She had never heard of the opera before and didn't know what to expect. Anna could see Bella was worried and offered to explain what the opera was. She said that it was a place of beauty and happiness, where special performers sang and danced on the stage. With Anna's explanation, Bella's fears vanished. She agreed to go. When Anna and Bella arrived at the opera, they were both amazed. The performers were extraordinary and the music was magical. They clapped along throughout the entire show. When the opera had finished, Bella thanked Anna for taking her. She knew she wouldn't have gone if Anna hadn't offered to explain. The two of them had a wonderful time at the opera and the memory would stay with them forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who liked to cook. She wanted to make something special for her friend who she knew was deaf. The little girl took some butter from the fridge and put it into a frying pan. She turned on the stove and waited for the butter to melt. When the butter was melted, the little girl took a spoon and started to stir the butter around in the pan. She smiled when she smelled the delicious smell of butter cooking. Suddenly, her friend came into the kitchen. The little girl was excited to show her friend what she was cooking. She pointed to the pan and signalled to her friend, "I'm cooking some butter!" Her friend clapped her hands and smiled. She signalled back, "It smells yummy!" The little girl grinned. She already knew it was going to be a delicious meal for her deaf friend!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the grass and watch the bugs. One day, she found a cricket who was stuck in a puddle of water. Lily knew she had to save the cricket, so she carefully picked it up and put it on a leaf. The cricket was so happy to be saved by Lily. It started to sing a beautiful song to show its gratitude. Lily's little brother, Max, saw how happy the cricket was and became envious. He wanted to save a bug too! So, Lily and Max went on a bug-saving adventure together. They found a ladybug and a butterfly who needed their help. At the end of the day, Lily and Max felt proud of themselves for being such good helpers to the bugs. They went to bed with happy hearts, dreaming of all the bugs they would save tomorrow. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max had a big paw and loved to play all day. One day, Max's friend Lily came to play with him. "Hi Max, are you ready to play?" asked Lily. "Yes, I am!" replied Max. They decided to play catch with a ball. Max ran to catch the ball but it was too high for him to reach. "I can't catch it, it's too high!" said Max. Lily said, "Don't worry Max, I can lift you up so you can catch it." So, Lily lifted Max up and he caught the ball with his big paw. Max was so happy that he gave Lily a big lick on her face. Lily laughed and said, "You are such a good dog, Max!" They continued to play catch until the sun went down. Max was tired but happy because he had so much fun with his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved music and always wanted to play the flute. One day, her mommy bought her a flute and she was so happy. Lily tried to play it, but it didn't sound good. She asked her mommy why it didn't sound like the music she heard. Her mommy said, "You have to examine the flute and see if everything is okay." Lily looked at the flute and found out that one of the holes was covered. She fixed it and tried to play again. This time, it sounded beautiful! She was so successful in playing the flute. The moral of the story is that if you want to do something, you have to examine everything to make sure it's right. If you do that, you can be successful in anything you want to do.

Molly the puppy was outside playing in the sun. She was running around and having lots of fun. Suddenly, she stopped and sniffed the air. She saw a pink bench and she wanted to go there. Molly ran up to the bench, and sat down. She looked around to see what she could find. She saw something tucked away, and she started to bark. "What have we here?" said Molly. She put her paw out, and said, "I'm going to open it!" She reached forward and opened up the thing. Inside, there was a big pile of balloons. Molly was so excited she jumped up and down. "Oh wow!" said Molly, "These balloons are so pink!" She grabbed one in her mouth and started to run around. Molly had so much fun playing with her new balloons. And she never forgot the special day she found them on the pink bench!

Once upon a time in a world far, far away, there was an ugly creature. This creature did not fit in anywhere and was always alone. It was very sad and had no friends. One day, the creature got an idea. It decided to create its own world! So the creature grabbed some rocks, mud and plants and began to make its own world. Slowly but surely, its world began to take shape. The creature created lakes and rivers, hills and valleys, forests and fields. It made the world just the way it wanted. When the creature was finally finished, it looked around and smiled. It had created a wonderful world! Now it was time to find some friends. So the creature invited some animals and birds to come and explore its beautiful new world. The creature had made a world that was bright and colourful! It was no longer ugly or alone. It was happy, and so were its new friends. They all lived happily ever after in their beautiful world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and sing songs. One day, she found a beautiful flute in her toy box. It was shiny and sparkly and made a pretty sound when she blew into it. Lily's mommy came into her room and saw her playing the flute. "Oh, Lily, that's an adorable flute! Can you play a song for me?" she asked. Lily tried to play a song, but she wasn't very good at it yet. "I don't know how to play," she told her mommy. "That's okay, sweetie," her mommy said. "I can teach you. Just keep practicing and you'll get better." Lily was happy that her mommy could tell her how to play the flute. She practiced every day and soon became very good at it. She would play for her mommy and daddy, and they would always tell her how proud they were of her. And that's how Lily learned to play the adorable flute. The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy named John. He was only three years old but he was very smart. Every day he dreamed of doing incredible work. One day, his parents said they had a surprise for him. They told John to close his eyes and then they took him outside. When John opened his eyes he saw an incredible, shiny new bike. He was so happy that he shouted with joy! He thanked his parents for the amazing gift. John quickly learned how to ride his new bike. He liked to race his friends and ride to the park. Everywhere he went, people kept saying his name and saying how fast he was. John was very proud of his work. He had learned to ride an incredible bike and everyone loved watching him! He was happiest when he was on his bike, feeling the wind against his face, and knowing that he was doing something incredible.

Once upon a time there was a silly angle. He was so silly that he thought it would be fun to try and prevent the sun! He was silly enough to think up this stupid idea. One day he started to build a giant triangle around the sun. He used rocks and trees and sticks to make it. But it was too tall and too wide. There was no way it could fit around the sun. But the silly angle kept trying. He worked and worked. But every time he finished a side of the triangle, the sun would move and he would have to start over. So much for his stupid plan! Then, one day a wise old man came along. He saw what the silly angle was trying to do. He told the silly angel that he couldn't prevent the sun, no matter how hard he tried. So, the silly angle finally gave up and the sun was safe. From then on, he learnt that some things are impossible and he stopped trying to do stupid things. The end.

Anna and Ben were bored. They had no toys to play with. Mom was busy with laundry. She had a big basket of clothes. She said, "Do not touch the laundry. It is clean and I need to fold it." But Anna and Ben did not listen. They saw the laundry as fun. They took some clothes out of the basket. They put them on their heads and bodies. They pretended to be animals and monsters. They made loud noises and ran around the house. Mom heard the noises and came to see. She was not happy. She saw the laundry on the floor and on the kids. She said, "What are you doing? You made a mess. You need to put the laundry back in the basket. Now!" Anna and Ben felt sorry. They did not want to make Mom angry. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were just playing. We wanted to decorate ourselves with the laundry. We thought it was fun." Mom sighed. She said, "I know you were just playing. But laundry is not for decorating. It is for wearing and keeping warm. You can decorate with other things, like stickers or crayons. But you need to ask me first. And you need to clean up after yourself. OK?" Anna and Ben nodded. They said, "OK, Mom. We will do that. We will help you with the laundry. We will put it back in the basket. And we will say sorry to the clothes. They are small and soft. They do not like to be on the floor." Mom smiled. She said, "Thank you, Anna and Ben. You are good kids. I love you. Now, let's finish the laundry and then we can have a snack. How does that sound?" Anna and Ben smiled too. They said, "That sounds good, Mom. We love you too. And we love the laundry. But only when it is in the basket or on us."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play dress-up. One day, she put on her pirate hat and her high boots and went to the park to play. There, she met a boy named Jack who was also dressed like a pirate. "Ahoy matey!" said Lily. "What's your name?" "My name is Jack," said the boy. "What's yours?" "My name is Lily," she replied with a frown. "Why do you have a bigger pirate hat than me?" Jack smiled and said, "Because I'm the captain of the ship!" Lily giggled and they played together all day long, pretending to sail the high seas and search for treasure. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to tell jokes to his friends. One day, Timmy told his best friend Billy a joke. Billy laughed so hard that he fell to the ground. Later that day, Timmy and Billy were playing hide-and-seek. Timmy found a really good hiding spot and whispered to himself, "Billy will never find me here." But Billy searched high and low and eventually found Timmy. As they were walking home, Timmy's shoelaces were too tight and hurting his feet. He asked Billy to help him untie them, but Billy was too busy laughing about Timmy's joke from earlier. Suddenly, Timmy tripped on his shoelaces and fell down. He hurt his head and had to go to the hospital. Timmy learned that it's important to take care of himself and not rely on others for help.

Once upon a time, there was a helpless crab who wanted to swim in the sea. She looked around and couldn't find a way to get to the water. Suddenly, she heard a voice. "Come here, little crab. I can help you," said the voice. The crab looked around and saw a beautiful white duck. "Jump on my back and we'll swim to the sea together," said the duck. The crab was so happy and jumped on the duck's back. Together, they swam off to the sea. The crab laughed as she watched the waves and felt the warm sun on her back. She knew she was safe and that the duck would look after her. The duck and the crab swam for hours until they reached the shore. The crab thanked the duck and hopped back onto the sand. From then on, the crab would always look back fondly on the day she had taken a ride on the beautiful duck's back and gone swimming in the sea.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big hole in the ground. They want to know what is inside. "Let's crawl in the hole," Tom says. "Maybe we can find something fun." "OK," Lily says. "But be careful. The hole looks deep." They crawl in the hole. It is dark and cold. They use their hands to feel the walls. They find some rocks and sticks. They also hear some noises. "What is that?" Lily asks. "It sounds scary." "I don't know," Tom says. "Maybe it is a monster. Or a snake. Or a spider." They are afraid. They want to go back. But they do not know how. They have crawled too far. They cannot see the light. "Help!" they shout. "Help us!" Their mom hears them. She is looking for them. She sees the hole. She runs to it. She calls their names. "Lily! Tom! Where are you?" "Mom!" they answer. "We are here! In the hole! Please get us out!" Mom sees their faces. They are dirty and scared. She reaches for them. She pulls them out. She hugs them. "Are you OK?" she asks. "What were you doing in the hole?" "We were curious," Tom says. "We wanted to explore." "But it was too deep," Lily says. "We got lost." Mom is not angry. She is glad they are safe. She tells them to be more careful next time. She helps them clean up. She gives them a snack. She tells them a story. They are happy. They love their mom.

Once upon a time, there were two sisters. They loved to play together, but sometimes they would quarrel. One day, they found a shiny mineral in the garden. They both wanted to keep it, but they couldn't decide who should have it. The older sister said, "I found it first, so it's mine!" But the younger sister said, "I want it too, it's so pretty!" They started to argue and shout at each other. Suddenly, a gust of cold wind blew and they both shivered. They realized that their quarrel was not worth it. They decided to share the mineral and play together nicely. The moral of the story is that sharing is better than fighting. It's important to be kind to each other and not let small things cause big problems.

Once upon a time, there was a very glad girl. She had a special hoop. Every day, she would take her hoop outside in her yard to play. She would keep throwing the hoop as far as she could, then she would chase it and throw it again. The girl kept playing with her hoop, she was so glad that it never seemed to get boring. One day, the girl's hoop rolled further than she had ever seen it go before. She was surprised and looked around for it. She couldn't see it anywhere! She was so sad because she wanted to keep playing with her hoop. The girl walked far and wide all around the neighbourhood, looking for her hoop. Finally, she reached a park. As she passed by a slide, she spotted her hoop on the grass nearby. She was so glad to see it again. The girl picked up her hoop and ran back home. After that, she always kept the hoop near her so she wouldn't lose it again. Every day, she would take it back outside and play with it. She was so glad she'd found her hoop, and she kept playing with it forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she asked her mom if she could plant some flowers in the soil. Her mom said yes and gave her some seeds to plant. Lily dug some holes in the soil and put the seeds inside. She watered them every day and waited patiently for them to grow. One day, she noticed that some of the flowers were missing. She asked her mom if she knew what happened to them. Her mom said, "I don't know, Lily. Did you see anyone near the flowers?" Lily thought for a moment and remembered that her little brother had been playing near the flowers. She went to ask him if he had done anything to the flowers. He looked guilty and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I picked some of the flowers because they looked pretty." Lily forgave her brother and they both learned an important lesson about taking care of things that belong to others. From then on, they worked together to take care of the rest of the flowers in the garden.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anna. Anna wanted to go outside and play but her mom wouldn't allow it. Anna was sad and asked, "Why can't I play?" "Because it's too dangerous," said Mom. "There's a big hole in the ground that's not safe." Anna was feeling very impatient. She wanted to go out and swing on the swing. She asked her mom again, "Can I please go outside and play?" Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you may. But first you need to promise to stay away from the big hole in the ground. Can you do that?" Anna smiled and said, "Yes, I promise!" So Mom allowed Anna to go play outside. Anna was so happy that she ran to the swing and started swinging higher and higher!

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Lily. She loved to draw and design things with her crayons. One day, she wanted to draw a picture of a car, but she didn't have any oil pastels. Her mom gave her some oil pastels and Lily was very happy. Lily started to draw a small car with her oil pastels. She made the car look very pretty with lots of colors. She was very proud of her design. When she finished, she showed her picture to her mom and dad. They both loved it and said it was very beautiful. From that day on, Lily always used oil pastels when she wanted to design something. She loved how the colors looked on paper. And every time she used them, she remembered the day she drew her small car with the oil pastels.

Once upon a time, there was an adventurous copper. He was always curious and wanted to explore places he hadn't been before. One day, he decided to make a special journey. He packed up his things and set off towards the mountains. When he arrived, he saw the beautiful snow-capped peaks. He felt so excited! He wandered around the mountain, admiring its beauty. Suddenly, he heard a voice. "What are you doing here?," it asked. He looked around to see where the voice was coming from and that's when he saw a group of foxes. The foxes were looking at him curiously. He told them he was on an adventure. The foxes were fascinated to hear this. They asked if he would help them make a special den in the mountain. The copper agreed. After a few hours of hard work, they had made an amazing den for the foxes. The grateful foxes thanked the copper for his help. He smiled and waved goodbye, ready for his next big adventure.

Once upon a time there was a nice potato. He wanted to find a place to belong. He looked everywhere but he couldn't find the right place. He felt so lonely and sad. One day he found a nice garden. In the garden there were other potatoes just like him. He knew this was the right place for him. The other potatoes were so happy to see him. They all said "Welcome! You belong here with us!" The nice potato finally found his place to belong. He was so happy to be with other potatoes like him. He enjoyed his new home in the garden and was so happy he finally found a place where he belonged.

Alice was an ordinary orange cat. Every day, she would go on walks in the park and explore. She was very content with her life, but one day, everything changed. Alice noticed a strange man walking around the park, and he seemed to be watching her carefully. She knew something was wrong and wanted to get away from him. But, he found her and began to follow her. Alice was scared and angry. She ran as fast as she could, but the man was too fast and he finally caught her. He put her in a cage and she was helpless. Alice tried to escape, but the cage was too strong. She felt sad and scared. No one came to her rescue and she started to give up hope. Alice was stuck in the cage, and she was never seen or heard from again. She had to spend the rest of her days in the cage, all because her ordinary life had changed.

Once upon a time, there was a bird who was looking for a place to call home. He looked everywhere, but nothing seemed to be just right. One day, he saw a nest in a tall tree. The bird flew up to it and said, "I like this nest! Can I become its family?" The nest replied, "Yes, of course! You can be my family!" So, the bird moved into the nest. He was so happy to have a home at last! But after a while, the bird began to get bored living in the nest. He knew he needed more adventure and excitement in his life. So, he decided to fly away and explore the world. The bird said goodbye to the nest and flew off. He never forgot how nice his nest had been. He was grateful to have found a home, even if it had become a bit boring.

Once there was a girl, who was very compassionate. She was always giving hugs and helping people who were in need. One day she was walking and saw a notebook on the ground. She stopped, picked up the notebook and decided to attach it to her bag. When she arrived home the girl showed the notebook to her mother. The mother said, "Why did you attach this notebook?" The girl smiled and said, "Because I wanted to help someone who may have lost it." The mother smiled and hugged her daughter. "That was very compassionate of you. I am so proud of you." The girl beamed and hugged her mother back. She was very happy that she did something to help someone in need. She was sure that someone would be very thankful for the kindness she had shown.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a hole in it. "Look, a cave!" Lily said. "Let's go inside!" Tom was scared. He did not like dark places. "No, it is too dark and cold. There might be bad things inside. Let's play somewhere else." He said. Lily was brave. She wanted to see what was in the cave. "Don't be scared, Tom. It will be fun. Maybe we will find treasure or animals or fairies. Come on, follow me!" She said. She ran to the cave and went inside. Tom did not want to be alone. He did not want to make Lily sad. He followed her to the cave. He held her hand. They walked inside. It was dark and cold. They could not see much. They heard strange noises. They felt scared. "Hello, who are you?" A voice said. Tom and Lily stopped. They saw a blue light. It was a blue bird. It was sitting on a nest. It had shiny feathers and a long tail. It looked nice. "Hello, we are Tom and Lily. We are playing in the park. We saw your cave and wanted to see what was inside. We are sorry if we bothered you." Lily said. The blue bird smiled. "You are not bothering me. You are welcome to my cave. I am Bluey. I live here with my eggs. They will hatch soon. Do you want to see them?" It said. Tom and Lily nodded. They were curious. They walked to the nest. They saw four blue eggs. They were pretty. They felt warm. "Wow, they are beautiful. When will they hatch?" Tom asked. "Soon, very soon. They will be like me. They will fly and sing and shine. They will be my friends. You can be my friends too. Do you want to stay and play with me?" Bluey asked. Tom and Lily looked at each other. They smiled. They liked Bluey. They wanted to stay and play with him. They nodded. "Yes, we want to stay and play with you. You are very nice. You have a nice cave. Can we see more of it?" Lily asked. Bluey clapped his wings. He was happy. He had new friends. He nodded. "Yes, you can see more of it. There are many things to see and do. Come, follow me. I will show you. But be careful. Do not touch anything. Some things are sharp or hot or break. Yield to me. I know the way." He said. Tom and Lily followed Bluey. They saw more of the cave. They saw rocks and crystals and water and fire. They saw colors and shapes and shadows and light. They saw more animals and plants and bugs and things. They played and learned and laughed and talked. They had fun. They were happy. They liked the cave. They liked Bluey. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a happy mine. Inside the mine were lots of treasure. Every day, the mine held something special. One day, a little girl found the mine. She was so happy. She held out her hands and started to fill them with the treasure. The girl felt so lucky! She ran back home and showed her mom what she had found. Her mom was so pleased. She smiled and said, "This is your special mine. You can keep all the treasure for yourself." The little girl was so excited! From that day, the mine was the little girl's special place. Whenever she wanted, she went back to the mine. She held the treasure close and was happy.

Once upon a time there lived an ancient rat. The rat wanted to study so he went looking for a teacher. He met a friendly cat and asked "Will you teach me?" The cat smiled and said "Yes, I'd be happy to teach you." The rat was so excited. He said "Thank you! Will you teach me lots?" The cat answered "Yes, I'll teach you lots." Together the cat and rat studied every day. They read books and played games. The rat learned so much and was so happy. One day the cat said to the rat "You have learned so much. You are now ready to go and share all that you have learned with the world." The rat smiled and said "Thank you for everything! I will always remember my teacher." The rat waved goodbye with a smile and left to share his knowledge with the world.

Once there was a little girl. She was very happy. She had a good swing in her garden. She loved to play on it. Every day she would cover herself with a blanket and swing as high as she could. One day, a strong wind blew and made her swing go higher and higher. She went so high that she could see past the trees in her garden. She kept going until she could see the sun in the sky. She was so happy and shouted, "Look at me! I'm so high!" When she had had enough, the little girl came back down to the ground. She used the blanket to cover herself up and snuggled in for a good nap. She had a big smile on her face as she dreamt of all the fun she had had on her swing.

Lily was very excited, because today she was going for a drive. She had never been in a car before and she couldn't wait to see what it was like. Lily's mom helped her into the car. She fastened the seatbelt around Lily and then she got in the driver's seat. Lily watched out the window as they drove. She saw lots of nice things. They drove past a park, with lots of flowers and trees. They drove over a bridge and saw boats floating in the river. Lily waved hi to all the people. Finally, Lily's mom pulled up in front of a big house. Lily smiled when she saw it; it was so nice! Lily's mom helped her out of the car and they went inside together. Lily had had the best time on her drive. She couldn't wait to go on another one soon!

Sophie went to the beach with her mom and dad. She was so excited to go for a swim. She put on her pink swimming suit and hopped into the water. She loved feeling the warm water on her skin. Sophie's mom dove in the water. She showed Sophie amazing swimming tricks. Sophie wanted to show off too, so she took a deep breath and dove under the water. She looked around and saw all kinds of fish and shells. It was so impressive! Sophie wanted to take something home, so she reached for a pretty shell. But when she got closer, she noticed it wasn't a shell, it was a note! She was so excited! She quickly grabbed it and placed it in her pocket. When they got home, Sophie showed her mom the note. It turned out it was a treasure map! They both jumped up and down, they were thrilled and couldn't wait to go on an adventure and find the treasure!

Once upon a time there was a really clean gun owned by a little boy named Mike. He would take great care of his gun and kept it shining everyday. Mike was very excited about his gun and showed it to all his friends. One day, Mike was over the moon because he had been to a gun show. He had seen so many different kinds of guns and that made him even more excited about his own gun. That evening, Mike asked his Dad, "Can I go out and show my gun to my friends?" His Dad replied, "No, of course not. That's too dangerous!" Mike was a bit disappointed but he understood. He knew his Dad was right. So he kept his gun nice and clean, and only showed it off to his friends in his bedroom. He was still very excited about his gun and wanted to show it off.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big jar of butter, but it was so heavy that she couldn't carry it. So, she asked her mommy to help her. Her mommy said, "Let's pull the jar together!" So, they both pulled the jar and carried it to the kitchen. But when they opened the jar, they saw that the butter was very ugly. It had turned brown and smelled bad. Lily's mommy said, "This butter is not good anymore. We can't eat it." So, they threw the ugly butter away and went to the store to buy some fresh butter. Lily was sad that she had wasted the butter, but her mommy told her that it was okay. They had tried their best to save it, but sometimes things just don't work out. And now they had learned to be more careful with their food.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to visit her grandma's house. One day, Lily's mom packed a lovely sandwich for her to eat on the way. When Lily arrived at her grandma's house, she showed her the sandwich. "That looks yummy!" said grandma. "Would you like to share it with me?" Lily thought about it for a moment and then said, "Yes, grandma. Sharing is caring." From that day on, Lily learned that sharing is important and it makes people happy. She continued to visit her grandma and share her lovely sandwiches with her.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who really wanted to eat an avocado. He asked his mom if he could bathe in it. His mom laughed and said, "No silly! You cannot bathe in an avocado!" The little boy was not happy, so he went and found a pink avocado. He thought if he could just bathe in it, he would feel better. When he touched it, it felt different than all the other avocados. The little boy jumped into the pink avocado and immediately began to feel sick. He became very sick, and he never got to eat his avocado. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, black dog named Max. Max loved to play outside in the yard with his ball. One day, Max's ball rolled under the fence and into the neighbor's yard. Max wanted to get his ball back, but he knew he wasn't supposed to go into the neighbor's yard. Max's owner, a little girl named Lily, urged him to come back inside the house. But Max couldn't stop thinking about his ball. He wanted it back so badly. Lily knew Max was upset, so she decided to help him. She found an old iron rod and used it to push the ball back under the fence. Max was so happy to have his ball back! He wagged his tail and licked Lily's face to show his gratitude. From then on, Max never went near the neighbor's yard again. He was just happy to have his ball and his best friend, Lily.
