Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy box that was very full. One day, her mom came in and said, "Lily, it's time to clean up your toys." Lily didn't want to clean up because she loved all of her toys. But her mom said, "You can't keep them all, it's too expensive." Lily started to cry because she didn't want to get rid of any of her toys. But then her mom said, "Let's open the toy box and see what we can give away. We can give away just an inch of toys." Lily thought about it and agreed. They opened the toy box and Lily saw that she had so many toys that she didn't even play with anymore. She picked out just an inch of toys to give away to kids who didn't have any toys. When they were done, Lily felt happy because she knew she was helping others. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's important to share with others, even if it's just an inch of what we have."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing dress-up and pretending to be different people. One day, she wanted to be a firefighter, but she didn't have a uniform. Lily went to her friend Max's house and asked if she could borrow his firefighter uniform. Max was happy to help and gave her the uniform. As Lily was walking home, she saw a big, scary dog. She was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, a real firefighter came to her rescue and scared the dog away. "Thank you for scaring the dog away," Lily said to the firefighter. "You're welcome," he replied. "And that's a nice uniform you have there. Are you a firefighter too?" Lily smiled and said, "No, I just borrowed it from my friend Max." The firefighter laughed and said, "Well, you make a great pretend firefighter." Lily was happy and felt proud of her borrowed uniform.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy cart. He would push it around the house and fill it with his favorite toys. One day, Tim saw his friend, Sam, playing with a big, shiny new cart. Tim felt envious of Sam's cart. He wanted one just like it. Tim's face showed a frown because he was sad. Tim's mom saw his frown and asked him what was wrong. Tim told her about Sam's cart. His mom said, "It's okay to feel envious, but remember to be happy with what you have." Tim thought about it and smiled. He played with his cart, happy that he had a toy he loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the water. One day, she went to the beach with her mom and dad. They played in the water and had a lot of fun. After a while, Lily's dad said, "Lily, do you want to learn how to swim?" Lily was a little scared, but she said, "Yes, please!" So, her dad taught her how to swim. At first, Lily was nervous, but she soon learned how to move her arms and legs. After she learned how to swim, Lily felt calm and happy. She loved being in the water and couldn't wait to go back to the beach again.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny who loved to hop. He hopped all around his backyard, looking for something fun to do. One day, he spied a bright, shiny package in the grass. He hopped over to the package and saw that it was a pale green. The bunny was curious and wanted to know what was inside the package. He tapped his rabbit friends on the shoulder and said, "Hey! Let's hop to the package and open it!" His friends were excited, and so the bunnies hopped over together. When they reached the package, they pulled open the ribbon and pulled out the contents. It was a pile of vegetables! All the bunnies were overjoyed. The bunnies happily hopped back to their burrow, each carrying a carrot or a cabbage. They enjoyed their treat, happily hopping around until bedtime.

Once there was a girl who was three years old. She was scared of the dark, but she wanted to peek at the big tree in the living room. She crept ever so softly so that no one would hear her. When she reached the tree she looked up and saw a beautiful ornament. It was so shiny and sparkly. She was scared to touch it, but could not resist its beauty. She reached up and grabbed it ever so carefully. The ornament was so light and felt nice in her hands. Suddenly, the lights turned on and the girl got scared. She quickly put back the ornament and ran out of the living room. She was so scared she never tried to peek at the tree again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was only three years old. One day, Sarah found an old original fan lying in the corner of her room. She was so excited that she decided to polish it. She picked up a cloth and began to rub it all over the fan. She felt so proud when it began to shine. Sarah ran over to show her mom the fan. She said, "Mommy look, I polished it all by myself!" But her mother was not happy at all. She said, "No! That fan is not safe for a little girl like you. You should not touch it again." Sarah was very sad. She wanted to keep polishing her fan but she knew she could not disobey her mother. She had to put it away and never touch it again. The end.

One day, there was a team of animals. They were all friends and they loved to play together. One of the animals was a big elephant. He was amazing because he could do tricks with his trunk. One day, the elephant wanted to show his friends how he could lean on one leg. He lifted his other leg up and leaned to the side. His friends were amazed! They had never seen an elephant do that before. The other animals on the team wanted to try leaning too. They all took turns leaning to the side and trying to balance on one leg. It was so much fun! The team of animals had a great day playing and trying new things together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play outside. One day, she found a shiny trophy in the grass. It was thin and had a picture of a soccer ball on it. Lily showed the trophy to her friend, Timmy. "Look what I found!" she said. "It's a trophy!" Timmy looked at the trophy and said, "Wow, that's cool! Where did you find it?" Lily replied, "I found it in the grass over there. Do you think it's special?" Timmy nodded his head and said, "Yes, it's very special. You should keep it safe and show it to your mom and dad." Lily smiled and said, "Okay, I will do that. Thanks, Timmy!" And with that, she ran off to show her parents her new trophy.

Once upon a time, there was a group of friends. They wanted to do something special, so they gathered together to plan. They decided they would have a picnic. It was easy to find food to bring, so each person brought something yummy. When they arrived, they spread out a blanket and set up the food. They ate and talked and laughed together. When it was time to go, they gathered up the blanket and food. It was not hard to do, because everyone worked together. Everyone felt happy and had a good time. The friends promised to gather together again soon. They had made a special wish, and with teamwork, it would be easy to make it come true.

Once upon a time there was a tiny pink boat that moved through a blue harbor. It was so small and fast, it looked like a little toy. The boat sailed both near and far, never stopping for too long. One day, the tiny pink boat had to move away from the harbor. It moved so far away, it couldn't be seen anymore. It was so sad to move, but in the harbor there was no more room for the tiny boat. The sun was bright, and the breeze was warm. The little boat went on and on, never stopping. One day, it arrived in a new harbor. This time it was not alone! There were many boats in the harbor, all different colors and sizes. The tiny pink boat found a spot and stayed. The tiny pink boat moved quietly in the harbor. It was happy to be around new friends, and was never too far out at sea.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Amy. She wanted to go for a walk, so she put on her coat and set out. As she walked through the park, she noticed something peculiar - a chain was lying on the ground. She wanted to find out what it was, so she picked it up and examined it. When she looked closely, she was surprised - it was very heavy. She decided to take it home with her. When Amy got back to her house, she went to the kitchen and placed the chain on the counter. She tugged on it, to see how strong it was, but the chain wouldn't budge. Suddenly, Amy's mom walked in and asked, "What are you doing?" Amy replied, "I found a chain, it's really strong!" Her mom said, "That's great! But, it looks really dirty and I don't know if it's safe. Let's throw it away, it looks disgusting!" Amy agreed, and they both took the chain outside and threw it in the trash can. Later, Amy found a pretty bracelet to take with her on her next walk.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play at the beach. They made sand castles and looked for shells. One day, they saw something unusual in the water. It was big and shiny and had a long tail. "What is that?" Lily asked. "I don't know," Tom said. "Let's go closer and see." They walked to the edge of the water. The thing was still there. It looked like a fish, but it had a face and hair. It smiled at them and waved. "Hello," the thing said. "I am a mermaid. Do you want to play with me?" Lily and Tom were surprised. They had never seen a mermaid before. "Are you nice?" Lily asked. "Yes, I am very nice," the mermaid said. "I like to make friends. You can trust me." "Can we touch you?" Tom asked. "Sure, you can touch me," the mermaid said. "But be gentle. My scales are delicate." Lily and Tom reached out and touched the mermaid. She felt smooth and wet. She giggled and splashed them with her tail. "You are fun," Lily said. "You are too," the mermaid said. "Do you want to see my home? I have a lot of treasures under the water." Lily and Tom looked at each other. They wanted to see the mermaid's home, but they were afraid of going under the water. "Can we breathe under the water?" Lily asked. "No, you can't," the mermaid said. "But I have a magic shell that can help you. If you hold it to your mouth, you can breathe like me." She showed them a shiny shell that had a hole in it. She put it to her mouth and blew a bubble. "See? It's easy," she said. "Do you want to try?" Lily and Tom nodded. They took the shell and put it to their mouths. They blew bubbles and felt air in their lungs. "Wow, this is amazing," Tom said. "Let's go then," the mermaid said. "Follow me." She took their hands and pulled them into the water. They saw colorful fish and coral and seaweed. They followed the mermaid to her home, where she had a lot of pearls and shells and jewels. They played with the mermaid and her treasures for a long time. They had a lot of fun. They were happy they met the mermaid. She was unusual, but she was nice. They trusted her and she trusted them. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there lived a small girl named Rose who loved to study. One day, Rose was studying in the forest, when she heard a loud caw. She looked around and saw a big black raven, who looked like it was trying to get her attention. Rose, curious, made friends with the raven and they spent the day flying and playing together. But then, the raven started to act strange. Instead of cawing, it was trying to talk in human words! Rose soon found out that the raven was fake. It was run by a machine! The raven had been trying to trick her into telling it secret things about her studies. Rose was angry and so threw the fake raven away. "Ravens are meant to fly, not to spy!" she said crossly. The tiny girl continued on with her studies, and never got tricked again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to play outside. He wanted to go out, but he had to put on his special hat first. "Mommy, can I go out now?" the boy asked. His mother smiled and said, "Yes, but you will have to put on your hat first." The boy smiled and ran to get his hat. He leaned against the wall as he put it on. When the hat was in place, he jumped up and clapped his hands in excitement. "I'm ready! I'm ready to go!" The boy ran outside with a big grin and his hat tilted to the side. He had so much fun playing outside, feeling the sun on his face with his hat keeping him cool. He spent the whole day outside, playing till it was time to go home. When he got home, he leaned against the wall again and took off his hat. He sighed happily, and then placed it somewhere safe for the next day. "Well, that was a fun day," he said, already ready for tomorrow.

Jim was a gifted three year old. He liked performing for his family and friends. One night after his performance, Jim had a terrible nightmare. He dreamt of lions chasing him, which scared him very much. The next day, Jim told his grandma about the nightmare. She comforted him and reminded him that it was only a dream. She explained that even his magical performance wouldn't make it go away. Jim thought hard about this and suddenly knew what to do. He put on extra-special show for his family that night. This time, instead of running away from the lions, he used his magical skills to make the lions bow like he taught them to do. The nightmare vanished and was never seen again. Jim was so relieved, he couldn't help but smile. He was thankful that his magic performance had made his bad dream go away.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived an old monster. He was big and had many colors on his body. The old monster was sad because he had no friends to play with. One sunny day, a little girl named Lily came to the house. She saw the old monster and was not scared. She said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play with me?" The old monster smiled and said, "Yes, I would like that." Lily and the old monster played all day. They ran, jumped, and laughed. Lily taught the old monster how to sign his name. They became best friends and were never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy, who had long, curly hair. She lived in the forest, and she loved exploring. One day, she was in the forest, looking for new places she had never been to. Then, she noticed something strange. In front of her, there was a hole with a big root next to it. The root was very hairy with lots of tiny threads. She wanted to see what was inside the hole, so she bent down and passed it. When she looked inside, her eyes lit up in surprise. There were lots of beautiful sparkly stones inside. She was so amazed that she reached in and picked some of them up. She put them in a pouch that she had around her waist and ran home, excited to show her family her discovery. At the end of the day, Daisy had a big smile on her face. She had made a wonderful discovery in the forest, and now she was richer than ever before! She was very proud of herself and hugged her pouch of sparkly stones tightly. She never forgot her special adventure in the forest and the hairy root that she had passed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a soft teddy bear that she loved very much. One day, Lily accidentally dropped her teddy bear down a well. She wept and wept because she thought she had lost her teddy bear forever. Lily's mom heard her weeping and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her mom that her teddy bear had fallen down the well. Her mom comforted her and said they would figure out a way to get the teddy bear back. Lily's dad came home and they told him what happened. He went to the well and used a long rope to pull the teddy bear out. Lily was so happy and hugged her teddy bear tightly. She thanked her dad and said, "I love you."

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin lived in the big sea with his family. They had a small home near some rocks. One day, Fin saw a big fish and wanted to become big like it. Fin asked his mom, "Mom, how can I become big like that fish?" His mom said, "Fin, you will become big when you grow up. Just eat your food and play with your friends." But Fin didn't want to wait. He swam far away from his home to find a way to become big. He saw a big, dark cave and went inside. In the cave, he found a magic rock that could make him big. Fin touched the rock and said, "I want to become big now!" Suddenly, he became very big. He was happy, but he didn't know that the rock was bad. As he swam back home, he was so big that he broke his family's home by accident. His family was sad and had no place to live. Fin wished he had listened to his mom and waited to become big.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the pool with their toys. One day, they decided to go on a journey under the water. They put on their goggles and held their breath. "Are you ready, Ben?" Lily asked. "Yes, I am, Lily. You are a dependable friend. You will not let go of my hand, right?" Ben said. "Of course not, Ben. I will always hold your hand. Let's dive together!" Lily said. They dived into the water and saw many colorful fish and plants. They felt like they were in a different world. They smiled at each other and waved to the fish. They had so much fun. But soon, they needed to breathe again. They looked up and saw the sun shining through the water. They let go of each other's hand and swam to the surface. They took a big breath and laughed. "That was an amazing journey, Lily. Thank you for diving with me," Ben said. "Thank you, too, Ben. You are a dependable friend. Let's do it again sometime," Lily said. They hugged and splashed each other. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess named Lily. She loved to wear her sparkling jewelry and dance around the castle. One day, she was twirling around and accidentally knocked over a vase. Her mother, the queen, came in and asked, "What happened, Lily?" "I'm sorry, Mama. I was dancing and the vase fell over," Lily said. "It's okay, my dear. Let's clean it up and settle down for some tea," the queen said. Lily gracefully picked up the broken pieces and they sat down for tea. As they sipped their tea, the queen said, "Lily, you are growing up to be such a graceful young lady." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mama. I love you." And they lived happily ever after. The end.

A family was on board a warm yacht. The mother and father were supervising their three-year-old child. They were having a wonderful time, breathing in the fresh sea air and looking at the beautiful scenery. The father asked the child, "Do you remember what we said about being safe on the yacht?" The child nodded, "Yes, Daddy." The mother smiled, "That's right. Now, don't forget." The child looked concerned and asked, "What will happen if I forget?" The father pointed to the side of the yacht, "If you forget, you will fall in the water and you won't be able to get back in. So always remember to stay safe on the yacht." The child nodded and said, "I won't forget. I'll stay safe." The mother and father smiled and hugged the child. They all settled down for a pleasant and warm sail around the bay.

John was an ordinary boy. He went out to play every day. One day, John wanted something special to do. He decided to push his red wagon at night. John went outside late, when it was dark. He got his wagon and pushed it in circles in the yard. He felt so brave! The night was colder than usual and it was darker. He sang to himself as he pushed his wagon. Soon, John got tired. He put his wagon away and went inside. He felt so special, like he had done something extra special. John lay in bed and wondered when he could push his wagon at night again. He giggled and went to sleep with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Joe. He was sad because he had done something wrong. He was so guilty that he decided to run away. He got on a boat and set sail. As Joe sailed away, he shouted to the people in the port, "Goodbye!" But they couldn't hear him, so he just kept on sailing. Days and days went by and Joe thought he was safe. But one day, he heard a loud call coming from the port. It was the people there. They had seen Joe running away and wanted him back. Joe was so scared, but he knew he was guilty and had to go back. He turned the boat around and sailed back to the port. When he got there, the people welcomed him back and told him everyone makes mistakes. Joe was so relieved and he was glad he had decided to go back.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl named Tori. She loved to explore and try new things. One day, Tori went to the park with her mom. While she was running around, she saw a big, shiny medal on the ground. She ran up to it, picked it up and asked her mom, "What is this?" "It looks like a medal," her mom said. Tori smiled and put it in her pocket. That night, Tori and her mom were eating dinner. Tori asked her mom if she could try the medal. Her mom said yes, so Tori put the medal in her mouth. It tasted sweet and salty. Tori's eyes lit up and she exclaimed, "It's so yummy!" Her mom said, "Yes, Tori. That medal is a clear winner!"

Molly was playing in the park when suddenly she heard a bright noise. She looked around and saw a telephone on the ground. She picked it up and said hello. On the other end of the line, a funny voice answered. It was a fairy! The fairy told her that she'd been chosen to go on a special mission to help the animals. Molly was so excited that she said yes right away. The fairy told her that she had to go to the magical pond and drink from it. So Molly set off, walking through the forest until she found it. It was so bright and sparkly! Molly filled her cup with water from the pond and took a big drink. Suddenly, the fairy appeared again, praising Molly for doing the right thing. Now the animals were going to have the help they needed. Molly smiled. She felt like she had done a great service and that made her feel really proud.

Tom and Sue are brother and sister. They share a room and a bed. Tom likes to sleep on the left side of the bed. Sue likes to sleep on the right side of the bed. One night, Tom and Sue are getting ready for bed. Tom says, "I want to sleep on the right side tonight. You sleep on the left side." Sue says, "No, I always sleep on the right side. You sleep on the left side." They start to argue and push each other. Their mom hears them and comes to their room. She is angry. She says, "Stop fighting, you two. You need to share the bed and be nice to each other. If you don't, I will give you a tip. A tip is when I take away something you like, like your toys or your books. Do you want a tip?" Tom and Sue shake their heads. They don't want a tip. They say, "Sorry, mom. We will share the bed and be nice to each other." Mom says, "Good. Now, hug and say good night." Tom and Sue hug and say good night. They lie down on the bed and close their eyes. They sleep on their own sides and don't fight anymore. Mom smiles and turns off the light. She says, "Sweet dreams, my loves."

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl called Lucy. She wanted to try something new - so she ate a lemon. It was a sour taste and she didn't like it. But then, next to the lemon there was something else. It was round and yellow and it looked like an orange. Lucy was nervous but she grabbed the orange and tried it. To her surprise the orange was sweet and yummy. Lucy was so happy that she decided to give the lemon to her old puppy. But her puppy was naughty and instead of eating the lemon he dropped it on the floor and destroyed it. Lucy was sad when she saw it. But soon she was happy again because she remembered the nice and sweet taste of the orange.

Sara and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to imagine different things. Sometimes they were pirates, sometimes they were astronauts, sometimes they were fairies. "Let's imagine we are explorers," said Sara. "We can find a secret well with magic water." "OK," said Ben. "But where is the well?" Sara pointed to a big stone. "There it is. We have to be careful. The well is very old and delicate. It might break if we touch it too hard." They walked slowly to the stone. They pretended it was a well. They looked inside. It was dark and deep. "What do you think is in there?" asked Ben. "Maybe there are jewels, or coins, or animals," said Sara. "Or maybe there is a fairy who can grant wishes." They leaned over the well and whispered their wishes. They hoped the fairy would hear them. Suddenly, they heard a splash. They jumped back and saw a frog hopping out of the well. "Look, it's a frog!" said Ben. "Maybe it's the fairy in disguise." "Maybe," said Sara. "Or maybe it's just a frog who likes the water." They laughed and picked up the frog. They decided to name it Wally. They played with Wally for a while. Then they put him back in the well and said goodbye. They ran back to the house, happy and hungry. They had a lot of fun imagining. They wondered if their wishes would come true.

Once there was a little boy who liked to jog. He had a lot of energy and liked to use it to run really fast. One day he was jogging in the park and saw a cop. When he saw the cop, he felt safe. He knew it was important to listen to the cops because they kept us safe. So he waved to the cop and smiled. The cop waved back and urged him to stay in the park and always jog safely. The boy was happy and thanked the cop. He continued jogging and felt grateful to the cop for keeping him safe. He knew that it was important to always be safe and jog in the park.

John was running in the park with his mom. He saw a huge plate. He thought it was very strange. He wondered why there was a plate in the park. John's mom asked him, "Do you want to touch it?" He shook his head yes and ran over to the plate. John touched the plate and it made a loud noise. It scared him and he ran back to his mom. His mom laughed and said, "Let's see if something else happened." John and his mom ran back over to the plate and saw that there was now a big pile of cookies. John was very excited! He ran over to the plate, and starting eating the cookies. He was so happy he had found such a huge plate of cookies.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved books and would read them every day. One day, Lily was reading her book when she saw the sun start to rise in the sky. "Look, Mommy!" she said excitedly. "The sun is rising!" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, it is. But don't forget to eat your breakfast before you read your book." Lily was persistent and said, "But Mommy, I want to read my book now. Can't I eat breakfast later?" Her mom thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, but just this once. You can read your book while you eat your breakfast." Lily was so happy and continued to read her book as she ate her cereal. She loved the story so much that she read it over and over again, even after the sun had risen high in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals who wanted to play together. There was a jolly rabbit, a happy dog, and a friendly cat. They all wanted to play, but they didn't know what game to play. The jolly rabbit suggested they play hide and seek. "I love hide and seek!" he said. "Let's all hide and try to find each other." The happy dog was excited, but the friendly cat didn't want to play. "I don't like hide and seek," she said. "I want to play tag instead." The jolly rabbit and the happy dog didn't want to play tag, so they tried to convince the friendly cat to play hide and seek. But the cat wouldn't budge. Finally, the jolly rabbit said, "Okay, we can play tag first, and then we can enter a new game of hide and seek." The friendly cat was happy with this compromise, and they all played together happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little rabbit called Flo. Flo loved learning new things and was always asking questions. One day, Flo asked her mum what a calendar was. Flo's mum smiled and said, "A calendar is a book with numbers and dates on it. We use it to keep track of time and things we need to remember." Flo was curious, so she asked her mum to show her. Flo's mum took out an old calendar from the drawer and let Flo look at it. Flo asked her mum why the calendar had funny drawings, and Flo's mum explained that each month had a different name and little symbol. She also told Flo that she needed to be careful when holding the calendar, as it was very important. Flo looked at the calendar, marvelling at all the different names. Finally, she came to the conclusion that a calendar was nosy. It was full of names and symbols and it was always asking questions. Flo smiled at how accurate her new-found understanding was.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, Lily and her mommy went to the park. They saw a big rock and Lily said, "Mommy, can we raise the rock?" Her mommy said, "No, it's too heavy for us." Lily was sad, but then she saw a fair in the park. She ran to her mommy and said, "Mommy, can we go to the fair?" Her mommy said, "Yes, let's go!" At the fair, Lily saw lots of games and toys. She played a game and won a prize. She was so happy and said, "Look mommy, I won a toy!" Then, Lily saw a boy who was crying. She asked him, "Why are you crying?" The boy said, "I lost my toy." Lily felt sad for him and said, "Don't worry, I'll give you my toy." The boy was happy and said, "Thank you!" Lily smiled and said, "It's okay, sharing is fair."

Mummy was talking to Grandma on the telephone. Grandma was asking questions from far away. Mummy explained, "It's a very long cord that stretches from here to Grandma's house so we can talk. It's a special cord." Teddy, a three-year-old, was watching with wide eyes. He was jealous of the cord. He wanted one! Mummy said, "Now Teddy, your Grandma is so far away we can't just drive to her house. But when she talks to us on the telephone it's like she's right here." Teddy was very excited. He wanted to play with the cord! Mummy explained, "We can't play with the cord Teddy. It's too special. We just use it to talk to Grandma, but it won't last forever. That's why we have to talk to each other as much as we can." Teddy smiled and hugged his Mummy, happy to have her close. He wasn't jealous of the cord anymore, now he understood its purpose.

Once upon a time there was a woman. She was walking in the forest when she found something special. It was a little hole in the ground. She knelt down and looked inside. "What do I see?" she thought. Suddenly, a little voice spoke to her. It said, "I'm safe inside here. Will you help me?" The woman smiled and said, "Yes, I will do my best." She carefully reached into the hole and pulled out a small kitten. It was a very scared kitten, but the woman held it gently and kissed its head. The kitten purred happily. Now it felt safe. The woman had done a very kind thing. She was glad that the kitten was safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat tasty cookies, but he didn't like to share them with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom caught him hiding a whole sheet of cookies under his bed. She was very angry and decided to punish Timmy by taking away his favorite toy. Timmy felt sad and realized that it was not nice to keep all the cookies for himself. He decided to apologize to his friends and share his cookies with them. His friends were happy and forgave him. Timmy learned that sharing is important and it feels good to make others happy. From that day on, Timmy always shared his cookies with his friends and he never hid anything under his bed again. His mom was proud of him for being a good friend and for learning to do the right thing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved muffins and she always asked her mom to bake them for her. One day, her mom baked a muffin for her and told her to be careful because it was very hot and dangerous. Lily was so excited to eat her muffin that she didn't listen to her mom's warning. She took a big bite and accidentally dropped the muffin on the floor. The muffin broke into pieces and made a big mess. Lily's mom came into the room and saw what happened. She told Lily that it's important to listen to warnings because they can keep us safe. Lily learned her lesson and promised to be more careful in the future. From that day on, Lily always listened to her mom's warnings and never dropped another muffin again.

Lily was a lazy girl. She often didn't want to do anything. Everything felt like too much effort. But one day, something inside of her changed. She found a paintbrush and some paints lying around. As she looked at them, she felt excited. She began painting on the wall next to her. She painted all sorts of things. She painted the sky, trees, and flowers. She really brought the painting to life! When she was finished, she stepped back and looked at what she had created. She was so proud of herself. She realized that if you put your mind to it, you can do anything. From then on, Lily never felt lazy anymore. Painting had made a huge difference in her life, and she was so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain and jump in puddles. One day, she got very muddy and her mom said, "Lily, you need to take a shower." Lily didn't want to take a shower because she liked being muddy. But her mom said, "You can't go to bed all dirty. You need to get clean." So Lily took a shower and it was so much fun! She splashed and played with the water. After her shower, Lily's mom gave her a big towel to dry off with. Lily wrapped herself up in the towel and said, "I love showers! They make me feel ancient!" Her mom laughed and said, "You mean refreshed, Lily. Showers make you feel refreshed." And Lily smiled and said, "Yes, refreshed!"

Lila was sad. She wanted to play with her friends, but they were far away. She could not see them or hug them. She could only talk to them on the network. The network was a big screen that showed their faces and voices. But it was not the same as being with them. She sighed and looked out the window. She saw a wide road with many cars. She saw a park with trees and swings. She saw a shop with toys and books. She wished she could go outside and have fun. But she could not. She had to stay inside and be safe. She heard a knock on the door. She ran to open it. She saw her grandma and grandpa. They were wearing masks and gloves. They smiled and waved at her. They had a big bag with them. "Hello, Lila!" they said. "We have a surprise for you!" Lila was happy. She loved her grandma and grandpa. She wondered what the surprise was. She hoped it was something fun. They came inside and put the bag on the table. They took off their masks and gloves. They hugged and kissed Lila. They said they missed her a lot. "We have something for you, Lila," grandma said. "We know you are bored and lonely. So we brought you some friends!" She opened the bag and took out some stuffed animals. There was a bear, a rabbit, a cat, and a dog. They were soft and cute. They had bright eyes and noses. Lila gasped and clapped her hands. She loved stuffed animals. She hugged them and thanked her grandma and grandpa. She said they were the best friends ever. She put them on the couch and played with them. She gave them names and voices. She made them talk and laugh. She pretended they were having a tea party. She looked at the network and saw her friends. They were also playing with their toys. They waved and smiled at her. They said they liked her new friends. Lila smiled and waved back. She said she liked their toys too. She said she was happy to see them. She said she hoped they could play together soon. She sighed and looked at her grandma and grandpa. They were watching her and smiling. They said they were proud of her. They said they loved her very much. Lila felt warm and cozy. She had her family and her friends. She had her stuffed animals and her network. She was not sad anymore. She was happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. Tim had a small cart that he wanted to pack with toys to play with. He put his ball, his toy car, and his teddy bear in the cart. At the park, Tim met a girl named Sue. Sue had a big, filthy toy truck. "Can I play with your truck?" Tim asked. Sue said, "Only if I can play with your toys in your cart." Tim didn't want Sue to play with his toys because her truck was filthy, and he didn't want his toys to get dirty. He said, "No, thank you. My toys don't want to get dirty." Sue was sad, but Tim had an idea. He said, "Let's clean your truck, and then we can play together." They found a water tap and cleaned the truck. After that, Tim and Sue played with their toys, and they became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pastel crayons. One day, her mommy gave her a big box of new pastels to use. Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to open the box. She was very restless and kept jumping up and down. Finally, her mommy helped her open the box and Lily's eyes grew big with excitement. She saw all the pretty colors and couldn't wait to start drawing. She picked up a pink pastel and started drawing a beautiful flower. She drew and drew until she had a whole garden of pretty flowers. Lily was so happy with her new pastels and wanted to draw more and more every day.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man. Every day he would dream about a big vegetable garden. He imagined how the vegetables would look - juicy carrots, delicious lettuce and sweet onions. Every night he dreamed of walking through the garden, picking all the vegetables he wanted. One day, the man made his dream come true and planted a garden. As he watered the soil, he watched the vegetables grow. Every morning he would sit and admire his garden and be so happy. The man was so proud of his vegetable garden. Every day he would pick vegetables and make delicious meals. He was so pleased that he had made his dream come true. And every day he still dreams of his garden and all the wonderful vegetables.

Once upon a time there was a dog who was very lucky. His name was Lucky. He had a long, fluffy tail that he was very proud of. Every day, Lucky the dog would wag his tail around and it brought him lots of joy. One day, something happened that changed his life. Lucky wanted to rub his tail but it wasn't very soft anymore. He was very sad and went to find his best friend, Toby the cat. He asked Toby why his tail wasn't soft anymore. Toby smiled and said, "Don't worry Lucky. Rub your tail like this and it will be nice and soft again." Lucky did what Toby said and was so happy when he felt his tail become soft and fluffy again. He thanked Toby and said, "Thank you so much Toby. I'm so lucky to have a tail like this!"

Once upon a time there was a brown rabbit. The rabbit was very happy and always hopping around. One day he noticed something was wrong with his foot. He couldn't hop like he used to. He hopped to the barn to ask for help. The farmer saw the rabbit and said, "I can help you. You need to get repaired." He brought out some tools and began to repair the rabbit's foot. The farmer asked, "Do you feel better now?" The rabbit hopped around, "Yes! Thank you farmer." The farmer smiled, "You're welcome, rabbit. Now go enjoy hopping around and be careful." The rabbit hopped away happily and enjoyed the rest of his day. He was grateful for the farmer and his repair.

Tom and Lily were playing cops and robbers in the yard. Tom was the cop and Lily was the robber. Tom had a toy gun and Lily had a bag of candy. Tom chased Lily around the trees and the swings. He shouted, "Stop, robber, or I will shoot!" Lily ran as fast as she could, but Tom was faster. He caught her and said, "You are under arrest! You stole the candy from the store!" He took her to the jail, which was a cardboard box with bars drawn on it. He put her inside and locked the door with a string. Lily was sad and scared. She did not like the jail. It was dark and small and cold. She said, "Please, Tom, let me out! I am sorry I took the candy. I will give it back to you. Please, please, please!" Tom said, "No, you have to stay in jail for a long time. You are a bad robber. You have to learn your lesson." He went to play with the candy and the gun. He did not care about Lily. Lily cried and cried. She wanted to go home. She wanted to hug her mom. She wanted to play with Tom again. She looked around the jail and saw a hole in the corner. She crawled to the hole and pushed it with her hands. The hole got bigger and bigger. She saw the sun and the grass and the flowers. She smiled and said, "I can get out! I can release myself from the jail!" She squeezed through the hole and ran away. She did not look back. She did not want to see Tom again. She ran to her house and knocked on the door. Her mom opened the door and said, "Lily, where have you been? I was worried about you." Lily hugged her mom and said, "I was in jail, mom. Tom put me in jail. But I released myself. It was easy. I found a hole and I escaped. I am sorry I took the candy. I will never do it again." Her mom said, "Oh, Lily, I am glad you are safe. But you should not take candy that is not yours. And you should not play with Tom if he is mean to you. He is not a good friend. Come inside and have some milk and cookies. I love you, Lily." Lily said, "I love you too, mom. And I love milk and cookies. And I love you more than candy." She went inside and ate and drank and felt happy. She did not miss the jail or Tom or the candy. She had her mom and her home and her love. And that was enough.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl named Amy. She was very alert and always looked for new things to explore. One day she decided to search for a painter who could help her. She went out of her house and looked everywhere. Amy walked along the street and soon she found a painter. She was so excited! She asked the painter, "Can you help me?" The painter smiled at Amy and said, "Yes, I can! What do you need help with?" Amy said, "Can you paint my bedroom? It would look so much better." The painter smiled again and said, "Yes, I can do that for you. I can make it very special." Amy was very happy and thanked the painter. She watched as he painted the room. It was as if magic had come to her bedroom. Amy was especially alert that day when she watched the painter working in her bedroom. She enjoyed every moment of it. When the painter was done, she thanked him again and gave him a big hug. The painter smiled before he left. Amy's bedroom had never looked so good before. She was so happy and smiled from ear to ear. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around outside. One day, she went to the store with her mommy and received a new toy. It was a big, fluffy teddy bear. Lily was so happy and hugged the teddy bear tight. She showed it to her mommy and said, "Look, mommy! I got a new toy!" Her mommy smiled and said, "That's great, Lily! I'm so proud of you. You were successful in picking out a toy you really wanted." Later that day, Lily accidentally poked herself in the eye while playing with her teddy bear. She cried and told her mommy, "Ow, my eye hurts!" Her mommy gave her a big hug and said, "It's okay, Lily. Let's put some ice on your eye to make it feel better." Lily felt better and continued to play with her new toy. She was happy and grateful to have such a wonderful mommy who cared about her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emily. She was three years old, and she liked finding new things. One day, Emily went on a walk with her mom. They were in the garden, and Mom said, "Look, Emily! What do you see?" "I see a zipper!" said Emily excitedly. Emily was very curious about the zipper, so she decided to be polite and ask. "Mommy, what is that?" "It's a zipper," replied Mom. Emily then discovered she could open the zipper. She carefully opened it and found a box inside. She was so excited to open the box! The box was full of fun toys! Emily had a great time playing with them. She and Mom played hide and seek with the toys for the rest of the day. At the end, Emily was happy and tired. She had a wonderful day discovering new things.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a big box where they kept their toys, and they had a key to unlock the box. Sometimes they shared their toys, and sometimes they fought over them. One day, Ben found a cane in the box. It was a long stick with a curve at the end. He thought it was fun to pretend he was a pirate with the cane. He said, "Arrr, matey, I'm the captain of the ship. Give me your treasure or walk the plank!" Lily wanted to play with the cane too. She was jealous of Ben. She said, "No, I want to be the pirate. You can be the parrot. Give me the cane, or I'll tickle you!" Ben did not want to give up the cane. He said, "No, it's mine. I found it first. You can't have it, or I'll poke you!" They started to tug on the cane, pulling it back and forth. They did not see their grandma coming into the room. She was using a cane to walk, because her legs were old and sore. She saw the twins fighting over her cane. She said, "Hey, hey, hey, what are you doing with my cane? That's not a toy, that's my helper. Give it back to me, please." Ben and Lily stopped fighting. They felt sorry for taking their grandma's cane. They said, "Sorry, grandma. We didn't know it was yours. We thought it was a toy. Here, you can have it back." They gave the cane back to their grandma. She smiled and thanked them. She said, "It's okay, my dears. I know you were just playing. But next time, ask me before you take something that belongs to me. And remember to share your toys with each other. How about we play a game together? I can be the pirate, and you can be my crew. How does that sound?" Ben and Lily nodded and agreed. They were happy to play with their grandma. They unlocked the box and took out some hats and scarves and coins. They put them on and followed their grandma to the living room. They pretended they were on a ship, sailing the seas and looking for treasure. They had fun and forgot about being jealous.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny. His name was Bob. Every day, Bob hopped around in the forest looking for fun. One day, Bob found a jar filled with light. It was very pretty. He shook it and it made a nice tinkling sound. Bob was so excited that he wanted to show his friends. He hopped over to the other animals in the forest and teased them with the jar. He waved the jar around and made them laugh. Soon, all the animals were gathered around the jar. They played a game and tried to catch the light. When the day was over, the animals said goodbye to Bob. He smiled as he hopped away with the jar and forever remembered the fun day spent relaxing in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a man called Joe. Joe wanted to buy a new suit, so he went to the shop. Joe was looking at a suit. It was orange - very, very orange! "This is the suit I want," Joe said. "I want to buy it!" The shopkeeper smiled. "That suit looks nice!" he said. "But why do you want an orange one?" Joe beamed. "I like the colour!" he said. So Joe bought the orange suit. He was very happy with it. He wore it to the party and everyone said it looked great. Joe was glad that he had bought a nice suit. The end.

Once upon a time there was an old wise tree. Every morning he would sit in his favourite spot, watching the birds fly and the animals playing in the fields. One day, a little girl called Sarah came up to the tree. She looked sad and didn't know what to do. She turned to the tree and said, "I'm feeling so low, tree. Can you help me feel better?" The tree smiled and said kindly, "Yes, my dear. I can help. All you need to do is promise to look after the animals and birds around you every day. It will make them very happy and make you happy too." Sarah smiled and said, "I promise, tree. I'll take care of them every day." The tree smiled again and said, "As a reward for your promise, here's a lovely piece of chocolate for you. Enjoy it!" Sarah thanked the tree and happily ate the chocolate. She still kept her promise and looked after the animals and birds every day. Moral of the Story: When you keep your promise, it makes you and those around you happy.

Once upon a time, there was a cat called John. John had a wide tail and bright blue eyes. One day, John was walking through the park when he saw a little bird. He was so curious about the bird that he reached out to touch it. The bird blinked quickly and made a chirping sound. "What do you want, little bird?" asked John. The little bird shook its head and said, "I want to show you something. Follow me!" John followed the little bird to the top of a big tree. From there, John could see the world around him. It was so wide, with so many colours and shapes. John blinked happily. Now he knew what the little bird wanted to show him. He took a deep breath and it felt like magic. Then the little bird flew away, but John had made a friend he would never forget.

Once there was a three-year-old named Nancy. She loved to play and explore new things. One day, Nancy was playing in the garden and she saw a hoop. She picked up the hoop and asked her mom,"What is it?" Her mom replied, "It looks like a hoop. Do you want to try and use it?" Nancy nodded and began to roll the hoop round and round. She was so happy that mom had showed her how to use it. She kept rolling the hoop and got better and better with every turn. Soon she found a friend in the garden. It was a little ladybug. The ladybug seemed to like it when Nancy had the hoop. She kept following it around. Nancy thought it was fun to have someone follow her, so she kept rolling the hoop with the ladybug. She kept getting faster and faster. The ladybug seemed really helpful in teaching Nancy how to use the hoop. Eventually, with the ladybug's help, Nancy became an expert hooper! She was so proud of herself. She had learned something new and it felt so fantastic.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who wanted to find something special. She searched and searched until she found the perfect thing - a wave in the ocean. It was bigger and brighter than any other wave. As she watched, the wave became more and more creative. It went up and down, moved side to side, and looked like it was dancing! The girl was so excited. She wanted to get a closer look, so she carefully stepped into the water. When she got close enough, the wave lifted her up and started to carry her away! The girl closed her eyes and started to laugh, feeling the wave's power and warmth. She had never been so happy. She thanked the wave and said goodbye, then watched it disappear into the sea. When the wave was gone, the girl knew she had found something special. She was amazed at all of the interesting, creative things nature had to offer!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pale face and loved to play outside. One day, she found a shiny rock and put it in her pocket. Lily's mom asked her, "What did you find, sweetie?" "I found a pretty rock and put it in my pocket," Lily said. Her mom smiled and said, "Let's wrap it in a tissue so it doesn't fall out of your pocket." Lily wrapped the rock in a tissue and put it back in her pocket. She was so happy to have her special rock with her wherever she went.

One day, a popular cricket appeared. It hopped around in the garden and attracted the attention of the little boy next door. The boy was only three years old, but he was very excited when he saw it. He asked his mom, "What is it?" His mom said, "It's a cricket. They make sound at night." The little boy was so curious. He wanted to get close to this cricket to have a look. So he slowly approached it and when he was close enough, the cricket flew away. The little boy was disappointed, but his mom said, "Don't worry, another cricket will soon appear." The little boy was so happy. He waited and waited, then finally, the next day, another popular cricket appeared! The little boy was so excited and watched it happily until it hopped away.

Lily liked to spoil her doll. She gave her doll a lot of hugs and kisses. She gave her doll nice clothes and shoes. She gave her doll a bed and a blanket. She gave her doll everything she wanted. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and her doll. She saw a boy playing with a truck. She wanted to play with the truck too. She left her doll on a bench and ran to the boy. She tried to touch his truck, but he said no. He said it was his truck and she could not touch it. Lily got angry. She said she wanted to touch the truck. She said she would give him her doll if he let her touch the truck. The boy looked at her doll. He said her doll was crazy. He said her doll had too many clothes and shoes. He said her doll looked silly. Lily felt sad. She said her doll was not crazy. She said her doll was pretty and nice. She said she loved her doll. She ran back to the bench and hugged her doll. She said she was sorry for leaving her doll. She said she would never spoil her doll again. She said she would always be with her doll. The boy watched Lily and her doll. He felt sorry too. He said he was sorry for being mean. He said he liked his truck, but he liked to share too. He said he wanted to be friends with Lily and her doll. He said he would let them touch his truck if they wanted. Lily smiled. She said she was sorry for being rude. She said she liked her doll, but she liked to play too. She said she wanted to be friends with the boy and his truck. She said she would let him touch her doll if he wanted. The boy and Lily became friends. They played with the truck and the doll. They had fun. They did not spoil their toys. They shared their toys. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a thin fisherman. He was a very brave man who loved to fish. Every day, he put on his hat, grabbed his fishing rod and went out on the sea. On this particular day, he sailed out further than usual. Suddenly, he heard a loud 'shrink' sound. He looked around, but he couldn't see anything. Then he felt himself start to shrink! He became so small that the fishing rod was too big for him. He could still swim, though. Suddenly, he saw something floating in the water. When he got closer, he realised it was his hat! He was so happy that he swam back to the boat as quickly as he could. As he climbed back onto the boat, he started to grow back to his normal size. He still had the hat - the shrinking was only a dream!

Jill and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a shiny thing in the grass. It is a diamond. "Wow, look at this!" Jill says. "It is so pretty and sparkly!" "Can I see?" Tom asks. He takes the diamond from Jill. He likes it too. "Where did it come from?" Jill wonders. "Maybe someone lost it. Maybe it is very expensive." "Or maybe it is cheap," Tom says. "Maybe it is not a real diamond. Maybe it is just glass." "How can we know?" Jill asks. They see a man walking by. He has a big hat and a coat. He looks at them and smiles. "Hello, kids," he says. "What do you have there?" "It is a diamond," Tom says. "We found it in the grass." "Really?" the man says. "That is very lucky. Do you want to sell it to me? I will give you ten dollars for it." "Ten dollars?" Jill says. "That is a lot of money. We can buy many toys with that." "Or we can keep the diamond," Tom says. "It is very pretty and sparkly." The man looks at them. He wants the diamond. He thinks it is real and worth a lot more than ten dollars. He tries to trick them. "Trust me, kids," he says. "The diamond is cheap. It is not worth anything. It is just glass. You should take the money and be happy." Jill and Tom look at each other. They are not sure. They like the diamond, but they also like money. They do not know who to believe. What do you think they should do?

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted to eat dinner. Her mommy made her favorite food, spaghetti and meatballs. Lily was so happy and ate all her dinner. After dinner, Lily's mommy read her a scary story. Lily got scared and couldn't relax. She tried to close her eyes, but she couldn't stop thinking about the scary story. Suddenly, Lily heard a loud noise outside her window. She got even more scared and started to cry. Her mommy came to her room to comfort her, but it was too late. A scary monster had come into her room and took her away. Lily was never seen again. Her mommy was very sad and missed her little girl. She wished she had never read her that scary story.

Tim and Jen were playing with their toy cars in the park. They liked to make noises and pretend they were racing. But then a big boy came and took Jen's car. He said it was his now and ran away. Jen was sad and angry. She wanted her car back. Tim had an idea. He saw a big truck near the fence. It had a long thing on the back. Tim thought it looked like a missile. He told Jen to follow him. They ran to the truck and climbed on it. Tim found a button and pushed it. The missile flew off the truck and made a loud boom. The big boy heard the boom and saw the smoke. He was scared and dropped Jen's car. He ran away too. Tim and Jen got the car back and smiled. They were happy and proud. They did not know that the missile was smelly. It was full of garbage and made a big mess. The truck driver was angry and shouted. He wanted his missile back. But Tim and Jen did not hear him. They ran back to the park and played with their toy cars. They did not steal anything again.

Once upon a time, there was a magical delivery truck. In it was a mysterious yellow box with a big red bow. With a huge rumble, the truck drove to an amazing house. The delivery truck stopped, and the driver hopped out. He grabbed the box carefully, and carried it up to the porch. As the kids watched from the window, the driver put down the box and rang the doorbell. When the door opened, the kids got excited. Their eyes lit up as the driver handed over the box. They took it in to the living room and started to open it. Inside was the most amazing toy they had ever seen! They gasped and cheered in delight! The delivery man was happy to see the kids so excited, and smiled before he went back to his truck. With a wave goodbye, the truck drove away. The kids hugged their new toy and went off to play.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Anna had a doll and Ben had a car. They were having fun, but then Anna saw Ben's car and wanted it. "Give me your car, Ben. It is shiny and fast. I like it more than my doll," Anna said. "No, Anna. This is my car. You have your doll. We can share, but you cannot take it," Ben said. Anna did not listen. She grabbed Ben's car and ran away. Ben was sad and angry. He chased Anna and tried to get his car back. They started to fight and yell. Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Anna and Ben pulling and pushing each other. She was not happy. "Anna, Ben, stop it right now. Why are you fighting?" Mom asked. "Anna took my car and she won't give it back. It is not fair," Ben said. "Ben has a nice car and I want it. It is better than my doll," Anna said. Mom shook her head. She took the car and the doll and put them on the table. "Listen to me, both of you. You have to be kind and respectful to each other. You cannot take someone else's toy without asking. You have to share and take turns. How would you feel if someone did that to you?" Mom said. Anna and Ben looked at each other. They realized that they were wrong. They felt sorry for what they did. "I'm sorry, Ben. I should not have taken your car. It was not nice. Can you forgive me?" Anna said. "I'm sorry, Anna. I should not have yelled at you. It was not nice. I forgive you," Ben said. They hugged and said sorry to Mom. Mom smiled and hugged them back. "That's good, Anna and Ben. I'm proud of you. You are compassionate. You care about how others feel. You can play with your toys again, but remember to share and take turns. OK?" Mom said. "OK, Mom. Thank you," Anna and Ben said. They took their toys and played together happily. They learned their lesson. They realized that being compassionate is better than being selfish.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little girl named Lulu. She loved to take off her shoes and socks and play with her toes in the sunshine. However, one day her mother scolded her and said, "Lulu! You must put your shoes and socks back on! You know you're not allowed to take them off!" Lulu didn't want to listen and she started to cry. She really just wanted to feel the sunshine on her toes. But her mother told her sternly, "No more removing your shoes and socks!" Lulu was very sad and sniffled, but she reluctantly put her shoes and socks back on. As she put them back on, she remembered the moral that her mother had taught her. Lulu said, "Sometimes it's okay to remove my shoes and socks and feel the sunshine, but I must be careful to not disobey my mother's rules." So, Lulu promised to always obey her mother's rules and she happily skipped away with her toe-wiggling.

Tim and Sam were playing knights in the garden. They had sticks for swords and pots for helmets. They pretended to fight dragons and bad guys. "Look, there is a big dragon!" Tim said, pointing to a bush. "Let's go and beat him!" "OK, but be careful!" Sam said, following Tim. They ran to the bush and swung their swords at the leaves. "Roar!" the dragon said. It was not a real dragon, but Tim's old dog, Rex. He liked to play with the boys, but he did not like their swords. He barked and jumped out of the bush. "Ah, it's Rex!" Tim said, dropping his sword. "He scared me!" "Me too!" Sam said, dropping his sword too. "But he is a good dragon, right?" "Yes, he is a good dragon," Tim said, hugging Rex. "He just wants to play with us." "OK, let's play with him then," Sam said, petting Rex. "But we have to finish our knight game first. We have to save the princess!" "Where is the princess?" Tim asked, looking around. "She is in the castle," Sam said, pointing to the shed. "We have to rescue her from the bad guy!" "OK, let's go then!" Tim said, picking up his sword. "But we have to be quiet, so the bad guy does not hear us." "OK, let's be quiet," Sam said, picking up his sword too. They tiptoed to the shed, ready to save the princess.

Sara and Max are playing in the park with their dog, Spot. They like to run and chase and throw the ball for Spot. Spot is a good dog and a healthy dog. He has soft fur and four paws. One day, they discover something new in the park. It is a big hole in the ground, near a tree. Sara and Max are curious. They want to see what is in the hole. They go closer and look inside. "Wow, look at that!" Sara says. "It is a baby fox!" The baby fox is small and cute. It has orange fur and a white tail. It also has four paws, like Spot. But it looks scared and lonely. It makes a soft noise. "Hello, baby fox," Max says. "Don't be afraid. We are your friends." He reaches out his hand to touch the baby fox. But Spot barks and jumps in front of him. He does not like the baby fox. He thinks it is a bad animal. He wants to protect Sara and Max. "Spot, no!" Sara says. "The baby fox is not bad. He is just lost. He needs our help." She tries to calm Spot down. She pets his fur and tells him to be nice. She also tells Max to be careful. She says they should not touch the baby fox. They should find his mom. They look around the park. They see a big fox near the fence. She has orange fur and a white tail, like the baby fox. She is looking for her baby. She hears his noise. She runs to the hole. The baby fox sees his mom. He is happy. He runs to her. She licks his fur and nuzzles his nose. She thanks Sara and Max for finding her baby. She says they are good kids and a good dog. Sara and Max are happy too. They wave goodbye to the foxes. They go back to playing with Spot. They have a fun day in the park. They learn something new. They discover that foxes have paws, like dogs. But they are different animals. And they need different homes.

Ben and Mia are twins. They like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They drive them on the floor, on the sofa, on the table. They make noises like vroom, beep, honk. One day, they find a big black car in the garage. It is their dad's car. It looks shiny and cool. They want to play with it. They open the door and climb inside. They see many buttons and levers. They touch them and pull them. The car makes noises like click, whirr, ding. "Look, Mia, I can drive!" Ben says. He turns the key in the ignition. The car starts to move. It goes forward and backward. It bumps into the wall and the shelves. It makes noises like crash, bang, screech. "Stop, Ben, stop!" Mia says. She is scared. She wants to get out. But the door is locked. She cries and screams. She pushes the horn. It makes a loud noise like honk, honk, honk. Dad hears the noise. He runs to the garage. He sees the car moving and shaking. He sees Ben and Mia inside. He is angry and worried. He opens the door and takes them out. He hugs them and checks if they are hurt. He is glad they are okay. He scolds them and tells them to never play with his car again. He says it is dangerous and not a toy. He says they could have broken the car or hurt themselves or others. Ben and Mia are sorry. They say they are sorry to dad and to the car. They promise to never do it again. They learn that they should not touch things that are not theirs. They learn that they should listen to dad and be careful. They learn that driving is not a game. They go back to their toy cars. They drive them safely and happily. They make noises like vroom, beep, honk.

Once upon a time there was an ancient poppy. The poppy lived in a warm meadow and was very beautiful. One day, a small 3 year old girl and her mum walked into the meadow. The little girl saw the ancient poppy and went over to it. She bent down, and asked her mum what it was. "That is an ancient poppy," her mum said. The little girl wanted to pick it, but her mum said no. Then the ancient poppy began to speak. It said, "Please don't pick me little girl. I'm too old and fragile. I need to stay here in this meadow." The little girl was surprised, she didn't know a poppy could talk. The little girl and her mum listened to what the poppy said. So they decided to leave it where it was and keep walking. As they were walking away, they heard the ancient poppy say, "Thank you for understanding, little girl." The girl smiled, and waved goodbye to the ancient poppy.

Once upon a time, there was a big and furry panda named Pandy. Pandy lived in a big zoo with lots of other animals. One day, a little girl named Lily came to visit the zoo with her mom. Lily saw Pandy and said, "Wow! Look at that big furry panda!" Pandy heard Lily and turned to stare at her. Lily smiled and said, "Hi, Pandy! You're so cute!" Pandy was happy to hear Lily's kind words. He said, "Thank you, Lily! Would you like to come closer and pet me?" Lily nodded her head and walked over to Pandy's enclosure. She reached out her hand and petted Pandy's soft and furry fur. From that day on, Lily visited Pandy every time she came to the zoo. They became good friends and Pandy always looked forward to seeing Lily's smiling face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sandy. She had a family that loved her very much. Every day, her mom and dad patiently cleaned the house while she played. One day, Sandy's mom had to go to work, so her dad cleaned the house by himself. He put away the toys, wiped the windows, and swept the floors. When Sandy saw this, she felt very happy. She wanted to help, too. So she got a rag and a bucket, and she cleaned with her dad. They worked all morning and the house was soon sparkly clean! Sandy was so excited to show her mom what a great job they'd done. At the end of the day, Sandy told her dad how much she loved him. He gave her a big hug and told her how much he loved her, too. Sandy's parents were always so patient with her, and she knew that their love was what made everything clean.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she found a brilliant spot on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her mom. "Mommy, look at this brilliant spot I found!" said Lily. "That's so pretty, Lily. Maybe we can mail it to your grandma," said her mom. Lily was so excited to mail the spot to her grandma. She ran inside to get a box and some stamps. She put the spot in the box and put the stamps on it. "Can we go mail it now, mommy?" asked Lily. "Of course, let's go to the post office," said her mom. Lily and her mom went to the post office and mailed the box to her grandma. A few days later, her grandma called and said how much she loved the brilliant spot Lily sent her. From that day on, Lily loved to mail things to her grandma.

Ben is a boy who likes to dig in the dirt. He has a shovel and a bucket. He digs and digs and finds many things. He finds rocks and worms and roots. He is happy. One day, he digs and finds something new. It is brown and furry and has a long nose. It is a mole. The mole is scared of Ben. It tries to run away. Ben is curious. He wants to see the mole. He puts the mole in his bucket and covers it with dirt. He thinks the mole will be his friend. He takes the bucket to his house. He shows the mole to his mom and dad. They are not happy. They say the mole belongs in the dirt. They say the mole is not a pet. Ben is sad. He likes the mole. He thinks the mole is clever. He thinks the mole can dig better than him. He wants to play with the mole. He does not want to let the mole go. But he sees the mole is not happy. The mole is scared and lonely. The mole wants to go back to the dirt. The mole wants to be free. Ben understands. He loves the mole. He wants the mole to be happy. He takes the bucket to the garden. He digs a hole and puts the mole in it. He says goodbye to the mole. He hopes the mole will find his family and friends. He hopes the mole will remember him. He smiles and waves. The mole pops his head out and winks. He is clever. He is grateful. He is free.

Once there was a little girl called Sarah who loved asking questions. One day she went to visit her father at the office. He said, "Do you want to meet my friends?" Sarah replied, "Yes please!" When they arrived, Sarah saw lots of adults talking and texting. She asked her father why they were here. He explained, "Everyone here has a very important job. They teach others about their work." Sarah was curious, "What kind of work do they do?" Her father smiled and said, "They help businesses make money and get ahead of the competition." Just then, one of Sarah's father's friends noticed her. His name was Alex and he asked Sarah, "Hey, would you like to join us? I can explain what we're all talking about." Sarah smiled and said, "Yes please! I want to learn." So Alex took Sarah around the office and told her all about the competitive business world. He used simple words like profits and skills, so Sarah could understand. When their tour was finished, Sarah thanked Alex and said she was very inspired by what she was learning. The next day, Sarah excitedly told her friends about her trip. She used the words profits and skills, to explain what she had learnt. She had become more curious about the world

Once upon a time, there was a big band. The band had many instruments like drums, guitars, and trumpets. They loved to play music and make people happy. One day, the band wanted to play a concert in a big park. They set up their instruments and started to play. But then, they saw a big bee buzzing around them. The bee was very angry and started to zoom around the band. The band tried to keep playing, but the bee was too loud and distracting. They didn't know what to do. Suddenly, a little girl came up to them and said, "I know how to help!" She had a big jar and caught the bee inside. The band was so happy and grateful that they played a special song just for the little girl. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly man named Jack. Jack had a wallet with lots of money inside. One day, Jack met a little girl named Lily. Lily asked Jack if she could have some money to buy candy. Jack said yes and gave her some money from his wallet. Later that day, Jack realized his wallet was missing. He asked Lily if she knew where it was. Lily said she didn't know. Jack searched everywhere but he couldn't find it. He was very sad because he needed the money in his wallet to pay for his rent. Days passed and Jack still couldn't find his wallet. He asked Lily again if she knew where it was. This time, Lily said she buried it in the ground because she wanted to keep the money for herself. Jack was very angry and sad. He couldn't pay his rent and had to leave his home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go fishing with her dad. One day, they caught a big fish. Lily said, "Wow, this fish is so tasty! Can we eat it for dinner?" Her dad replied, "Yes, let's take it home and cook it." When they got home, Lily's mom cooked the fish for dinner. It smelled so good and they couldn't wait to eat it. But when they took a bite, they realized something was wrong. The fish didn't fit right in their mouths and it tasted really bad. Lily's dad said, "I think this fish was spoiled. We can't eat it." They were all disappointed and had to throw the fish away. Lily said, "I'm sad we can't eat the fish, but at least we had fun fishing together." Her parents agreed and they all hugged. From then on, they made sure to always check if the fish was fresh before cooking it.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. They lived near a big river. The river was very pretty and had lots of fish in it. The family loved to go for walks by the river and watch the fish swim. One day, the family went for a walk but they forgot to close the gate. Their dog saw the open gate and ran away. The family was very worried and looked for the dog everywhere. After a while, the dog returned! He had been playing by the river and chasing the fish. The family was very happy to see him again. They hugged him and promised to always remember to close the gate. From then on, they never forgot to close it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went for a walk in the woods and noticed how quiet it was. The silence seemed strange and mysterious to her. As she walked further, she saw a small pond. She saw some fish swimming in the water and they seemed to be having fun. But then, Lily noticed something else. There was a mysterious creature hiding in the bushes. She couldn't see it clearly, but it seemed to be watching her. Lily felt a little scared, but she decided to be brave and investigate. She slowly walked towards the bushes and peeked inside. To her surprise, she saw a cute little bunny hiding there. It wasn't mysterious at all! Lily felt relieved and happy to have made a new friend. From that day on, she visited the bunny every time she went for a walk in the woods.

Once there was a bunny. His fur was white and he was very happy. He hopped to the store every single day and said hello to everyone. The store had lots of goodies the bunny liked to buy. He wanted candy and toys. One day, the bunny had an urge to buy something special. It was so strong, he couldn't resist it so he hopped right away. He hopped into the store and saw a big, white box. It was filled with lots of goodies. He reached inside and finally got what he wanted. He was so excited that he hopped back home with his new treat. He smiled and enjoyed his surprise on the way back. He was very happy that his urge led him to such a special surprise.

Tina and her mom were visiting a stream. Tina was very shy as she walked along the bank. She looked down into the stream and all sorts of interesting things caught her eye. Suddenly, she saw a fish swimming around in the water. Excited, Tina ran to her mom and asked, "Mommy, can I visit the fish?" Eagerly, her mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course! Let's see if we can find a way to get closer to the stream." So they went exploring until they found a bridge that crossed over the stream. Tina walked slowly because she was still feeling shy. But when she got close to the water she couldn't help but smile. The fish swam closer to the bridge, as if it wanted to visit Tina too. Tina gasped and said to her mom, "Look mommy, the fish came to visit!" Her mom said, "Yes! And maybe it even wants to be friends with you!" Tina was filled with joy and waved at the fish. She knew she had made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on trips with her family. One day, they went on a long car ride. Lily saw lots of cars on the road. She said, "Mommy, why is there so much traffic?" Her mommy said, "Because lots of people are going on trips too, just like us." When they arrived at their destination, Lily helped her daddy unpack the car. She saw a big green field and said, "Look, Daddy! The grass is so green!" They all had a picnic on the green grass and enjoyed the beautiful day. Lily said, "I love going on trips with my family!"

Once upon a time, there was a small boy. He wanted to find out what life was all about, so he decided to follow it. He walked and walked, trying to follow life. But it was hard. He kept getting frustrated because life was so unpredictable. He turned corners and looked for clues, but he just couldn't figure it out. He felt so down that he wanted to give up. But then one day, he had an idea. Instead of trying to follow life, he decided to take life one step at a time. He found that if he just enjoyed each step and embraced each moment, life started to feel a little easier. All of a sudden, he was filled with joy, and he wasn't so scared of life any more. He was happy and excited to see what the future would bring. The little boy had finally figured out that the best way to follow life was to live it and enjoy it. He was no longer frustrated and instead filled with joy and love. He would never forget this lesson and continued to follow life with a smile on his face.

Once there was a little girl called Alice. She was very intelligent and loved stories. One day, Alice read the most amazing story about a prince saving a princess from a giant dragon. Alice was so excited about the story that she decided to go and find a giant dragon of her own! She travelled far and wide, but alas, she could not find one. Alice was about to turn back and go home when she spotted a giant dragon in the distance. She was so excited and ran towards it. The dragon saw Alice coming and opened its mouth wide, ready to eat her! Alice was so scared, but it was too late. The dragon ate her and the story had a bad ending.

One day, Emma was feeling very bored so she decided to have some fun. She went to find her mum's paints, and started to paint a picture. As Emma was painting, she could feel a warm, graceful breeze. Suddenly, Emma heard her mum laughing. Emma asked her mum why she was laughing. Mum said,"Oh Em, your painting! It looks like a delicious dessert!" Emma thought her painting was even better than a dessert so she kept on painting. She used the colours blue and yellow to create bright and beautiful pictures. With a satisfied smile, Emma told her mum, "Now I have a yummy looking dessert and I didn't even have to eat it!"
