Sara had a big cut on her knee. It hurt a lot and she cried. Mommy came and hugged her. She said, "Don't worry, Sara. Your cut will heal soon. You are very brave." Mommy took Sara to the bathroom. She put some water and shampoo on a soft cloth. She said, "This shampoo is harmless. It will not sting your cut. It will make it clean and help it heal faster." She gently washed Sara's knee with the cloth. Sara felt the shampoo tickle her skin. She smiled a little. Mommy dried Sara's knee with a towel. She put a band-aid on it. She said, "There, all done. Now your cut is covered and protected. You can play again, but be careful not to hurt your knee again." She kissed Sara's cheek. Sara said, "Thank you, Mommy. You are the best. I love you." She hugged Mommy. She felt better. She ran to her room to find her favorite toy. She was happy. Her cut would heal soon.

Steve was out for a walk one morning. As he strolled along, he kept an eye out for something exciting. Suddenly, Steve discovered a crocodile in the grass. He was very sleepy and didn't move at all. Steve knew he had to move quickly so he carefully grabbed a stick. He poked the crocodile to see if he would wake up, but the crocodile lay still. After a few more pokes, Steve got bored. He decided to take a nap under a nearby tree. While Steve was sleeping, he did not notice that the crocodile had slowly started to follow him. When Steve woke up, he was surprised to see the crocodile right next to him. He had not expected to find a crocodile so close by, but he was excited to have discovered a new friend. Steve and the crocodile became good friends and they both enjoyed playing in the grass together.

Tim and Mia were playing in the park with their bikes. They liked to go fast and make turns and jumps. They had fun and laughed a lot. But then Tim saw a big hole in the fence. He wanted to see what was behind it. He told Mia to follow him. He pushed his bike through the hole and went to the other side. Mia was scared. She did not want to go to the other side. She saw a lot of smoke and noise and big machines. She thought it was a bad place. She shouted to Tim, "Come back, Tim! Come back!" Tim did not listen. He was curious. He rode his bike closer to the machines. He saw a big pipe that was spitting out fire. He thought it was cool. He wanted to touch it. But then he felt very hot and dizzy. He could not breathe well. He realized that the fire was taking away the oxygen. The oxygen was the air that he needed to live. He started to cough and cry. He wanted to go back to the park. He turned his bike around and tried to ride back to the fence. But it was hard. He was very tired and sick. He fell off his bike and lay on the ground. Mia saw him fall. She was very worried. She ran to the hole and called for help. She saw a man who was wearing a big hat and a coat. He was a firefighter. He had a hose that could spray water. The firefighter saw Mia and Tim. He understood what happened. He ran to Tim and picked him up. He put a mask on his face that gave him oxygen. He said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will restore you. I will make you better." He carried Tim to his truck and drove him to the hospital. Mia followed him on her bike. She was glad that the firefighter was there. She hoped that Tim would be okay. She learned a lesson. She would never go to the bad place again. She would stay in the park with her bike.

Once upon a time, there was a little goat who lived on a farm. Every day she would eat the grass and play in the sunshine. But one day it started to get really cold. The goat was so cold that she shivered, and she just wanted to sleep. The goat looked around for somewhere to sleep, but everywhere was cold and nowhere was snug. She started to feel very sad, until she saw a barn further away. In the barn it was warm and she thought it was the perfect place to sleep. But when she got close to the barn, the goat realized that it wasn't empty. Inside, a big pig was sleeping, so the goat couldn't go in. She was stuck and didn't know what to do. Then, she had an idea. She jumped on top of the pig and snuggled down into the warmth of its fur. Soon, the goat stopped shaking and happily fell asleep. And they both lived happily ever after!

Sam and Ben were brothers. They liked to play outside in the yard. One day, they saw a big hole in the ground. They wanted to see what was inside. "Let's crawl in the hole," Sam said. "Maybe we can find treasure." "No, Sam, that's not a good idea," Ben said. "Mom told us to stay away from holes. They can be dangerous." "Mom won't know," Sam said. "She is busy in the house. Come on, Ben, don't be scared. I'm honest. It will be fun." Sam crawled in the hole. Ben followed him. They crawled deeper and deeper. It was dark and cold. They could not see anything. "Sam, I don't like this," Ben said. "Let's go back." "OK, OK, let's go back," Sam said. "But first, let me see what's that shiny thing over there." Sam crawled towards the shiny thing. It was a metal trap. It snapped on Sam's leg. Sam screamed. It hurt a lot. "Help, help, Ben, help me!" Sam cried. Ben tried to help Sam. But the trap was too strong. He could not open it. He could not pull Sam out. "Help, help, someone, help us!" Ben shouted. But no one heard them. They were too far in the hole. They were stuck. They were scared. They were sorry.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat oatmeal for breakfast every day. One morning, her mom made her oatmeal with some yummy fruits on top. Lily loved it so much that she asked her mom to make it every day. One day, Lily's little brother came into her room and started being bossy. He wanted to play with her toys, but she didn't want to share. So, Lily decided to test him. She gave him a puzzle to solve and said if he could do it, then he could play with her toys. Her brother tried really hard and finally solved the puzzle. Lily was proud of him and decided to share her toys with him. From that day on, Lily and her brother played together every day and enjoyed their oatmeal breakfasts together.

The little girl was very excited. She was waiting for her parents to buy her an orange. She was smiling and cheerful as she watched her parents looking through the oranges. Finally, her dad found the perfect one and said, "This looks like the best one." Her mum said, "Let's buy it for our daughter." So, her parents bought the orange and gave it to the little girl. She was so happy, she couldn't stop laughing. She proudly held up the orange and said, "It looks so nice!" The little girl was so delighted. She ran back home with the orange, smiling and cheerful all the way. From that day on, she ate oranges every day and asked her parents to buy her more.

Lila and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the woods. One day, they saw a big hole in the rocks. It was a cave. "Let's go inside!" Tom said. He was brave. "I don't know," Lila said. She was scared. "It looks dark and cold." "Come on, it will be fun!" Tom said. He took Lila's hand and pulled her into the cave. They walked for a while. They saw bats and spiders and shiny stones. Lila felt a little better. She liked the shiny stones. "Look, there's a light!" Tom said. He pointed to a small opening at the end of the cave. "Maybe it's a way out!" They ran to the opening. But it was not a way out. It was a fire. And next to the fire, there was a big bear. The bear was angry. It roared at them. "Welcome to my cave!" the bear said. "You are my dinner!" Lila and Tom were very afraid. They tried to run back, but the bear was faster. It blocked their way. "Please, don't eat us!" Lila said. She was crying. "Too bad!" the bear said. "You look tasty!" The bear reached out its paw to grab them. But then, something happened. The cave shook. Rocks fell from the ceiling. The fire went out. The bear was hit by a big rock. It fell to the ground. It was weak. Lila and Tom saw their chance. They ran past the bear. They found another opening. It was a way out. They saw the sun and the trees and the birds. They were safe. They hugged each other. They were happy. "Let's never go into a cave again!" Lila said. "Me neither!" Tom said. They went back to their homes. They told their parents what happened. Their parents were glad they were okay. They gave them hugs and kisses and cookies. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat pasta, especially spaghetti with tomato sauce. One day, Timmy's mom made a big pot of pasta for dinner. Timmy was so excited to eat it that he ate a big bowl of it all by himself. After dinner, Timmy went to play with his toys. He noticed that one of his favorite toys, a little dinosaur, was missing. Timmy searched and searched but couldn't find it anywhere. Suddenly, he remembered that he had left it on the kitchen table. Timmy ran back to the kitchen and saw that his dinosaur had shrunk! It was now the size of a pea! Timmy couldn't believe his eyes. He realized that his dinosaur must have fallen into the pot of pasta and shrunk because of the hot water. From that day on, Timmy made sure to keep his toys away from the kitchen when his mom was cooking.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was only 3 years old. She was playing in a huge park with lots of other kids, when she saw a big path up ahead. The path was huge and meandered through the park and across the grassy fields. The little girl wanted to follow the path, so she started walking along it. As she followed the path, she saw a big crack in the ground. The crack was so big that it made the path impossible to cross. The little girl became very angry and sad. She asked her mom, "Mom, can you help me fix the crack in the path?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course I can help. I'll get your dad and he can help us fix it." Mom and Dad brought shovels from home and started digging around the edges of the crack. After a lot of work, the crack was filled and the path was fixed. The little girl was so happy and excited! She smiled and ran back to her friends to tell them that the path was fixed. They all rejoiced and ran along the huge path together. The End.

Once upon a time there were two friends Mo and Bob. Mo was very independent and Bob was very dependent. One day, Mo asked Bob if he could help him make dinner. Bob said no because he wanted to do things on his own. Mo got angry and decided to make dinner without Bob. He boiled some potatoes and put them on the table. When Bob went to the kitchen, he saw the potatoes and asked Mo why he hadn't served them. Mo replied "You don't need help. You're independent. You can serve yourself." Bob felt sad and started crying. Mo realized that independence isn't always something to brag about. Everyone needs help sometimes. The moral of this story is that it's ok to ask for help when you need it.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them some bread. "Look, Lily, a watch!" Ben said. He pointed to a shiny thing on the ground. It was a watch with a blue strap and a silver face. It had numbers and hands that moved. "Wow, Ben, it's pretty!" Lily said. She picked up the watch and put it on her wrist. "Do you think someone lost it?" "Maybe. Or maybe they left it for us to find. Like a treasure!" Ben said. He smiled and took Lily's hand. "Let's go feed the ducks!" They ran to the pond and threw some bread crumbs into the water. The ducks came closer and quacked. The fish jumped and splashed. Ben and Lily laughed and clapped. But they did not see the dark clouds in the sky. They did not hear the thunder. They did not feel the wind. Soon, it started to rain. Big drops of water fell on their heads and clothes. They got wet and cold. "Oh no, Ben, it's raining!" Lily said. She looked at the watch. It was still shiny, but it did not move. The numbers and hands were still. "Oh no, Ben, the watch is broken!" Ben looked at the watch too. He felt sad. He liked the watch. He wanted to keep it. He wondered who it belonged to. He wondered if they would be angry. "Maybe we should give it back, Lily," Ben said. He took the watch off Lily's wrist. "Maybe someone is looking for it. Maybe they will fix it." "OK, Ben," Lily said. She nodded. She was wet and cold too. She wanted to go home. "But how will we find them?" Ben looked around. He saw a sign on a tree. It had a picture of a watch and some words. He could not read them, but he guessed what they said. "Look, Lily, a sign!" Ben said. He pointed to the sign. "Maybe this is their sign. Maybe they display it to find their watch. Let's go there!" They ran to the sign and knocked on the tree. A man opened a door. He had a hat and a coat. He looked surprised. "Hello, kids, what are you doing here?" he asked. "Hello, sir, we found your watch!" Ben said. He held out the watch. "We're sorry, it's wet and broken. We didn't mean to hurt it." The man looked at the watch. He smiled and took it. He thanked Ben and Lily. He told them his name was Sam. He told them he was a watchmaker. He told them he could fix the watch. He told them he lost it when he was walking in the park. He told them he was happy they found it. He told them they were very kind and honest. He gave them each a candy and a hug. He invited them to come inside and see his workshop. He showed them how he made and fixed watches. He gave them each a new watch. He told them they could keep them. He told them they could come back anytime. Ben and Lily were happy. They liked Sam. They liked his workshop. They liked their new watches. They thanked him and said goodbye. They ran back to the park. They looked at the sky. It was clear and blue. They looked at their watches. They were shiny and moved. They looked at each other. They smiled and hugged. They had a new friend. They had a new adventure. They had a new treasure.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to chew on bones. One day, Max found a big bone in the backyard. It was so big that he had to chew on it for a long time. As he was chewing, he heard a voice say, "Hey, that's my skeleton!" Max was surprised and looked around. He saw a hairy monster standing behind him. Max was scared but the monster said, "Don't be afraid, I just need my skeleton back. It helps me stand up straight." Max understood and gave the skeleton back to the monster. The monster was happy and said, "Thank you, Max! You are a good dog." Max wagged his tail and barked happily. From that day on, Max and the monster became friends and played together in the backyard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and her cat, Daisy. Every day, Lily and Daisy would go for a walk down a path near their house. They loved to see the flowers, trees, and birds. One sunny day, Lily and Daisy met a new friend on the path. It was a tiny ant. The ant said, "Hello, I am Andy the Ant. Can you please help me? I need some water for my family." Lily wanted to be useful, so she said, "Yes, I can help you, Andy." Lily found a small cup and poured some water from a nearby stream. She carried the cup back to Andy and his family. The ants were very happy and thanked Lily for her help. From that day on, Lily, Daisy, and Andy the Ant became best friends and had many fun adventures together on the path.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a doll named Daisy. Daisy was a lonely doll because Lily did not play with her. Daisy sat on the shelf all day, wishing for a friend. One day, Lily's mom saw that Lily was not being nice to her little brother. She decided to punish Lily by taking away her favorite toy. Lily was sad and went to her room. She saw Daisy on the shelf and decided to play with her. Lily and Daisy became best friends. They played together every day. Lily learned that being nice to others made her happy too. The moral of the story is to always be kind to others and you will never be lonely.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to start a lemonade stand. She asked her mom for help. "Mommy, can you help me start a lemonade stand?" Lily asked. "Of course, sweetie. We can make lemonade together," her mom replied. Lily made a lot of lemonade and started selling it. One day, a naughty boy came and tried to steal some lemonade. "You have to pay for the lemonade," Lily said to the naughty boy. The boy apologized and paid for the lemonade. From that day on, Lily's lemonade stand became very popular.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was very playful, and always wanted to have fun. One morning, her grandmother showed her something called a whip. It was very long and shiny. Sarah thought it was funny, so she took it and ran around the house. Grandmother said, "Let me show you how to use it!" She taught Sarah how to polish it, and Sarah was excited to be able to make the whip shine even brighter. Grandmother said, "See how shiny it is now? That's what we call polishing." Sarah giggled and said, "Can I keep playing with it? It's so fun!" Grandmother smiled and said, "Yes, you can keep playing with it, as long as you remember to always polish it when you're done." Sarah was so happy that she ran around the house, playing with her whip. Every time she was done playing, she would always make sure to polish it until it was nice and shiny again. Sarah and her grandmother had lots of fun together, polishing the whip and playing with it.

Once upon a time there was a bunny who loved to hop. Every day the bunny would jump around and explore the area. One day it came across a large field of dandelions. It was so lovely! The bunny hopped over to smell the sweet scent and it was even better than it expected. The bunny hopped around the field and enjoyed it. After a while it noticed a small girl sitting and watching it. The bunny hopped over to the girl and they started talking. The bunny learned that the girl had many opinions on life. The girl said that she loved the bunny's hopping and that she wished she could do the same. The bunny and the girl became friends and talked to each other every day. They shared their opinions on the world and the bunny shared its wonderful hopping. Every day, they enjoyed the lovely view of the dandelions and the bunny showed the girl how to hop around just like it did. They were so full of love!

Little Jimmy was so excited. He was going to examine his dream today. He had been dreaming about it for weeks and now he was almost ready to see it. He could barely contain his excitement. He slowly opened the door to his dream and examined it carefully. It was filled with amazing things that he never knew he wanted. Everywhere he looked there was something amazing. His dream was even bigger and better than he ever imagined. He couldn't believe he was seeing something so incredible. He looked down and saw a little toy car and he had to stop himself from running to it. He felt like his dream was even bigger now and it was so exciting. Little Jimmy knew that he had the best dream ever. He couldn't wait to tell his friends all about what he had found in his dream. He went to bed that night excited to have his dream with him forever.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, John and Jane. Every day they would play together in the warm sun. One day, they were so excited because they were planning a big celebration. They gathered up their things and went to the woods to find an axe. John and Jane searched for hours for an axe, but they could not find one. They were sad and did not know what to do. Then one of the friends had an idea! They decided to build a fort out of sticks they found in the woods. Soon they had built a really big and strong fort! The two friends were so happy! They celebrated by sitting inside their fort and eating treats. They were warm and happy, and they made a promise to play together forever.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little boy named Oscar. He was in his room and he wanted to play with his toys, but he was surrounded by boxes full of Christmas ornaments. His mother had asked him to sort out the decorations for the Christmas tree but he was having too much fun playing and didn't want to do it. "Oscar," his mum said from the door, "why aren't you reversing the ornaments? I need your help to get ready for Christmas. Oscar frowned and reluctantly started to reverse the ornaments. At first, it was quite boring, but once he got into it, he started to enjoy it. After a while, he had finished sorting the decorations and the Christmas tree looked beautiful. Oscar was happy and so was his mum. She praised him for being so helpful, but warned him to always remember to be a good boy. Oscar smiled and promised he would be a good little boy from now on.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to watch television after lunch. They sit on the sofa and hold the remote. They press the buttons to change the channels. One day, they see a show about animals. They see a big cat with stripes. It is a tiger. The tiger is in a cage. It looks sad. Anna and Ben feel sorry for the tiger. "Can we help the tiger?" Anna asks Ben. "I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe we can rub its fur. It might feel better." They get up from the sofa and walk to the television. They reach out their hands and try to rub the tiger's fur. But they are clumsy. They bump into the television and make it fall. It makes a loud noise and breaks. "Oh no!" Anna and Ben say. They are scared. They run back to the sofa and hide under a blanket. Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees the broken television and the twins under the blanket. She is angry. "What did you do?" Mom asks. "We wanted to help the tiger," Anna says. "We tried to rub its fur," Ben says. Mom sighs. She is not happy. She tells the twins that they cannot touch the television. It is not a real tiger. It is a picture. They can only watch it, not rub it. She picks up the television and takes it to the garage. She says she will try to fix it later. She tells the twins to play with their toys instead. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She says she loves them, but they have to be careful. Anna and Ben say they are sorry. They promise to be careful. They play with their toys and forget about the tiger. They hope Mom can fix the television soon. They want to watch more shows about animals. But they will not try to rub them anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and see all the animals. She loved her mommy and daddy too. One day, Lily went for a walk and saw the earth. It was big and blue and she thought it was charming. She loved the earth and wanted to take care of it. So, she picked up some trash and threw it away. Her mommy and daddy were proud of her for loving the earth and being a good helper.

Once upon a time there was a small green frog called Luther who lived in a pond under a thicket of trees. One day, he heard some noise coming from the pond and he decided to explore it. He came across an old tree with a box underneath it. He thought it was a little odd, so he hopped closer to take a better look. He opened the lid of the box and saw something wrapped in a blanket. It was cold to the touch. Luther jumped back and said, "Who is that?" A quiet voice said, "It's me. I'm Jack. I value your kindness." Luther was surprised because he did not expect to find a person inside the box. He said, "It's my pleasure. Do you need help or food?" "I need a warm wrap and a comfortable place to sleep," said Jack. "Come with me," Luther replied. "I know just the place." Together, they hopped out of the pond and found a cosy spot nearby. Luther found Jack some warm clothes and tucked him into a soft blanket. When they were done, Luther said, "Goodnight, Jack. I'm so glad I could help." Jack smiled and said, "Me too. Thank you."

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Sally. Tom had a very creative idea for the day. He was going to make a turkey. Tom said to Sally, "Would you like to help me make a turkey?" Sally agreed and the two of them started gathering the things they needed. Tom asked Sally, "What do you think we need for a turkey?" Sally replied, "We need some feathers and some glue." So Tom and Sally got some feathers and glue, and set off on their creative mission. Tom said, "We need to make a turkey shape". So they got to work cutting the feathers and gluing them to the paper. When they were done, they stepped back and admired their work. "It looks so good," said Sally. "Let's show everybody," said Tom. So they ran off to show all of their friends their turkey. Everyone was impressed by their creative work and allowed them to keep it! The two friends had so much fun making the turkey and were so happy that all their friends allowed them to keep it. They decided to make a different turkey every week, and each one was more creative than the last!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved muffins, especially blueberry muffins. One day, Timmy's sister wanted to eat the last blueberry muffin, but Timmy wanted it too. They started to quarrel and shout at each other. Their mom came in and told them to stop quarrelling and to share the muffin. Timmy's sister took a bite of the muffin and said it tasted funny. Timmy got nervous and thought maybe he had put something bad in it. But then they realized that their mom had accidentally put salt instead of sugar in the muffin batter. They all laughed and decided to make another batch of muffins together, this time with the right ingredients. And they all lived happily ever after. The end.

One day, Tom and his mom had a good idea. They wanted to go ice skating! Tom knew that he needed skates, so they went to the store to get them. When they arrived at the store, Tom was amazed by all the skates. He wanted to try them all! Tom tried the red pair, the blue pair, and the white pair. None of them felt quite right. Then Tom and his mom saw the sparkly skates. They were all different colors! Everything about them seemed special. Tom tried them on and they felt perfect. Tom and his mom went to the icy center to try out the skates. Tom loved the feeling of gliding across the ice. He had a great idea-he and his mom should go ice skating every week! Tom and his mom laughed and smiled as they raced around the rink. Tom knew he needed those special sparkly skates!

The ocean was calm and beautiful. There were lots of fish in the water and they were swimming around and having a great time. Suddenly, an octopus started to splash in the water. It was so happy! The octopus was loyal to its friends, and they all wanted to hang out together. The octopus started to play a game with the other fish. It would splash near them, and the fish would swim away really fast. It was so funny! The fish loved the game, and the octopus was very proud of being loyal. The fish kept swimming away from the octopus each time it splashed, but they eventually realized that the octopus was only playing. They all swam back to the octopus and surrounded it in a big circle. They started to splish and splash together and have lots of fun. The octopus was so happy and loyal to its new friends. All the fish learned that having a loyal friend can be the best thing in the world!

Once upon a time, there lived a happy little girl named Tina. She had a bouncing ball that she loved to play with. Every day, she would take her bouncing ball to the park and roll it down the trail. She would watch it as it rolled far away, and followed it with her eyes until a new adventure began. One cold and chilly day, Tina found that her bouncing ball had suddenly disappeared down a deep dark hole! She looked around to see what she could do and spotted a tall man standing near her. "Can you help me find my bouncing ball?" she asked the tall man. The tall man smiled and replied, "Yes I can! Follow me! I know the exact spot where your bouncing ball is." So, Tina followed the tall man on a new trail. After walking for a while, they finally arrived at the deep dark hole where Tina's bouncing ball was hidden! The tall man retrieved the bouncing ball, and returned it with a smile. Tina was so happy to have her bouncing ball back! She thanked the tall man for his help and ran back home to play with her bouncing ball.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to go to the museum with Mom and Dad. The museum has many things to see and learn. Sara likes the animals and Ben likes the cars. One day, they go to the museum and see a big sign. The sign says "Hide and Seek". Sara and Ben love to play hide and seek. They ask Mom and Dad if they can play. Mom and Dad say yes, but they have to stay in the same room and not run or touch anything. Sara and Ben start to play. Sara counts to ten and Ben runs to hide. He sees a big car with a shiny hood. He thinks it is a good hiding spot. He crawls under the car and waits for Sara to find him. Sara looks around the room. She sees many cars, but not Ben. She thinks he is very good at hiding. She walks to the other side of the room and sees a helpful lady. The lady wears a badge that says "Museum Guide". Sara asks the lady, "Have you seen my brother? He is hiding from me." The lady smiles and says, "I think I have. He is under the car with the shiny hood. Do you want me to show you?" Sara nods and says, "Yes, please. Thank you for being helpful." The lady takes Sara to the car and points under the hood. Sara sees Ben's feet sticking out. She says, "I found you, Ben! You are a good hider, but the lady helped me." Ben crawls out from under the car and says, "You are a good finder, Sara. And the lady is very nice. Can we say thank you to her?" Sara and Ben say thank you to the lady and give her a hug. The lady says, "You are very welcome. You are both very polite and smart. I hope you enjoy the museum." Sara and Ben smile and say, "We do. We love the museum. And we love playing hide and seek."

Once upon a time there lived a fish. He was a bright green fish and was very happy. One day he swam past a rock and noticed something shiny. He swam closer and saw that it was a symbol. So he swam over and tried to grab it. It was very difficult because it was slippery. He tried again and again. "Hey little fish", said a voice. A bigger fish popped up and smiled kindly. "What are you doing?" The little fish was embarrassed. "I was trying to get that symbol, but it's very difficult." The big fish smiled. "That is a special symbol, it's very special and rare. I'm glad you've noticed it but it is not for taking. It must stay here to bring the sea peace and joy." The little fish was disappointed but he respected the big fish's words. He stopped trying, and instead applauded the symbol. The little fish was happy to have seen it and they swam away together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. Mary's mom gave her a cookie. Mary was so excited that she said, "Yay! Cookie!" Her mom smiled and said, "How wonderful! What do you say?" Mary replied, "Thank you, mommy." Mary bit into her cookie, savoring its wonderful taste. She closed her eyes and said, "This is so yummy!" Her mom replied, "Glad you like it!" Mary then asked her mom, "Can I have another cookie?" Her mom said, "That's not very normal. How about an apple instead?" Mary thought for a minute, then said, "Ok, Mommy. I'll have an apple." Her mom smiled and said, "That's better! Here you go." She handed Mary the apple and Mary replied, "Thank you!" Mary enjoyed the fresh, delicious taste of the apple. She said, "This is really good too!" Her mom replied, "Glad you like it." Mary smiled and hugged her mom. All was well again in the house.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. It was a sunny day and the park was peaceful. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside. "Let's find out what's in there!" Tom said. "OK, but be careful!" Lily said. They went to the tree and looked inside the hole. They saw something shiny and black. It looked like a toy. "Wow, look at this!" Tom said. He reached inside and pulled out the shiny thing. It was a gun. "What is that?" Lily asked. "It's a toy gun. It makes a loud noise. Watch!" Tom said. He pointed the gun at the sky and pulled the trigger. BANG! The gun was not a toy. It was real. The loud noise scared Tom and Lily. They dropped the gun and ran away. But it was too late. The bullet hit a bird that was flying in the sky. The bird fell down and died. The park was not peaceful anymore. It was sad and scary. Tom and Lily cried. They wished they never found the gun. They wished they never hurt the bird. They wished they could go back to playing. But they couldn't. They had done something very bad.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to play outside and chase squirrels. One day, Max saw a collar on the ground. It was a messy collar with dirt and leaves all over it. Max picked up the collar in his mouth and ran to his owner, Lily. "Lily, look what I found!" Max said, dropping the collar at her feet. "Oh, Max, that's not ours. It belongs to someone else," Lily said. Max looked sad. "Can I keep it?" he asked. "No, Max. That wouldn't be right. We need to find the owner," Lily explained. Just then, a little girl came running up to them. "That's my dog's collar!" she said, taking it from Max's mouth. Max didn't mean to bite it, but he was just trying to play. The little girl thanked Max for finding it and Max wagged his tail happily.

Mum and her little daughter were very excited. Mum had bought two tickets to the big circus show. Her daughter was very happy. She had a little seat just for her. Mum and her daughter arrived at the circus. It was very busy and people were buying tickets. The tickets were very cheap. Mum said, "Let's buy a ticket for you." Her daughter was really happy. She wanted to sit in the best seat she could find. Mum and her daughter finally found their seats. Mum said to her daughter, "This is the best seat in the house." The show was about to start. Everyone was taking their seats. Mum's daughter was clapping her hands and laughing. She was so excited to see the show.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play at the park. They see a big swing. They want to swing on it. "Can I swing first?" Anna asks. "OK, but not too long," Ben says. Anna runs to the swing. She sits on it. She holds the ropes. She pushes with her feet. She swings high and low. She feels happy. "Wow, you swing so fast!" Ben says. "I like to swing fast. It is fun," Anna says. "Can I swing now?" Ben asks. "OK, it is your turn," Anna says. She jumps off the swing. She gives it to Ben. Ben sits on it. He holds the ropes. He pushes with his feet. He swings high and low. He feels happy. "Wow, you swing so high!" Anna says. "I like to swing high. It is fun," Ben says. They swing for a long time. They laugh and smile. They get thirsty. "Let's have some juice," Anna says. "OK, let's go to the bench," Ben says. They leave the swing. They walk to the bench. They see a bottle of juice. They share it. They drink it. It is sweet and cold. They feel good. "Juice is yummy," Anna says. "Juice is yummy," Ben says. They finish the juice. They hug each other. They are friends. They like to play at the park. They like to swing.

Katie was a fat cat. One day, she saw a trophy that she wanted to have. She knew it didn't belong to her, but she really wanted it. She climbed and stretched to get it, but it was too high for her. Katie looked around and thought of a way to get the trophy. She saw a little mouse, who wasn't fat like she was. She asked the mouse if he could help her. The mouse said he could. He climbed on the shelf and got the trophy for Katie. Katie was so happy! She said thank you to the mouse and went home with her new trophy. She knew it belonged to her now.

Once there was a little girl who had a hose. She liked to spray water everywhere and have fun. One day, she was playing in the garden and noticed a deaf cat nearby. She wanted to play with it, but the cat was scared and ignored her. The girl was sad her friend didn't want to play with her. She tried to coax the cat with her hose, but the cat was too scared and ran away. The little girl had to accept that the cat wasn't her friend. Even though the cat was deaf and couldn't hear her, she wanted it to be her friend and had to learn to ignore it. Still, she hoped that one day the cat would come back and they could play together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy fell down and hurt his knee. He cried and cried because it hurt so much. His mommy came over and picked him up. She hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. It's okay. I'm here to comfort you." She gave him a snack, a yummy apple, to make him feel better. After a little while, Timmy's knee started to feel normal again. He smiled and went back to playing with his toys. He was happy because his mommy was there to make him feel better.

Bella looked at the clay. She wanted to get it. She wanted to make something beautiful with it. Bella ran to the store and asked her mom to get her some clay. Mom said yes and took her to the store. The store had all kinds of clay: red, green, blue, and more. Bella picked out some blue clay. She couldn't wait to get started! Mom and Bella got back home with the clay. Bella washed her hands and began building. Her hands moved the clay around. She made a vase, then a bowl. Finally, Bella made a beautiful flower. It was so pretty that Mom couldn't believe it. They looked at the beautiful flower together and it was the best thing ever!

One day, a little boy named Tim went to get a haircut. He was very excited because he wanted to look nice for his friend's birthday party. His mom took him to a reliable hairdresser, who always gave good haircuts. As they walked in, the hairdresser said, "Hi Tim! Are you ready for your haircut?" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, I am ready!" The hairdresser put a cape on him and started to cut his hair. Tim sat very still so the hairdresser could do a good job. After the haircut, Tim's mom wanted to test how good it was. She asked Tim, "Do you like your new haircut?" Tim looked in the mirror and saw his short, neat hair. He smiled and said, "I love it! Thank you for the nice haircut!" Tim and his mom left the hairdresser, happy with the reliable haircut. Now, Tim was ready for his friend's party.

Mia was very excited. She had a magical train ride to take. She wore her fun polka dot dress and her purply boots for the special day. Her mommy pushed her in the train car and showed her where to sit. Mia was so excited for the mysterious ride. As the train started moving, Mia looked out the window. Trees and houses flew by quickly. When the train stopped, Mia's mommy opened the door and said "Look, look Mia". Mia's eyes lit up when she saw a castle with a big pond and lots of colorful flowers. Mia just couldn't believe how wonderful and mysterious the train ride was. She was so excited to be able to explore the incredible place.

Once, there was a little girl who loved to play the flute. She would put on her pretty dress and run to the park, her favorite spot to perform. One day, she was playing her flute, when she heard a strange noise. She saw a pale cat stuck in a bush. She quickly put down her flute and ran to rescue the cat. The girl stuck her arm in the bush, and the cat jumped out, into her arms. She said to the cat, "Are you ok?" The cat purred and rubbed against her neck. The little girl was so happy to have rescued the cat. She hugged the cat and thanked it for joining her for a flute performance in the park. The cat meowed and seemed to understand. From then on, the little girl was never alone when she went to play her flute in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom was making a cake and asked Lily to polish the silverware. Lily found it difficult to hold the silverware, but she tried her best. While she was polishing, her mom asked her, "Lily, do you know what season it is outside?" Lily looked out the window and said, "It's summer!" "That's right," said her mom. "And in the summer, we like to eat cake with fresh fruit on top. Can you go pick some strawberries from the garden?" Lily was excited to help and quickly ran outside to pick some strawberries. When she came back inside, her mom had finished the cake and they sat down to eat it together. "This cake is delicious!" said Lily. "I'm glad you like it," said her mom. "And thank you for helping me polish the silverware and pick the strawberries. You're such a good helper." Lily smiled and felt proud of herself for being such a good helper in the kitchen.

Lily liked to count. She counted her fingers, her toes, her dolls, and her books. She counted everything she saw. One day, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a man playing music on a big guitar. He had a hat on the ground with some coins in it. "Mom, can I count the coins?" Lily asked. "Sure, honey, but be careful and polite. The man is working hard to make music for us," her mom said. Lily walked over to the hat and knelt down. She picked up a coin and said, "One." She picked up another coin and said, "Two." She kept counting until she reached ten. She was very proud of herself. The man noticed her and smiled. He stopped playing and said, "Hello, little girl. You are very good at counting. Do you like my music?" Lily nodded. She liked the music. It made her happy. "Thank you. I'm glad you like it. You know, you are very generous to count my coins. You can keep one if you want. It's a gift from me to you," the man said. Lily was surprised. She looked at the coin in her hand. It was shiny and round. She liked it. "Thank you, sir. You are very generous too. You make beautiful music for everyone," she said. She gave the man a hug and ran back to her mom. She showed her the coin and told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "You are very lucky, Lily. You met a kind and talented man. And you learned a new word today. Generous. Do you know what it means?" Lily thought for a moment. She remembered how the man shared his music and his coin with her. She remembered how happy she felt. "It means to give and make others happy," she said. Her mom smiled and said, "That's right, Lily. You are very smart and sweet. I love you." Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, mom. And I love counting and music."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small hut with her mommy and daddy. The hut was very tight, and they didn't have a lot of space to play. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to go to the store to supply some milk. Lily was very excited to help and ran to the store. When she got there, she saw her friend Timmy. "Hi Timmy!" Lily said. "Hi Lily!" Timmy replied. "What are you doing here?" "I'm here to supply some milk for my mommy," Lily said proudly. "That's great!" Timmy said. "Do you want to come play with me?" Lily thought about it for a moment, but then remembered that she needed to get the milk for her mommy. "Sorry, Timmy. I can't play right now. I need to go back to my tight hut and give the milk to my mommy." "Okay, maybe we can play later," Timmy said. Lily smiled and ran back home to supply the milk to her mommy. When she got back, her mommy was very happy and gave her a big hug. "Thank you, Lily!" she said. Lily felt very proud of herself for helping her mommy and smiled as she snuggled into her tight bed.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny named Benny. Benny liked to eat carrots and hop around in the grass. One day, Benny went on a walk and left a trail of footprints behind him. As he hopped along, he saw a butterfly and tried to catch it. But the butterfly flew away and Benny got sad. Suddenly, he remembered his mommy telling him that when he feels sad, he should spread kindness to others. So, Benny hopped over to his friend Sally's house and gave her a big hug. Sally smiled and thanked Benny for being a good friend. Benny felt happy again and hopped back home, leaving a new trail of happy footprints behind him. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdy named Tweetie. Tweetie was very happy in her birdcage. She had food and water and toys to play with. One day, a little girl named Lily came to visit Tweetie. Lily said, "Oh, Tweetie, you look so pale. Don't you want to come out and play with me?" Tweetie said, "I can't come out. I'm stuck in my birdcage." Lily said, "Don't worry, I'll help you." So, Lily opened the birdcage and Tweetie flew out. They played together and had a lot of fun. But then, the sun got very hot and Tweetie started to feel very warm. She said, "Oh no, I think I'm starting to melt!" Lily said, "Don't worry, I'll take care of you." So, Lily brought Tweetie back to her cage and gave her some water to cool down. The moral of the story is that it's important to help our friends when they need us, even if it means doing something that might be a little scary or difficult.

Tim and Sue like to play with balls. They have many balls of different colors and sizes. They like to throw them, catch them, kick them and roll them. Sometimes they play with their friends in the park, and sometimes they play in their backyard. One day, they decide to play a new game with their balls. They call it strike and strip. The game is easy and fun. They take turns to throw a ball at a big box. The box has many strips of paper taped on it. If they hit the box, they can take off one strip. If they miss, they have to wait for their next turn. "Are you ready, Sue?" Tim asks, holding a red ball. "Yes, I am ready, Tim!" Sue answers, standing behind the box. Tim throws the ball hard. He hopes to strike the box and take off a strip. But the ball flies too high and lands on the roof. "Oh no, Tim! You missed!" Sue says, laughing. "It's okay, Sue. I will try again later. Now it's your turn!" Tim says, smiling. Sue picks up a blue ball. She aims at the box. She throws the ball gently. She wants to strike the box and take off a strip. And she does! The ball hits the box and makes a loud noise. Sue runs to the box and peels off a yellow strip. "Yay, Sue! You did it!" Tim says, clapping. "Thank you, Tim! This game is easy and fun!" Sue says, holding the strip. They continue to play strike and strip until they run out of balls and strips. They have a lot of fun and laugh a lot. They like their new game very much.

One day a small pig was walking around in the woods. The pig saw something and he was very curious. So he went a bit closer and he saw a big black spider. The pig was scared, but he was brave. He decided to stay and watch the spider. The spider looked back at the pig and the pig jumped. Then the spider moved closer and the pig felt a bit scared. But he stayed still. The spider got closer and closer and the pig started to get really scared. The spider was about to bite the pig. But before it could, something made a noise in the woods. The spider ran away, scared. The pig was relieved and he was very happy. He knew that he had been very brave and that the noise had saved him from being bitten.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Jimmy and Sarah. They both loved to be creative and thought of lots of fun ideas. One day, Jimmy came up with a special game. He found a big empty stage and said it could be a special question game. Sarah thought this sounded fun and wanted to play. Jimmy started by asking Sarah a question. She had to think really hard before answering. After Sarah answered Jimmy's question, it was her turn to ask a question. The two friends played the special question game for a long time. They liked to try and come up with tricky questions for each other. It was a lot of fun to be creative! At the end, Jimmy and Sarah were very happy. They had had a lot of fun with their special question game.

Once there was a city full of people. Everyone was very selfish and didn't care about each other. Then one day, a funny little mouse came along. He was so fun and friendly that everyone in the city started smiling. Everyone was so happy that they clapped their hands and applauded the mouse. Everyone enjoyed spending time with him, too. Soon the whole city was no longer selfish, but full of love and friendship. All the people celebrated and applauded the little mouse in gratitude. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a dead armchair in the corner of the room. One day, it began to ring! The little boy was very surprised. He couldn't understand why the armchair was ringing. He started to jump up and down and laugh. The ringing became louder and louder. Suddenly, the ringing stopped and a funny voice came from the armchair. It said, "Boo! Did I scare you?". The little boy was so shocked! Then he saw a little mouse peeking out from the armchair's cushion. The little mouse was the one who had been ringing the armchair! The boy started to laugh and they both played together until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with cardboard boxes. One day, she found a huge cardboard box and decided to make a castle out of it. As she was building her castle, her little brother Max came over and accidentally knocked it down. Lily started to cry and said, "My castle is ruined!" Max felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Let's build a bigger and better castle together!" Lily stopped crying and smiled. They worked together to build an even bigger castle out of the huge cardboard box. They had so much fun playing in their new castle and forgot all about the old one. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a tasty squirrel. He was a very small squirrel, but he was full of energy and brave. One day, he decided to explore the world around him. He jumped from tree to tree and ran across the grass. Suddenly he heard a noise. He looked around, but he couldn't find out what it was. Curious, he decided to investigate and see what he could find. He kept running until he arrived at a giant tree. It was so big that he had never seen anything like it before. Suddenly, he heard the noise again. He looked up and saw a big bird flying above him. He was so excited to see something new. The squirrel watched the bird fly away, until he was too far away to be seen. The squirrel was happy and full of joy after his adventure and he ran back to his family. From then on, he always enjoyed exploring the world around him. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, she went to the store with her mommy. Her mommy told her that they didn't have enough money to buy everything she wanted. Lily asked, "Why not?" Her mommy said, "We only have a little bit of money available right now." Lily thought for a moment and then said, "That's okay. I just want to buy this toy." Her mommy smiled and they went to the cashier. When the cashier gave them the change, Lily started to laugh. She loved the sound of money jingling in her hand. From that day on, Lily learned that even though they didn't have a lot of money, they could still have fun and be happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to make things with her hands. One day, she decided to make a cake for her mommy's birthday. She mixed flour, sugar, and eggs together to make the batter. Then, she put the batter into the oven to bake. When the cake was done, Lily wanted to test it to make sure it was yummy. She took a little piece and tasted it. It was so delicious! She was so happy that she made a cake that her mommy would love. But when she took the cake out of the oven, she accidentally dropped it on the floor. The cake looked so ugly and messy. Lily was sad, but she didn't give up. She decided to make another cake for her mommy, and this time, she was extra careful. When the cake was done, she tested it and it was perfect! Her mommy loved it, and Lily was so proud of herself for making such a yummy cake.

One day, a little girl was running fast through the park. Her feet felt light and she had a big smile on her face. Suddenly, she tripped and dropped to the ground. Her knee started to hurt. She started crying, but her mom was nearby. She gave her a big hug, and then she helped her up again. Her mom promised to be more careful next time, and reminded her to not run so fast. The little girl promised to be more careful and keep her speed down. With a smile on her face, she was ready to keep playing. The next day, the little girl was running again. She was going faster that usual and the ground was slippery. Her foot slipped and she felt herself drop. She hit the ground and it hurt. But then, mom was there. She hugged her and reminded her to always pay attention and keep her speed down. The little girl was sad, but she learned an important lesson: pay attention and don't run too fast. She was ready to start playing again, this time a little slower.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play outside. One day, she saw a big yellow ball in the sky that looked like it was glowing. She asked her mommy what it was and her mommy said it was the sun. Lily loved watching the sun move across the sky. Sometimes it was slow and other times it moved with great speed. But when it got really late, the sun would disappear and the sky would turn dark. Then, the stars would come out and they looked so tiny and distant. Lily loved to look at the stars and imagine what it would be like to fly up and touch them. She would close her eyes and dream of flying through the sky, feeling the wind in her hair and the stars glowing all around her. It was her favorite thing to do before going to bed.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play dress-up. She had many pretty clothes in her closet, but she wanted more. One day, she saw her mom's laundry basket in the hall. It had some big clothes that looked nice and soft. Lily decided to borrow some of them and try them on. She took a pink sweater, a blue skirt, and a yellow scarf from the basket. She put them on and looked at herself in the mirror. She felt very happy and pretty. She did not think her mom would mind if she borrowed them for a little while. She went outside to show her friends her new outfit. They were playing in the yard with a ball. Lily joined them and threw the ball around. She did not notice that the sweater was too long and the skirt was too wide. They got caught on a branch and ripped. The scarf got dirty from the grass and mud. Lily's mom came out to see what was going on. She saw Lily wearing her clothes and how they were ruined. She was very angry and sad. She asked Lily why she took her clothes without asking. Lily said she just wanted to borrow them and play dress-up. She said she was sorry and did not mean to hurt them. But Lily's mom did not forgive her. She said Lily was naughty and selfish. She said she had to pay for the clothes and do extra chores. She took Lily inside and made her take off the clothes. She did not let her play with her friends or watch TV. She sent her to her room and told her to think about what she did. Lily felt very bad and lonely. She wished she had not borrowed her mom's clothes. She wished she had asked first or used her own clothes. She wished she could say sorry again and make her mom happy. She cried and cried until she fell asleep. She had a bad day.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly crocodile who lived in a small pond. He had lived there his whole life and very rarely met anyone on his adventures. One day, he decided to explore the pond to see what he could find. He was very surprised to come across a delicious fruit in the water! It tasted sweet and he knew he just had to have a taste. He gobbled up the fruit whole and it made his tummy feel so good. He continued to explore around the pond and found more fruit for himself. The elderly crocodile was so happy he had discovered this wonderful treat. He enjoyed the fruity taste and spent his days swimming in the pond, searching for more fruit. Eventually, he decided to share his secret with the animals around him, but he never told anyone else where he had found it. Even to this day, no one knows how the elderly crocodile found that magical fruit in the pond!

Once upon a time, there was a little three-year-old girl called Sarah. She loved playing with her toys, and she was very good at managing them. One day, Sarah was playing with her toy animals in the living room when her mom came over to her. Mom said, "Sarah, I need you to manage your toys and put them back in the box. Can you do that for me?" Sarah smiled and said, "Yes, Mom. I can do it. I'm very good at managing!" So Sarah carefully picked up each of her toys and put them back in the box. When she was finished, Mom gave her a hug and said, "That was a very good job, Sarah. You did a great job of managing your toys!" Sarah smiled happily and said, "Thank you, Mom. I love managing my toys!"

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to wear her favorite bracelet every day. It was a shiny and sparkly bracelet that made her feel happy. One day, Lily was playing in the park when she saw a poor boy crying. She went to him and asked, "Why are you crying?" The boy answered, "I lost my bracelet, and it was my only treasure." Lily felt sad for the poor boy and decided to help him. She asked him what the bracelet looked like, and he described it to her. Lily remembered seeing a bracelet like that on the ground earlier that day. She ran back to the spot and found the bracelet. Lily gave the bracelet to the poor boy, and he was so happy that he hugged her. He thanked her for her kindness, and Lily felt happy too. She learned that helping others can make them happy and make her happy too.

Once there was a child who was very persistent. Everywhere she went she would try her best to make people laugh by telling jokes. One day she went to the park with her family and ran around telling jokes to anyone who would listen. The child never got tired of telling jokes. Even when people didn't laugh she kept trying to make them smile. Everyone she passed was happy to hear her jokes and even though sometimes it wasn't funny, they were impressed by her persistent nature. After a while, the child had gotten so good at telling jokes, that people were soon coming from other parts of the park to listen to her funny stories. People would smile and laugh and even the adults would be amazed by her ability to make them smile. By the end of the day, everyone in the park was happy and roaring with laughter, thanks to the child and her contagious jokes. She felt proud that her efforts had made so many people smile.

The sun was shining and the birds were singing. Sam saw a stick lying on the ground. He decided to pick it up. But when he went to grab it, he realised that it wasn't an ordinary stick. It was furry! Sam was surprised. He tried to pick it up again, but the stick started to move! Sam was amazed. It was a fuzzy little animal. He could see it was a squirrel. The squirrel ran away quickly and Sam couldn't catch him. Sam was very disappointed. He wanted to play with the furry squirrel. Suddenly he had an idea. He went and got some nuts from his house. Then he put the nuts near the tree where the squirrel had gone. He waited patiently. Finally the squirrel came back. Sam put some of the nuts in his hand and waited. The squirrel came up to Sam and started to eat the nuts right out of his hand, much to Sam's delight. Sam and the squirrel were now friends. Every afternoon they played together, running and chasing each other around the park. Sam was happy to have a new furry friend.

Once upon a time there was a fish who wanted to climb a mountain. He was a brave little fish, but the mountain was very high and it look heavy to climb. He asked his friend the bird to help him, "Please help me to climb, my friend?" The bird said, "It is too heavy for you. I can help you find a better way, let's think together." The bird and the little fish thought and thought until they finally came with a plan. The fish and the bird decided to go to the sea together. When they got there, the fish swam up and slowly, slowly made his way up the mountain by swimming and jumping. The bird flew ahead to the top and shouted and waved. The little fish made it! He was so proud and grateful for his friend's help and shouted, "You are the best, my friend!" The fish enjoyed the beautiful view from the top and after a while, started to make his way down again, back to the sea. So, with the help of a friend and a lot of courage, the fish was able to climb the heavy mountain.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor. He loved to go out on his boat, so one sunny day, he did just that. The sailor moved his boat around the lake, and all around he could see, the birds flying and the fish swimming. He was having lots of fun. Suddenly, the wind began to blow. The sailor was so excited! The wind meant that he could spread the big sail and go faster. So he did. He spread the sail out, and soon the boat was sailing fast around the lake. The sailor clapped with joy. He was having the best time ever! But then, the wind died down. The sailor was impatient for it to come back. He clapped and asked the sky for more wind. Finally, the wind came back, and the sailor continued to sail around the lake. He was so happy and never wanted the day to end.

One day, a little boy was walking in the park. Suddenly he heard something that sounded like a loud roar. But it didn't sound like a lion! It was coming from the mailbox. The little boy was so surprised that he ran over to it. When he got there, he saw that it was an angry cat. The cat was roaring and hissing at the little boy. Suddenly the cat jumped out of the mailbox, and the little boy ran away, scared. The little boy was very happy to get home. He told everyone about the angry cat roaring in the mailbox. Everyone thought it was funny, but he was still a little scared!

Once upon a time, there was a kind fireman named Tim. He wore a big red hat and drove a shiny red truck. One day, Tim went to a school to speak to the children. He told them how to be safe if there was a fire. The children listened carefully because Tim was very polite and spoke in a friendly voice. After Tim finished speaking, the children asked him questions. They asked how he became a fireman and if he had ever rescued a cat from a tree. Tim answered all of their questions and made them laugh with silly jokes. The children were so happy to meet Tim and learn about fire safety. They waved goodbye as Tim drove away in his big red truck. From that day on, they knew that if there was ever a fire, a polite fireman like Tim would be there to help them.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside in the dirt and mud. One day, his mom told him to come inside and wash his hands before eating his food. Timmy didn't want to stop playing, so he ignored his mom's reminder. Later that day, Timmy's tummy started to hurt. He realized he had eaten his food with dirty hands. He went to his mom and said, "Mommy, my tummy hurts. I think I ate my food with dirty hands." His mom said, "I reminded you to wash your hands before eating. Now you know why it's important." From that day on, Timmy always remembered to wash his hands before eating his food. He didn't want his tummy to hurt again.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big black balloon. It was a very special balloon. It could fly high up in the sky. One sunny day, a little girl named Lily found the black balloon. She wanted to see it fly. So, she took it outside to release it. She let go of the balloon and it went up, up, up into the sky. As the black balloon flew higher, it started to release some gas. The gas made the balloon go even higher. Lily laughed and clapped her hands as she watched it fly away. She knew the black balloon was happy to be free.

Once there was a little boy named Timmy. He was 3 years old and very curious. He wanted to understand the world around him. One day Timmy was looking at an old mural his Grandma had created. It had lots of symbols painted on it. One of the symbols was a big blue circle. Timmy asked his Grandma, "What does this symbol mean?" She explained to him that this symbol was the symbol of understanding. It meant that if you understand something, it will be easier to learn. Timmy felt happy to know what this blue symbol meant. He was now one step closer to understanding the world around him.

Once upon a time, a friendly bunny was hopping across the forest. He liked to collect things he found along the way. He found a big trunk filled with all sorts of treasures. He liked all the shiny bits so much he opened it and started to collect them. The bunny was so happy with his new trinkets that he wanted to take them home, so he grabbed the trunk and hopped away again. He kept collecting along the way and the trunk got heavier and heavier until he could barely carry it. He needed help, so he found a friendly bear. He asked the bear to help him carry the trunk, and the bear was so friendly that he said yes. The bunny hopped along with the bear, collecting more things until they arrived at the bunny's home. The bunny was so happy to see his home again. He looked inside the trunk and smiled. All of his treasures were safe and sound, and he was so proud of the things he had collected. He thanked the friendly bear, who waved goodbye and left. The bunny was so excited to be able to show everyone all the wonderful things he had collected. He had had a very fun day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Bear and Rabbit. They loved to play together and have fun. One day, they decided to make a pizza. Bear brought the cheese and Rabbit brought the sauce. They put the sauce on the pizza and it tasted really good. But then, they started to argue about who made the pizza better. Bear said his cheese was the best and Rabbit said his sauce was better. They both felt angry and sad. Then, they remembered they were friends and decided to stop arguing. They apologized and decided to unite and make another pizza together. This time, they both agreed that the pizza tasted better with both the cheese and the sauce. They were happy and not ashamed anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to jog every day. He would run around his house and count how many times he could go around. One day, Timmy met a girl named Sarah. Sarah was very nice and they became friends. Timmy and Sarah would play together every day. They would play hide and seek and tag. Timmy liked Sarah a lot and he wanted to marry her when they grew up. Sarah thought Timmy was very kind and funny, but she thought they were just ordinary friends. One day, Timmy asked Sarah if she wanted to jog with him. Sarah said yes and they jogged together around the house. Timmy was very happy because he got to spend time with Sarah. Even though Sarah only thought they were ordinary friends, Timmy knew that one day they would be more than that.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the beach with his mommy and daddy. He loved the sand and the water. One day, Timmy saw the tide coming in. He got excited and ran towards the water. The waves were big and made Timmy feel restless. He jumped up and down and laughed as the water splashed on his feet. His mommy and daddy watched him play and smiled. They loved seeing Timmy have fun. As the sun began to set, Timmy got tired and sat down on the beach. The waves continued to come in and go out, but Timmy was too tired to play anymore. He watched the tide and felt peaceful. He was happy to rest after a fun day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a cool otter who lived alone at the bottom of the river. Every single day, the otter had lots of fun swimming in the water, eating fish and playing with its friends. One day, while the otter was swimming, it saw a little boy and his mom looking down into the water. The boy was so excited to see the otter and shouted, "Look, mommy! An otter!" The otter smiled and said, "Hi! Would you like me to show you something cool?" The little boy was so excited, he jumped and said, "Yes please!" So, the otter jumped up out of the water, did a big somersault and then came back down with a splash. The little boy and his mom laughed as the otter swam back up to them. "That was so cool", said the little boy. The otter smiled, said goodbye, and swam away. The little boy and his mom waved goodbye and continued to laugh, even after the otter was gone.

Once upon a time, there were twin dogs named Tim and Tom. They lived in a big house with a nice yard. They liked to play with their ball and run around. One day, a fierce cat came to their yard. The cat looked mean and wanted to play with Tim and Tom's ball. Tim and Tom did not like the cat, so they tried to lead the cat away from their ball. They ran around the yard, and the cat followed them. They led the cat to a big tree. The cat saw a bird in the tree and forgot about the ball. The cat climbed the tree to chase the bird. Tim and Tom were happy that they led the cat away. They got their ball back and played together all day. The fierce cat never came back to their yard again.

Once upon a time, there was a honest boy named Peter. On a Tuesday he wanted to speak to someone. So he went outside, and saw his neighbor Mrs. Barbara in her garden. He walked up to her and said "Hello Mrs. Barbara, can I talk to you?" Mrs. Barbara smiled at Peter and said "Sure, what do you want to talk about?" Peter was excited and said "I want to talk about my new toy car! It's red and shiny." Mrs. Barbara was listening carefully and asked "Oh really, that sounds very nice. Is it honest?". Peter nodded and said "Yes, it is honest and I love it. I can play with it for hours and hours and it's so much fun!" Mrs. Barbara was happy to hear that, and said "Well that's wonderful! I'm so glad you're enjoying it." Peter thanked Mrs. Barbara and said goodbye. He went back home, very happy in his heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved sausages, they were his favourite food. One day, Timmy's mom told him he couldn't have any more sausages because he had already eaten too many. Timmy felt sad and angry, but he knew his mom was right. Later that day, Timmy saw his little sister playing with a ball near the road. He had a foolish idea to kick the ball as hard as he could, even though he knew it was dangerous. His mom saw what he was about to do and urged him to stop. Timmy listened to his mom and didn't kick the ball. He realized his mom was trying to keep him safe and he felt grateful. From that day on, Timmy made sure to always listen to his mom's advice.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy gun that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy's mom saw the gun and didn't like it. She told Timmy that guns are not safe and can hurt people. She took the gun away from Timmy and gave him a new toy to replace it. The new toy was very attractive and colorful. Timmy loved his new toy and forgot about the old gun. He played with his new toy every day and had lots of fun. Timmy's mom was happy that he was playing with a safe toy. Timmy learned that guns are not toys and should not be played with. He was happy to have his new toy to play with instead.

Lily loved to skip. She skipped in the park, she skipped in the school, she skipped at home. She liked to skip with her family, too. Her mom, her dad, and her baby brother. They skipped and laughed and had fun. One day, Lily saw a big dog in the park. The dog was bad. It barked and growled and chased people. Lily was scared. She ran to her mom and dad and held their hands. The dog came near them and tried to bite. "Go away, bad dog!" Lily's dad shouted. He picked up a stick and threw it at the dog. The dog ran after the stick and left them alone. "Are you okay, Lily?" Lily's mom asked. She hugged Lily and kissed her cheek. "I'm okay, mom," Lily said. "But I don't like the bad dog." "Me neither, Lily," Lily's mom said. "But don't worry, the bad dog is gone now. We are safe." Lily smiled and nodded. She felt better. She looked at her family and said, "Can we skip again?" "Of course, Lily," Lily's dad said. "We love to skip with you." They skipped and laughed and had fun. Lily was happy. She loved her family and they loved her.

Lila and Ben love to watch the parade. They see big balloons, loud drums, and pretty costumes. They wave at the people who walk by and smile. One day, they see a little dog in the parade. The dog has a red hat and a blue coat. He looks very happy. But then, he trips on a string and falls down. He starts to cry. Lila and Ben feel sad for the dog. They want to help him. They run to the dog and hug him. They say, "It's okay, dog. You are brave and cute. We are your friends." The dog stops crying and wags his tail. He licks their faces and thanks them. He says, "You are very kind and compassionate. You make me feel better. Can I join you and watch the parade?" Lila and Ben nod and smile. They take the dog to their spot and share their snacks with him. They watch the parade together and have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, heavy rock. It sat in the middle of a field where the flowers grew. The rock didn't move, and the flowers grew all around it. One day, a little bird came to the field. The bird saw the rock and thought it would be a good place to rest. But when the bird landed on the rock, something strange happened. The rock started to disappear! The bird was scared and flew away. But later, a kind lady came to the field. She saw the flowers and wanted to give them a massage. As she walked, she saw the rock was gone! She looked all around, but it was nowhere to be found. The lady realized that the rock must have disappeared because it was too heavy. It sank into the ground and became a part of the earth. From that day on, the lady always looked carefully before she gave the flowers a massage. She didn't want to disappear like the heavy rock.

Jenny and her mom went outside to the park. It was a sunny day and the outdoor was full of children playing. Jenny and her mom saw a huge tree and started running after it. The tree looked so big and their eyes sparkled in admiration. Jenny and her mom started disagreeing because Jenny wanted to climb the tree but her mom said it was too dangerous and that she should wait until it stopped raining. But Jenny kept insisting and she just wanted to explore the huge tree. But it started raining and the lightning lit up the sky and the thunder roared, Jenny's mom held her hand and told her to come back inside. As soon as they reached home, the storm worsened and Jenny heard her mom saying, "Jenny, I told you not to go play outside in this kind of weather. It's too dangerous." Then, the lightning struck the very same spot where Jenny had wanted to climb the tree. Ten minutes later, the tree was completely dead. Jenny dropped her jaw and tears filled her eyes. Jenny's mom hugged her and said, "See, I told you it was too dangerous to be outside in this kind of weather. Let's learn from this and listen to mom next time." Jenny nodded and said, I will.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful sailor named Tom. Tom had a big boat with a large sail. He loved to sail on the blue sea with his friends. One sunny day, Tom and his friends were sailing when they saw a little bird with a hurt wing. The bird could not fly. Tom said to his friends, "We must help this little bird. Let's support it and make it feel better." Tom's friends agreed, and they all worked together to take care of the bird. They gave it food and a safe place to rest on the boat. The bird felt much better, and soon it could fly again. Before the bird flew away, it said, "Thank you, Tom and friends, for supporting me. You are all very kind." Tom and his friends felt happy, and they continued to sail on the sea, always ready to help when needed.

Mabel was throwing a party for her 3rd birthday. She invited all of her friends over for a big celebration. Everyone showed up with a big smile, excited for the day. Mabel welcomed all the kids to the party and showed them the fun activities she had prepared. There was a big sandbox, lots of books and games, and a giant birthday cake. The kids were cheerful as they began to enjoy the fair. At the end of the party, Mabel noticed that there were a few presents that still hadn't been opened. She asked her friends, "Who has the present that I haven't opened yet?" One of her friends stepped forward and said, "I do! I wanted to surprise you!" Mabel gasped with delight as she opened the present. Inside were all the materials to complete a big jigsaw puzzle of a rainbow. After everyone clapped and cheered, Mabel put on her cardigan and the children finished the puzzle together. Mabel looked around and smiled. The party was complete. Everyone had a fair and fun time!

Lily was in her classroom. She saw a large desk in the corner which was the teacher's. Although it was distant, she could see the colorful papers and objects on it. Lily was only three but she was learning a lot in school. She wanted to learn new things! So one day, while her teacher was not around, Lily decided to walk to the desk. When she got there she looked carefully at all the things on the desk. She touched a pencil and pretended to write like her teacher did. She also looked at a book and pretended to be a scientist. Even though she couldn't read yet, she had fun pretending! After a few minutes, Lily heard someone coming. It was her teacher. She quickly ran back to her seat. On her way she was very careful to make sure she didn't get caught. The next day, Lily was very happy when the teacher asked her to come to the desk. She had learned that it was OK for her to explore and use her imagination. So, she went to the desk with a smile on her face, ready to learn something new.

Once there was a mouse who was very lazy. He never wanted to work and was always looking for something to do. One day he was very bored and he decided to take a walk. As he was walking, he saw an old twig lying on the floor. The mouse decided to take it and play with it. He started to swing the twig around in the air and suddenly he noticed something amazing - he could see a clear image of his reflection in the twig! The mouse was so happy with his discovery and from that day, he never stopped playing with the twig. This story teaches us that when we work hard, we can find incredible things around us.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally loved playing outside when the sunshine was out. One day, Sally's mom said they were going to celebrate her birthday with a big party. Sally was so happy and excited! At the party, Sally's mom brought out a big cake with lots of frosting and candles. Sally blew out the candles and everyone cheered. Sally's friends gave her presents and they all played games together. Sally felt so special and loved. After the party, Sally's mom said she was spoiled with all the presents and cake. Sally didn't understand what that meant, but she knew she had a fun day with her friends and family. She couldn't wait to celebrate her birthday again next year!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with colorful pens and ink.
